questions.q: ऋषिप्रोक्तः means 'told (asked) by the sages'. By the same pattern, what does गुरुप्रोक्तः mean?
optionExplain: The teacher is the one who tells, not the one told.
The compound describes what was told.
It is not a pair; the first member says by whom.
Right: The first member names the one who tells; the second is 'told'.
questions.explain: A first member like ऋषि- or गुरु- names the one by whom something was told.
questions.rule: X-प्रोक्तः = told by X.
questions.teaches: In X-प्रोक्तः the first member names the speaker, as in ब्रह्मणा प्रोक्तम् (verse 4).

questions.q: The verse speaks of diseases as विघ्नभूताः. Which meaning of विघ्न do you expect?
optionExplain: Right: विघ्न means an obstacle or hindrance.
Medicine would be the opposite of what the verse says.
The sages come in the next verse.
No teacher is meant here.
questions.explain: Diseases became obstacles (विघ्न) to the practices named in the second line.
questions.rule: विघ्न = obstacle.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words tell what happened and to whom.
questions.rule: विघ्नभूताः = having become obstacles; प्रादुर्भूताः = arose; शरीरिणाम् = of embodied beings; यदा = when.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: The word for 'of embodied beings' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: शरीरिणाम् names those who have a body.
questions.teaches: -णाम् is the genitive plural, 'of ...'. शरीरिन् means 'one who has a body', so शरीरिणाम् is 'of the embodied'.
questions.rule: शरीरिणाम् = of embodied beings.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रादुर्भूताः?
optionExplain: There is no अ in front of भूताः.
Right: A visarga before the voiced भ becomes र्, so प्रादुः + भूताः is written प्रादुर्भूताः.
र्भूताः is not a word.
आदुर्भूताः is not a word.
questions.explain: प्रादुर्भूताः = प्रादुः ('into view') + भूताः ('become'): they came into being.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: The second line ends in -आयुषाम्, a genitive plural. On the usual reading, what does that say about the list?
options: These are the people who study
These are the things the diseases got in the way of
These are the sages who gather
optionExplain: The diseases are रोगाः in the first line.
The people are शरीरिणाम्.
Right: 'Of austerity ... and life': the genitive links the list to the obstacles.
The sages gather in verse 7.
questions.explain: The list in the genitive names what the obstacles are for: practices and life itself.
questions.rule: The genitive list = what was obstructed.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: A sentence begins यदा रोगाः प्रादुर्भूताः. Which word would begin the clause that completes it?
optionExplain: कदा asks 'when?'; it does not answer यदा.
यथा pairs with तथा, 'as ... so'.
तथा means 'so, likewise', not 'then'.
Right: यदा … तदा is the matching pair: 'when ... then'.
questions.explain: यदा 'when' is answered by तदा 'then'; verse 7 begins with तदा.
questions.rule: यदा … तदा = when … then.
questions.teaches: Sanskrit pairs words like यदा–तदा and यथा–तथा; seeing one tells you which will answer it.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Diseases have appeared. What do you expect moved the great sages to assemble?
options: A plan to hold a sacrifice
optionExplain: Right: The verse says they put compassion first.
No command is mentioned.
Nothing of the kind is said.
No sacrifice is mentioned.
questions.explain: They assembled out of compassion (अनुक्रोश) for living beings.
questions.rule: अनुक्रोश = compassion, the reason they gathered.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say why and how the sages met.
questions.rule: अनुक्रोशम् = compassion; पुरस्कृत्य = putting foremost; समेताः = assembled; शुभे = auspicious.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: The word for 'great sages' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: महर्षयः are the doers of the assembling.
questions.teaches: महर्षयः = महा + ऋषयः, and -अयः is the nominative plural: the sages are the subject.
questions.rule: महर्षयः = great sages (the subject).
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Which is the right split of भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम्?
optionExplain: भूतेष्व is not a word.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, so भूतेषु + अनुक्रोशम् is written भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम्.
वनुक्रोशम् is not a word.
षु is only an ending, not a word.
questions.explain: भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम् = भूतेषु ('for beings') + अनुक्रोशम् ('compassion').
questions.rule: भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम् = भूतेषु + अनुक्रोशम्.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: भूतेषु ends in -षु, the locative plural. How does it relate to the compassion?
options: It is felt by the beings
It is felt toward the beings
optionExplain: The doer would end differently.
'From' would need the ablative.
Right: The locative gives the one at whom the feeling is directed.
questions.explain: भूतेषु + अनुक्रोशम् = compassion toward living beings.
questions.rule: Locative of the object of a feeling = 'toward' (the locative itself means 'in, among').
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: In verse 3, बुद्ध्वा named an earlier act (having understood). By the same pattern, what is true of पुरस्कृत्य?
options: It is a noun naming a place
It is a verb in the future tense
It names an earlier act, and its doer is the sages
optionExplain: The place is पार्श्वे.
It does not end like a future.
Indra is not in this verse.
Right: -त्य ends a 'having done' word, as -त्वा does, with the same doer as the main sentence.
questions.explain: बुद्ध्वा and पुरस्कृत्य are the same kind of word: an earlier act by the same doer.
questions.rule: -त्वा / -त्य words = 'having done', with the sentence's own doer.
questions.teaches: -त्वा and -त्य both mean 'having done'; -त्य is used when a prefix comes before the root (पुरस्-कृ).
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Verse 8 begins a list of sages. Which of these names do you expect in it?
optionExplain: Right: Vasiṣṭha is one of the sages of the list.
Indra is a god, not one of the gathered sages.
Prajāpati is a god in the chain of verse 4.
The Aśvins are the twin gods of verse 4.
questions.explain: The list names sages; the gods of the chain (Brahmā, Prajāpati, the Aśvins, Indra) are not in it.
questions.rule: Verse 8 lists sages, not gods.

questions.q: Put these four names in the order of verse 8.
questions.explain: These four follow अङ्गिरा in the first line.
questions.rule: जमदग्नि → वसिष्ठ → कश्यप → भृगु.

questions.q: In the first line the name after कश्यपः is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: भृगुः closes the first line.
questions.teaches: भृगुः is the last name of the first line; the second line opens with आत्रेयः.
questions.rule: Line 1 ends with भृगुः; line 2 begins with आत्रेयः.

questions.q: Which gives the two words of नारदो ऽसितः before sandhi?
optionExplain: The original ending is -ः; ो comes from the join.
Right: -ः before अ becomes ो, and ऽ marks the dropped अ.
The name is असित, with its अ.
दोऽसितः is not a word.
questions.explain: नारदो ऽसितः = नारदः + असितः: two names.
questions.rule: नारदो ऽसितः = नारदः + असितः.

questions.q: Taking साङ्ख्यः as a separate name, which comes right after गौतमः in verse 8?
optionExplain: पुलस्त्यः comes after साङ्ख्यः.
नारदः comes near the end of the line.
Right: The second line runs आत्रेयः, गौतमः, साङ्ख्यः.
असितः is the last name.
questions.explain: आत्रेयः → गौतमः → साङ्ख्यः → पुलस्त्यः → नारदः → असितः.
questions.rule: After गौतमः comes साङ्ख्यः.

questions.q: आत्रेयः appears in the second line of this verse. Where did you meet the same name earlier in the chapter?
options: In verse 3, as the one who approached Indra
In verse 4, as the first receiver
In the opening formula इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः
optionExplain: Verse 3 names Bharadvāja.
Verse 4 names Prajāpati.
Verse 6 names diseases, not people.
Right: Line 2 of the chapter names Ātreya as the speaker.
questions.explain: The same name occurs again; the verse does not say whether it is the same person.
questions.rule: आत्रेयः: the speaker named in line 2 and a name in verse 8 (same name; same person is not stated).
questions.teaches: A name can recur in a text; check where else you have met it before deciding it is new.

questions.q: One name in verse 9 is a sage you met in verse 3. Which do you expect?
optionExplain: Right: Bharadvāja, who approached Indra in verse 3, is named again.
Indra is a god, not one of the sages.
Prajāpati is a god in the chain of verse 4.
Śakra is another name of Indra.
questions.explain: भरद्वाजः appears in the list.
questions.rule: भरद्वाजः is in verse 3 and again in the list of verse 9.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading the names in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: अगस्त्यः = Agastya; वामदेवः = Vāmadeva; पारिक्षिः = Pārikṣi; कपिञ्जलः = Kapiñjala.

questions.q: The ending -औ on a name like मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ shows that it names ____ sages (type the number).
questions.explain: -औ is the dual ending: two items in one word.
questions.teaches: On names in -अ, -औ marks the dual. मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ joins two names, Mārkaṇḍeya and Āśvalāyana. (Do not confuse आदौ in verse 4: that is the locative singular of आदि.)
questions.rule: On names in -अ, -औ = two.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ?
optionExplain: श्वलायनौ is not a name.
Right: -अ + आ- merge into आ, so मार्कण्डेय + आश्वलायनौ is written मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ.
याश्वलायनौ is not a name.
Sandhi alone cannot tell अ + अ from अ + आ here, but the sage's name is आश्वलायन, with a long आ.
questions.explain: मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ = मार्कण्डेय + आश्वलायनौ: two sages.
questions.rule: मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ = मार्कण्डेय + आश्वलायनौ.

questions.q: A copy has कपिष्ठलः where this edition has कपिञ्जलः. What kind of difference is this?
options: A different sage in the list
A variant reading of the same name, recorded in the notes
A mistake made by the edition
optionExplain: Nothing in the text adds another name here.
Sandhi changes letters only where two words meet; this difference is inside the name.
Right: The edition itself lists कपिष्ठलः as a variant.
The edition records both readings.
questions.explain: Variant readings of a name are noted, not silently corrected.
questions.rule: कपिञ्जलः / कपिष्ठलः = two readings of the name in the text.

questions.q: A new line reads वसिष्ठभरद्वाजौ. How many sages does it name, and why?
options: One, because it is a single compound name
Three, because the word is long
Two, because -औ is the dual ending
optionExplain: -औ would not appear on a single name like that.
Length does not count names.
The ending tells you.
Right: The dual joins वसिष्ठ and भरद्वाज in one word.
questions.explain: The dual ending -औ works with any pair of names in -अ.
questions.rule: Name + name + -औ = two sages.
questions.teaches: You can count the items in a dual compound from the ending, even for names you have not met.

questions.q: विश्वामित्राश्मरथ्यौ ends in -औ, like मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ in verse 9. How many sages do you expect it to name?
optionExplain: Right: On names in -अ, -औ marks a pair (the dual).
A single name would not take -औ here.
-औ is for two, not three.
-औ is for two, not four.
questions.explain: विश्वामित्राश्मरथ्यौ names two sages: Viśvāmitra and Āśmarathya.
questions.rule: -औ = two sages.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading these names in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: च्यवनः = Cyavana; गार्ग्यः = Gārgya; वार्क्षिः = Vārkṣi; गालवः = Gālava.

questions.q: Complete the last pair of the verse: देवल और ____ (type the name in Devanagari).
questions.explain: देवलगालवौ is the last pair of the verse.
questions.teaches: देवलगालवौ is a dual compound of देवल and गालव, and it closes the verse.
questions.rule: देवलगालवौ = देवल + गालव.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भार्गवश्च्यवनः?
optionExplain: श्च्यवनः is not a name.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, so भार्गवः + च्यवनः is written भार्गवश्च्यवनः.
The name is च्यवन, with च.
श् is not a word-ending that stands on its own.
questions.explain: भार्गवश्च्यवनः = भार्गवः ('the Bhārgava') + च्यवनः (Cyavana).
questions.rule: भार्गवश्च्यवनः = भार्गवः + च्यवनः.

questions.q: Which of these are dual pairs in verse 10?
optionExplain: Right: -औ names Viśvāmitra and Āśmarathya.
A single name, with -ः.
Right: -औ names Śāṇḍilya and Kauṇḍilya.
Right: -औ names Devala and Gālava.
A single name.
questions.explain: Three words end in -औ and name pairs; the other two are single names.
questions.rule: विश्वामित्राश्मरथ्यौ, शाण्डिल्यकौण्डिल्यौ, देवलगालवौ are pairs.

questions.q: In another book you find कौण्डिन्य where verse 10 has कौण्डिल्य. What should you conclude?
options: Likely the same name spelt differently; check the note
Nothing can be said about it
optionExplain: The edition's own note shows both spellings occur for this name.
Neither spelling can be called wrong without evidence.
Right: The edition itself records कौण्डिन्य as a variant of this name.
Variants are recorded precisely so you can compare.
questions.explain: Variant spellings of names are common; compare notes before deciding.
questions.rule: Same name, two spellings: check the variant note first.
questions.teaches: A name spelt differently in another source may be a variant; the edition's note is the first place to look.

questions.q: Verse 11 ends …कात्यायनावुभौ. उभौ is a dual word. What do you expect it to say about Kāpya and Kātyāyana?
options: That many more sages follow them
That they are not in the list
That both of them are meant, as a pair
optionExplain: The pair काप्यकात्यायनौ names both; उभौ does not narrow it.
A dual word is for two, not for many.
They are named in this very line.
Right: A dual word names exactly two; here it stresses the pair Kāpya and Kātyāyana.
questions.explain: उभौ means 'both' and underlines the pair Kāpya and Kātyāyana.
questions.rule: उभौ = both (two).

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading these four names of line 1 in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: साङ्कृत्यः = Sāṅkṛtya; बैजवापिः = Baijavāpi; कुशिकः = Kuśika; बादरायणः = Bādarāyaṇa.

questions.q: The word that means 'both' in the last line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: उभौ closes the verse.
questions.teaches: उभौ is a dual word, 'both'. After a dvandva already in the dual (काप्यकात्यायनौ) it stresses that these two are meant together.
questions.rule: उभौ = both, a dual word.

questions.q: Which is the right split of काप्यकात्यायनावुभौ?
optionExplain: Right: The ending -औ turns into आव् before a vowel, so काप्यकात्यायनौ + उभौ is written काप्यकात्यायनावुभौ.
आवुभौ is not a word.
वुभौ is not a word.
A bare ending in -व् does not stand as a word.
questions.explain: काप्यकात्यायनावुभौ = काप्यकात्यायनौ (Kāpya and Kātyāyana) + उभौ (both).
questions.rule: औ + a vowel → आव् + the vowel.

questions.q: Which of these are single names (not pairs) in verse 11?
optionExplain: Right: one name, with -ः.
A pair: the -औ ending names two.
Right: one name, with -ः.
Right: Śaraloman is labelled nominative singular, one person.
questions.explain: Only काप्यकात्यायनौ is a dual pair; the others are single names.
questions.rule: -ः (or nominative singular) = one sage; -औ = two.

questions.q: A new line reads वसिष्ठकश्यपावुभौ. By the rule of verse 11, what does it say?
options: Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa and one more sage
optionExplain: The dual -औ names both names in the compound.
Right: वसिष्ठकश्यपौ + उभौ joins as वसिष्ठकश्यपावुभौ: a pair, stressed by उभौ.
A dual is for two, not three.
Nothing here speaks of teaching; it only joins two names.
questions.explain: The same joining works for any dual pair followed by उभौ.
questions.rule: Dual pair in -औ + उभौ → ...आवुभौ, 'both of them'.
questions.teaches: When you meet ...आवुभौ, undo it as ...औ + उभौ and read it as 'both of the two named'.

questions.q: Three names in line 2 of verse 12 end in -अक्ष. Which of these is one of them?
optionExplain: Dhaumya ends in -य, and it is in line 1.
Paiṅgi ends in -इ.
Right: It ends in -अक्ष: Hiraṇyākṣa is in line 2.
Kaikaśeya ends in -य, and it is in line 1.
questions.explain: शर्कराक्षः, हिरण्याक्षः and लोकाक्षः are the three -अक्ष names.
questions.rule: Line 2 begins with three names in -अक्ष.

questions.q: Put these four names in the order of verse 12.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives कैकशेयः then धौम्यः; line 2 gives शर्कराक्षः before लोकाक्षः.
questions.rule: कैकशेय → धौम्य → शर्कराक्ष → लोकाक्ष.

questions.q: पैङ्गिः + एव is written पैङ्गिरेव. Before the vowel ए, the visarga after इ turns into ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The visarga becomes र् before a vowel.
questions.teaches: After इ (or उ) a visarga followed by a vowel becomes र्: पैङ्गिः + एव → पैङ्गिरेव. Verse 6 (प्रादुः + भूताः → प्रादुर्भूताः) shows the same र् before a voiced consonant.
questions.rule: Visarga after इ/उ + vowel → र्.

questions.q: Why is कैकशेयः written कैकशेयो before धौम्यः?
options: Because कैकशेयो is a dual form
Because ध drops out of धौम्यः
Because a visarga always becomes ओ
अः becomes ओ before a voiced consonant, here ध
optionExplain: It is not dual; the ending is simply sandhi.
धौम्यः keeps its ध.
Before च it becomes श्, and after इ before a vowel it becomes र्.
Right: Visarga after अ turns into ओ before voiced consonants such as ध.
questions.explain: कैकशेयः + धौम्यः → कैकशेयो धौम्यः (अः → ओ before the voiced ध).
questions.rule: अः + voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Which word in line 1 has the dual ending -औ?
optionExplain: Right: Right: the dual -औ (the notes say it may also be read as one name).
Single name, with -ः.
Single name; the -ओ comes from the visarga.
Single name; the -ओ comes from the visarga, although it contains औ inside.
questions.explain: Only मारीचकाश्यपौ ends in the dual -औ.
questions.rule: A name ending in -औ is a pair; -ो from a visarga is not.

questions.q: Join अग्निः + एव (अग्नि = fire) by the rule of पैङ्गिरेव. What results?
optionExplain: A visarga before a vowel after इ does not simply vanish; it becomes र्.
Right: After इ, the visarga becomes र् before the vowel ए.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not here.
श् appears only before च.
questions.explain: The same rule works for any word in -इः before a vowel.
questions.rule: इः + vowel → इर् + vowel.
questions.teaches: You can join and split any word ending in -इः or -उः before a vowel: the visarga turns into र्.

questions.q: Verse 13 names a few sages and then some groups. Which of these is a group?
optionExplain: A single name, with -ः.
A single name.
Right: The plural -आः names a group of ascetics, not one person.
A single name, with -इः.
questions.explain: वैखानसाः and वालखिल्याः are plural groups.
questions.rule: The plural -आः names a group.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 2 moves from named groups to unnamed 'other great sages'.
questions.rule: वैखानसाः and वालखिल्याः = groups; अन्ये = other; महर्षयः = great sages.

questions.q: महा + ऋषयः is written महर्षयः. The आ + ऋ turn into ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: आ + ऋ become अर्.
questions.teaches: When अ or आ meets ऋ they join as अर्: महा + ऋषयः → महर्षयः. The same happens in सुर + ऋषि → सुरर्षि in verse 20.
questions.rule: अ/आ + ऋ → अर्.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वालखिल्यास्तथा?
optionExplain: स्तथा is not a word.
आस्तथा is not a word.
A bare -स् does not stand as a word-ending; the real ending is the visarga.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, so वालखिल्याः + तथा is written वालखिल्यास्तथा.
questions.explain: वालखिल्यास्तथा = वालखिल्याः (the Vālakhilyas) + तथा (likewise).
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स् + त.

questions.q: Which of these words are plural, naming more than one person?
optionExplain: Right: plural, a group.
A single name, with -ः.
Right: plural, a group.
Right: plural, 'great sages'.
questions.explain: Three words are plural; शाकुनेयः is one person.
questions.rule: -आः / -अयः plurals name several persons; -ः on a name in -अ is one.

questions.q: Join ऋषयः + तथा (ऋषि = sage) by the rule of वालखिल्यास्तथा. What results?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before त becomes स्.
ओ appears before voiced consonants; त is unvoiced.
श् appears only before च.
र् appears before vowels or voiced consonants, not before त.
questions.explain: The same rule works for any word in a visarga before त.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स्त.
questions.teaches: Any word ending in a visarga followed by त joins with स्: the visarga becomes स्.

questions.q: Verse 14 compares the sages to something blazing. What?
optionExplain: No river appears in the verse.
Right: The verse says हूयमाना इवाग्नयः: like fires receiving oblations.
No star appears in the verse.
No king appears in the verse.
questions.explain: The comparison is इव अग्नयः, 'like fires', fed with oblations.
questions.rule: The sages blaze like fires receiving oblations.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say what the sages hold and what makes them blaze.
questions.rule: निधयः = repositories; दमस्य = of self-restraint; नियमस्य = of observances; तेजसा = with radiance.

questions.q: The word for 'blazing' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: दीप्ताः comes from √दीप्, 'to blaze'.
questions.teaches: दीप्ताः is a past participle from √दीप् in the nominative plural, agreeing with निधयः: the sages are the ones who blaze.
questions.rule: दीप्ताः = blazing (nominative plural).

questions.q: Which is the right split of तपसस्तेजसा?
optionExplain: स्तेजसा is not a word.
The ending is a visarga, not a bare स्.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, so तपसः + तेजसा is written तपसस्तेजसा.
स्तेजसा is not a word, and तपसा is a different ending.
questions.explain: तपसस्तेजसा = तपसः (of austerity) + तेजसा (with radiance).
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स् + त.

questions.q: Which words name things the sages are 'repositories of'?
optionExplain: Right: of the knowledge of Brahman.
Right: of self-restraint.
No: the fires are the thing they are compared to.
Right: of observances.
questions.explain: Three genitives name what they hold; the fires are only the comparison.
questions.rule: X-स्य + निधयः = repositories of X.

questions.q: A new phrase reads ज्ञानस्य निधयः. By the pattern of verse 14, what does it mean?
optionExplain: That would need the endings the other way round.
निधयः is plural.
The genitive -स्य means 'of', not 'from'.
Right: X-स्य names what is held, and निधयः is plural: repositories.
questions.explain: The genitive -स्य before निधयः names what the repositories hold.
questions.rule: X-स्य + निधयः = repositories of X.
questions.teaches: You can read a phrase 'X-स्य निधयः' as 'repositories of X' for any X.

questions.q: What does the sages' holy discussion name as the supreme root of the four aims?
optionExplain: Right: The verse says आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम्.
Austerity is named in verse 14, not here as the root.
Wealth is one of the four aims, not their root.
Liberation is one of the four aims, not their root.
questions.explain: Health is called the supreme root of the four.
questions.rule: आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम् = health is the supreme root.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 sets the scene of the sages' talk.
questions.rule: सुखोपविष्टाः = seated at ease; पुण्याम् = holy; कथाम् = discussion; तत्र = there.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: The word for 'health' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: आरोग्यम् is the subject of the claim.
questions.teaches: आरोग्यम् ends in -म्, the neuter nominative singular: health is what is said to be the root.
questions.rule: आरोग्यम् = health, called the supreme root.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Which is the right split of सुखोपविष्टाः?
optionExplain: पविष्टाः is not a word.
Right: अ + उ join as ओ, so सुख + उपविष्टाः is written सुखोपविष्टाः.
पविष्टाः is not a word.
ए + उ becomes अव्, not ओ; and सुखे is not the word here.
questions.explain: सुखोपविष्टाः = सुख ('ease') + उपविष्टाः ('seated').
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Which of these are among the four aims of which health is called the root?
optionExplain: Right: dharma, righteousness.
Right: artha, wealth.
Right: kāma, pleasure.
Right: mokṣa, liberation.
Not in this line: the four are धर्म, अर्थ, काम and मोक्ष.
questions.explain: The four aims are धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष; तपः is not one of them in this line.
questions.rule: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् names four aims.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: In an invented line विनयो गुणानां मूलम् (विनय = humility, गुण = virtue), what is the root and of what?
options: The virtues are the root of humility
Humility and virtues are both roots
Humility is the root of the virtues
Nothing is said to be a root
optionExplain: That would need the endings the other way round.
Only the nominative is said to be the root.
Right: The genitive plural names the group, and the nominative before मूलम् is the root.
मूलम् says that something is a root.
questions.explain: Same pattern as ...णाम् आरोग्यं मूलम्: [genitive plural] [nominative] मूलम्.
questions.rule: Genitive plural + nominative + मूलम् = the nominative is the root of the genitive group.
questions.teaches: In 'X-णाम् Y मूलम्', Y is the root and X are the things it supports.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Verse 15 called health the supreme root. What does verse 16 say diseases do to it?
options: They have nothing to do with it
They destroy it, together with well-being and life
optionExplain: रोगाः are its destroyers, not strengtheners.
तस्य ties them to health as its destroyers.
Nothing in the verse says this.
Right: रोगाः are called its अपहर्तारः, destroyers.
questions.explain: रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः says diseases are the destroyers of health.
questions.rule: Diseases are destroyers of health, well-being and life.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the main claim.
questions.rule: रोगाः = diseases; अपहर्तारः = destroyers; अन्तरायः = obstacle; महान् = great.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: तस्य in this verse refers back to the word ____ of verse 15 (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: तस्य means 'of it', and the thing meant is health.
questions.teaches: तस्य is the genitive of तद् ('that'); here it picks up आरोग्यम्, the subject of verse 15.
questions.rule: तस्य = of it = of आरोग्य.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Which is the right split of रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, and अ + अ join as आ: रोगाः + तस्य + अपहर्तारः.
स्तस्य is not a word.
पहर्तारः is not a word here.
आस्तस्य is not a word.
questions.explain: The chunk joins three words: रोगाः, तस्य, अपहर्तारः.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स्त; अ + अ → आ.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say diseases destroy?
optionExplain: Right: health, from verse 15.
Right: of well-being.
Right: of life.
No: humans are those for whom the obstacle arose, not what is destroyed.
questions.explain: Three genitives name what is destroyed; मनुष्याणाम् names who has the trouble.
questions.rule: अपहर्तारः takes the genitives: of it, of well-being, of life.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: In an invented line चोरा धनस्यापहर्तारः (चोर = thief, धन = wealth), who takes what?
options: Wealth and thieves are both taken
optionExplain: The genitive names what is taken, not who takes.
Right: The doers are the nominative plural; धनस्य names what is taken.
अपहर्तारः means those who take away.
Only the genitive is the thing taken.
questions.explain: The same pattern as रोगाः ... अपहर्तारः.
questions.rule: [nominative plural] + [genitive] + अपहर्तारः = the first take away the second.
questions.teaches: With अपहर्तारः, the genitive names what is taken, and the nominative names who takes it.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: The sages first put a question about the means of curing the diseases. What do they do next?
options: They go to Indra at once
optionExplain: First they meditate; only then do they see Śakra.
No one is asked in this verse.
Right: इत्युक्त्वा ध्यानमास्थिताः: having said this, they entered meditation.
The next words say they entered meditation.
questions.explain: After the question they sink into meditation.
questions.rule: Question, then meditation, then sight of Śakra.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the sequence of the verse.
questions.rule: शमोपायः = means of cure; ध्यानम् = meditation; शरणम् = refuge; ददृशुः = they saw.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: इति + उक्त्वा is written ____ (type the joined word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: इति + उक्त्वा → इत्युक्त्वा.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so इति + उक्त्वा joins as इत्युक्त्वा, 'having said this'. उक्त्वा has no prefix, so it takes -त्वा.
questions.rule: इ + उ → य् + उ.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Which is the right split of ददृशुर्ध्यानचक्षुषा?
optionExplain: र्ध्यानचक्षुषा is not a word.
उर्ध्यानचक्षुषा is not a word.
A bare -र् does not stand as a word-ending; the word is ददृशुः.
Right: After उ, a visarga before a voiced consonant like ध appears as र्: ददृशुः + ध्यानचक्षुषा.
questions.explain: ददृशुर्ध्यानचक्षुषा = ददृशुः (they saw) + ध्यानचक्षुषा (with the eye of meditation).
questions.rule: Visarga after उ + voiced consonant → र्.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: ध्यानचक्षुषा ends in the instrumental ending. What does it tell you about how they saw Śakra?
options: They saw him by means of the eye of meditation
They saw the eye of meditation
They saw him in order to get the eye of meditation
The eye of meditation saw them
optionExplain: Right: The instrumental names the means: seeing with the eye of meditation.
The thing seen is शक्रम्, with -म्.
The instrumental names the means, not the purpose.
The doers are ते (they); the instrumental is only the means.
questions.explain: ध्यानचक्षुषा (instrumental) = with the eye of meditation.
questions.rule: Instrumental = the means or tool by which the action is done.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: In an invented line शिष्यो ज्ञानचक्षुषा गुरुं पश्यति (ज्ञान = knowledge, गुरु = teacher, पश्यति = sees), how does the student see?
options: He sees the eye of knowledge
He sees for the sake of knowledge
optionExplain: The thing seen is गुरुम्.
Right: The instrumental in -चक्षुषा names the means, as in ध्यानचक्षुषा.
The doer is शिष्यः.
The instrumental names the means, not the purpose.
questions.explain: The same pattern as ध्यानचक्षुषा.
questions.rule: X-चक्षुषा = with the eye of X (the means of seeing).
questions.teaches: A word in -चक्षुषा names the means of seeing: with the eye of that thing.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: The verse calls one person 'lord of the immortals', 'thousand-eyed' and 'husband of Śacī'. Who is meant?
optionExplain: Brahmā is not meant by these epithets.
Bharadvāja is a sage, not the lord of the immortals.
Right: The notes say all three are epithets of Indra.
Ātreya is a sage named in verse 9, not the lord of the immortals.
questions.explain: अमरप्रभुः, सहस्राक्षः and शचीपतिः name Indra.
questions.rule: Three epithets, one person: Indra.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the person and the aim of the journey.
questions.rule: अमरप्रभुः = lord of the immortals; शचीपतिम् = husband of Śacī; भवनम् = abode; प्रष्टुम् = to ask.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: The word meaning 'will tell' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: वक्ष्यति is from √वच्, 'to speak'.
questions.teaches: वक्ष्यति is labelled a future, third person singular: 'he will tell'. The sages expect an answer from Indra.
questions.rule: वक्ष्यति = he will tell (future).
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Which is the right split of यथावदमरप्रभुः?
optionExplain: A word यथावद would join with अ as आ, giving …दामर…
मरप्रभुः is not a word.
वदमरप्रभुः is not a word.
Right: A final त becomes द before a vowel, so यथावत् + अमरप्रभुः is written यथावदमरप्रभुः.
questions.explain: यथावदमरप्रभुः = यथावत् ('properly') + अमरप्रभुः ('lord of the immortals').
questions.rule: त् + vowel → द् + vowel.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: कः ... गच्छेत् is a question. गच्छेत् is the optative of √गम्, 'should go'. What does the question ask?
optionExplain: Right: The optative asks about a person who should go.
गच्छेत् is not a past form.
The optative is 'should', not a sure future.
कः asks who, not why.
questions.explain: कः गच्छेत्? = Who should go?
questions.rule: कः + optative = 'who should…?'.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: An invented line reads ऋषिर्नगरं गच्छेद् राजानं द्रष्टुम् (नगर = city, द्रष्टुम् = to see, राजन् = king). What is the purpose of going?
options: To be seen by the king
optionExplain: The purpose is the infinitive: to see.
Right: The infinitive in -तुम् (here द्रष्टुम्) gives the purpose, as प्रष्टुम् does.
द्रष्टुम् is active: to see.
द्रष्टुम् states the purpose.
questions.explain: The infinitive in -तुम् names the aim of going, as in गच्छेत् प्रष्टुम्.
questions.rule: Verb of going + infinitive in -तुम् = going in order to do that.
questions.teaches: An infinitive in -तुम् such as प्रष्टुम् or द्रष्टुम् tells the purpose of the going.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: The sages asked who should go to Indra. Who answers first, and what does he say?
options: Bharadvāja: 'Let me be appointed to this task'
All the sages together, at once
optionExplain: Indra is not present in this verse.
Ātreya is not mentioned in this verse.
Right: अहमर्थे नियुज्येयमत्र is his word, spoken first.
The verse says the first word was Bharadvāja's.
questions.explain: Bharadvāja spoke first and was appointed.
questions.rule: Bharadvāja volunteers; the sages appoint him.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the volunteering and the appointment.
questions.rule: अहम् = I; अत्र = here/in this; प्रथमम् = first; नियोजितः = appointed.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: अत्र + इति joins as अत्रेति. The अ + इ turn into ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: अ + इ become ए.
questions.teaches: अ or आ followed by इ joins as ए: अत्र + इति → अत्रेति. The इति then closes the quotation.
questions.rule: अ + इ → ए.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Which is the right split of भरद्वाजो ऽब्रवीत्?
optionExplain: उब्रवीत् is not a word.
Neither part is a word here.
The name ends in -ः, not -आ.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ, and the dropped अ is shown by ऽ.
questions.explain: भरद्वाजो ऽब्रवीत् = भरद्वाजः (Bharadvāja) + अब्रवीत् (spoke).
questions.rule: अः + अ → ओ + ऽ.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: Put the events in the order of verses 18 and 19.
items: The sages ask who should go to Indra
questions.explain: The question comes first, then the volunteer's words, then the appointment.
questions.rule: Question → volunteer → appointment.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: An invented line reads अहं गच्छेयमिति शिष्यो ऽब्रवीत् (गच्छेयम् = may I go). What did the student say?
optionExplain: Right: The words before इति are what he said: अहं गच्छेयम्.
अब्रवीत् says he spoke.
अहम् means 'I'.
The quote is 'may I go'.
questions.explain: इति closes the quotation, as in …नियुज्येयमत्रेति.
questions.rule: Words before इति + verb of speaking = what was said.
questions.teaches: You can find what someone said by reading back from इति to the start of the quoted words.
questions.section: आरोग्य की चिन्ता, भरद्वाज का चयन

questions.q: After being appointed, where does Bharadvāja go?
optionExplain: The verse sends him to Śakra's abode.
Right: शक्रभवनं गत्वा: having gone to Śakra's abode.
Brahmā is not mentioned in this verse.
The Aśvins are not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: He goes to Śakra's abode.
questions.rule: He goes to Śakra's abode and sees Indra.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the journey, the seeing and the comparison.
questions.rule: गत्वा = having gone; ददर्श = saw; बलहन्तारम् = slayer of Bala; अनलम् = fire.

questions.q: The word meaning 'having gone' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: गत्वा comes from √गम्, 'to go'.
questions.teaches: गत्वा is a 'having done' word in -त्वा. √गम् has no prefix here, so it takes -त्वा. With a prefix it would take -य, as उपागम्य.
questions.rule: गत्वा = having gone (before ददर्श).

questions.q: Which is the right split of दीप्यमानमिवानलम्?
optionExplain: मिवानलम् is not a word.
Neither part is a word.
Right: अ + अ join as आ, so इव + अनलम् is written इवानलम्; the m before इव joins by sandhi.
इवा and नलम् are not words.
questions.explain: दीप्यमानमिवानलम् = दीप्यमानम् (blazing) + इव (like) + अनलम् (fire).
questions.rule: इव + अनलम् → इवानलम्.

questions.q: Which words describe the one Bharadvāja saw?
optionExplain: Right: amid the hosts of gods and sages.
Right: slayer of Bala.
No: it is the place he went to.
Right: blazing.
questions.explain: Three accusatives describe the one seen; शक्रभवनम् is the place.
questions.rule: The accusatives of person: amid hosts, slayer of Bala, blazing.

questions.q: In an invented line शिष्यो गुरुं दीप्यमानमिव रविं ददर्श (रवि = sun; दीप्यमानम् goes with गुरुम्), what is compared to what?
options: The sun is compared to the teacher
The student is compared to the sun
The teacher is said to be the sun itself
The teacher, blazing, is compared to the sun
optionExplain: दीप्यमानम् describes the teacher.
The student is the one who sees.
इव means 'like', so it is a comparison, not an identity.
Right: इव ('like') links the blazing teacher to the sun.
questions.explain: The same pattern as दीप्यमानमिवानलम्.
questions.rule: X blazing + इव + Y = X blazes like Y.
questions.teaches: इव means 'like': it makes a comparison between the one described and the thing named after it.

questions.q: Before delivering the sages' message, what does Bharadvāja do to Indra?
options: He greets him with blessings of victory
He demands the remedy at once
He ignores him and speaks to the other gods
He recites the names of the sages
optionExplain: Right: जयाशीर्भिः अभिनन्द्य: he greeted the lord of the gods with blessings of victory.
The request comes in verse 22, after the greeting.
The verse says he approached and greeted Indra.
The names were given earlier in the chapter, not here.
questions.explain: He approaches, greets with blessings of victory, then speaks humbly.
questions.rule: Approach, greet, then speak.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the three actions of the verse.
questions.rule: अभिगम्य = having approached; अभिनन्द्य = having greeted; सुरेश्वरम् = lord of the gods; प्रोवाच = he said.

questions.q: The word for out of humility (humbly) is ____ (type it in Devanagari, before sandhi).
questions.explain: The verse says विनयाद्धीमान्, that is विनयात् + धीमान्.
questions.teaches: विनयात् ends in the ablative -आत्, 'from, out of': he spoke out of humility. Before a voiced letter (ध) the final त् is written द्.
questions.rule: An ablative in -आत् can give the reason or manner: 'out of humility'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विनयाद्धीमान्?
optionExplain: आद्धीमान् is not a word.
Right: त् before the voiced ध becomes द्, so विनयात् + धीमान् is written विनयाद्धीमान्.
हीमान् is not a word; the second word is धीमान्, the wise one.
दीमान् is not a word.
questions.explain: विनयाद्धीमान् = विनयात् + धीमान्: 'out of humility' + 'the wise one'.
questions.rule: Final त् becomes द् before ध (and before ग, घ, ब, भ, द and vowels).

questions.q: Why is सः written सो in सो ऽभिगम्य?
options: सो is a different word meaning 'to him'
Before a following अ, the visarga of सः becomes ओ, and the अ is shown by ऽ
optionExplain: It is the same word सः, 'he'.
The ओ here is only a sandhi result, not an ending.
Right: -अः + अ gives -ओ ऽ.
A call would be in a different form and context; here it is plain 'he'.
questions.explain: सः + अभिगम्य → सो ऽभिगम्य: the visarga turns into ओ and the following अ is dropped, marked by ऽ.
questions.rule: -अः before अ gives ओ ऽ.

questions.q: A new line says a pupil went up to his teacher using prefix उप- with root गम्, then spoke. Which form means having gone up to?
optionExplain: -त्वा is used when there is no prefix, as in बुद्ध्वा.
That is a finite past verb, 'approached', not 'having gone up to'.
That is a 'must be approached' form, not 'having approached'.
Right: With a prefix, the 'having done' form ends in -य, as in अभिगम्य.
questions.explain: Prefix + root + -य is the pattern shown by अभिगम्य and अभिनन्द्य.
questions.rule: Prefix present: 'having done' ends in -य; no prefix: -त्वा.
questions.teaches: A prefix on the root tells you to expect a -य form for 'having done'.

questions.q: What reason does Bharadvāja give for his request to Indra?
options: Diseases that terrify all beings have arisen
The sages have lost their vows
The gods are asking for medicine
optionExplain: Right: व्याधयः समुत्पन्नाः सर्वप्राणिभयङ्कराः says exactly this.
That worry belongs to the earlier verses about the obstacles, not to this verse.
Nothing here complains about honour.
The request is made on behalf of the sages and living beings.
questions.explain: The reason is the rise of frightening diseases.
questions.rule: Reason first (diseases), request second (tell the remedy).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole sentence.
questions.rule: व्याधयः = diseases; भयङ्कराः = causing fear; ब्रूहि = tell; शमोपायम् = means of cure.

questions.q: The command meaning tell in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The line begins तद्ब्रूहि, that is तत् + ब्रूहि.
questions.teaches: ब्रूहि is the command form of the root ब्रू, 'speak': Bharadvāja asks Indra to tell.
questions.rule: ब्रूहि = 'tell!', a command to one person.

questions.q: Which is the right split of शमोपायम्?
optionExplain: पायम् is not the word here; the second word is उपायम्, the means.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, so शम + उपायम् is written शमोपायम्.
ओपायम् is not a word.
इ + उ would give यु, written शम्युपायम्.
questions.explain: शमोपायम् = शम (calming) + उपाय (means).
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: In verse 18 the form is अमरप्रभुः; here it is अमरप्रभो. What does the ending -ओ show here?
options: He is being addressed: 'O lord of the immortals'
optionExplain: The verse speaks to one lord, Indra.
It is a noun, not a verb.
Right: The ending -ओ is the form used when calling someone, matching the translation 'O lord'.
That was the verse 18 form, अमरप्रभुः, the one who will tell.
questions.explain: In verse 18 he is spoken about (अमरप्रभुः); here he is spoken to (अमरप्रभो).
questions.rule: -उः (spoken about) vs -ओ (spoken to).

questions.q: By the same rule that gives तद्ब्रूहि from तत् + ब्रूहि, how is तत् + गच्छ written?
optionExplain: Left unchanged, it would break the rule shown by तद्ब्रूहि.
The त् does not turn retroflex here.
A nasal न् appears only before a nasal letter.
Right: Final त् before a soft stop such as ग becomes द्.
questions.explain: Final त् before a soft stop such as ग, घ, ब, ध, द is written द्.
questions.rule: त् + soft stop → द्.
questions.teaches: Final त् changes to द् before a soft stop such as ग, घ, ब, ध, द.

questions.q: Who teaches Āyurveda to whom in this verse?
optionExplain: Right: भगवान् शतक्रतुः is Indra, and तस्मै … परमर्षये is Bharadvāja.
It is the other way round: Indra is the teacher here.
That was in verse 4.
The six disciples come much later, from verse 30.
questions.explain: Indra, called Śatakratu, teaches Bharadvāja.
questions.rule: Indra → Bharadvāja.

questions.q: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explain: विपुलाम् describes the intellect (मतिम्).
questions.rule: तस्मै = to him; प्रोवाच = he spoke; पदैरल्पैः = with few words; विपुलाम् = vast.

questions.q: The word meaning having known in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The second line has मतिं बुद्ध्वा विपुलाम्: having known the intellect to be vast.
questions.teaches: बुद्ध्वा has -त्वा, which marks an action that happens before the main verb: first Indra recognised the intellect, then he taught.
questions.rule: -त्वा on a root with no prefix = 'having done', an earlier action.

questions.q: Which is the right split of परमर्षये?
optionExplain: इ + ऋ would give य्, written परम्यृषये.
Right: अ + ऋ gives अर्, so परम + ऋषये is written परमर्षये.
षये is not a word.
A visarga before ऋ would not give this form.
questions.explain: परमर्षये = परम (supreme) + ऋषये (to the sage).
questions.rule: अ + ऋ → अर्.

questions.q: According to the verse, what did Indra recognise before he taught in few words?
options: That the other sages had already learned it
That Āyurveda is a short science
optionExplain: Nothing about tiredness is said.
Nothing about other sages is said in this verse.
Right: मतिं बुद्ध्वा विपुलाम्: having known the intellect to be vast.
The verse does not say so; the few words are linked to his intellect.
questions.explain: बुद्ध्वा links the recognition of his vast intellect to the teaching in few words.
questions.rule: Vast intellect recognised → few words enough.

questions.q: By the rule that gives परमर्षये from परम + ऋषये, how is देव + ऋषि written?
optionExplain: The अ would not disappear leaving ऋ alone.
अ + ऋ does not give ए.
The result is अर्, not आर.
Right: अ + ऋ gives अर्.
questions.explain: अ + ऋ → अर् turns देव + ऋषि into देवर्षि, just as महा + ऋषि gives महर्षि.
questions.rule: अ/आ + ऋ → अर्.
questions.teaches: You can join any word ending in -अ with a following ऋ-word by writing अर्.

questions.q: The first word of verse 24 names three things whose knowledge Āyurveda is. Which three?
optionExplain: Right: हेतु, लिङ्ग and औषध: cause, sign (symptom) and remedy.
Those are not in the first word.
Time is not mentioned in this verse.
None of these three appears in the verse.
questions.explain: हेतुलिङ्गौषधज्ञानम् = the knowledge of cause, sign and remedy.
questions.rule: हेतु + लिङ्ग + औषध = cause, sign, remedy.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first three form the triad of the verse; आतुर is the second of the two people it serves.
questions.rule: हेतु = cause; लिङ्ग = sign; औषध = remedy; आतुर = sick person.

questions.q: Brahmā is called ____ , 'the grandfather', in the last word of the verse (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse ends बुबुधे यं पितामहः: the Grandfather understood it.
questions.teaches: पितामह means grandfather; the translation reads it as a name of Brahmā. It is the subject of बुबुधे, 'understood'.
questions.rule: पितामहः = the Grandfather, here Brahmā.

questions.q: Which is the right split of लिङ्गौषध (inside the first compound)?
optionExplain: षध is not a word.
Right: अ + औ gives औ, so लिङ्ग + औषध is written लिङ्गौषध.
A word लिङ्गो with this ending is not in the verse.
A visarga before औ would leave a gap, not merge the words.
questions.explain: लिङ्गौषध = लिङ्ग (sign) + औषध (remedy).
questions.rule: अ + औ → औ.

questions.q: Which of these are said of Āyurveda in verse 24? Pick all that apply.
optionExplain: Right: eternal.
Right: holy.
Right: the supreme resort of the healthy and the sick.
Wrong: this word appears in verse 25, not here.
Wrong: this word appears in verse 27, not here.
questions.explain: The three right words are all in the second line or the first-line compound; the other two come in later verses.
questions.rule: शाश्वतम्, पुण्यम्, स्वस्थातुरपरायणम् are said here.

questions.q: By the rule that gives स्वस्थातुर from स्वस्थ + आतुर, how is पुस्तक + आलय written?
optionExplain: That drops the आ instead of lengthening the vowel.
अ + आ does not give ओ.
Right: अ + आ gives आ.
अ + आ does not give ऐ.
questions.explain: अ + आ → आ: पुस्तक + आलय = पुस्तकालय, as स्वस्थ + आतुर = स्वस्थातुर.
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ.
questions.teaches: Any word ending in -अ joined with a following आ-word merges into a single long आ.

questions.q: What did the sage of great intellect do, according to verse 25?
options: He taught it to the six disciples
He wrote it down at once
He understood the whole of Āyurveda quickly and properly
optionExplain: The verse says he understood it.
That comes in verse 30.
Nothing is said about writing.
Right: यथावदचिरात् सर्वं बुबुधे: properly, quickly, all, he understood.
questions.explain: He understood the whole of Āyurveda quickly and properly.
questions.rule: बुबुधे = he understood; सर्वम् = the whole.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each word adds one detail about the sage or about Āyurveda.
questions.rule: अनन्तपारम् = boundless; त्रिस्कन्धम् = three divisions; अचिरात् = quickly; तन्मनाः = mind fixed on it.

questions.q: The word for the whole (all) in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The second line reads यथावदचिरात् सर्वं बुबुधे.
questions.teaches: सर्वम् goes with आयुर्वेदम्: he understood the whole of it, not a part.
questions.rule: सर्वम् = the whole, all.

questions.q: Why is तन्मना, and not तन्मनाः, written before मुनिः?
options: A visarga after आ is dropped before a voiced letter such as म
It is a different word, तन्मना, meaning 'we'
optionExplain: Right: आः + voiced letter → आ, so तन्मनाः + मुनिः is written तन्मना मुनिः.
ओ appears after -अः, not after -आः.
र् appears after vowels other than अ and आ.
It is the same word तन्मनाः, 'with mind fixed on it'.
questions.explain: तन्मनाः + मुनिः → तन्मना मुनिः: the visarga after आ falls away before a voiced letter.
questions.rule: -आः + voiced letter → -आ.

questions.q: What does अनन्तपारम् (far shore endless) say about Āyurveda?
options: It can be learned only slowly
optionExplain: A far shore that has no end is the opposite of short.
Right: A shore with no end means no limit to its extent.
That contradicts त्रिस्कन्धम्, three divisions.
The verse says the sage understood it quickly.
questions.explain: अनन्तपार means boundless in extent, yet the sage understood it quickly.
questions.rule: अनन्तपार = boundless.

questions.q: A poet calls an ocean अपार. Using the idea of 'not' in अनन्त and अचिरात्, what does it mean?
optionExplain: अ- negates; it does not mean 'near'.
Nothing in the word speaks of depth.
Right: अ- negates पार, 'far shore': no far shore.
Nothing in the word speaks of age.
questions.explain: अ-/अन्- means 'not': अनन्त = not-end, अचिरात् = not-long, अपार = not-having-a-far-shore.
questions.rule: अ-/अन्- = not.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ-/अन्- reverses the meaning of the word that follows.

questions.q: What did Bharadvāja obtain by means of Āyurveda?
options: A treatise in his own name
optionExplain: No kingdom is mentioned.
The verse does not say he became Indra.
No treatise by him is mentioned.
Right: आयुरमितं लेभे: he obtained an immeasurable life.
questions.explain: He gained an immeasurable life, and the sages received the teaching from him.
questions.rule: Bharadvāja: long life gained, teaching passed on.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the two things Bharadvāja does in the verse.
questions.rule: अमितम् = immeasurable; लेभे = he obtained; ऋषिभ्यः = to the sages; शशंस = he told.

questions.q: The word meaning 'adding nothing' in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The line reads ऋषिभ्यो ऽनधिकम् तच्च शशंसानवशेषयन्.
questions.teaches: अनधिकम् is अन् + अधिकम्, 'not more': he added nothing of his own.
questions.rule: अनधिकम् = without adding; अनवशेषयन् = without leaving anything out.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तेनायुरमितम्?
optionExplain: Right: अ + आ gives आ; the visarga of आयुः before अ becomes र्.
युर and मितम् are not words here.
नायु and रमितम् are not words here.
The second word is आयुः, with a long आ.
questions.explain: तेनायुरमितम् = तेन ('by it') + आयुः (life) + अमितम् (immeasurable).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ; -उः + अ → -उर्.

questions.q: What do अनधिकम् and अनवशेषयन् together say about how Bharadvāja taught the sages?
options: He passed on exactly what he had received
He left out the hard parts
optionExplain: अनधिकम् says he added nothing.
Right: Nothing added and nothing left out means an exact transmission.
अनवशेषयन् says he left nothing out.
The verse says he told it to the sages.
questions.explain: Neither more nor less: the teaching is passed on exactly.
questions.rule: अनधिक + अनवशेष = exact transmission.

questions.q: By the rule that gives तच्च from तत् + च, how is सत् + चरित्र written?
optionExplain: The त् must change before च.
त् before च becomes च्, not ज्.
Right: Final त् before च is written च्, giving च्च.
The त् does not turn retroflex here.
questions.explain: Final त् followed by च becomes च्: तत् + च = तच्च, सत् + चरित्र = सच्चरित्र.
questions.rule: त् + च → च्च.
questions.teaches: A word ending in त् before च takes on च, so the sound is doubled.

questions.q: From whom did the sages receive the Veda in this verse?
optionExplain: Indra taught Bharadvāja; the sages got it from Bharadvāja.
Brahmā is at the start of the chain, verse 4.
Punarvasu appears in verse 30.
Right: भरद्वाजात् जगृहुः: they received it from Bharadvāja.
questions.explain: The sages took it from Bharadvāja.
questions.rule: ऋषि ← भरद्वाज.

questions.q: Put these three in the order the knowledge passed, following verses 23 and 27.
questions.explain: Indra taught Bharadvāja (verse 23); the sages received it from Bharadvāja (verse 27).
questions.rule: इन्द्र → भरद्वाज → ऋषि.

questions.q: The sages wished to make their ____ life (Devanagari word for 'long', as in the verse).
questions.explain: The second line begins दीर्घमायुश्चिकीर्षन्तः.
questions.teaches: दीर्घम् goes with आयुः: a long life is what they wanted.
questions.rule: दीर्घम् आयुः = long life.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ऋषयश्च?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, so ऋषयः + च is written ऋषयश्च.
श्च is not a word.
The plural of ऋषि is ऋषयः, not ऋषयाः.
ऋषयश is not a word.
questions.explain: ऋषयश्च = ऋषयः + च: 'and the sages'.
questions.rule: Visarga + च → श्च.

questions.q: Why did the sages receive the Āyurveda from Bharadvāja, according to the verse?
options: They wished to make their life long
They wished to become rulers of the gods
They wished to compose a new treatise
optionExplain: Nothing like that is said here.
Right: दीर्घमायुश्चिकीर्षन्तः: wishing to make life long.
The verse names only a wish for long life.
The verse does not say so; the treatise appears later.
questions.explain: The reason is stated in चिकीर्षन्तः: wishing to make (their life) long.
questions.rule: Reason: wish for a long life.

questions.q: By the rule that gives भरद्वाजाज्जगृहुः from भरद्वाजात् + जगृहुः, how is सत् + जन written?
optionExplain: Left unjoined, it breaks the rule shown here.
The doubled sound ज्ज must stay.
Right: Final त् before ज is written ज्, giving ज्ज.
A nasal न् appears only before a nasal letter.
questions.explain: Final त् before ज becomes ज्: भरद्वाजात् + जगृहुः = भरद्वाजाज्जगृहुः, सत् + जन = सज्जन.
questions.rule: त् + ज → ज्ज.
questions.teaches: A word ending in त् before ज takes on ज, so the sound is doubled.

questions.q: Which item does the list in verse 28 begin with?
optionExplain: कर्म comes last in this verse.
समवाय is added in verse 29.
द्रव्याणि comes fourth, not first.
Right: The second line starts सामान्यं च विशेषं च.
questions.explain: The list runs सामान्य, विशेष, गुण, द्रव्य, कर्म.
questions.rule: First item: सामान्यम्.

questions.q: Put the items in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: They follow one another in the second line.
questions.rule: सामान्य → विशेष → गुण → द्रव्य → कर्म.

questions.q: The last item of the list, meaning 'action', is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The line ends गुणान् द्रव्याणि कर्म च.
questions.teaches: कर्म is the last of the five items in this verse; the sentence continues with one more item in verse 29.
questions.rule: कर्म = action, the fifth item.

questions.q: Why is महर्षयः + ते written महर्षयस्ते?
options: A visarga before त becomes स्
A visarga becomes ओ before a voiced letter
A visarga becomes र् before a vowel
The visarga drops out before any consonant
optionExplain: Right: The visarga becomes स् before the dental त.
त is not voiced, and ओ follows only -अः before voiced letters.
ते begins with a consonant, not a vowel.
Before त it becomes स्.
questions.explain: Visarga + त → स्त: महर्षयः + ते = महर्षयस्ते.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स्त.

questions.q: The verse ends with कर्म च, but its sentence goes on in verse 29. What does that tell you about the list?
options: It is not complete; समवाय follows in verse 29
The list repeats from the start
optionExplain: Verse 29 adds another item to the same sentence.
Right: Verse 29 begins समवायं च: one more item of the same sentence.
यत् in verse 29 refers back to the whole list, so the sentence continues.
Nothing repeats; a new item is added.
questions.explain: The list continues in the next verse.
questions.rule: Verse 28 + verse 29 = one sentence.

questions.q: By the rule that gives महर्षयस्ते from महर्षयः + ते, how is मुनयः + तत्र written?
optionExplain: ओ appears only after -अः before a voiced letter.
The visarga does not simply vanish before त.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्.
र् appears only before a vowel or a voiced letter.
questions.explain: Visarga + त → स्त: मुनयः + तत्र = मुनयस्तत्र.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स्त.
questions.teaches: Before a त, a visarga turns into स् and joins the next word.

questions.q: Which item does verse 29 add to the list begun in verse 28?
optionExplain: गुण is already in verse 28.
कर्म is already in verse 28.
सामान्य is already in verse 28.
Right: The verse opens समवायं च: and inherence.
questions.explain: समवाय completes the list.
questions.rule: Verse 29 adds समवाय.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the verse's chain: know, follow, obtain.
questions.rule: ज्ञात्वा = having known; विधिम् = regimen; लेभिरे = they obtained; शर्म = well-being.

questions.q: The word meaning 'not transient' in the last line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The last words are जीवितं चाप्यनित्वरम्.
questions.teaches: अनित्वरम् is अन् + इत्वरम्, 'not passing': the life they gained does not fade quickly.
questions.rule: अनित्वर = not transient, long-lasting.

questions.q: Why does ज्ञात्वा end in -त्वा rather than -य?
options: The root ज्ञा here has no prefix
Because the sentence is about the past
optionExplain: Right: The ‘having done’ form of a root without prefix ends in -त्वा.
That is not what decides it; the prefix does.
-त्वा does not mark number.
It is not a command; it means 'having known'.
questions.explain: No prefix → -त्वा (ज्ञात्वा, बुद्ध्वा); a prefix → -य (अभिनन्द्य).
questions.rule: No prefix: -त्वा. Prefix: -य.

questions.q: Which two things did the sages obtain, according to this verse? Pick all that apply.
options: A life that is not transient
optionExplain: Right: परमं शर्म.
Right: जीवितं चाप्यनित्वरम्.
Wrong: no such gain is mentioned.
Wrong: wealth is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The verse names exactly these two gains.
questions.rule: परमं शर्म + अनित्वरं जीवितम्.

questions.q: By the rule that gives तन्त्रोक्तम् from तन्त्र + उक्तम्, how is शास्त्र + उक्त written?
optionExplain: The अ does not disappear leaving उ.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ.
अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
The उ does not become अ.
questions.explain: अ + उ → ओ: शास्त्र + उक्त = शास्त्रोक्त, like तन्त्र + उक्तम् = तन्त्रोक्तम्.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: Any word ending in -अ followed by उ merges into ओ.

questions.q: Who gave Āyurveda to six disciples in this verse?
optionExplain: Bharadvāja gave it to the sages, in verses 26 and 27.
Indra taught Bharadvāja, verse 23.
Right: पुनर्वसुः … दत्तवान् षड्भ्यः: Punarvasu gave it to six.
Agniveśa is named as a receiver in the next verse.
questions.explain: Punarvasu is the giver; six disciples are the receivers.
questions.rule: Punarvasu → six disciples.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: षड्भ्यः goes with शिष्येभ्यः: 'to the six disciples'.
questions.rule: शिष्येभ्यः = to the disciples; षड्भ्यः = to six; दत्तवान् = he gave; अनुकम्पया = out of compassion.

questions.q: Type the last word of the verse, which means 'out of compassion for all beings' (Devanagari): ____.
questions.explain: The verse ends सर्वभूतानुकम्पया: out of compassion for all beings.
questions.teaches: अनुकम्पा is compassion; the ending -या means 'by, out of': his reason for giving.
questions.rule: अनुकम्पया = out of compassion, the reason.

questions.q: Why is शिष्येभ्यः written शिष्येभ्यो before दत्तवान्?
options: The ओ shows a call, 'O disciples'
A visarga after -अ becomes ओ before a voiced consonant such as द
optionExplain: This is a sandhi result, not a calling form.
The word means 'to the disciples', plural.
र् follows other vowels, not -अ.
Right: -अः + voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.explain: शिष्येभ्यः + दत्तवान् → शिष्येभ्यो दत्तवान्.
questions.rule: -अः + voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: What does षड्भ्यः add to शिष्येभ्यः?
optionExplain: Right: षट् is six; षड्भ्यः is 'to six'.
The names come in the next verse.
No country is mentioned.
Nothing like that is said.
questions.explain: षड्भ्यः says six; the names follow in verse 31.
questions.rule: षड्भ्यः = to six.

questions.q: By the pattern शिष्येभ्यः + दत्तवान् → शिष्येभ्यो दत्तवान्, how is वृक्षेभ्यः + जलम् written?
optionExplain: The visarga does not stay before a voiced letter in joined text.
Right: -अः before a voiced consonant (ज) becomes ओ.
र् follows other vowels, not -अ.
स् appears before त or थ, not before ज.
questions.explain: -अः + voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.rule: -अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.teaches: Any plural dative in -एभ्यः becomes -एभ्यो before a voiced consonant or अ.

questions.q: Verse 30 says Punarvasu gave Āyurveda to six disciples. Which of these do you expect among them?
optionExplain: Indra is a god of the earlier story, not one of the six.
Prajāpati is in the chain of verse 4, not among the six.
Right: Agniveśa is the first of the six names in verse 31.
Brahmā begins the chain of verse 4; he is not a disciple here.
questions.explain: The six names of verse 31 begin with Agniveśa.
questions.rule: Verse 31 names the six disciples, beginning with Agniveśa.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading the names in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: अग्निवेशः = Agniveśa; जतूकर्णः = Jatūkarṇa; पराशरः = Parāśara; क्षारपाणिः = Kṣārapāṇi.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'they received' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: जगृहुः is the verb of the verse; the subject is the six names.
questions.teaches: जगृहुः is the plural of जग्राह (verse 4, 'he received'): the same root √ग्रह्, but 'they' instead of 'he'.
questions.rule: जगृहुः = they received (जग्राह = he received).

questions.q: Which is the right split of जगृहुस्तन्मुनेर्वचः?
optionExplain: These pieces are not words; they are only the joined sounds.
स्तन् is not a word.
That drops तत् ('that'), which the joined form still contains.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, त् before म becomes न्, and a visarga before the voiced व becomes र्.
questions.explain: जगृहुस्तन्मुनेर्वचः = जगृहुः ('they received') + तत् ('that') + मुनेः ('of the sage') + वचः ('teaching').
questions.rule: जगृहुः + तत् + मुनेः + वचः joins as जगृहुस्तन्मुनेर्वचः.

questions.q: Which of these are among those who received the sage's teaching in verse 31?
optionExplain: He is the seeker of verse 3, not one of the six.
Right: the first of the six.
He is the teacher of verse 30, not a disciple.
Right: the third of the six.
Right: the last of the six.
questions.explain: Verse 31 names exactly the six disciples; Bharadvāja and Punarvasu are named elsewhere.
questions.rule: Only the six names of verse 31 are the receivers here.

questions.q: An invented line begins मित्रश्च सोमश्च. What stands before the join in मित्रश्च?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, exactly as in अग्निवेशः + च = अग्निवेशश्च.
That would be written मित्रं च, without श्.
That would be written मित्रा च; there is no visarga to turn into श्.
श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: The same pattern as अग्निवेशश्च and भेलश्च: -ः + च gives -श्च.
questions.rule: -श्च at the end of a name = -ः + च ('and').
questions.teaches: When a name ends in -श्च, undo it as -ः + च ('and'); this works for any name in -अ.

questions.q: The six disciples got the same teaching. What does the verse give as the difference among them?
options: A difference in the sage's teaching
optionExplain: The verse says there was no difference in the teaching.
Right: बुद्धेः विशेषः: the distinction lay in intellect.
Age is not mentioned.
Home is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The distinction lay in intellect (बुद्धि); the sage's teaching did not differ.
questions.rule: Same teaching, different intellect.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole argument of the verse.
questions.rule: बुद्धेः = of intellect; विशेषः = distinction; उपदेशान्तरम् = difference in teaching; कर्ता = author.

questions.q: The word meaning 'first' in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: प्रथमम् tells that Agniveśa came first as author.
questions.teaches: प्रथमम् is read as an adverb, 'first'; the other reading, 'of the first treatise', also uses the same word.
questions.rule: प्रथमम् = first.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नोपदेशान्तरम्?
optionExplain: पदेशान्तरम् is not a word.
नु is not the negative word here; the negative is न.
Right: अ + उ joins as ओ, so न + उपदेशान्तरम् is written नोपदेशान्तरम्.
The word is उपदेश, with उ.
questions.explain: नोपदेशान्तरम् = न ('not') + उपदेशान्तरम् ('difference in teaching').
questions.rule: नोपदेशान्तरम् = न + उपदेशान्तरम्.

questions.q: A reader says the sage taught the six differently. Which words of the verse speak against this?
optionExplain: These words say who became an author, not how the teaching was given.
This single word says 'first'; it says nothing about the teaching.
These words say 'that is why he became'; they do not describe the teaching.
Right: न + उपदेशान्तरम् + मुनेः = no difference in the sage's teaching.
questions.explain: नोपदेशान्तरं मुनेः says that the sage's teaching had no difference.
questions.rule: न + उपदेशान्तरम् = no difference in the teaching.

questions.q: By the pattern of नोपदेशान्तरम्, how is न + उदकम् (not water) written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ joins as ओ, as in न + उपदेशान्तरम् = नोपदेशान्तरम्.
अ + उ does not give a short उ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not from अ + उ.
The two vowels must join; they do not stay apart.
questions.explain: The rule अ + उ → ओ works in any word, not only here.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -अ, followed by a word starting with उ, joins as ओ.

questions.q: Agniveśa was the first author (verse 32). What do you expect Bhela and the others did?
options: They also composed treatises of their own
They went to Indra for more teaching
optionExplain: Nothing of the kind is said.
Right: The verse says each composed his own treatise.
Indra is not in this verse.
No journey is mentioned.
questions.explain: Bhela and the others each composed his own treatise.
questions.rule: भेलादयः चक्रुः स्वं स्वं तन्त्रम् = each composed his own treatise.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the composing and the reciting.
questions.rule: तन्त्रम् = treatise; स्वं स्वम् = each his own; श्रावयामासुः = they made hear; सुमेधसः = highly intelligent.

questions.q: The word meaning 'treatise' in the first line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: तन्त्रम् is what each of them composed.
questions.teaches: तन्त्र is the treatise or science; the same word occurs in verse 29 (तन्त्रोक्तम्) and verse 32 (तन्त्रस्य).
questions.rule: तन्त्रम् = treatise.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सर्षिसङ्घम्?
optionExplain: षिसङ्घम् is not a word.
The prefix is short स ('with'), not सा.
Right: अ + ऋ joins as अर्, so स + ऋषिसङ्घम् is written सर्षिसङ्घम्.
इसङ्घम् is not a word.
questions.explain: सर्षिसङ्घम् = स ('with') + ऋषिसङ्घम् ('assembly of sages'): together with the assembly of sages.
questions.rule: सर्षिसङ्घम् = स + ऋषिसङ्घम्.

questions.q: श्रावयामासुः means 'they made hear'. Which word names the one made to hear?
optionExplain: These are the works that were recited, not the hearer.
These are the doers, the reciters.
These are also the doers, the reciters.
Right: It is the person who heard; the works are what was heard.
questions.explain: आत्रेयम् is the hearer; कृतानि is what was heard; both are in the accusative.
questions.rule: With 'made hear', the hearer and the thing heard are both accusative.

questions.q: An invented line reads शिष्याः गुरुं श्लोकान् श्रावयामासुः. Who was made to hear?
optionExplain: Right: The one who hears is named in the accusative, as आत्रेयम् is here.
The pupils are the doers, who recited.
The verses are what was heard, not the hearer.
श्रावयामासुः says that someone was made to hear.
questions.explain: The same pattern as आत्रेयं … कृतानि श्रावयामासुः: the hearer and the thing heard are both accusative.
questions.rule: Hearer (a person) + thing heard + श्रावयामासुः: the person is the hearer.
questions.teaches: After 'made hear', the person is the hearer and the thing is what was heard; sense tells you which is which.

questions.q: The sages heard the treatises recited. What do you expect their reaction was?
options: They asked the authors to rewrite them
optionExplain: The verse says they approved.
Right: प्रहृष्टाः and अनुमेनिरे say this.
No rewriting is mentioned.
They spoke, with the words ending in इति.
questions.explain: The sages were delighted (प्रहृष्टाः) and approved (अनुमेनिरे).
questions.rule: Heard → delighted → approved.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give what the sages did and how they judged it.
questions.rule: श्रुत्वा = having heard; प्रहृष्टाः = delighted; अनुमेनिरे = they approved; यथावत् = properly.

questions.q: The word that closes the sages' spoken remark is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: इति stands right after the remark यथावत्सूत्रितम्.
questions.teaches: इति closes a quotation, as it did in verse 2 (इति ह स्माह): the words before it are what the sages said.
questions.rule: इति = closing mark of what was said.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सूत्रणमर्थानामृषयः?
optionExplain: मर्थानाम् is not a word.
षयः is not a word.
Right: A final म् is simply written together with the vowel that follows (म् + अ gives म).
नामृषयः is not a word.
questions.explain: सूत्रणमर्थानामृषयः = सूत्रणम् ('composition') + अर्थानाम् ('of the subjects') + ऋषयः ('the sages').
questions.rule: सूत्रणम् + अर्थानाम् + ऋषयः.

questions.q: श्रुत्वा means 'having heard'. Whose act of hearing is it?
options: The disciples', who composed the works
optionExplain: The disciples recited; the sages are the doers of अनुमेनिरे.
Indra is not in this verse.
Normally a 'having done' word shares the doer of the main verb.
Right: A 'having done' word shares the doer of the main verb अनुमेनिरे.
questions.explain: श्रुत्वा and अनुमेनिरे have the same doer: the sages heard, then approved.
questions.rule: A 'having done' word shares the doer of the main verb.

questions.q: An invented line reads ऋषयो ग्रन्थं दृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्टा अभवन्. Which act came first?
optionExplain: Right: A -त्वा / -य word names the earlier act, as श्रुत्वा does here.
That is the main verb, so it comes after.
A 'having done' word names an act finished before.
The ending tells you.
questions.explain: दृष्ट्वा is the same kind of word as श्रुत्वा and बुद्ध्वा.
questions.rule: -त्वा word = the earlier act, by the doer of the main verb.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -त्वा names an act done before the main verb, by the same doer.

questions.q: The sages approved the treatises. What do you expect they called out together?
optionExplain: No command is given.
Right: The verse has them cry साधु, 'well done'.
They praised, not complained.
Rain is not mentioned.
questions.explain: They praised the authors and called out साधु.
questions.rule: Praise ends with the shout साधु.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say how the sages praised.
questions.rule: अस्तुवन् = they praised; साधु = well done; उच्चैः = loudly; समम् = together.

questions.q: The word meaning 'loudly' in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: उच्चैः is joined to the next word as उच्चैरब्रुवन्.
questions.teaches: उच्चैः is an adverb, 'loudly'; before the vowel of अब्रुवन् its visarga becomes र्.
questions.rule: उच्चैः = loudly.

questions.q: Which is the right split of इत्युच्चैरब्रुवन्?
optionExplain: च्चैरब्रुवन् is not a word.
च्चैः is not a word; the word is उच्चैः.
Right: इ + उ becomes य् + उ, and the visarga of उच्चैः becomes र् before the vowel of अब्रुवन्.
The word that closes the quotation is इति, ending in -ि, not इत.
questions.explain: इत्युच्चैरब्रुवन् = इति (closes the quoted words) + उच्चैः (loudly) + अब्रुवन् (they said).
questions.rule: इत्युच्चैरब्रुवन् = इति + उच्चैः + अब्रुवन्.

questions.q: The first line reads सर्व एव, yet many sages are meant. Why does the verse have सर्व and not सर्वे?
options: सर्व is singular, so one sage speaks
सर्व is a different word meaning 'a little'
It is a mistake in the text
Final -ए before a vowel turns into अ: सर्वे + एव = सर्व एव
optionExplain: The verbs अस्तुवन् and अब्रुवन् are plural.
सर्व means 'all'.
It is the regular result of sandhi.
Right: The plural सर्वे loses its ए to अ before the vowel of एव.
questions.explain: सर्वे + एव → सर्व एव: ए before a vowel becomes अ and the vowel stays apart (सर्वः + एव would also give सर्व एव; the plural verbs and the note decide).
questions.rule: सर्व एव = सर्वे + एव (all, indeed).

questions.q: An invented line reads सर्व आगताः. By the same pattern, how many came, and what is the word before the join?
optionExplain: Right: ए before a vowel becomes अ, so सर्वे + आगताः is written सर्व आगताः.
सर्वः + आगताः would also join as सर्व आगताः, but singular सर्वः cannot agree with plural आगताः, so सर्वे is meant.
नागताः is not what is written.
The pattern of सर्व एव shows it.
questions.explain: A bare -अ before a vowel can hide a plural -ए, as in सर्व एव.
questions.rule: सर्व + vowel can be सर्वे + vowel (all).
questions.teaches: Before a vowel, final -ए can shrink to -अ; it may be read as the plural 'all' (सर्वे) when the verbs are plural.

questions.q: The sages cried साधु aloud. Who do you expect heard it, according to this verse?
options: The divine sages in heaven, with the gods
optionExplain: The disciples are not the hearers named here.
Right: दिवि स्थिताः देवर्षयः सामराः are the hearers.
Indra is not named in this verse; the hearers are plural.
शुश्रुवुः says that it was heard.
questions.explain: The divine sages and the gods in heaven heard the holy sound.
questions.rule: Heaven heard the sages' cry.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say who heard, where, and how they felt.
questions.rule: दिवि = in heaven; देवर्षयः = divine sages; शब्दम् = sound; मुमुदिरे = they rejoiced.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: The word meaning 'in heaven' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: दिवि tells where the hearers were.
questions.teaches: दिवि ends in -इ, the locative: 'in heaven'. The hearers are stationed (स्थिताः) there.
questions.rule: दिवि = in heaven.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Which is the right split of देवर्षयः?
optionExplain: षयः is not a word.
The first word is देव, with short अ.
Right: अ + ऋ joins as अर्, so देव + ऋषयः is written देवर्षयः.
वर्षयः is not a word.
questions.explain: देवर्षयः = देव ('god') + ऋषयः ('sages'): divine sages.
questions.rule: देवर्षयः = देव + ऋषयः.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: सामराः is स + अमराः, 'together with the gods'. Who is with the gods?
options: The divine sages standing in heaven
optionExplain: The sages on the Himalaya are the ones who cried out.
The disciples are not part of this verse.
The word is plural.
Right: सामराः agrees with देवर्षयः, in the plural nominative.
questions.explain: सामराः describes the hearers: the divine sages, accompanied by the gods.
questions.rule: सा- at the start = 'together with'.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: An invented line reads सशिष्यो गुरुरागतः. By the pattern of सामराः, who came?
options: The teacher, together with his pupils
The pupils, with the teacher left behind
optionExplain: Right: स- at the start means 'together with', as in सामराः.
The doer is गुरुः, who comes with them.
स- means 'with', not 'without'.
आगतः says that someone came.
questions.explain: The same pattern as सामराः and सर्षिसङ्घम्: स- = together with.
questions.rule: स + noun = together with the noun.
questions.teaches: A word beginning with स- ('with') describes the doer as accompanied by what follows स-.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Heaven rejoiced over the sages' praise. What do you expect resounded through the three worlds?
options: A cry of praise: 'Ah, well done!'
optionExplain: Joy (हर्ष) is the cause named, not grief.
Right: The verse gives the cry अहो साधु.
No ruler is mentioned.
No thunder is mentioned; it is a cry of words.
questions.explain: The cry अहो साधु resounded through the three worlds.
questions.rule: Joy in heaven becomes a cry of praise.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say what sounded, where, and why.
questions.rule: निर्घोषः = resounding cry; लोकान् = worlds; नभसि = in the sky; हर्षात् = out of joy.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: The Sanskrit word for 'three' in the first line (right after लोकान्) is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
