questions.explain: त्रीन् stands with लोकान्: the three worlds.
questions.teaches: त्रीन् is the accusative plural of 'three', matching लोकान्: the cry made the three worlds resound.
questions.rule: त्रीन् = three (the three worlds, accusative).
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Which is the right split of हर्षाद्भूतैरुदीरितः?
optionExplain: द्भूतैः is not a word.
These pieces carry the joined sounds, not the words.
Right: त् before the voiced भ becomes द्, and the visarga of भूतैः becomes र् before the vowel of उदीरितः.
रुदीरितः is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: हर्षाद्भूतैरुदीरितः = हर्षात् ('out of joy') + भूतैः ('by beings') + उदीरितः ('uttered').
questions.rule: हर्षात् + भूतैः + उदीरितः.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Which words describe the quality of the cry, not where or why it sounded?
optionExplain: Right: smooth, soft.
This tells where: in the sky.
Right: deep.
This tells why: out of joy.
questions.explain: स्निग्धगम्भीरः = smooth and deep; नभसि gives the place, हर्षात् the cause.
questions.rule: Quality of the cry: स्निग्ध and गम्भीर.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: By the pattern हर्षात् + भूतैः = हर्षाद्भूतैः, how is the invented जगत् + भद्रम् written when joined?
optionExplain: त् does not stay before a voiced भ.
No extra त is added.
त् becomes द्, not ध्.
Right: A final त् before a voiced letter like भ becomes द्.
questions.explain: The same sandhi as हर्षाद्भूतैः: त् + voiced consonant → द् + voiced consonant.
questions.rule: त् before a voiced consonant → द्.
questions.teaches: A word-final त् turns into द् before a voiced consonant such as भ, ग, ब, द.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: After the cry resounded, what kind of signs do you expect the verse to describe?
options: Auspicious signs: a wind, light and flowers
A storm that destroys the Himalaya
optionExplain: Right: The verse names a good wind, lit directions and flowers.
Disease is not mentioned here.
No destruction is mentioned.
The signs are natural events, not commands.
questions.explain: An auspicious wind blew, the directions were lit, and flowers fell.
questions.rule: Three good signs follow the cry.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Put the three signs in the order the verse names them.
questions.explain: The wind comes first, then the lit directions, then the showers of flowers.
questions.rule: वायु → दिशः → कुसुमवृष्टयः.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: The word meaning 'auspicious', which describes the wind, is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: शिवः describes वायुः: the auspicious wind.
questions.teaches: शिवः is an ordinary adjective here ('auspicious'), agreeing with वायुः; the verse does not speak of a god.
questions.rule: शिवः = auspicious (of the wind).
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Which is the right split of सजलाश्चैव?
optionExplain: श्चैव is not a word.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, and च + एव joins as चैव (अ + ए → ऐ).
श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
आश्चैव is not a word.
questions.explain: सजलाश्चैव = सजलाः ('with water') + च ('and') + एव ('indeed').
questions.rule: सजलाः + च + एव.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: On the usual reading, what falls in the last line?
options: Heavenly showers of flowers, together with water
optionExplain: The showers are of flowers, with water.
Gems are not named.
Right: सजलाः = with water; कुसुमवृष्टयः = showers of flowers.
Fire is not named.
questions.explain: निपेतुः सजलाः दिव्याः कुसुमवृष्टयः = heavenly showers of flowers fell, with water.
questions.rule: सजलाः = स + जल: with water.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: By the pattern सर्वाः + भाभिः = सर्वा भाभिः, how is the invented बालाः + गच्छन्ति written when joined?
optionExplain: In the joined form the visarga is dropped.
ो comes from a visarga after short अ, not after आ.
A visarga after आ does not become र् before a voiced consonant.
Right: A visarga after आ is dropped before a voiced consonant such as ग.
questions.explain: The same pattern as सर्वा भाभिः and उन्मीलिता दिशः: -आः disappears before a voiced consonant.
questions.rule: -आः + voiced consonant → -आ.
questions.teaches: After आ, a visarga is dropped before a voiced consonant; after short अ it would become ो.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: The sages approved the treatises and heaven rejoiced. Who or what do you expect entered the disciples, according to this verse?
options: The gods Indra and the Aśvins
optionExplain: Right: ज्ञानदेवताः are the ones who entered.
The diseases are not mentioned here.
They are not the ones who entered the disciples.
No beasts are named.
questions.explain: The deities of knowledge entered Agniveśa and the other disciples.
questions.rule: ज्ञानदेवताः entered the disciples.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Match each name of the list to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the eight deities, with their usual meanings.
questions.rule: बुद्धिः = intellect; स्मृतिः = memory; धृतिः = fortitude; दया = compassion.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: The verb meaning 'entered' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: विविशुः is the verb of the sentence.
questions.teaches: विविशुः is a plural past form of √विश् ('enter'): 'they entered'. Its doers are the deities and its objects are the disciples.
questions.rule: विविशुः = they entered.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Which is the right split of विविशुर्ज्ञानदेवताः?
optionExplain: विविशुर् is the joined sound, not the word.
Right: A visarga before the voiced ज becomes र्.
उर्ज्ञानदेवताः is not a word.
र्ज्ञानदेवताः is not a word.
questions.explain: विविशुर्ज्ञानदेवताः = विविशुः ('they entered') + ज्ञानदेवताः ('deities of knowledge').
questions.rule: विविशुः + ज्ञानदेवताः.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Which of these are among the deities named in verse 39?
optionExplain: Right: retentive intelligence.
Not named in this verse.
Right: fame.
Not named in this verse.
Right: forbearance.
questions.explain: The verse names बुद्धि, सिद्धि, स्मृति, मेधा, धृति, कीर्ति, क्षमा and दया; श्रद्धा and शान्ति are not in it.
questions.rule: Only the eight names of the verse count.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: By the pattern स्मृतिः + मेधा = स्मृतिर्मेधा, how is the invented मतिः + बलम् written when joined?
optionExplain: The visarga does not simply vanish after इ.
ो comes from a visarga after short अ, not after इ.
Right: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a voiced consonant such as ब.
In the joined form the visarga must change.
questions.explain: The same sandhi as स्मृतिर्मेधा and धृतिः कीर्तिः: -इः + voiced consonant → -इर्.
questions.rule: -इः + voiced consonant → -इर्.
questions.teaches: After इ or उ, a visarga becomes र् before a voiced consonant.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: The treatises were approved by the supreme sages. What does the verse say became of them?
options: They were kept secret in heaven
They were handed over to Indra
They gained a firm standing on earth
optionExplain: The verse speaks of standing, not loss.
The standing is on earth (भुवि).
Indra is not in this verse.
Right: प्रतिष्ठां भुवि लेभिरे says this.
questions.explain: The treatises gained a firm standing on earth.
questions.rule: Approved treatises → a firm standing on earth.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say what, how, where and for whom.
questions.rule: तन्त्राणि = treatises; अनुमतानि = approved; भुवि = on earth; भूतसङ्घानाम् = of the multitudes of beings.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: The word meaning 'on earth' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: भुवि tells where the treatises gained their standing.
questions.teaches: भुवि ends in -इ, the locative: 'on earth'. It contrasts with दिवि ('in heaven') in verse 36.
questions.rule: भुवि = on earth.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Which is the right split of तानि चानुमतान्येषाम्?
optionExplain: Right: च + अ joins as चा, and the इ of अनुमतानि before ए becomes य्.
चानु and मतानि are not words here.
इचानुमतानि is not a word.
The word is एषाम् ('of these'), not येषाम्.
questions.explain: तानि चानुमतान्येषाम् = तानि ('those') + च ('and') + अनुमतानि ('approved') + एषाम् ('of these').
questions.rule: तानि + च + अनुमतानि + एषाम्.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Who approved the treatises, and which word shows it?
options: The supreme sages; परमर्षिभिः, with -भिः meaning 'by'
optionExplain: एषाम् means 'of these', naming the owners of the treatises.
Right: -भिः is the ending for 'by', so the supreme sages are the approvers.
भुवि means 'on earth', the place where they stand.
This means 'of the multitudes of beings', the ones who benefit.
questions.explain: परमर्षिभिः (-भिः = by) names the approvers: the supreme sages.
questions.rule: -भिः = by (the agent).
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: An invented line reads शिष्याः कीर्तिं लेभिरे. By the pattern प्रतिष्ठां लेभिरे, who obtained what?
optionExplain: The endings are the other way round.
लेभिरे means 'they obtained', not 'they gave'.
Right: शिष्याः (-आः) is the doer; कीर्तिम् (-म्) is what was obtained.
लेभिरे means 'they obtained', not 'they lost'.
questions.explain: The same pattern as प्रतिष्ठां लेभिरे: the thing obtained is accusative (here -म्); the doer is nominative.
questions.rule: Doer (nominative) + thing obtained (accusative) + लेभिरे.
questions.teaches: With लेभिरे ('they obtained'), the accusative word (e.g. प्रतिष्ठाम्) is what was obtained; the nominative is who obtained.
questions.section: देवों की स्वीकृति, ज्ञान की प्रतिष्ठा

questions.q: Verse 41 says Āyurveda is the science in which certain things about life are stated. Which do you expect to be among them?
options: The names of the kings of a country
The rules of a fire sacrifice
What is wholesome and unwholesome for life
optionExplain: Kings are not mentioned in this verse.
No sacrifice is mentioned in this verse.
The mountains were only the place of the meeting in verse 7.
Right: The verse names what is good and bad for life, and also its measure.
questions.explain: The verse lists life, its happy and unhappy kinds, its measure and what is good or bad for it.
questions.rule: Āyurveda is where life and what is wholesome or unwholesome for it are stated.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words describe life and what is stated about it.
questions.rule: हिताहितम् = beneficial and harmful; तस्य = its, for it; सुखम् = happy; मानम् = measure.

questions.q: In the last line the word for 'is stated' is ____ (type it in Devanagari, as it is written before the sandhi).
questions.explain: The line is यत्र + उक्तम्, joined as यत्रोक्तम्: 'where it is stated'.
questions.teaches: उक्तम् is the past participle of √वच् ('to say'): said, stated. The same root gives उच्यते, 'is called', at the end of the verse.
questions.rule: उक्तम् = said, stated (√वच्).

questions.q: Which is the right split of यत्रोक्तम्?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ join as ओ, so यत्र + उक्तम् is written यत्रोक्तम्.
क्तम् is not a word.
रोक्तम् is not a word.
The second word begins with उ, not ओ.
questions.explain: यत्रोक्तम् = यत्र ('where') + उक्तम् ('stated').
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: यत्र + उक्तम् = यत्रोक्तम्.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 41 say are stated in Āyurveda?
options: What is wholesome and unwholesome for life
optionExplain: Right: sukham and duḥkham are named.
Right: mānam is named.
Right: tasya hitāhitam is named.
No herb is named in this verse.
The verse says nothing of any genealogy.
questions.explain: The verse names life, its happy and unhappy kinds, its measure, and what is wholesome or unwholesome for it.
questions.rule: Verse 41 lists the topics of Āyurveda: life, its kinds, its measure, its wholesome and unwholesome things.

questions.q: An invented line reads यत्र पाकविधिरुक्तस्तत्पाकशास्त्रमुच्यते (पाकविधि cooking method, शास्त्र science). By the pattern of verse 41, what does it say?
options: The science of cooking is named after a place called Yatra
The science of cooking is that in which the cooking method is stated
The cooking method will be stated tomorrow
The cooking method is a secret that is not stated
optionExplain: यत्र is 'where', not a place name.
Right: यत्र … उक्तम् … उच्यते: 'where it is stated, that is called'. This is the same frame as the definition of Āyurveda.
उक्त is a past form: 'stated', not a future.
उक्तः means it is stated.
questions.explain: The frame 'where X is stated, that is called Y' defines a science by its contents.
questions.rule: यत्र … उक्तम् … उच्यते = where … is stated, that is called ….
questions.teaches: You can read a new definition built on the frame यत्र … उक्तम् … उच्यते: the thing named at the end is the science that states the listed contents.

questions.q: Verse 42 defines life (āyus) as a union. Which four things does it unite?
options: Body, sense faculties, mind and self
optionExplain: None of these is named in the verse.
The verse names no elements.
Right: These are the four members of the compound शरीर-इन्द्रिय-सत्त्व-आत्म.
The verse names none of these.
questions.explain: Life is the union of शरीर, इन्द्रिय, सत्त्व and आत्मा.
questions.rule: Life = union of body, senses, mind, self.

questions.q: Match each member of the union to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are what the union joins.
questions.rule: शरीरम् = body; इन्द्रियम् = sense faculties; सत्त्वम् = mind (here); आत्मा = self.

questions.q: The word for 'union' in the verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first line ends शरीरेन्द्रियसत्त्वात्मसंयोगः: the union of the four.
questions.teaches: संयोगः is formed from सम् + √युज् ('to join'). The verse defines life as this joining, not as any one of the four alone.
questions.rule: संयोगः = union, joining.

questions.q: Which is the right split of शरीरेन्द्रिय?
optionExplain: न्द्रिय is not a word.
The second word begins with इ, not ए.
Neither part is a word.
Right: अ + इ join as ए, so शरीर + इन्द्रिय is written शरीरेन्द्रिय.
questions.explain: शरीरेन्द्रिय = शरीर ('body') + इन्द्रिय ('sense faculties').
questions.rule: अ + इ → ए: शरीर + इन्द्रिय = शरीरेन्द्रिय.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse give as other names (synonyms) of life?
optionExplain: Right: dhāri is the first synonym.
Right: nityaga is a synonym.
Right: anubandha is a synonym.
The body is one member of the union, not a name for life.
The senses are one member of the union, not a name for life.
questions.explain: Four synonyms are given (dhāri, jīvita, nityaga, anubandha); body and senses are members of the union.
questions.rule: पर्याय (synonyms) of life: धारि, जीवित, नित्यग, अनुबन्ध.

questions.q: An invented line defines a boat-crew as the union of captain, oarsmen, drummer and boat. By the pattern of verse 42, what is the boat-crew?
options: The union of all four, not any one of them
Any one of the four, whichever you choose
optionExplain: Right: As life is the union of the four members, the crew is their joining.
One member alone is not the union.
One member alone is not the union.
The definition requires all four together.
questions.explain: A definition by saṃyoga names the joining of all members.
questions.rule: Definition by saṃyoga = all the members together.
questions.teaches: When a verse defines something as a saṃyoga of several parts, no single part is the thing; the joining of all is.

questions.q: Verse 43 says Āyurveda is regarded as the most holy. By whom?
options: By the kings of the earth
By the knowers of the Vedas
optionExplain: The verse names no kings.
Right: The phrase वेदविदां मतः says it is the view of the Veda-knowers.
The Aśvins are not mentioned in this verse.
Indra is not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: वेदविदां मतः: regarded by those who know the Vedas.
questions.rule: The holiness of Āyurveda is stated as the view of the Veda-knowers.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
pairs: of the knowers of the Vedas
questions.explain: These words give who regards it, and for whom the teaching is.
questions.rule: पुण्यतमः = most holy; वेदविदाम् = of the knowers of the Vedas; मनुष्याणाम् = of human beings; उभयोः = of both.

questions.q: The word for 'most holy' in the verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first line has पुण्यतमो वेदः: the most holy Veda.
questions.teaches: पुण्यतमः = पुण्य + तम. The ending -तम makes a superlative: 'most'.
questions.rule: पुण्य + -तम = most holy.

questions.q: Which is the right split of यन्मनुष्याणाम्?
optionExplain: यन् is not a word.
न्मनुष्याणाम् is not a word.
Right: A final त् before the nasal म becomes न्, so यत् + मनुष्याणाम् is written यन्मनुष्याणाम्.
अनुष्याणाम् is not a word.
questions.explain: यन्मनुष्याणाम् = यत् ('which') + मनुष्याणाम् ('of human beings').
questions.rule: त् + म → न्म: यत् + मनुष्याणाम् = यन्मनुष्याणाम्.

questions.q: A student writes: 'Verse 43 states as plain fact that Āyurveda is the holiest science.' What does the verse actually say?
options: That Brahmā himself declared it the holiest
That it is more holy than the Vedas themselves
That nobody holds any view about it
That the knowers of the Vedas regard it as most holy
optionExplain: Brahmā is not named in this verse.
The verse compares nothing with the Vedas.
मतः says a view is held.
Right: मतः, 'regarded', and वेदविदाम्, 'of the Veda-knowers', make it their view.
questions.explain: The verse reports a view (मतः) of the Veda-knowers.
questions.rule: मतः = regarded; the holiness is attributed to the Veda-knowers' view.

questions.q: An invented phrase reads पादयोरुभयोर्हितम् (पाद = foot). The ending -योः is dual, as in लोकयोरुभयोः. What does the phrase mean?
optionExplain: Right: -योः with उभयोः makes it 'of both' two things, here both feet.
उभयोः means 'both', not 'one'.
A dual ending names two, not many.
हितम् means beneficial, not harmful.
questions.explain: A noun in dual -योः together with उभयोः names exactly two things.
questions.rule: लोकयोरुभयोः = of/in both worlds; पादयोरुभयोः = of both feet.
questions.teaches: The pairing of dual -योः with उभयोः carries over to any pair of things: it reads 'both'.

questions.q: Verse 44 pairs sāmānya (commonality) with viśeṣa (distinctiveness). Which would you expect to be named the cause of increase?
optionExplain: Viśeṣa is named as the cause of decrease.
Right: The verse says सामान्यं वृद्धिकारणम्.
The two are given opposite effects.
Each is given an effect.
questions.explain: Sāmānya is the cause of increase; viśeṣa the cause of decrease.
questions.rule: सामान्यं वृद्धिकारणम्; विशेषो ह्रासहेतुः.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the two effects and their scope.
questions.rule: सर्वदा = always; सर्वभावानाम् = of all entities; वृद्धिकारणम् = cause of increase; ह्रासहेतुः = cause of decrease.

questions.q: In ह्रासहेतुः the first part is the word for 'decrease', ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: ह्रासहेतुः = ह्रास + हेतुः: the cause of decrease.
questions.teaches: ह्रास is 'decrease'; the compound ह्रासहेतुः joins it to हेतुः ('cause'). It mirrors वृद्धिकारणम्, 'cause of increase'.
questions.rule: ह्रास = decrease; वृद्धि = increase.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ह्रासहेतुर्विशेषश्च?
optionExplain: र्विशेषश्च is not a word.
The word is च; the श् comes from the visarga before it.
Right: A visarga before the voiced व becomes र्, and one before च becomes श्.
ह्रासहेतुर् is not a word; the word ends in a visarga.
questions.explain: ह्रासहेतुर्विशेषश्च = ह्रासहेतुः + विशेषः + च.
questions.rule: विसर्ग → र् (before voiced); विसर्ग + च → श्च.

questions.q: Which statements does verse 44 make?
options: Sāmānya is always a cause of increase of all entities
Viśeṣa is a cause of decrease
Sāmānya is the cause of decrease
Viśeṣa is the cause of increase
optionExplain: Right: सर्वदा सर्वभावानां सामान्यं वृद्धिकारणम्.
Right: विशेषो ह्रासहेतुः.
Right: प्रवृत्तिरुभयस्य.
It is the cause of increase.
It is the cause of decrease.
questions.explain: Three statements follow from the verse; two swap the effects.
questions.rule: सामान्य → वृद्धि; विशेष → ह्रास; प्रवृत्ति दोनों की।

questions.q: An invented compound reads तेजोवृद्धिकारणम् (तेजस् = brightness). By the pattern of वृद्धिकारणम्, what does it name?
options: The cause of decrease of brightness
The cause of increase of brightness
optionExplain: Here the cause is what is named last (कारणम्), not तेजः.
वृद्धि is increase, not decrease.
The compound ends in कारणम्, 'cause'.
Right: X-वृद्धि-कारणम् = the cause of increase of X.
questions.explain: In X-वृद्धि-कारणम् the last member is the thing named: a cause; what comes before says 'of the increase of X'.
questions.rule: …वृद्धिकारणम् = cause of the increase of ….
questions.teaches: You can read any compound of the type X-वृद्धि-कारणम् as 'the cause of the increase of X'.

questions.q: Sāmānya (commonality) and viśeṣa (distinctiveness) are opposites. Which one would you expect to produce separateness?
optionExplain: Right: The verse says विशेषस्तु पृथक्त्वकृत्.
Sāmānya produces oneness.
They are given opposite effects.
Each is given an effect.
questions.explain: Viśeṣa produces separateness (pṛthaktva); sāmānya produces oneness (ekatva).
questions.rule: सामान्य → एकत्व; विशेष → पृथक्त्व.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words define the pair.
questions.rule: एकत्वकरम् = producing oneness; पृथक्त्वकृत् = producing separateness; तुल्यार्थता = sameness of purpose; विपर्ययः = the opposite.

questions.q: The verse calls distinctiveness the opposite of commonality. The word for 'opposite' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The last words are विशेषस्तु विपर्ययः: distinctiveness is the opposite.
questions.teaches: विपर्ययः is the opposite, the reverse. It tells you viśeṣa is defined by reversing sāmānya.
questions.rule: विपर्ययः = the opposite.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विशेषस्तु?
optionExplain: स्तु is not a word.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, so विशेषः + तु is written विशेषस्तु.
विशेषस् is not a word; the word ends in a visarga.
स्तु is not a word.
questions.explain: विशेषस्तु = विशेषः + तु ('but').
questions.rule: विसर्ग + त → स्त: विशेषः + तु = विशेषस्तु.

questions.q: Two herbs have the same effect on the body. Which of the two principles in verse 45 does this match?
options: Viśeṣa, because there are two herbs
Neither; the verse is only about words
optionExplain: The herbs are alike in effect, so this is not viśeṣa.
Viśeṣa is separateness of kind, not a count.
Right: तुल्यार्थता is sameness of effect or purpose, which is how the verse defines sāmānya.
The verse defines both principles.
questions.explain: Sameness of effect = sāmānya.
questions.rule: सामान्यं तुल्यार्थता: likeness of effect or purpose.

questions.q: An invented word समवेगता (सम = equal, वेग = speed) is built like तुल्यार्थता. What does it mean?
options: A person who has equal speed
The state of having equal speed
optionExplain: -ता names a state, not a person.
The word contains सम, 'equal', not 'opposite'.
-ता adds the sense 'state of equal …'.
Right: The ending -ता makes an abstract noun: 'the state of being …'.
questions.explain: तुल्यार्थ + ता = the state of having the same purpose; सम-वेग + ता = the state of equal speed.
questions.rule: -ता = the state or quality of being ….
questions.teaches: The ending -ता turns a descriptive compound into a noun for the state; you can read many such words from their parts.

questions.q: Verse 46 compares three things to a tripod. Which three?
optionExplain: Right: The first line names सत्त्वम्, आत्मा and शरीरम्.
These are not named in the verse.
These are not named in the verse.
These are not named in the verse.
questions.explain: सत्त्व, आत्मा and शरीर form the triad.
questions.rule: The triad is mind, self, body.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the three members and what holds them.
questions.rule: सत्त्वम् = mind; आत्मा = self; शरीरम् = body; संयोगात् = by union.

questions.q: The word for 'like a tripod' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first line has त्रयमेतत्त्रिदण्डवत्: this triad is like a tripod.
questions.teaches: त्रिदण्डवत् = त्रिदण्ड ('tripod') + वत् ('like'). The ending -वत् here makes the word mean 'like …'.
questions.rule: त्रिदण्ड + -वत् = like a tripod.

questions.q: Which is the right split of त्रयमेतत्त्रिदण्डवत्?
optionExplain: मेतत् is not a word.
Right: A final म् joins directly to the following vowel, and एतत् ends in त् before the त्र of त्रिदण्डवत्.
त्रयमे is not a word.
The word is एतत् ('this'); the extra त् belongs to it.
questions.explain: त्रयमेतत्त्रिदण्डवत् = त्रयम् ('triad') + एतत् ('this') + त्रिदण्डवत् ('like a tripod').
questions.rule: म् + vowel join without change: त्रयम् + एतत् = त्रयमेतत्.

questions.q: A student says the verse makes the body alone the support of the world. Which word in the verse corrects this?
options: शरीरम्: because it is named last in the list
लोकः: because it is the subject of the sentence
संयोगात्: the world stands by the union of all three
optionExplain: Being named in a list does not make it the sole support.
लोकः is what stands; it does not say which member alone stands.
Right: संयोगात् = 'by union', and the union is of mind, self and body.
नित्यः is not in this verse.
questions.explain: The support is the union (संयोगात्) of the triad, not one member alone.
questions.rule: The world stands by the union (संयोगात्) of the three.

questions.q: An invented line reads गृहं स्तम्भसंयोगात्तिष्ठति (गृह = house, स्तम्भ = pillar). By the pattern of लोकस्तिष्ठति संयोगात्, what does it say?
options: The pillars stand by the house alone
The house stood in the past
The house stands by the union of pillars
optionExplain: तिष्ठति means 'stands', not 'destroys'.
The house stands by the pillars' union, not the other way round.
तिष्ठति is present: 'stands'.
Right: -आत् on संयोग gives 'by / through the union', as in the verse.
questions.explain: The ablative -आत् names the means or support: standing by union.
questions.rule: X तिष्ठति Y-संयोगात् = X stands by the union of Y.
questions.teaches: The ending -आत् on a noun like संयोग names what something stands on or by; you can read new sentences of this kind.

questions.q: Verse 46 spoke of the union of mind, self and body. In the first words of verse 47, स पुमान्, what is that union called?
optionExplain: Right: पुमान् is the person, the one the union makes.
No god is named.
No disease is named.
No medicine is named.
questions.explain: The union is called the person, the sentient being and the subject of this Veda.
questions.rule: स पुमान् = that (union) is the person.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say what the union is and what the Veda is for.
questions.rule: पुमान् = person; चेतनम् = sentient being; अधिकरणम् = subject; तदर्थम् = for its sake.

questions.q: The last word of the verse, meaning 'revealed', is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: वेदो ऽयं संप्रकाशितः: this Veda has been revealed.
questions.teaches: संप्रकाशितः is the causative past participle of √काश् with सम् and प्र: 'made known, revealed'. वेदः (masculine) is its subject.
questions.rule: संप्रकाशितः = revealed, made known.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तच्चाधिकरणम्?
optionExplain: धिकरणम् is not a word.
Right: त् + च joins as च्च, and च + अ gives चा, so तत् + च + अधिकरणम् is written तच्चाधिकरणम्.
चा is not a word; the word is च.
The word begins with अ, not आ.
questions.explain: तच्चाधिकरणम् = तत् ('that') + च ('and') + अधिकरणम् ('subject').
questions.rule: त् + च → च्च; अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: For whom, according to verse 47, was this Veda revealed?
options: For the herbs of the mountains
For the union of mind, self and body, the person
optionExplain: No herbs are named in this verse.
The verse names no gods.
Right: तदर्थं refers back to that union, called puruṣa.
Fame is not mentioned here (verse 39 named it among deities).
questions.explain: This Veda was revealed for the sake of that union.
questions.rule: तदर्थम् = for its sake: the union called puruṣa.

questions.q: An invented word शिष्यार्थम् is built like तदर्थम् (तत् + अर्थम्). What does it mean?
options: For the sake of the student
optionExplain: -अर्थम् does not mean 'away from'.
It is a 'for the sake of' word, not the student.
-अर्थम् does not mean 'after'.
Right: X-अर्थम् is the form 'for the sake of X'.
questions.explain: X-अर्थम् = for the sake of X.
questions.rule: तद्-अर्थम् = for its sake; शिष्य-अर्थम् = for the student's sake.
questions.teaches: The ending -अर्थम् after a word X reads 'for the sake of X'; you can read new words of this type.

questions.q: Verse 48 gives a summary of substances (dravya). Which of these is named in it?
optionExplain: Right: कालः is named in the first line.
No disease is named in this verse.
No medicine is named in this verse.
Memory was named among the deities in verse 39, not here.
questions.explain: The summary names kha and the rest, self, mind, time and the directions.
questions.rule: द्रव्यसंग्रह = kha-ādi, ātmā, manas, kāla, diś.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are four of the items in the summary.
questions.rule: आत्मा = self; मनः = mind; कालः = time; दिशः = directions.

questions.q: A substance with sense faculties is चेतन; one without them is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse ends निरिन्द्रियमचेतनम्: without senses is non-sentient.
questions.teaches: अचेतनम् = अ + चेतनम्: the prefix अ- negates, so 'not sentient'.
questions.rule: अचेतन = non-sentient.

questions.q: Which is the right split of खादीन्यात्मा?
optionExplain: खादीन्य is not a word.
Right: A final इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so खादीनि + आत्मा is written खादीन्यात्मा.
दीन्यात्मा is not a word.
न्यात्मा is not a word.
questions.explain: खादीन्यात्मा = खादीनि ('kha and the rest') + आत्मा ('self').
questions.rule: इ + आ → य्+आ: खादीनि + आत्मा = खादीन्यात्मा.

questions.q: Which of these are named in the verse as substances?
optionExplain: Right: ātmā is named.
Right: kāla is named.
Right: diśaḥ are named.
No medicine is named in this verse.
No disease is named in this verse.
questions.explain: Self, time and directions are named; medicine and disease are not.
questions.rule: द्रव्यसंग्रह: खादि, आत्मा, मनः, कालः, दिशः.

questions.q: By the pattern of सेन्द्रियम् and निरिन्द्रियम्, what does the invented word निष्पत्रम् (पत्र = leaf) mean?
optionExplain: That would be the स- form, सपत्रम्.
निः- does not mean 'many'.
Right: निः- gives 'without', as निः + इन्द्रियम् gave 'without senses'.
निः- does not mean 'only'.
questions.explain: स- = with; निः- = without.
questions.rule: स-X = with X; निः-X = without X.
questions.teaches: The prefixes स- ('with') and निः- ('without') let you read pairs like सपत्रम् / निष्पत्रम् for any noun.

questions.q: Verse 49 defines two terms: guṇa (qualities) and karma (action). Which of them is described as movement (ceṣṭita) beginning with effort?
optionExplain: The qualities are listed in the first line, not described as movement.
Only karma is called a movement here.
Karma is described this way.
Right: The second line says प्रयत्नादि कर्म चेष्टितम्.
questions.explain: Karma is movement beginning with effort; guṇas are the listed qualities.
questions.rule: कर्म = प्रयत्न से आरम्भ होने वाली चेष्टा.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two definitions.
questions.rule: गुणाः = qualities; कर्म = action; चेष्टितम् = movement; प्रयत्नादि = beginning with effort.

questions.q: The word for 'are declared' in the verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first sentence ends गुणाः प्रोक्ताः: these are declared to be qualities.
questions.teaches: प्रोक्ताः = प्र + उक्ताः, from √वच्: 'declared'. The same root appeared in उक्तम् and उच्यते.
questions.rule: प्रोक्ताः = declared (√वच्).

questions.q: Which is the right split of गुर्वादयः?
optionExplain: Right: A final उ before a different vowel becomes व्, so गुरु + आदयः is written गुर्वादयः.
वादयः is not a word here.
र्वादयः is not a word.
ओ + आ would give a different form.
questions.explain: गुर्वादयः = गुरु ('heavy') + आदयः ('and the rest').
questions.rule: उ + आ → व्+आ: गुरु + आदयः = गुर्वादयः.

questions.q: In the phrase प्रयत्नादि कर्म चेष्टितम्, which word says that action begins with effort?
optionExplain: That word is in the first line and means 'ending with effort', a group of qualities.
Right: आदि means 'beginning with' or 'and the rest'.
That word names another group of qualities.
That word names the qualities, not action.
questions.explain: प्रयत्नादि means beginning with effort; प्रयत्नान्ताः means ending with effort.
questions.rule: आदि = beginning with; अन्त = ending with.

questions.q: An invented phrase reads बीजादयः फलान्ताः (बीज = seed, फल = fruit). By the pattern of गुर्वादयः and प्रयत्नान्ताः, what does it describe?
options: A series beginning with fruit and ending with seed
A series that contains only seed and fruit
A series beginning with seed and ending with fruit
A series with no seed in it
optionExplain: The order is reversed.
आदि means more follow after the first.
Right: आदि = beginning with; अन्त = ending with.
बीज is the first member.
questions.explain: X-आदि = beginning with X; Y-अन्त = ending with Y.
questions.rule: X-आदयः Y-अन्ताः = a series from X to Y.
questions.teaches: The endings -आदि and -अन्त let you read where a series starts and where it ends, even with new words.

questions.q: Samavāya is described as an inseparable relation. Between what does verse 50 say it holds?
options: Earth and the rest, and their qualities
optionExplain: No teacher is named in this verse.
No disease is named in this verse.
Nothing of the kind is in the verse.
Right: भूम्यादीनां गुणैः: earth and the rest with their qualities.
questions.explain: Samavāya joins substances (earth and the rest) with their qualities.
questions.rule: Samavāya = inseparable existence of substances with their qualities.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the definition and the reason.
questions.rule: समवायः = inherence; अपृथग्भावः = inseparable existence; नित्यः = eternal; गुणः = quality.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'inseparable existence' is ____ (type it in Devanagari, with or without the ऽ sign).
questions.explain: The first line has समवायो ऽपृथग्भावो: samavāya is aprthag-bhāva.
questions.teaches: अपृथग्भावः = अपृथक् + भावः: 'not-separate existence'. The अ- negates पृथक् ('separate').
questions.rule: अपृथक् = not separate; अपृथग्भाव = inseparable existence.

questions.q: Which is the right split of समवायो ऽपृथग्भावः?
optionExplain: Right: अः + अ joins as ओ with ऽ marking the dropped अ, so समवायः + अपृथग्भावः is written समवायो ऽपृथग्भावः.
That would mean 'separate existence', the opposite; the ऽ sign shows an अ was dropped.
योऽपृथग्भावः is not a word.
The sign ऽ is not a word.
questions.explain: समवायो ऽपृथग्भावः = समवायः ('inherence') + अपृथग्भावः ('inseparable existence').
questions.rule: अः + अ → ओ ऽ (ऽ marks the hidden अ).

questions.q: A student says: 'Earth can exist without its qualities, so samavāya is not eternal.' What does the verse say against this?
options: Qualities are rare and appear only sometimes
Where there is a substance, quality is never absent (न तत्रानियतो गुणः)
optionExplain: The verse says the opposite: never absent.
Right: The second line gives this as the reason for its being eternal.
भूमि is the example of the substances the verse names.
स नित्यः says it is eternal.
questions.explain: The verse gives the reason: no substance without its qualities.
questions.rule: यत्र द्रव्यं न तत्रानियतो गुणः = where there is substance, quality is not absent.

questions.q: An invented line: where there is fire, heat (उष्णता) is न अनियत ('not absent'). By the pattern of verse 50, what does it mean?
options: Heat is sometimes absent where fire is
Fire is absent where heat is
Wherever there is fire, heat is present
Heat exists only far from fire
optionExplain: That would contradict 'not absent'.
The line speaks of heat where fire is.
Right: 'Not absent' means present: the same logic as न तत्रानियतो गुणः.
Nothing in the line says this.
questions.explain: Two negatives (not … not fixed/absent) give 'always present'.
questions.rule: यत्र X तत्र न अनियतः Y = wherever X is, Y is present.
questions.teaches: The pattern 'where X, there Y is not absent' states that one thing is always present where the other is; you can read it for new pairs.

questions.q: Which one does verse 51 name as that in which actions and qualities reside?
optionExplain: Quality is called a cause without movement; it is not said to hold actions.
Actions are among the things that reside; they are not the seat.
Time is not mentioned in this verse.
Right: The verse says that in which कर्मगुणाः reside is द्रव्यम्.
questions.explain: तद्द्रव्यम् picks out the thing in which कर्मगुणाः are आश्रित (reside).
questions.rule: Substance is the seat of actions and qualities.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 51 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry both definitions.
questions.rule: आश्रिताः = reside; कारणम् = cause; समवायि = inhering; निश्चेष्टः = devoid of movement.

questions.q: Verse 51 calls quality a cause that is ____, 'devoid of movement' (type the word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The last quarter reads समवायी तु निश्चेष्टः कारणं गुणः.
questions.teaches: निश्चेष्ट = निः (without) + चेष्ट (movement). चेष्टितम् in verse 49 comes from the same root. Movement is not a feature of a quality here.
questions.rule: निश्चेष्टः = without movement; this is what marks guṇa in verse 51.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निश्चेष्टः?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, so निः + चेष्टः is written निश्चेष्टः.
श्चेष्टः is not a word.
निश is not a prefix here; the prefix is निः, 'without'.
The second word is चेष्टः; the श् comes only from sandhi.
questions.explain: निश्चेष्टः = निः ('without') + चेष्टः ('movement').
questions.rule: निः + चेष्टः = निश्चेष्टः (visarga → श् before च).

questions.q: Which statements fit guṇa (quality) in verse 51?
options: It is that in which actions and qualities reside
optionExplain: Right: the verse calls guṇa samavāyī kāraṇam.
Right: निश्चेष्टः is said of guṇa.
That is said of substance, not quality.
द्रव्यम् is the other term, defined in the first line.
questions.explain: Guṇa is an inhering cause without movement; the seat of actions and qualities is dravya.
questions.rule: Dravya: seat of karma and guṇa. Guṇa: inhering cause, niśceṣṭa.

questions.q: Join यत्र + आगताः by the same rule that makes यत्र + आश्रिताः into यत्राश्रिताः. What do you get?
optionExplain: Sandhi joins the two; the vowels do not stay apart.
Right: अ + आ merge into a single आ, as in यत्राश्रिताः.
अ + आ does not give ऐ.
The long आ stays; it does not vanish.
questions.explain: अ + आ → आ is the same sandhi that joined यत्र and आश्रिताः.
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ.
questions.teaches: You can join any two words of this type by the rule अ + आ → आ.

questions.q: Verse 52 says karma is a cause of two things. Which two?
optionExplain: These are qualities listed earlier; verse 52 does not name them.
Neither is mentioned in this verse.
Right: The verse says संयोगे च विभागे च कारणम्.
Neither is mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: संयोग and विभाग are the two things for which karma is the cause.
questions.rule: Karma causes conjunction and disjunction.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 52 to its meaning.
pairs: of what is to be done
questions.explain: These words carry the description of karma.
questions.rule: संयोगे = in conjunction; विभागे = in disjunction; कर्तव्यस्य = of what is to be done; क्रिया = doing.

questions.q: In कर्म नान्यदपेक्षते, the verb meaning 'depends on' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verb is अपेक्षते, 'depends on'.
questions.teaches: अपेक्षते is a verb in the third person singular: karma 'depends on' (nothing else, because of न). The thing depended on is अन्यत्, 'anything else'.
questions.rule: न + अन्यत् + अपेक्षते = does not depend on anything else.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नान्यदपेक्षते?
optionExplain: The word is न ('not'); the long ा comes only from joining न + अ.
The verb is अपेक्षते, with the initial अ; पेक्षते is not the word.
यदपेक्षते is not a word; the verse has अन्यत् and अपेक्षते.
Right: न + अ gives ना; and the final त् of अन्यत् softens to द् before the vowel अ.
questions.explain: नान्यदपेक्षते = न + अन्यत् + अपेक्षते: 'does not depend on anything else'.
questions.rule: न + अन्यत् + अपेक्षते = नान्यदपेक्षते.

questions.q: Which statements about karma are in verse 52?
options: It is a cause of conjunction and disjunction
It is the performance of what is to be done
optionExplain: Right: संयोगे च विभागे च कारणम्.
Right: द्रव्यमाश्रितम्.
Right: कर्तव्यस्य क्रिया कर्म.
The verse says the opposite: it does not depend on anything else.
That was said of guṇa in verse 51, not of karma.
questions.explain: Three statements come from the verse; the other two are false of karma here.
questions.rule: Karma: cause of conjunction and disjunction, in substance, doing; nothing else needed.

questions.q: A ball rolls until it touches a wall. By verse 52, the rolling is the cause of what?
options: The conjunction (संयोग) of ball and wall
The disjunction (विभाग) of ball and wall
A new quality of the wall
Nothing, since karma cannot be a cause
optionExplain: Right: Karma is the cause of conjunction: the rolling brings ball and wall together.
They come together here; they do not part.
The verse says nothing about karma creating qualities in another thing.
The verse names karma as a cause of conjunction.
questions.explain: Karma that brings two things together is the cause of their conjunction.
questions.rule: Karma brings about conjunction (joining) or disjunction (parting).
questions.teaches: Karma can be recognised by what it does: it joins or parts things in a substance.

questions.q: Verse 53 names an effect (kārya). Which is it?
optionExplain: The note reads the cause as those categories; they are not the effect.
Right: The verse says the effect is धातुसाम्यम्.
Seats of diseases come in verse 55, not here.
The verse names equilibrium, not disease, as the effect.
questions.explain: कार्यं धातुसाम्यम्: the effect is the equilibrium of the dhātus.
questions.rule: Effect: dhātusāmya.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 53 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the structure of the verse.
questions.rule: कारणम् = cause; कार्यम् = effect; धातुसाम्यम् = equilibrium of the dhātus; प्रयोजनम् = purpose.

questions.q: The word for 'purpose' in verse 53 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The last word of the verse is प्रयोजनम्.
questions.teaches: प्रयोजनम् is neuter nominative singular: 'the purpose'. The verse says what the purpose of this treatise is: धातुसाम्यक्रिया.
questions.rule: प्रयोजनम् = purpose of the treatise.

questions.q: Which is the right split of इत्युक्तम्?
optionExplain: इत् is not the word here; the word is इति, 'thus'.
The word is उक्तम्, 'stated'; the य् comes only from sandhi.
Right: A final इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so इति + उक्तम् is written इत्युक्तम्.
इत्य is not a word; the particle is इति.
questions.explain: इत्युक्तम् = इति ('thus') + उक्तम् ('has been stated').
questions.rule: इति + उक्तम् = इत्युक्तम् (इ → य् before a different vowel).

questions.q: Verse 53 names both an effect and a purpose. Which pairing is right?
options: Effect: bringing it about. Purpose: dhātusāmya itself
Effect and purpose are both disease
Effect: dhātusāmya. Purpose: the six categories
Effect: dhātusāmya. Purpose: bringing dhātusāmya about (dhātusāmyakriyā)
optionExplain: This swaps the two.
Disease is named in neither.
The six categories are read as the cause, not the purpose.
Right: The verse puts the state as the effect and the bringing about as the purpose.
questions.explain: धातुसाम्यं is called कार्यम्; धातुसाम्यक्रिया is called प्रयोजनम्.
questions.rule: Effect: the equilibrium. Purpose: the doing that brings it about.

questions.q: An invented manual says its purpose is बलसाम्यक्रिया. By the pattern of धातुसाम्यक्रिया, what is that purpose?
options: Equilibrium of strength itself, with no doing involved
optionExplain: Right: X-साम्य-क्रिया means bringing about equilibrium of X; here X is बल, strength.
क्रिया adds the sense of doing: the bringing about.
साम्य means equilibrium, not removal.
The word names a doing, not a list.
questions.explain: X-sāmya-kriyā: the doing (kriyā) that brings about equilibrium (sāmya) of X.
questions.rule: X-साम्य-क्रिया = bringing about equilibrium of X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -साम्यक्रिया can be read for any X: it means bringing about equilibrium of X.

questions.q: Verse 54 names wrong joining as one fault of time, intellect and sense-objects. Which two others do you expect?
optionExplain: The verse does not name early or late.
Right: The verse adds न (read as deficient, a-yoga) and अति (excessive).
Speed is not mentioned.
Purity is not mentioned.
questions.explain: मिथ्या, न and अति make the three faults.
questions.rule: Three faults: wrong, deficient, excessive.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 54 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the three faults.
questions.rule: योगः = joining; मिथ्या = wrong; अति = excessive; त्रिविधः = threefold.

questions.q: The word in the verse for 'excessive' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: In न चाति च the word अति is hidden inside चाति = च + अति.
questions.teaches: अति means 'too much'. It is hidden inside चाति = च + अति, so you must split the sandhi to see it.
questions.rule: अति = excessive, the third fault.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चाति?
optionExplain: The च is the word 'and'; it is short before the sandhi.
आति is not a word in the verse; the word is अति.
Right: अ + अ merge into आ, so च + अति is written चाति.
ति is not a word.
questions.explain: चाति = च ('and') + अति ('excessive').
questions.rule: च + अति = चाति.

questions.q: Which three things are joined wrongly, deficiently or excessively in verse 54?
optionExplain: Right: named first.
Right: named second.
Right: named third.
The body is named as a seat of diseases in the next verse, not as something joined here.
Rajas appears in the next verses as a mental doṣa, not here.
questions.explain: The verse names three things whose joining can go wrong: time, intellect and sense-objects.
questions.rule: Joined: time, intellect, sense-objects.

questions.q: A person hears loud noise all day, far more than is fit. Which fault of verse 54 is this, for a sense-object?
options: Joining of the wrong kind only
No fault, since the senses are meant to be used
optionExplain: The amount is too great, not too small.
The fault described is a matter of too much, not of kind.
The verse says that excess is a fault.
Right: The amount is too great, which is atiyoga.
questions.explain: Too much of a sense-object is excessive joining (atiyoga).
questions.rule: Too much = ati; too little = na; wrong kind = mithyā.
questions.teaches: You can sort a new case by asking: too much, too little, or the wrong kind?

questions.q: Verse 54 spoke of diseases with two seats. Which two does verse 55 name?
optionExplain: Right: The verse names शरीरम् and सत्त्वसंज्ञम्.
Time is something joined in verse 54, not a seat.
Sense-objects are joined, not named as seats.
Neither is named as a seat.
questions.explain: शरीरं सत्त्वसंज्ञं च are the seats.
questions.rule: Seats: body and sattva (mind).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 55 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the answer of the verse.
questions.rule: शरीरम् = body; सत्त्वसंज्ञम् = called sattva; आश्रयः = seat; समः = balanced.

questions.q: The word for 'seat' in verse 55 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse reads व्याधीनामाश्रयो मतः.
questions.teaches: आश्रय is related to आश्रित in verses 51 and 52: that which one rests on. The body and the mind are what diseases rest on.
questions.rule: आश्रयः = seat; related to आश्रित, 'resting on'.

questions.q: Why does आश्रयः appear as आश्रयो in आश्रयो मतः?
options: ो is the dual ending, so it means two seats
Sandhi: a visarga after अ becomes ो before a voiced consonant (here म)
आश्रयो is a different word from आश्रयः
The visarga drops because a vowel follows
optionExplain: आश्रयो is masculine nominative singular, not dual.
Right: आश्रयः + मतः is written आश्रयो मतः.
It is the same word; only sandhi changes its end.
The next word मतः begins with a consonant, not a vowel.
questions.explain: आश्रयः + मतः → आश्रयो मतः.
questions.rule: अः + voiced consonant → ो.

questions.q: Verse 54 gave three faulty joinings. Which kind of joining of time, intellect and sense-objects does verse 55 name as the cause of well-being?
optionExplain: That is one of the faults.
That is one of the faults.
Right: The verse says सम योगः is the cause of well-being.
That is one of the faults.
questions.explain: Well-being comes from the balanced joining; the three faults are what the verse sets it against.
questions.rule: Sama yoga = cause of well-being.

questions.q: Join the invented pair नरः गतः by the same rule that makes आश्रयः मतः into आश्रयो मतः. What do you get?
optionExplain: The visarga does not turn into आ.
र् appears after other vowels, not after अ.
The visarga drops before vowels, not before a consonant like ग.
Right: A visarga after अ before the voiced ग becomes ो.
questions.explain: अः + voiced consonant → ो, exactly as in आश्रयो मतः.
questions.rule: अः + voiced consonant → ो.
questions.teaches: You can predict how any word in -अः joins a following voiced consonant.

questions.q: Which description of the self fits verse 56?
options: Changing, short-lived and a doer of every action
A heavy substance made of earth
optionExplain: Right: The verse says निर्विकारः, नित्यः and द्रष्टा.
The verse says the self is unchanging and eternal, and that it sees actions.
The verse does not describe the self as heavy or of earth.
The self is not called a disease.
questions.explain: निर्विकारः, नित्यः, द्रष्टा describe the self.
questions.rule: Self: unchanging, eternal, seer.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 56 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the verse's description.
questions.rule: निर्विकारः = unchanging; नित्यः = eternal; द्रष्टा = seer; चैतन्ये = for consciousness.

questions.q: The self is a 'seer'. The Sanskrit word is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The second line reads नित्यो द्रष्टा पश्यति हि क्रियाः.
questions.teaches: द्रष्टा is built on the root √दृश् (to see), like पश्यति ('sees') in the same line. The verse gives it as the reason: the self sees actions.
questions.rule: द्रष्टा = seer; पश्यति = sees.

questions.q: Which is the right split of परस्त्वात्मा?
optionExplain: The particle is तु; the स् comes from the visarga.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, and the उ of तु becomes व् before the vowel आ.
त्वा is not a word here; the particle is तु.
The word is परः with a visarga, not परा.
questions.explain: परस्त्वात्मा = परः + तु + आत्मा: 'the supreme, however, self'.
questions.rule: परः + तु + आत्मा = परस्त्वात्मा.

questions.q: Which word of verse 56 says that the self does not alter?
optionExplain: This says the self sees; it says nothing about alteration.
This is the verb 'sees'.
Right: विकार means change, and निः means without.
This names the actions seen.
questions.explain: निर्विकारः = without change.
questions.rule: निः + विकार = without change.

questions.q: In an invented line you meet the new word निर्धनः. By the pattern of निर्विकारः, what does it mean?
optionExplain: निः means without, not full of.
The pattern gives 'without', not 'with'.
द्रष्टा, not निः, gives the sense of 'seer'.
Right: निः + धन: 'without wealth', as निः + विकार is 'without change'.
questions.explain: The prefix निः/निर् plus a noun gives 'without that noun'.
questions.rule: निः + X = without X.
questions.teaches: The prefix निः/निर् at the start of a compound often means 'without', as in निर्विकारः and निश्चेष्टः.

questions.q: Which pair of names does verse 57 give as the mental group of doṣas?
optionExplain: Right: The verse names रजः and तमः for the mental group.
Vāyu, pitta and kapha are the bodily group.
Vāyu, pitta and kapha are the bodily group.
Kapha is bodily; only rajas and tamas are the mental group.
questions.explain: The mental group is रजः and तमः.
questions.rule: Bodily group: three. Mental group: two.

questions.q: Put the bodily doṣas in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse reads वायुः पित्तं कफश्चोक्तः.
questions.rule: Order in the verse: वायुः, पित्तम्, कफः.

questions.q: The mental group is रजः and ____ (type the second name in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse reads रजश्च तम एव च.
questions.teaches: तम is the second member of the mental group. Its visarga is dropped before एव (तमः + एव → तम एव).
questions.rule: मानस group = रजः + तमः.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कफश्चोक्तः?
optionExplain: श्चोक्तः is not a word.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, and अ + उ merge into ओ: च + उक्तः → चोक्तः.
कफश् is not a word-ending that stands on its own.
चो and क्तः are not words.
questions.explain: कफश्चोक्तः = कफः ('Kapha') + च ('and') + उक्तः ('is stated').
questions.rule: कफः + च + उक्तः = कफश्चोक्तः.

questions.q: Which of these belong to the bodily group of doṣas in verse 57?
optionExplain: Right: first of the bodily group.
Right: second.
Right: third.
This belongs to the mental group.
This belongs to the mental group.
questions.explain: Three are named bodily; the other two are the mental group.
questions.rule: Bodily: वायुः, पित्तम्, कफः.

questions.q: Join the invented pair बलः + एव by the rule that makes तमः + एव into तम एव. What do you get?
optionExplain: The visarga rule does not merge अ and ए.
ो appears before a voiced consonant, not before a vowel.
Right: A visarga after अ drops before a vowel other than अ, and the vowels stay apart.
र् appears after other vowels, not after अ.
questions.explain: अः + a vowel other than अ: the visarga drops, as in तम एव.
questions.rule: अः + vowel (not अ) → the visarga drops.
questions.teaches: You can predict how any word in -अः joins a following vowel other than अ.

questions.q: The bodily group is treated by remedies. What do you expect for the mental group in verse 58?
options: Stronger remedies of the same kind
Knowledge, understanding, fortitude, memory and concentration
optionExplain: The verse gives different means for the mental group.
Those are the bodily doṣas of the previous verse.
Season is not named in this verse.
Right: The verse names ज्ञान, विज्ञान, धैर्य, स्मृति and समाधि.
questions.explain: The mental group is pacified by ज्ञान, विज्ञान, धैर्य, स्मृति and समाधि.
questions.rule: Bodily: remedies. Mental: knowledge, understanding, fortitude, memory, concentration.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 58 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two treatments.
questions.rule: पूर्वः = the former (bodily); औषधैः = by remedies; धैर्य = fortitude; समाधि = concentration.

questions.q: The word for 'memory' among the mental remedies is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The mental list ends with ...धैर्यस्मृतिसमाधिभिः; the fourth item is स्मृति.
questions.teaches: स्मृति is memory, and it sits in the compound between धैर्य and समाधि. The whole compound ends in -भिः, 'by'.
questions.rule: स्मृति = memory, one of five mental remedies.

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रशाम्यत्यौषधैः?
optionExplain: Right: A final इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so प्रशाम्यति + औषधैः is written प्रशाम्यत्यौषधैः.
प्रशाम्यत्य is not a word; the verb is प्रशाम्यति.
The word is औषधैः; the य् comes only from sandhi.
प्रशाम्यत् and यौषधैः are not the words here.
questions.explain: प्रशाम्यत्यौषधैः = प्रशाम्यति ('is pacified') + औषधैः ('by remedies').
questions.rule: प्रशाम्यति + औषधैः = प्रशाम्यत्यौषधैः.

questions.q: Which of these are named as means of pacifying the mental group?
optionExplain: Right: first on the list.
Right: third on the list.
Right: last on the list.
Remedies are named for the bodily group, the former.
This describes the remedies of the bodily group.
questions.explain: Knowledge, fortitude and concentration are mental means; remedies and the divine or reasoned basis belong to the bodily group.
questions.rule: Mental: ज्ञान, विज्ञान, धैर्य, स्मृति, समाधि.

questions.q: In an invented line रोगः क्वाथैः शाम्यति (क्वाथ means decoction), what does the ending -ऐः on क्वाथैः show?
options: Decoctions as the doer of the line
optionExplain: That sense would need a different ending, as in -आनाम्.
Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural, as in औषधैः: 'by'.
The doer of शाम्यति is रोगः; the plural -ऐः marks the means.
-ऐः is plural, not singular.
questions.explain: -ऐः on a name in -अ marks the means: by these.
questions.rule: -ऐः = by (plural), as in औषधैः.
questions.teaches: Endings -ऐः and -भिः on a noun often mark the means by which something is done.

questions.q: Vāta is called māruta (wind) in verse 59. Which pair of qualities would you expect to be in its list?
optionExplain: Neither hot nor heavy is in the list; they are the opposites of cold and light.
Neither is in Vāta's list.
Right: The verse lists शीतः and लघुः.
Neither is in Vāta's list.
questions.explain: Vāta's list includes शीतः and लघुः.
questions.rule: Vāta: rough, cold, light, subtle, mobile, clear, coarse.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 59 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are four of the seven qualities.
questions.rule: रूक्षः = rough; शीतः = cold; चलः = mobile; खरः = coarse.

questions.q: Vāta is pacified by substances of ____ qualities: the word for 'opposite' is the first part of विपरीतगुणैः (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The compound is विपरीत-गुणैः, 'with opposite qualities'.
questions.teaches: विपरीत means opposite. The verse gives the principle, not a list: whatever has qualities opposite to Vāta's pacifies Vāta.
questions.rule: विपरीतगुण = having opposite qualities.

questions.q: In विपरीतगुणैर्द्रव्यैर्मारुतः, which split of the first joint is right?
optionExplain: र्द्रव्यैः is not a word.
The र् comes from the visarga; the next word is द्रव्यैः.
The word is विपरीतगुणैः; the र् appears only by sandhi.
Right: A visarga after ऐ becomes र् before a voiced consonant (here द).
questions.explain: The first joint: विपरीतगुणैः ('with opposite qualities') + द्रव्यैः ('by substances') = विपरीतगुणैर्द्रव्यैः-.
questions.rule: विपरीतगुणैः + द्रव्यैः = विपरीतगुणैर्द्रव्यैः-.

questions.q: Which of these are listed as qualities of Vāta in verse 59?
optionExplain: Right: first in the list.
Right: second.
Right: third.
Heavy is not in this list.
Hot is not in this list; it is the opposite of cold.
questions.explain: Rough, cold and light are in the list; heavy and hot are not.
questions.rule: Vāta: रूक्ष, शीत, लघु, सूक्ष्म, चल, विशद, खर.

questions.q: An invented substance is heavy, hot, unctuous and stable. By verse 59, how does it stand to Vāta (rough, cold, light, mobile...)?
options: It has qualities opposite to Vāta's, so it can pacify Vāta
It has the same qualities as Vāta, so it pacifies Vāta
It cannot affect Vāta at all
It would increase every quality of Vāta
optionExplain: Right: Heavy opposes light, hot opposes cold, unctuous opposes rough, stable opposes mobile.
Same qualities do not pacify; opposites do.
The verse says opposite qualities pacify Vāta.
It does not share Vāta's qualities.
questions.explain: The principle of the verse is pacification by opposites.
questions.rule: Vāta + opposite qualities = pacified.
questions.teaches: To judge any new substance, set its qualities beside the doṣa's: opposite qualities pacify.

questions.q: Vāta was cold in verse 59. Which pair of qualities fits Pitta in verse 60?
optionExplain: These are in Vāta's list.
Right: The verse lists उष्णम् and तीक्ष्णम्.
These are in Vāta's list.
सूक्ष्म is not in Pitta's list; this pair is Vāta's.
questions.explain: Pitta's list includes उष्णम् and तीक्ष्णम्.
questions.rule: Pitta: unctuous, hot, sharp, liquid, sour, flowing, pungent.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 60 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are four of the seven qualities of Pitta.
questions.rule: उष्णम् = hot; तीक्ष्णम् = sharp; अम्लम् = sour; कटु = pungent.

questions.q: Pitta is pacified ____ , 'quickly' (type the Sanskrit word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The last line reads ...द्रव्यैराशु प्रशाम्यति.
questions.teaches: आशु is an indeclinable word: 'quickly'. It is joined to द्रव्यैः by sandhi (द्रव्यैः + आशु → द्रव्यैराशु). Verse 59 had no such word; it said संप्रशाम्यति, 'fully pacified'.
questions.rule: आशु = quickly.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सस्नेहमुष्णम्?
optionExplain: मुष्णम् is not a word.
Neither part is a word.
Right: A final म् takes on the next vowel: म् + उ → मु, so सस्नेहम् + उष्णम् is written सस्नेहमुष्णम्.
ष्णम् is not a word.
questions.explain: सस्नेहमुष्णम् = सस्नेहम् ('unctuous') + उष्णम् ('hot').
questions.rule: सस्नेहम् + उष्णम् = सस्नेहमुष्णम्.

questions.q: Put Pitta's first four qualities in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse reads सस्नेहमुष्णं तीक्ष्णं च द्रवम्.
questions.rule: Order: सस्नेहम्, उष्णम्, तीक्ष्णम्, द्रवम्.

questions.q: An invented drink is cold and liquid. Using verse 60, which quality of Pitta does it oppose?
options: Liquid (द्रव), because the drink is liquid
Sour (अम्ल), because all drinks are sour
None, since cold is not a quality at all
Hot (उष्ण), because cold is its opposite
optionExplain: Liquid is one of Pitta's own qualities, so it does not oppose it.
Nothing in the example says it is sour or not.
Cold is a quality; it is in Vāta's list in verse 59.
Right: Cold stands against hot; liquid is already one of Pitta's own qualities.
questions.explain: Opposition works quality by quality: cold against hot.
questions.rule: A quality opposes only its own opposite; a shared quality does not oppose it.
questions.teaches: When judging a new substance, check each of its qualities against the doṣa's list: only opposites pacify.

questions.q: Verses 59 and 60 gave qualities of Vāta and Pitta. Which quality do you expect in the list for Kapha?
optionExplain: Right: गुरु opens the list of Kapha's qualities.
रूक्ष is the first quality of Vāta in verse 59.
उष्ण is a quality of Pitta in verse 60.
चल is a quality of Vāta in verse 59.
questions.explain: Kapha's list begins गुरु, शीत, मृदु; the other three words belong to the lists of Vāta and Pitta.
questions.rule: Kapha's qualities: गुरु, शीत, मृदु, स्निग्ध, मधुर, स्थिर, पिच्छिल.

questions.q: Match each quality in Kapha's list to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are among the seven qualities of Kapha.
questions.rule: गुरु = heavy; मृदु = soft; स्थिर = stable; पिच्छिल = slimy.

questions.q: In this verse the quality meaning 'slimy' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: पिच्छिल is the last quality of the list.
questions.teaches: The note on verse 59 gives विशद ('clear, non-slimy') as the opposite of पिच्छिल: Vāta's list and Kapha's list hold a pair of opposites.
questions.rule: पिच्छिल = slimy, the opposite of विशद in Vāta's list.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विपरीतगुणैर्गुणाः?
optionExplain: The second word is गुणाः, with no initial अ.
Right: A visarga after -ऐ before the voiced ग becomes र्, so विपरीतगुणैः + गुणाः is written विपरीतगुणैर्गुणाः.
गुणैर्गुणाः is not a single word.
णाः is not a word.
questions.explain: विपरीतगुणैर्गुणाः = विपरीतगुणैः ('by opposite qualities') + गुणाः ('the qualities').
questions.rule: विपरीतगुणैर्गुणाः = विपरीतगुणैः + गुणाः.

questions.q: A patient's troubles are heavy, cold and slimy. Whose list of qualities in verses 59-61 do these match?
options: Vāta's: it has the quality शीत
Pitta's: it has the quality सस्नेह
Kapha's: गुरु, शीत and पिच्छिल are all in it
None, since the lists never share a quality
optionExplain: Vāta's list has शीत but also लघु (light) and विशद (non-slimy), not गुरु or पिच्छिल.
Pitta's list has उष्ण (hot), which does not fit cold.
Right: All three words stand in the list of verse 61.
Kapha's list holds all three.
questions.explain: The three qualities together point to Kapha's list in verse 61.
questions.rule: Match a set of qualities to the list that holds them all.

questions.q: An invented substance is light, hot and dry. Which doṣa's qualities in verse 61 are these three opposite to?
options: Vāta's: it is light and dry too
Nobody's: only substances with a taste can oppose
Kapha's: light, hot and dry are opposite to heavy, cold and unctuous
optionExplain: Light and dry are Vāta's own qualities (verse 59), not opposites of them.
Hot is Pitta's own quality (verse 60), not an opposite.
The verse speaks only of opposite qualities.
Right: These are opposites of गुरु, शीत and स्निग्ध, which stand in Kapha's list.
questions.explain: Light, hot and dry are the reverse of heavy, cold and unctuous, so the substance stands opposite to Kapha's qualities.
questions.rule: Opposite qualities calm; qualities shared with a list do not make a substance opposite to it.
questions.teaches: To test a substance against a doṣa, compare its qualities with that doṣa's list: the verse names opposite qualities as what calms.

questions.q: Verse 62 says medicines of opposite qualities remove disorders. Which disorders does it say this about?
options: Only the disorders of the mind
optionExplain: Right: साध्यसंमताः limits the statement to disorders regarded as curable.
The word साध्यसंमताः narrows the claim.
The verse does not mention the mind.
No single doṣa is named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse speaks of विकाराः साध्यसंमताः, disorders regarded as curable.
questions.rule: विकाराः साध्यसंमताः = disorders regarded as curable.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three conditions and the medicine itself carry the verse.
questions.rule: देश = place; मात्रा = dose; काल = time; भेषजैः = by medicines.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'disorders' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: विकाराः is the subject of विनिवर्तन्ते.
questions.teaches: विकाराः ends in -आः, the nominative plural of a masculine name in -अ: the disorders are the ones that turn back.
questions.rule: विकाराः = disorders (the subject).

questions.q: Which is the right split of कालोपपादितैः?
optionExplain: पपादितैः is not a word.
Right: अ + उ joins as ओ, so काल + उपपादितैः is written कालोपपादितैः.
The second word begins with उ (उपपादित), not अ.
कालोप is not a word.
questions.explain: कालोपपादितैः = काल ('time') + उपपादितैः ('administered'): given at the right time.
questions.rule: कालोपपादितैः = काल + उपपादितैः.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say must be taken into account when giving the medicine?
optionExplain: Right: देश is the first of the three.
Right: मात्रा is the second.
Right: काल is the third.
Not in the verse.
Not in the verse.
questions.explain: देशमात्राकाल names exactly place, dose and time; nothing else is added.
questions.rule: The medicine is given with regard to place, dose and time.

questions.q: An invented physician gives a medicine of the right opposite qualities, but in a double dose and in the wrong season. What does verse 62 say is lacking?
options: Due regard to dose and time
Nothing: opposite qualities alone are enough
optionExplain: The medicine already has them.
A medicine has been given.
Right: The verse puts मात्रा and काल beside opposite quality as conditions.
The verse adds देश, मात्रा and काल after the opposite qualities.
questions.explain: Right quality is not enough; the verse joins it with place, dose and time.
questions.rule: Opposite qualities + place, dose, time together.
questions.teaches: A medicine of the right quality still has to be given in the right measure, time and place, as the verse joins them.

questions.q: Verse 62 covered curable disorders. What do you expect verse 63 to say about treatment of incurable diseases?
options: A stronger medicine is taught for them
They are said not to exist
Their treatment follows in the next verse
optionExplain: The verse teaches no treatment for them.
The verse speaks of them as असाध्य, not as non-existent.
The next announcement is about qualities and actions of substances.
Right: न … उपदिश्यते says treatment is not taught for them.
questions.explain: साधनं न उपदिश्यते असाध्यानां व्याधीनाम्: treatment is not taught for incurable diseases.
questions.rule: असाध्य व्याधि: no treatment taught.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the limit and the promise.
questions.rule: साधनम् = treatment; असाध्यानाम् = of incurable; व्याधीनाम् = of diseases; वक्ष्यते = will be stated.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'treatment' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: साधनम् is what is not taught for incurable diseases.
questions.teaches: साधनम् ends in -म्: neuter, nominative singular, the subject of उपदिश्यते.
questions.rule: साधनम् = treatment (the subject).

questions.q: Which is the right split of न त्वसाध्यानाम्?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a vowel becomes व्, so तु + असाध्यानाम् is written त्वसाध्यानाम्.
The word begins with अ (असाध्य, incurable); this split would turn the meaning round.
The particle is तु ('but'); त्व is only what तु becomes before a vowel.
वसाध्यानाम् is not a word.
questions.explain: न त्वसाध्यानाम् = न ('not') + तु ('but') + असाध्यानाम् ('of the incurable').
questions.rule: त्वसाध्यानाम् = तु + असाध्यानाम्.

questions.q: उपदिश्यते is present passive; वक्ष्यते is future. What does this say about the two halves of the verse?
options: Both halves refer to the past
The first half states what the text does not teach; the second promises what it will state
The first half is future and the second present
optionExplain: Neither verb is a past form.
Right: Present 'is taught' (negated) in line 1; future 'will be stated' in line 2.
Line 1 negates a teaching; it is not a promise.
It is the other way round.
questions.explain: The tenses divide the verse: a limit in the present, a promise for what follows.
questions.rule: Present = what holds in this text; future = what is yet to come.

questions.q: An invented teacher says यथाशिष्यं पाठान् दास्यामि. By the pattern of यथाद्रव्यम्, what is his plan?
options: To give the same lesson to all together
To give lessons pupil by pupil, each as suits that pupil
optionExplain: यथा- + noun means 'according to each', not one lesson for all.
The pattern is 'according to each', not 'only one'.
Right: यथा- + a noun = 'according to each X', as यथाद्रव्यम् = substance by substance.
दास्यामि says he will give them.
questions.explain: यथाद्रव्यम् = substance by substance; so यथाशिष्यम् = according to each pupil.
questions.rule: यथा- + noun = according to each such thing.
questions.teaches: A word of the form यथा + noun (यथाद्रव्यम्) means 'according to each X', so you can read similar words you have not met.

questions.q: Taste (rasa) is the object of one sense organ. Which organ do you expect the verse to name?
optionExplain: The eye is not named in this verse.
The ear is not named in this verse.
The skin is not named in this verse.
Right: रसनार्थः means 'object of the tongue'.
questions.explain: रसनार्थः रसः: taste is what the tongue takes in.
questions.rule: रसनार्थः = object of the tongue.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say what taste is and what it rests on.
questions.rule: रसनार्थः = object of the tongue; द्रव्यम् = material basis; आपः = water; क्षितिः = earth.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'water' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: आपः and क्षितिः together are the material basis of taste.
questions.teaches: आपः is feminine and plural in form (the gram label is f. nom. pl.) even though it means water.
questions.rule: आपः = water, plural in form.

questions.q: Which is the right split of रसस्तस्य?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before the unvoiced त becomes स्, so रसः + तस्य is written रसस्तस्य.
स्तस्य is not a word.
The ending becomes ो only before a voiced sound; त is unvoiced.
The word is तस्य ('its'), which begins with त.
questions.explain: रसस्तस्य = रसः ('taste') + तस्य ('its').
questions.rule: रसस्तस्य = रसः + तस्य.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse give as the material basis (dravya) of taste?
optionExplain: Right: named as the basis.
Right: named as the basis.
Ether is named only as the first of the three causes of production and differentiation.
The tongue is the organ whose object taste is, not its basis.
questions.explain: द्रव्यम् आपः क्षितिः तथा: water and earth are the basis; the three beginning with ether are the causes.
questions.rule: Basis = water and earth; causes = the three beginning with ether.

questions.q: An invented line calls sound श्रवणार्थः (श्रवण = hearing). By the pattern of रसनार्थः, what is sound called?
options: The cause of hearing in the ear
optionExplain: The organ is श्रवण itself; -अर्थः names its object.
Right: X-अर्थः = object of X, as रसनार्थः = object of the tongue.
-अर्थः names the thing perceived, not the hearer.
The compound only says sound is what hearing takes in.
questions.explain: In रसनार्थः the first member is the sense, the second its object; श्रवणार्थः works the same way.
questions.rule: X-अर्थः = the object of X.
questions.teaches: In a compound like रसनार्थः the first member names the sense and -अर्थः its object, so you can read similar compounds.

questions.q: The verse lists the tastes (rasa). Which of these is one of the six it names?
optionExplain: उष्ण is a quality of Pitta in verse 60, not a taste of this list.
गुरु is a quality of Kapha in verse 61, not a taste.
Right: तिक्त is the fifth taste of the list.
द्रव is a quality listed for Pitta in verse 60, not a taste.
questions.explain: The six tastes are स्वादु, अम्ल, लवण, कटुक, तिक्त, कषाय; the other words are qualities (guṇa).
questions.rule: Six tastes; qualities such as उष्ण, गुरु, द्रव are not among them.

questions.q: Put the six tastes in the order the verse names them.
questions.explain: The verse runs sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, astringent.
questions.rule: स्वादु → अम्ल → लवण → कटुक → तिक्त → कषाय.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'bitter' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: तिक्तः is the fifth taste, named just before कषायः.
questions.teaches: तिक्तः ends in -ः, the nominative singular of a masculine word in -अ (तिक्त).
questions.rule: तिक्त = bitter.

questions.q: How do the first two words of स्वादुरम्लो ऽथ split before sandhi?
optionExplain: रम्लः is not a word.
The first word is स्वादुः, ending in -उ.
There is no ल्; the join is made with र्.
Right: A visarga after -उ before a vowel becomes र्, so स्वादुः + अम्लः is written स्वादुरम्लः; before ऽथ the second word shows as अम्लो.
questions.explain: स्वादुरम्लो = स्वादुः ('sweet') + अम्लः ('sour'), and the -ः of अम्लः becomes ो before the next word's अ.
questions.rule: स्वादुरम्लो = स्वादुः + अम्लः (+ अथ).

questions.q: What does the second line say with षट्कोऽयं रसानां संग्रहः स्मृतः?
options: This group of six is known as the summary of the tastes
Each of the six tastes belongs to one doṣa
The six are one taste under six names
optionExplain: Right: षट्कः = group of six, रसानाम् = of tastes, संग्रहः = summary, स्मृतः = is known.
षट्कः names the group of six tastes, not six varieties of each.
The line names no doṣa.
The six are listed as six separate tastes.
questions.explain: The line closes the list: these six are the summary of tastes.
questions.rule: षट्कः … संग्रहः = a group of six, the summary.

questions.q: An invented line ends पञ्चकोऽयं गुणानां संग्रहः. By the pattern of षट्कः, what is a पञ्चकः?
options: The fifth one in a list
optionExplain: The fifth would be a different form; -कः here names the group.
Right: A number + -क names a group of that many, as षट्कः = group of six.
-कः here makes a group, not a repeat.
पञ्च is five, not fifty.
questions.explain: षट्कः is six + -क = a group of six; पञ्चकः is five + -क = a group of five.
questions.rule: Number + -क = a group of that number.
questions.teaches: A number with -क can name a group of that size, so you can read similar words (षट्कः, पञ्चकः) without a gloss.

questions.q: The verse names three tastes for each doṣa. Which doṣa do sweet, sour and salty overcome?
optionExplain: Pitta's tastes are astringent, sweet and bitter.
Kapha's tastes are astringent, pungent and bitter.
Right: स्वाद्वम्ललवणाः (sweet, sour, salty) go with वायुम्, Vāta.
Each doṣa has its own three tastes.
questions.explain: Sweet, sour and salty overcome Vāta.
questions.rule: वायु ← स्वादु, अम्ल, लवण.

questions.q: Match each group of tastes to what it overcomes.
questions.explain: Three groups of three tastes, and the one verb they share.
questions.rule: स्वादु-अम्ल-लवण → Vāta; कषाय-स्वादु-तिक्त → Pitta; कषाय-कटु-तिक्त → Kapha; जयन्ति = they overcome.

questions.q: The verb that means overcome, in its plural form, is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: जयन्ति stands once and serves all three groups.
questions.teaches: जयन्ति ends in -न्ति, the third person plural: it agrees with the plural groups of tastes, and it is read again with each of them.
questions.rule: जयन्ति = they overcome (one verb for three groups).

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वाद्वम्ललवणाः?
optionExplain: स्वाद्व is not the word here; the taste is स्वादु.
Neither स्वाद nor वम्ल is a taste of the list.
वम्ल is not a word; the taste is अम्ल.
Right: उ before a vowel becomes व्, so स्वादु + अम्ल is written स्वाद्वम्ल.
questions.explain: स्वाद्वम्ललवणाः = स्वादु ('sweet') + अम्ल ('sour') + लवणाः ('salty').
questions.rule: स्वाद्वम्ल = स्वादु + अम्ल.

questions.q: Which tastes overcome both Pitta and Kapha, according to the verse?
optionExplain: Right: in the list of Pitta and in the list of Kapha.
Right: in the list of Pitta and in the list of Kapha.
In the lists of Vāta and Pitta, not of Kapha.
In the list of Kapha only.
In the list of Vāta only.
questions.explain: Only कषाय and तिक्त appear in both the Pitta line and the Kapha line.
questions.rule: Pitta ∩ Kapha = कषाय, तिक्त.

questions.q: An invented line says लवणस्वादुतिक्ताः पित्तं जयन्ति. Compared with verse 66, which taste does not belong in the list for Pitta?
optionExplain: Right: Salty is not among the three tastes named for Pitta in this verse.
Sweet is one of Pitta's three tastes.
Bitter is one of Pitta's three tastes.
The doṣa is the one the line is about; the question is about a taste.
questions.explain: Pitta's three tastes in verse 66 are कषाय, स्वादु, तिक्त; the line swaps कषाय for salty.
questions.rule: Check each taste against the three the verse names for that doṣa.
