questions.teaches: You can test any claimed pairing of taste and doṣa by looking it up in the three-taste list the verse gives for that doṣa.

questions.q: Verse 66 used जयन्ति, 'overcome'. This verse uses कोपयन्ति. What do you expect it to mean?
optionExplain: That is जयन्ति, the verb of verse 66.
Right: कोपयन्ति is the causative of √कुप् (to be angry): they provoke, aggravate, the converse of overcoming.
The verb has no sense of digesting.
The verb does not mean tasting.
questions.explain: The causative of √कुप् means to make angry: they aggravate the doṣa.
questions.rule: कोपयन्ति = they aggravate.

questions.q: Match each group of tastes to the doṣa it aggravates in this verse.
questions.explain: Three groups of three tastes, and the verb they share.
questions.rule: कटु-अम्ल-लवण → Pitta; स्वादु-अम्ल-लवण → Kapha; कटु-तिक्त-कषाय → Vāta (समीरण); कोपयन्ति = they aggravate.

questions.q: The word this verse uses for Vāta, instead of वायु, is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: समीरणम् closes the verse.
questions.teaches: समीरणम् ends in -म्, the accusative: Vāta is what is aggravated. The same doṣa can have different names (वायु in verse 66).
questions.rule: समीरण = Vāta.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कटुतिक्तकषायाश्च?
optionExplain: श्च is not a word.
The joining word is च, not श्च.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, so कटुतिक्तकषायाः + च is written कटुतिक्तकषायाश्च.
आश्च is not a word.
questions.explain: कटुतिक्तकषायाश्च = कटुतिक्तकषायाः ('pungent, bitter, astringent') + च ('and').
questions.rule: कटुतिक्तकषायाश्च = कटुतिक्तकषायाः + च.

questions.q: Which tastes aggravate both Pitta and Kapha, according to this verse?
optionExplain: Right: in the list of Pitta and in the list of Kapha.
Right: in the list of Pitta and in the list of Kapha.
In the lists of Pitta and Vāta, not of Kapha.
In the list of Kapha only.
In the list of Vāta only.
questions.explain: Only sour and salty are in both the Pitta line and the Kapha line.
questions.rule: Pitta ∩ Kapha (aggravating) = अम्ल, लवण.

questions.q: An invented herb has only the sweet taste. Reading verses 66 and 66.1 together, what do they say it does?
options: It aggravates Vāta and Pitta and overcomes Kapha
It overcomes Vāta and Pitta and aggravates Kapha
optionExplain: Sweet aggravates Kapha in this verse.
That is the reverse of what the verses say.
Sweet is not in Kapha's overcoming list in verse 66.
Right: Sweet is in the lists of Vāta and Pitta in verse 66, and in Kapha's aggravating list here.
questions.explain: Look the taste up in every doṣa's list in both verses: sweet overcomes Vāta and Pitta and aggravates Kapha.
questions.rule: One taste can overcome one doṣa and aggravate another.
questions.teaches: To read a taste's whole effect, look it up in every doṣa's list in both verses; the same taste can calm one doṣa and aggravate another.

questions.q: Verse 67 sorts substances (dravya) into three kinds. By what do you expect it to sort them?
options: By taste: sweet, sour and the rest
By the season in which it is gathered
optionExplain: Right: The three kinds are pacifying doṣas, vitiating dhātus, and maintaining health.
The tastes were in verses 65-66.
Origin is the sorting of verse 68, the next verse.
No season is mentioned.
questions.explain: The sorting is by function: दोषप्रशमन, धातुप्रदूषण, स्वस्थवृत्ति.
questions.rule: Three kinds of dravya, by what each does.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole division.
questions.rule: दोषप्रशमनम् = pacifying the doṣas; धातुप्रदूषणम् = vitiating the dhātus; स्वस्थवृत्तौ = in maintaining health; त्रिविधम् = threefold.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'substance' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: द्रव्यम् is the subject of उच्यते.
questions.teaches: द्रव्यम् is neuter singular, and the repeated किंचित् ('some') is neuter too, agreeing with it.
questions.rule: द्रव्यम् = substance (neuter subject).

questions.q: Which is the right split of किंचिद्दोषप्रशमनम्?
optionExplain: द्दोषप्रशमनम् is not a word.
Right: त् before the voiced द becomes द्, so किंचित् + दोष… is written किंचिद्दोष….
The second word begins with द: दोष, not ओष.
षप्रशमनम् is not a word.
questions.explain: किंचिद्दोषप्रशमनम् = किंचित् ('some') + दोषप्रशमनम् ('pacifying the doṣas').
questions.rule: किंचिद्दोष… = किंचित् + दोष….

questions.q: An invented line calls an herb धातुप्रदूषणम्. What does that say about it?
optionExplain: That is दोषप्रशमनम्.
That is स्वस्थवृत्तौ मतम्.
Right: धातुप्रदूषणम् = vitiating the dhātus.
Origin is not what this word says.
questions.explain: धातुप्रदूषणम् names the second kind: a substance that vitiates the tissues.
questions.rule: धातुप्रदूषणम् = vitiating the dhātus.

questions.q: An invented line reads किंचिद्गुरु किंचिल्लघु किंचिन्मृदु द्रव्यमुच्यते. By the pattern of verse 67, what does it say?
options: One substance is heavy, light and soft at once
Some substance is heavy, some light, some soft: one subject sorted into three
optionExplain: Repeated किंचित् separates the kinds, it does not merge them.
No names are given, only किंचित्.
Three qualities are named.
Right: Repeated किंचित् gives 'some … some … some', as in verse 67.
questions.explain: A repeated किंचित् splits one subject (द्रव्यम्) into 'some … some … some'.
questions.rule: किंचित् … किंचित् … किंचित् = some … some … some.
questions.teaches: When किंचित् is repeated before one subject, it sorts that subject into groups, as verse 67 sorts द्रव्यम् by what it does.

questions.q: Verse 67 sorted substances by function. Verse 68 sorts them again. By what do you expect it to sort?
options: By taste: sweet, sour and the rest
optionExplain: Right: जङ्गम, औद्भिद, पार्थिव name three sources of substances.
The tastes belong to verses 65-66.
No dose is mentioned in this verse.
No season is mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: The three words name the animal, plant and earthly sources of substances.
questions.rule: जङ्गम (animal), औद्भिद (plant), पार्थिव (earthly).

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the three sources and the count.
questions.rule: जङ्गम = animal; औद्भिद = plant; पार्थिव = earthly; त्रिविधम् = threefold.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'honeys' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: मधूनि opens the list in line 2.
questions.teaches: मधूनि is the neuter nominative plural of मधु: the list begins with 'honeys', in the plural.
questions.rule: मधूनि = honeys (neuter plural).

questions.q: Which is the right split of तत् पुनस्त्रिविधम्?
optionExplain: स्त्रिविधम् is not a word; the word is त्रिविधम्.
Right: A visarga before the unvoiced त becomes स्, so पुनः + त्रिविधम् is written पुनस्त्रिविधम्.
रिविधम् is not a word.
ो appears only before a voiced sound; त is unvoiced.
questions.explain: पुनस्त्रिविधम् = पुनः ('again') + त्रिविधम् ('threefold').
questions.rule: पुनस्त्रिविधम् = पुनः + त्रिविधम्.

questions.q: Line 2 lists honeys, cow products, bile, fat, marrow, blood and flesh. Where does the text say what they are?
options: In line 1, which calls all of them earthly
Not in this verse: the list continues and verse 69 ends 'used from animals'
In this verse, which says they are plants
optionExplain: A single item does not name the source.
Line 1 only names the three sources.
Right: Verse 68 breaks off mid-list; जङ्गमेभ्यः प्रयुज्यन्ते comes in verse 69.
This verse does not say so; the list is completed in verse 69.
questions.explain: The list is tied to animals only by verse 69; verse 68 begins it without saying whose it is.
questions.rule: A list that continues across verses: read on before assigning it.

questions.q: An invented word is रसौषधम्. Is its -औ a dual ending, as in a pair of names?
options: No: it comes from रस + औषधम् by sandhi
optionExplain: The -औ comes from joining two words; the word is not dual.
रसौषधम् ends in -म्; a dual would end differently.
Splitting the word shows the sandhi.
Right: A final -अ plus a word beginning with औ gives औ; no pair is meant.
questions.explain: As in जङ्गमौद्भिद = जङ्गम + औद्भिद, the औ arises from अ + औ; check the split before reading it as a dual.
questions.rule: Inside a word, -औ may come from अ + औ sandhi, not from the dual.
questions.teaches: Before reading -औ as a dual ending, try splitting the word: अ + औ also gives औ, as in जङ्गमौद्भिद.

questions.q: Verse 68 began a list of materials without naming its source. Verse 69 ends जङ्गमेभ्यः प्रयुज्यन्ते. Which source is that?
optionExplain: Right: जङ्गमेभ्यः means 'from animals'.
The plant source is औद्भिद, not named here.
The earthly source is पार्थिव, not named here.
The verse names one source.
questions.explain: जङ्गमेभ्यः is the ablative plural of जङ्गम: the items are used from animals.
questions.rule: जङ्गमेभ्यः = from animals.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are among the animal products named.
questions.rule: चर्म = skin; अस्थि = bone; शृङ्ग = horn; खुराः = hooves.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'body hair' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: लोमानि comes just after केशाः, 'head hair'.
questions.teaches: लोमानि is neuter plural (-आनि), while केशाः beside it is masculine plural: the list mixes genders.
questions.rule: लोमानि = body hair (neuter plural).

questions.q: How does रेतोस्थि in the first compound split?
optionExplain: There is no word उस्थि.
Right: After अ, a visarga before अ becomes ो and the अ is dropped (अः + अ → ोऽ), so रेतः + अस्थि is written रेतोस्थि.
स्थि is not a word.
स्थि is not a word; the second word is अस्थि.
questions.explain: रेतोस्थि = रेतः ('semen') + अस्थि ('bone'); the edition prints it without a mark for the dropped अ.
questions.rule: रेतोस्थि = रेतः + अस्थि.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 69 itself, not in verse 68?
optionExplain: Right: named in verse 69.
Right: named in verse 69.
Named in verse 68, line 2.
Named in verse 68, line 2.
questions.explain: Hooves and nails are in verse 69; honeys and marrow are in the list's first half in verse 68.
questions.rule: Verse 68 line 2 and verse 69 together form one list.

questions.q: An invented line reads वृक्षेभ्यः पत्राणि प्रयुज्यन्ते. By the pattern of जङ्गमेभ्यः प्रयुज्यन्ते, what does it say?
options: Trees are used to make leaves
optionExplain: The source is the -एभ्यः word, trees.
The verb is passive and the -एभ्यः word is the source, so trees are not the thing used.
Right: The model जङ्गमेभ्यः प्रयुज्यन्ते gives the -एभ्यः word as the source, and the plural nominative names what is used.
The verb is passive: things are used, they do not use.
questions.explain: The -एभ्यः word is the source and the nominative plural is what is used: so leaves from trees.
questions.rule: X-एभ्यः + nominative + प्रयुज्यन्ते = (things) are used from X.
questions.teaches: In a line like जङ्गमेभ्यः प्रयुज्यन्ते, the -एभ्यः word is the source and the nominative plural is what is used from it.

questions.q: Verse 70 lists gold, metals, lime, gems and salt. What kind of substances do these belong to?
optionExplain: Animal products were listed in verse 69: dung, skin, horn and so on.
Plant parts come later, from verse 73.
No water is named in this verse.
Right: These come from the earth; verse 71 line 1 closes the list as भौम, earthly.
questions.explain: The list is of earthly (mineral) substances; verse 71 line 1 says they are the earthly medicines.
questions.rule: Gold, metals, lime, gems, salt: earthly (mineral) medicines.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four items sit in the list of earthly substances.
questions.rule: सुवर्णम् = gold; सुधा = lime; लवणम् = salt; मणयः = gems.

questions.q: The word for 'gems' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: मणयः is the plural of मणि, a gem.
questions.teaches: मणयः is a plural, so several gems are meant. Items in -इ take -अयः in the plural.
questions.rule: मणयः = gems (plural of मणि).

questions.q: Which is the right split of गैरिकाञ्जने?
options: गैरिक + अञ्जन, with the dual ending -ए: two items
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ gives आ, and the -ए at the end marks two items (red ochre and collyrium).
Neither part is a word.
आञ्जने is not a word in this verse.
This would be written गैरिकोऽञ्जनम्, and would not end in -ए.
questions.explain: गैरिकाञ्जने = गैरिक (red ochre) + अञ्जन (collyrium), a pair joined into one word.
questions.rule: गैरिकाञ्जने = गैरिक + अञ्जन, two items.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 70 itself?
optionExplain: Right: gold opens the verse.
Right: salt is in the second line.
Right: gems are in the second line.
Honeys are in verse 68, an animal product.
Head hair is in verse 69, an animal product.
questions.explain: Gold, salt and gems are in this verse; honeys and hair belong to the earlier animal lists.
questions.rule: Verse 70 names gold, salt and gems; honeys and hair come earlier.

questions.q: In a list of metals, the joined word रजतताम्रे is a neuter dual like गैरिकाञ्जने. How many items does it name?
optionExplain: One item would not take the paired ending.
Right: Like गैरिकाञ्जने, the -ए on a neuter pair joined into one word marks two items.
The ending is for two.
Five is the count of the metals in the verse, not a dual.
questions.explain: A dual ending on a joined word means a pair, here रजत and ताम्र.
questions.rule: Neuter dual compound in -ए = two items.
questions.teaches: A joined neuter word in dual -ए, as in मनःशिलाले and गैरिकाञ्जने, names two things.

questions.q: After the earthly medicines, the verse turns to plant medicine (औद्भिद). How does it divide plant medicine?
optionExplain: Two is not what the verse says.
Threefold is how substance is divided in verse 68 (animal, plant, earthly), not plant medicine.
Right: The verse says औद्भिदं तु चतुर्विधम्: plant medicine is fourfold.
Five is not what the verse says.
questions.explain: चतुर्विधम् means fourfold: four classes of plant medicine.
questions.rule: Plant medicine is fourfold.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: These are the four classes named in the verse.
questions.rule: वनस्पतिः = vanaspati; वीरुत् = vīrut;वानस्पत्यः = vānaspatya; ओषधिः = oṣadhi.

questions.q: The word for 'fourfold' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: चतुर्विधम् = चतुर् (four) + विध (kind).
questions.teaches: A number followed by -विध means 'of that many kinds': त्रिविधम् in verse 68 is 'threefold', चतुर्विधम् 'fourfold'.
questions.rule: चतुर्विधम् = fourfold.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वीरुद्वानस्पत्यः?
optionExplain: A visarga before व would give वीरुर्वानस्पत्यः.
द्वानस्पत्यः is not a word.
आनस्पत्यः is not a word.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before the voiced व, so वीरुत् + वानस्पत्यः is written वीरुद्वानस्पत्यः.
questions.explain: वीरुत् (a creeper class, the nominative of वीरुध्) and वानस्पत्यः are two of the four.
questions.rule: वीरुद्वानस्पत्यः = वीरुत् + वानस्पत्यः.

questions.q: A learner lists the plant classes as वनस्पति, वीरुत्, वानस्पत्य and जङ्गम. Which entry does not belong?
options: जङ्गम: it is the animal class of verse 68, not a plant class
वनस्पति: it is not named in verse 71
वीरुत्: it is not named in verse 71
वानस्पत्य: it is not named in verse 71
optionExplain: Right: The fourth plant class in verse 71 is ओषधि.
It is the first of the four.
It is named in line 2.
It is named in line 2.
questions.explain: जङ्गम belongs to the threefold division of substance (animal, plant, earthly); the plant classes are the four named here.
questions.rule: Plant classes: वनस्पति, वीरुध्, वानस्पत्य, ओषधि.

questions.q: An invented line says पार्थिवं तु द्विविधम्, like औद्भिदं तु चतुर्विधम्. What does it say?
options: Earthly substance is the same as plants
optionExplain: द्वि is two, not four.
Right: द्वि + विधम् = twofold, and तु marks the turn to a new group.
तु marks a contrast, not sameness.
विधम् names kinds; द्वि gives their number.
questions.explain: Number + -विधम् gives 'n-fold'; तु signals a turn to a different group.
questions.rule: द्विविधम् = twofold; तु = however.
questions.teaches: Number + -विध gives 'n-fold' (द्वि = two, त्रि = three, चतुर् = four), and तु turns the sentence to a new topic.

questions.q: Which of the four classes does verse 72 say is known by its spreading shoots?
optionExplain: Oṣadhis are tied to the ripening of the fruit.
Vanaspatis are known by fruits.
Right: प्रतानैर्वीरुधः स्मृताः: vīrudhs are known by spreading shoots.
Vānaspatyas are known by flowers and also fruits.
questions.explain: The mark of the वीरुध् is the spreading shoot (प्रतान).
questions.rule: वीरुध् = spreading shoots.

questions.q: Match each class to the mark the verse gives for it.
pairs: known by flowers and also fruits
end with the ripening of the fruit
questions.explain: Each class has one mark in the verse.
questions.rule: वनस्पतिः = fruits; वानस्पत्यः = flowers and fruits; ओषधयः = end when fruit ripens; वीरुधः = spreading shoots.

questions.q: The word for 'by flowers' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: पुष्पैः is the instrumental plural of पुष्प, 'by flowers'.
questions.teaches: The ending -ऐः on a word in -अ is the instrumental plural, 'by (them)'. Here it names the mark by which a class is known; before व the visarga turns to र् (पुष्पैर्वानस्पत्यः).
questions.rule: पुष्पैः = by flowers (instrumental plural).

questions.q: Which is the right split of फलैरपि?
optionExplain: पि is not a word.
अरपि is not a word.
आपि is not the word in the verse; the word is अपि, 'also'.
Right: A visarga before a vowel becomes र्, so फलैः + अपि is written फलैरपि.
questions.explain: फलैरपि = फलैः (by fruits) + अपि (also), the 'also fruits' of the vānaspatya.
questions.rule: फलैरपि = फलैः + अपि.

questions.q: A plant's life ends when its fruit ripens. Which class does verse 72 give it?
optionExplain: Right: ओषध्यः फलपाकान्ताः: oṣadhis are those whose end is the ripening of the fruit.
Vanaspatis are known by fruits; nothing is said of their end.
Vānaspatyas are known by flowers and also fruits.
Vīrudhs are known by spreading shoots.
questions.explain: फलपाकान्ताः = those whose end (अन्त) is the ripening (पाक) of the fruit (फल).
questions.rule: Life ends at fruit-ripening: ओषधि.

questions.q: An invented line says पत्रैः क्षुपः स्मृतः, built like फलैर्वनस्पतिः. By what is a क्षुप known?
optionExplain: The mark named is पत्रैः, leaves.
Right: पत्रैः is 'by leaves', the same pattern as फलैः 'by fruits': the class is known by that mark.
Flowers are पुष्पैः, a different word.
That is प्रतानैः, the mark of the वीरुध्.
questions.explain: Mark in -ऐः (by ...) + class name + स्मृतः (is known) = the class is known by that mark.
questions.rule: X-ऐः Y स्मृतः = Y is known by X.
questions.teaches: A word in -ऐः names the mark 'by which' a class is known; with स्मृतः it reads 'is known by'.

questions.q: Verse 73 begins a list of parts of plants used as medicine. Which of these would you expect in it?
optionExplain: Hooves belong to the animal list in verse 69.
Bile belongs to the animal list in verse 68.
Right: मूल, root, opens the list.
Gold belongs to the earthly list in verse 70.
questions.explain: The list is of plant parts; the root opens it.
questions.rule: Verse 73 lists plant parts, starting with root.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are part of the first and second lines.
questions.rule: त्वक् = bark; सारः = heartwood; पल्लवाः = tender leaves; कण्टकाः = thorns.

questions.q: The word for 'flower' in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: पुष्पम् sits between फलम् (fruit) and भस्म (ash).
questions.teaches: पुष्पम् ends in -म्: a neuter singular, one item in a list of separate words.
questions.rule: पुष्पम् = flower.

questions.q: The edition notes a variant -नाडस्व- for -नालस्व- in the first line. What does the card say about it?
options: नाड is a different part, such as the root
The verse is then about animals
The list then has one item fewer
Same sense: नाड and नाल both mean the hollow stalk
optionExplain: The root is already named, as मूल.
Nothing in the variant changes the plant list.
The variant replaces a word with a near-equivalent; it adds or removes nothing.
Right: The note says नाड ~ नाल, 'hollow stalk': the meaning does not change.
questions.explain: A variant that means the same thing does not change the list.
questions.rule: नाल/नाड = hollow stalk; no change in sense.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 73 itself?
optionExplain: Right: the list begins with मूल.
Right: it is in the first line.
Right: it closes the second line.
Tubers come in verse 74.
Leaf-buds come in verse 74.
questions.explain: Root, exudate and thorns are in verse 73; tubers and leaves come in verse 74, where the list ends.
questions.rule: Verse 73: root, exudate, thorns; verse 74: tubers, leaves.

questions.q: An invented verse reads पर्णं मूलं फलं पुष्पम् and stops, with no verb. By the pattern of verse 73, what should a reader expect?
options: The sentence goes on in the next verse
The verse is a complete prayer
The words mean nothing without a verb
optionExplain: Right: Verse 73 also gives only a list; its closing words come in verse 74.
A list that runs on into the next verse is normal here.
A bare list is not a prayer.
The list says what the items are; the verse that follows says what group they form.
questions.explain: Verse 73 lists the items; verse 74 supplies the closing words 'this is the plant group'.
questions.rule: A verse may be only a list, completed in the next.
questions.teaches: A list may fill a whole verse and be completed by words in the next; when a verse has no verb, look at the one after.

questions.q: The verse names two kinds of drug-plants, मूलिनी and फलिनी. What do their names point to?
options: The part used: root (मूल) and fruit (फल)
optionExplain: Leaves and flowers are not what the names are built on.
Right: मूलिनी is built on मूल, root; फलिनी on फल, fruit.
Bark and sap are not what the names are built on.
Those are named as parts of the plant group in line 1.
questions.explain: मूलिनी = root-drug; फलिनी = fruit-drug.
questions.rule: मूलिनी = root used; फलिनी = fruit used.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first two are the drug-plants counted in line 2; the others close the list in line 1.
questions.rule: मूलिन्यः = root-drugs; फलिन्यः = fruit-drugs; कन्दाः = tubers; शुङ्गाः = leaf-buds.

questions.q: The word for 'tubers' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: कन्दाः are the tubers, the third item of the first line.
questions.teaches: कन्दाः is a masculine plural; च follows it and joins it with the next item, प्ररोहाः.
questions.rule: कन्दाः = tubers.

questions.q: On the card's reading of षोडशैकोना, how does the verse give the number of फलिनी?
optionExplain: एकोना takes one away from twenty.
षोडश (sixteen) goes with the मूलिनी; एकोना goes with twenty.
Right: फलिन्यो विंशतिः … एकोना: twenty, less by one.
एकोना means 'less by one', not 'plus one'.
questions.explain: षोडश goes with मूलिन्यः, and एकोना with विंशतिः; so 16 mūlinīs and 19 phalinīs.

questions.q: Which of these items are named in verse 74 itself?
optionExplain: Right: it opens the verse.
Right: it is in line 1.
Right: it ends the list.
Thorns are the last item of verse 73.
Latex is in verse 73.
questions.explain: Verse 74 names leaves, tubers and sprouts (and leaf-buds); thorns and latex are in verse 73.
questions.rule: Verse 74 line 1: पत्र, शुंग, कन्द, प्ररोह.

questions.q: An invented line has मूलिन्यः त्रिंशदेकोनाः, built like एकोना विंशतिः. By that pattern, how many mūlinīs?
optionExplain: एकोन takes away one.
एकोन takes away one.
One is taken from thirty, not nine.
Right: त्रिंशत् (thirty) with एकोन (less by one) gives 29.
questions.explain: Number + एकोन(ा) = that number less one.
questions.teaches: एकोन / एकोना after a number means 'that number less one', as in विंशतिः एकोना = nineteen.

questions.q: Verse 75 counts four groups of medicinal substances. Which of these is NOT counted there?
optionExplain: Right: Gems (मणयः) are in verse 70, in the earthly list; verse 75 does not count them.
Salts are counted as five.
Urines are counted as eight.
Milks are counted as eight.
questions.explain: Verse 75 counts mahāsnehas, salts, urines and milks.
questions.rule: Counted: mahāsneha, salts, urines, milks.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four groups counted.
questions.rule: महास्नेहाः = great unctuous substances; लवणानि = salts; मूत्राणि = urines; पयांसि = milks.

questions.q: The word for 'four' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: चत्वारः goes with महास्नेहाः.
questions.teaches: चत्वारः is the masculine plural of 'four', agreeing with the masculine plural महास्नेहाः.
questions.rule: चत्वारः = four.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पञ्चैव?
optionExplain: व is not a word.
Right: अ + ए joins as ऐ, so पञ्च + एव is written पञ्चैव.
ऐव is not a word; the word is एव.
ए + ए would not give ऐ.
questions.explain: पञ्चैव = पञ्च (five) + एव (just), 'just five'.
questions.rule: पञ्चैव = पञ्च + एव.

questions.q: A learner says the verse gives eight salts. What is the correction?
options: The verse gives salts as four
The verse gives no count for salts
Salts are five; eight is the count of urines and of milks
optionExplain: Four is the count of the mahāsnehas.
It says पञ्चैव लवणानि.
Right: पञ्चैव लवणानि: five salts; अष्टौ मूत्राणि … अष्टावेव पयांसि: eight urines and eight milks.
Salts are five.
questions.explain: Counts in verse 75: mahāsneha 4, salts 5, urines 8, milks 8.
questions.rule: Salts = five.

questions.q: Join नौ + एव by the rule seen in अष्टौ + एव → अष्टावेव. What is the result?
optionExplain: The two words are joined by sandhi, not simply set side by side.
औ becomes आव्, not अव्.
That is न + एव, a different word.
Right: Final औ before a vowel becomes आव्, as in अष्टावेव.
questions.explain: औ before a vowel becomes आव्.
questions.rule: औ + vowel → आव् + vowel.
questions.teaches: Final -औ before a vowel turns into आव्, so अष्टौ + एव is अष्टावेव.

questions.q: A verse praises someone who knows how to use remedies in disorders. What title do you expect it to give him?
optionExplain: Right: The verse says स वेदवित्, he is a knower of the science.
Nothing in the verse concerns a king.
He applies the remedies; he is not the one treated.
The verse speaks of knowing how to apply, not of studying.
questions.explain: वेदवित् = veda-vit, 'knower of the science'.
questions.rule: Knowing how to apply remedies in disorders = वेदवित्.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four carry the point of the verse.
questions.rule: शोधनार्थाः = meant for purification; वृक्षाः = trees; विकारेषु = in disorders; संयोक्तुम् = how to apply.

questions.q: The word for 'knower of the science' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: वेदवित् = वेद (science) + वित् (knower).
questions.teaches: -वित् at the end of a compound means 'one who knows': वेदवित् is 'one who knows the science'.
questions.rule: वेदवित् = knower of the science.

questions.q: Which is the right split of षड् वृक्षाः?
optionExplain: That would be written षो वृक्षाः.
Right: Final ट् becomes ड् before the voiced व, so षट् + वृक्षाः is written षड् वृक्षाः.
The word in the verse is वृक्षाः, trees.
The number is षट्, six.
questions.explain: षट् (six) + वृक्षाः (trees): six trees.
questions.rule: षड् वृक्षाः = षट् + वृक्षाः.

questions.q: By verse 76, who is a वेदवित्?
options: One who can recite the whole list
One who owns the six trees
One who knows how to apply these in disorders
optionExplain: The verse speaks of applying, not of reciting.
Owning is not mentioned.
Right: यो वेत्ति संयोक्तुं विकारेषु स वेदवित्.
The verse speaks of anyone who knows how to apply them.
questions.explain: The test is knowing how to apply (संयोक्तुम्) in disorders (विकारेषु).
questions.rule: Knowing how to apply, not just the list.

questions.q: An invented line says स वेत्ति पठितुम्, built like वेत्ति संयोक्तुम्. What does it mean?
options: He does not know the text
optionExplain: वेत्ति is present, 'knows', and -तुम् is not a past ending.
Nothing negates वेत्ति.
That would need a verb of wishing; वेत्ति is 'knows'.
Right: वेत्ति + a word in -तुम् (the infinitive) = 'knows how to ...'.
questions.explain: वेत्ति plus the infinitive in -तुम् means 'knows how to'.
questions.rule: वेत्ति + -तुम् = knows how to.
questions.teaches: A verb of knowing with an infinitive in -तुम् reads 'knows how to ...', as in वेत्ति संयोक्तुम्.

questions.q: Verse 74 counted sixteen mūlinīs (root-drugs) without naming them. What do you expect verse 77 to give?
options: The first names of the sixteen mūlinīs
The names of the five salts
optionExplain: Right: The names begin here and run on into verse 78.
The five salts are only counted, in verse 75.
Only the count of the urines is given, in verse 75.
Only the count is given, in verse 75.
questions.explain: Verse 74 gives the count; verses 77-78 give the names.
questions.rule: Verse 77 begins the names of the sixteen mūlinīs.

questions.q: Put these four plant names in the order of verse 77.
questions.explain: These are the first four names of the verse.
questions.rule: हस्तिदन्ती → हैमवती → श्यामा → त्रिवृत्.

questions.q: The plant named right after त्रिवृत् is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: In the verse the two are written together: त्रिवृदधोगुडा.
questions.teaches: The word space is lost by sandhi: त्रिवृत् + अधोगुडा → त्रिवृदधोगुडा.
questions.rule: त्रिवृत् is followed by अधोगुडा.

questions.q: Which is the right split of त्रिवृदधोगुडा?
optionExplain: धोगुडा is not a word.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before a vowel, so त्रिवृत् + अधोगुडा is written त्रिवृदधोगुडा.
दधोगुडा is not a word.
A visarga before अ would give त्रिवृरधोगुडा, not द.
questions.explain: Two plant names: त्रिवृत् and अधोगुडा.
questions.rule: त्रिवृदधोगुडा = त्रिवृत् + अधोगुडा.

questions.q: Which of these names are in verse 77 itself?
optionExplain: Right: the third name.
Right: the sixth name.
Right: it closes the verse.
बिम्बी is named in verse 78.
क्षीरिणी is named in verse 78.
questions.explain: The first nine names are in verse 77; बिम्बी and क्षीरिणी follow in verse 78.
questions.rule: श्यामा, सप्तला, गवाक्षी are in verse 77.

questions.q: A new text names a plant सुवृत् followed by अमला. By the rule in त्रिवृत् + अधोगुडा, how is it written?
optionExplain: त् should become द् before the vowel.
The change is to द्, not ध्.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before a vowel, as in त्रिवृदधोगुडा.
In sandhi the two are joined into one word.
questions.explain: Final त् before a vowel becomes द्.
questions.rule: त् + vowel → द् + vowel.
questions.teaches: A word ending in त् changes it to द् when a vowel follows, so त्रिवृत् + अधोगुडा is त्रिवृदधोगुडा.

questions.q: A list of sixteen names ends with क्षीरिणी चात्र षोडशी. What does the last word do?
options: It begins a second list of sixteen
It says क्षीरिणी is a disease
It names क्षीरिणी as the first of sixteen
It marks क्षीरिणी as the sixteenth item, closing the list
optionExplain: The sixteenth item closes this list.
षोडशी is a number word, not a disease.
षोडशी is the sixteenth, not the first.
Right: षोडशी = 'the sixteenth' (feminine, like क्षीरिणी).
questions.explain: षोडशी is the ordinal 'sixteenth', and it agrees with क्षीरिणी.
questions.rule: षोडशी = the sixteenth.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading these names in Devanagari is the point.
questions.rule: ज्योतिष्मती = Jyotiṣmatī; बिम्बी = Bimbī; शणपुष्पी = Śaṇapuṣpī; विषाणिका = Viṣāṇikā.

questions.q: The last plant named in the verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: क्षीरिणी is the sixteenth, closing the list.
questions.teaches: The ordinal षोडशी ('sixteenth') is attached to it.
questions.rule: क्षीरिणी = the last, sixteenth plant.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चात्र?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ joins as आ, so च + अत्र is written चात्र.
त्र is not a word.
आत्र is not a word here; the word is अत्र, 'here'.
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: चात्र = च (and) + अत्र (here).
questions.rule: चात्र = च + अत्र.

questions.q: Which of these names are in verse 78 itself?
optionExplain: Right: the second name.
Right: the fifth name.
Right: the sixth name.
हैमवती is named in verse 77.
गवाक्षी is named in verse 77.
questions.explain: Verse 78 gives the last seven names; हैमवती and गवाक्षी are in verse 77.
questions.rule: बिम्बी, अजगन्धा, द्रवन्ती are in verse 78.

questions.q: By the rule in च + अत्र → चात्र, join च + अस्ति. What is the result?
optionExplain: The two words are joined by sandhi.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, as in चात्र.
अ + अ gives आ, not ए.
अ + अ gives आ, not औ.
questions.explain: A final अ and an initial अ merge into आ.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: When a word ending in अ meets one beginning with अ, the two merge into one long आ.

questions.q: In verse 79 the word छर्दने names a treatment. Which one?
optionExplain: That is शीर्षविरेचने, in the second line.
That is विरेचन, named in verse 80.
Right: छर्दन is emesis; छर्दने is its locative, 'in emesis'.
No bathing is mentioned.
questions.explain: छर्दने = in emesis; शीर्षविरेचने = in head-purgation.
questions.rule: छर्दने = in emesis.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the use of each plant.
questions.rule: छर्दने = in emesis; शीर्षविरेचने = in head-purgation; योज्या = to be used; श्वेता = a plant.

questions.q: The word for 'in emesis' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: छर्दने is the locative of छर्दन, written च्छर्दने after च.
questions.teaches: A word in -ए can be a locative, 'in (a treatment)'. After च the initial छ is doubled, so the verse writes च्छर्दने.
questions.rule: छर्दने = in emesis.

questions.q: Which is the right split of च्छर्दने?
optionExplain: र्दने is not a word.
चि is not the word in the verse; it is च, 'and'.
The word is छर्दने, with छ.
Right: After च the initial छ doubles, so च + छर्दने is written च्छर्दने.
questions.explain: च्छर्दने = च ('and') + छर्दने ('in emesis').
questions.rule: च्छर्दने = च + छर्दने.

questions.q: A physician needs a plant for head-purgation. Which one does verse 79 give?
optionExplain: Right: श्वेता ज्योतिष्मती चैव योज्या शीर्षविरेचने.
Bimbī is for emesis.
Śaṇapuṣpī is for emesis.
Haimavatī is for emesis.
questions.explain: Head-purgation: śvetā and jyotiṣmatī; the other three are for emesis.
questions.rule: Head-purgation: श्वेता, ज्योतिष्मती.

questions.q: An invented line says बला च पटोली च विरेचने योज्ये. By the pattern of verse 79, what does विरेचने tell you?
options: The name of a third plant
The treatment in which the two plants are to be used
optionExplain: A word in -ए after the plants names where they are used.
Right: A locative in -ए names the treatment, as छर्दने does in verse 79.
A locative names a situation, not a person.
Nothing in the pattern gives a growing season.
questions.explain: Plants + treatment in -ए + योज्य = plants to be used in that treatment.
questions.rule: Locative -ए = the treatment in which they are used.
questions.teaches: A locative in -ए beside योज्य names the treatment in which the plants are to be used.

questions.q: Verse 79 puts three of the sixteen mūlinīs in emesis and two in head-purgation. How many are left for purgation?
optionExplain: Five is the number already placed, not the number left.
That forgets the two placed in head-purgation.
Right: The rest of the sixteen after the five already placed.
Sixteen is the whole set; five are already placed elsewhere.
questions.explain: The verse itself says एकादश (eleven) remain for virecana.
questions.rule: 16 mūlinīs − 3 (emesis) − 2 (head-purgation) = 11 for purgation.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the verse's two statements.
questions.rule: एकादश = eleven; अवशिष्टाः = remaining; विरेचने = in purgation; शृणु = hear.

questions.q: The last word of verse 80 is a command meaning 'hear'. Type it in Devanagari: ____
questions.explain: शृणु is the imperative of √श्रु, 'hear'.
questions.teaches: फलिनीः शृणु = 'hear the phalinīs': the verse hands over to the next topic.
questions.rule: शृणु = hear (command); it ends the mūlinī section.

questions.q: In मूलिन्यः फलिनीः शृणु, which word is the thing to be heard, the object of शृणु?
optionExplain: It is nominative plural, the subject of उक्ताः: 'the mūlinīs have been described'.
It means 'by name and action' and says how the mūlinīs were described.
It is the verb itself, 'hear', not the thing heard.
Right: It is accusative plural: 'hear the phalinīs'.
questions.explain: मूलिन्यः are the ones already described; फलिनीः are the ones now to be heard.
questions.rule: Nominative = subject (मूलिन्यः); accusative = object (फलिनीः).

questions.q: Which statements does verse 80 make?
options: The eleven that remain are to be used in purgation.
The mūlinīs have been described by name and action.
Now the phalinīs are to be heard.
The eleven that remain are for emesis.
The phalinīs have already been described.
optionExplain: Right: प्रयोज्यास्ता विरेचने.
Right: इत्युक्ता नामकर्मभ्यां मूलिन्यः.
Right: फलिनीः शृणु.
Wrong: they are for virecana (purgation).
Wrong: they are only announced here.
questions.explain: The verse closes the mūlinīs and opens the phalinīs.
questions.rule: Eleven for purgation; mūlinīs done; phalinīs next.

questions.q: A new text lists 20 herbs: 5 are sent to bath and 4 to massage. By the method of verse 80, how many remain for drinking?
optionExplain: Right: The remainder after the uses already assigned.
Nine is the size of the two assigned groups together, not the remainder.
That subtracts only the bath herbs.
That subtracts only the massage herbs.
questions.explain: As in verses 79-80, the remainder is the total minus the groups already placed.
questions.rule: Remaining = total − the groups already assigned.
questions.teaches: When a text assigns some drugs to uses and says the rest remain for one more use, subtract the assigned groups from the total.

questions.q: Verse 80 ended with 'now hear the phalinīs'. What kind of text do you expect in verse 81?
options: A list of names of fruit-drugs
optionExplain: Nothing in verse 80 announces diseases.
Right: Hearing the phalinīs means hearing them named.
The story part of the chapter is long over.
Verse 80 promises fruit-drugs, not food rules.
questions.explain: Verse 81 begins naming the phalinīs.
questions.rule: After 'hear the phalinīs', the names follow.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading the plant names in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: शङ्खिनी = Śaṅkhinī; मदनानि = Madana; जीमूतम् = Jīmūta; कृतवेधनम् = Kṛtavedhana.

questions.q: क्लीतक is said to be of two kinds: आनूप (marshland) and ____ (dry land). Type the second kind in Devanagari.
questions.explain: स्थलजम् is the dry-land kind of क्लीतक.
questions.teaches: The verse gives क्लीतक two kinds: आनूपम् (growing in marshland) and स्थलजम् (growing on dry land).
questions.rule: क्लीतक = आनूप + स्थलज.

questions.q: Which is the right split of शङ्खिन्यथ?
optionExplain: थ is not a word.
आ + अ would merge into आ and give शङ्खिनाथ.
Right: ई before a different vowel becomes य्: शङ्खिनी + अथ is written शङ्खिन्यथ.
That would give शङ्खिनोऽथ, with ओ.
questions.explain: शङ्खिन्यथ = शङ्खिनी (the plant) + अथ (then).
questions.rule: ई + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 81 itself?
optionExplain: Right: मदनानि च is in the first half-line.
Wrong: it comes in verse 82.
Right: it is in the second half-line.
Wrong: it comes in verse 83.
Right: it is in the first half-line.
questions.explain: Three of the five are in verse 81; the others come in the next verses.
questions.rule: 81: शङ्खिनी, विडङ्ग, त्रपुष, मदन | धामार्गव, इक्ष्वाकु, जीमूत, कृतवेधन | क्लीतक.

questions.q: A new line says अन्नं त्रिविधं स्मृतम्, meaning food is known to be of how many kinds, by the verse-81 pattern?
options: Threefold: three kinds of food follow
optionExplain: त्रि is three; द्वि would be two.
चतुर् would be four.
विध means a kind or fold; the line names kinds.
Right: Number + विध means '-fold', as in द्विविध, twofold.
questions.explain: द्विविधं gives 'twofold'; त्रिविधं gives 'threefold' in the same way.
questions.rule: Number + विध = so many kinds.
questions.teaches: A number word before -विध tells how many kinds the text will name.

questions.q: Verse 81 began the phalinīs and its list was not finished. What do you expect verse 82 to do?
options: State the uses of all of them
optionExplain: Right: The list continues across verses 81-83.
The salts come much later, in verses 88-89.
The uses begin only in verse 83, line 2.
The chapter goes on for many more verses.
questions.explain: Verse 82 gives six more phalinīs.
questions.rule: The phalinī list runs on from 81 into 82.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading the plant names in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: प्रकीर्या = Prakīryā; उदकीर्या = Udakīryā; अभया = Abhayā; अन्तःकोटरपुष्पी = Antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī.

questions.q: चोदकीर्या is a joined form: च + ____ (type the plant name in Devanagari).
questions.explain: च + उदकीर्या = चोदकीर्या.
questions.teaches: अ + उ → ओ: च + उदकीर्या is written चोदकीर्या.

questions.q: Which is the right split of हस्तिपर्ण्याश्च?
optionExplain: श्च is not a word.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, so हस्तिपर्ण्याः + च is written हस्तिपर्ण्याश्च.
याश्च is not a word.
The श् comes from the visarga; it is not a separate word.
questions.explain: हस्तिपर्ण्याः is genitive: 'of हस्तिपर्णी', and च follows.
questions.rule: Visarga + च → श्च.

questions.q: A reader sees शारदम् ('autumnal') with no noun after हस्तिपर्ण्याः. What does the card say is understood?
options: फलम्, the fruit, so 'the autumnal fruit of हस्तिपर्णी'
Nothing is understood; it is a name on its own
optionExplain: Roots belong to the mūlinīs, already finished.
Nothing in the verses speaks of leaves.
Right: The list is of phalinīs (fruit-drugs), and शारदम् is neuter like फलम्.
शारदम् is an adjective, 'autumnal', and needs a noun.
questions.explain: The sentence is about phalinīs, so a fruit is understood.
questions.rule: शारदम् (neuter, 'autumnal') takes फलम् understood.

questions.q: A new line joins वचायाः and च. How is it written, by the same rule as हस्तिपर्ण्याश्च?
optionExplain: The visarga does not stay before च.
Before च the sound is श्, not स्.
The sound श् is not dropped.
Right: The visarga of वचायाः becomes श् before च.
questions.explain: A visarga before च is written श्च, in any word.
questions.teaches: The rule that turns the visarga into श् before च applies to any word.

questions.q: Verses 81-82 gave sixteen phalinīs in all. If the total is nineteen, how many does line 1 of verse 83 add?
optionExplain: Right: 19 − 16 = 3, and line 1 names three plants.
One would leave the total at seventeen.
Two would leave the total at eighteen.
Nineteen is the whole total, not the new part.
questions.explain: Line 1 names कम्पिल्लक, आरग्वध and कुटज: three more, making nineteen.
questions.rule: 16 + 3 = 19 phalinīs.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line is built on the genitive: 'the fruit of ...'.
questions.rule: फलम् = fruit; यत् = which; कुटजस्य = of kuṭaja; कम्पिल्लकारग्वधयोः = of kampillaka and āragvadha.

questions.q: The ending -योः of कम्पिल्लकारग्वधयोः is a genitive dual, so the word names ____ plants (type the number).
questions.explain: -योः here marks the genitive dual: two items.
questions.teaches: कम्पिल्लक and आरग्वध are joined in one word with a dual ending: 'of the two'.
questions.rule: -योः = 'of the two'.

questions.q: Line 2 repeats words of verse 81. As the card reads it, what is the difference?
options: In 83 they are new phalinīs, numbers 20-23
In 81 they are list members; in 83 they begin a statement of uses
The line in 83 is only a copying error
optionExplain: The total is nineteen, completed in line 1.
Right: The same four fruits are first named, then used as the start of a new sentence.
The mūlinīs were finished in verse 80.
The card reads it as genuine: the counts of verses 84-85 need it.
questions.explain: The repeated line is the opening of a sentence that ends in verse 84.
questions.rule: 81 line 2: list members. 83 line 2: subject of the next sentence.

questions.q: The sentence begun in line 2 of verse 83 has no verb yet. Where does it end?
options: In verse 84, where the fruits are said to be used in emesis and āsthāpana
optionExplain: Verse 82 comes before 83 and cannot finish it.
Line 1 is a separate statement about the fruit of three plants.
Right: Verse 84 gives the verb योज्यानि.
Verse 84 completes it.
questions.explain: Verses 83 (line 2) and 84 form one sentence.
questions.rule: Verse 83 line 2 + verse 84 = one sentence of use.

questions.q: 12 jars are listed; 4 are repeated as for sale, 3 go as gifts, 5 stay in the shop. Is the repeat a mistake?
options: Yes: a repeated name is always an error
Yes: the book should list only 8 jars
It cannot be told by counting
No: 12 − 4 − 3 = 5, so the repeated four are needed in the count
optionExplain: Counts can show that a repeat is deliberate.
That would break the stated 5 for the shop.
Here the counting settles it.
Right: The repeat starts a new statement, and the counts fit it.
questions.explain: As in verses 83-85, check the counts before calling a repeated line an error.
questions.rule: A repeat that makes the stated counts work is not a scribal error.
questions.teaches: Before deleting a repeated line as a copying error, test whether the counts the text states depend on it.

questions.q: Verse 83 line 2 started a sentence naming four fruits. What do you expect verse 84 to give?
options: More names and the verb that says what to do with them
optionExplain: Right: A sentence needs its verb; the verse supplies it.
A verse in the middle of a chapter does not give a title.
The sages came at the start of the chapter.
Salts come in verses 88-89.
questions.explain: Verse 84 adds four names and the verb योज्यानि.
questions.rule: 84 completes the sentence begun in 83.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole statement.
questions.rule: वमने = in emesis; आस्थापनेषु = in āsthāpana enemas; योज्यानि = to be used; एतानि = these.

questions.q: योज्यान्यास्थापनेषु is a joined form: योज्यानि + ____ (type the second word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: योज्यानि + आस्थापनेषु = योज्यान्यास्थापनेषु.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: योज्यानि + आस्थापनेषु is written योज्यान्यास्थापनेषु.
questions.rule: इ + आ → ्य + आ.

questions.q: Which is the right split of योज्यान्यास्थापनेषु?
optionExplain: यास्थापनेषु is not a word.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्; योज्यानि agrees with एतानि.
A visarga here would not give न्य.
That would give योज्यान्वास्थापनेषु, with व्.
questions.explain: योज्यानि is neuter plural, like एतानि.
questions.rule: योज्यानि + आस्थापनेषु = योज्यान्यास्थापनेषु.

questions.q: Which of these fruits are named in verse 84 itself?
optionExplain: Right: first word of the verse.
Wrong: it is in verse 83, line 2.
Right: second word.
Wrong: it is in verse 83, line 2.
Right: it ends the first line.
questions.explain: Verse 84 names मदन, कुटज, त्रपुष and हस्तिपर्णिनी; जीमूत and इक्ष्वाकु are in 83.
questions.rule: 84 names 4 fruits; the other 4 are in 83 line 2.

questions.q: A new line says इमानि पाने नस्ये च योज्यानि. Where are 'these' to be used?
options: In both drinking and nasal use
optionExplain: नस्ये च adds a second use.
पाने names the first use.
Right: Two uses are joined by च, as in verse 84.
योज्यानि says they are to be used.
questions.explain: Verse 84 pairs वमने with आस्थापनेषु in the same way.
questions.rule: Use 1 + च + use 2 + योज्यानि = used in both.
questions.teaches: Two locative uses joined by च with योज्यानि mean 'to be used in both'.

questions.q: The second line says ten remain. Remain after what?
options: After the eight of verses 83-84 and the one for the nose
optionExplain: The mūlinīs are a different group, finished in verse 80.
The snehas begin only in verse 86.
The salts come in verses 88-89.
questions.explain: The ten are the remainder of the nineteen phalinīs.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the verse's two statements.
questions.rule: नस्तः = through the nose; विधीयते = is prescribed; दश = ten; अवशिष्टानि = remaining.

questions.q: The ten remaining phalinīs are stated for the procedure called ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse ends: तान्युक्तानि विरेचने.
questions.teaches: विरेचने = in purgation: the use of the ten that remain.
questions.rule: The ten remain for विरेचन (purgation).

questions.q: Which is the right split of यान्यवशिष्टानि?
optionExplain: Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: यानि + अवशिष्टानि is written यान्यवशिष्टानि.
वशिष्टानि is not a word.
यवशिष्टानि is not a word.
That would give यान्ववशिष्टानि, with व्.
questions.explain: यानि is neuter plural: 'those which'.
questions.rule: यानि + अवशिष्टानि = यान्यवशिष्टानि.

questions.q: Which statements follow from verses 83-85?
options: प्रत्यक्पुष्पा is prescribed for the nose.
The ten that remain are stated for purgation.
मदन is among the ten left for purgation.
प्रत्यक्पुष्पा is among the eight of verse 84.
The eight of 83-84 are used in emesis and āsthāpana.
optionExplain: Right: नस्तः प्रच्छर्दने प्रत्यक्पुष्पा विधीयते.
Right: दश यान्यवशिष्टानि तान्युक्तानि विरेचने.
Wrong: मदन is among the eight of verse 84.
Wrong: it is not named there; it is the one for the nose.
Right: एतानि वमने चैव योज्यान्यास्थापनेषु च.
questions.explain: The nineteen divide into 8 (emesis, āsthāpana), 1 (nose) and 10 (purgation).

questions.q: A text lists 24 roots: 9 go to bath, one (bhṛṅga) to the nose, the rest to drinking. How many are for drinking?
optionExplain: That forgets the one for the nose.
Right: The remainder after both groups assigned.
Ten is the size of the two assigned groups together, not the remainder.
That subtracts only the one for the nose and forgets the bath roots.
questions.explain: As in verse 85, subtract each assigned group, including the single one.
questions.rule: Remaining = total − all assigned groups, even a group of one.
questions.teaches: A group of one counts like any other group when you work out how many remain.

questions.q: Verse 86 begins 'नामकर्मभिरुक्तानि फलानि'. Which number do you expect it to give for the fruits?
optionExplain: Sixteen is the number of mūlinīs.
Eight is only the group used in emesis and āsthāpana.
Right: The phalinīs counted across verses 81-83 come to nineteen.
Ten is only the group left for purgation.
questions.explain: The verse says एकोनविंशतिः: nineteen.
questions.rule: All nineteen fruits are closed off in the first line.

questions.q: Match each sneha to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four snehas of the verse.
questions.rule: सर्पिः = ghee; तैलम् = oil; वसा = fat; मज्जा = marrow.

questions.q: In चतुर्विधः, the first part चतुर् means ____ (type the number).
questions.explain: चतुर् = four, विध = fold or kind.
questions.teaches: स्नेहो दिष्टश्चतुर्विधः: sneha is indicated as fourfold, and four are named.
questions.rule: चतुर्विध = fourfold.

questions.q: Why is it written सर्पिस्तैलम् and not सर्पिःतैलम्?
options: A visarga becomes र् before any consonant
A visarga becomes श् before every letter
A visarga before त is written स्
optionExplain: Before a voiceless consonant like त it becomes स्, not र्.
श् appears before च/छ, as in दिष्टश्चतुर्विधः, not before त.
It is the regular sandhi.
Right: सर्पिः + तैलम् becomes सर्पिस्तैलम्.
questions.explain: सर्पिः is the word 'ghee'; तैलम् follows it.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स्त.

questions.q: Which are among the four snehas named in verse 86?
optionExplain: Right: ghee.
Wrong: milk is not named here.
Right: fat.
Wrong: honey is not named here.
Right: marrow.
questions.explain: सर्पिः, तैलम्, वसा, मज्जा are the four.
questions.rule: Four snehas: ghee, oil, fat, marrow.

questions.q: A new text counts एकोनत्रिंशत् herbs. If त्रिंशत् is thirty, how many herbs are meant?
optionExplain: Right: एकोन- means 'one less than', as in एकोनविंशति = nineteen.
That would be one more than thirty.
एकोन- takes one away.
That would be a different number word.
questions.explain: एकोनविंशति = twenty minus one = nineteen; एकोनत्रिंशत् = thirty minus one.
questions.rule: एकोन + N = N − 1.
questions.teaches: The prefix एकोन- gives 'one less than' the number that follows.

questions.q: Verse 86 named the four snehas. What do you expect verse 87 to tell about them?
options: How they are used and what they do
optionExplain: Nothing in these verses speaks of prices.
Right: The verse gives uses and effects.
The sages belong to the early part of the chapter.
The verse speaks of uses, not of source plants.
questions.explain: Verse 87 gives four uses and four effects.
questions.rule: After naming the snehas, the text gives their uses and effects.

questions.q: Match each use to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four uses.
questions.rule: पान = drinking; अभ्यञ्जन = inunction; बस्ति = enema; नस्य = nasal administration.

questions.q: बलोपचयवर्धनाः is built from बल + ____ + वर्धनाः (type the middle word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: बल + उपचय = बलोपचय.
questions.teaches: अ + उ → ओ: बल + उपचय is written बलोपचय; the whole word means 'increasing strength and bulk'.
questions.rule: बल + उपचय → बलोपचय.

questions.q: Which is the right split of बलोपचय?
optionExplain: बलोप is not a word.
ओपचय is not a word.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, so बल + उपचय is written बलोपचय.
ओ would not simply join an उ here.
questions.explain: बलोपचय = बल (strength) + उपचय (bulk, growth).
questions.rule: बल + उपचय = बलोपचय.

questions.q: Which effects does verse 87 itself name?
optionExplain: Right: named in line 2.
Wrong: that is said in verse 88.
Right: named in line 2.
Wrong: that is said of the salts in verse 89.
Right: named in line 2.
questions.explain: Verse 87 gives स्नेहनाः, जीवनाः, वर्ण्याः and बल–उपचय बढ़ाने वाले.
questions.rule: 87: oleating, vitalizing, complexion, strength and bulk.

questions.q: A new line says स्नानपानार्थम्, built like पानाभ्यञ्जनबस्त्यर्थम्. With स्नान meaning bath and पान meaning drinking, what does it say?
optionExplain: -अर्थम् means 'for', not 'from'.
The two items are added together.
There is no 'without' in the word.
Right: Items + -अर्थम् means 'for the purpose of ... '.
questions.explain: The compound lists uses and ends in -अर्थम्, as in verse 87.
questions.rule: Items + -अर्थम् = for the purpose of those items.
questions.teaches: A list of nouns joined into one word and ended with -अर्थम् states what something is used for.

questions.q: The word वातपित्तकफापहाः ends in अपहाः, 'removers'. What do the snehas of this verse remove?
optionExplain: Right: The three doṣas named in the compound.
The compound names all three.
The salts are a separate topic that begins on line 2.
The sages are not in this verse.
questions.explain: वात-पित्त-कफ-अपहाः = removers of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha.
questions.rule: अपहाः = removers; the three doṣas are the object.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari salt to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading the salt names in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: सौवर्चलम् = Sauvarcala; सैन्धवम् = Saindhava; विडम् = Viḍa; औद्भिदम् = Audbhida.

questions.q: स्नेहा ह्येते is a joined form of स्नेहाः + हि + ____ (type the last word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: हि + एते = ह्येते.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: हि + एते is written ह्येते. एते means 'these'.
questions.rule: हि + एते → ह्येते.

questions.q: Why does स्नेहाः lose its visarga in स्नेहा ह्येते?
options: A visarga after आ drops before a voiced sound such as ह
optionExplain: ओ comes after अ, not after आ.
Right: स्नेहाः + हि becomes स्नेहा हि.
र् appears after इ/उ (e.g. सर्पिः + वसा → सर्पिर्वसा), not after आ; after आ the visarga drops.
The loss is regular sandhi.
questions.explain: स्नेहाः is nominative plural: 'the snehas'.
questions.rule: -आः + voiced sound → -आ.

questions.q: Which are named as salts in verse 88?
optionExplain: Right: first word of line 2.
Wrong: sea salt comes in verse 89.
Right: it is in line 2.
Wrong: marrow is a sneha, from verse 86.
Right: it ends line 2.
questions.explain: Verse 88 names four salts; the fifth, sea salt, is in 89.
questions.rule: 88: सौवर्चल, सैन्धव, विड, औद्भिद.

questions.q: A new line joins हि and आगताः. How is it written, by the rule of ह्येते?
optionExplain: The vowels must join; य् replaces the इ.
The इ does not simply drop.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्.
Inside a sentence the two vowels are joined.
questions.explain: ह्येते shows हि + एते → ह्य + एते; the same happens before आ.
questions.rule: हि + vowel → ह्य + vowel.
questions.teaches: The rule that turns इ into य् before a different vowel works for हि with any following vowel.

questions.q: Verse 88 named four salts, and verse 89 begins 'सामुद्रेण सह'. What does 'together with sea salt' do to the group?
options: Adds sea salt as a fifth salt
optionExplain: सह means 'together with', which adds.
Sea salt is called a salt, लवणम्, not a sneha.
The verse joins, not splits.
Right: The verse says the group, with sea salt, is five.
questions.explain: सह + instrumental = 'together with'; so 4 + 1 = 5.
questions.rule: सामुद्रेण सह = together with sea salt.

questions.q: Match each quality to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four qualities of the salts.
questions.rule: स्निग्ध = unctuous; उष्ण = hot; तीक्ष्ण = sharp; दीपनीयतम = most stimulating to digestion.

questions.q: सहैतानि is a joined form: सह + ____ (type the second word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: सह + एतानि = सहैतानि.
questions.teaches: अ + ए → ऐ: सह + एतानि is written सहैतानि.
questions.rule: सह + एतानि → सहैतानि.

questions.q: In सामुद्रेण सह, what does the ending of सामुद्रेण show?
optionExplain: Right: सह takes the instrumental.
The genitive would be सामुद्रस्य.
The locative would be सामुद्रे.
The nominative would be सामुद्रम्.
questions.explain: -एण ending + सह = 'with'.
questions.rule: सह + instrumental = together with.

questions.q: Which qualities does verse 89 give to the salts?
optionExplain: Right: unctuous.
Wrong: the verse says उष्णानि, hot, not cold.
Right: sharp.
Right: hot.
Wrong: that is said of the snehas in verse 88.
questions.explain: The salts are unctuous, hot, sharp and the most stimulating to digestion.
questions.rule: 89: स्निग्ध, उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, दीपनीयतम.

questions.q: A new line says आम्रेण (आम्र = mango) सहैतानि पञ्च फलानि, after four fruits were named. How many fruits are there, and which is the fifth?
options: Four; the mango is only a comment
Five; the mango is the fifth
Six; the mango is counted twice
Five; the mango is among the four
optionExplain: पञ्च says five.
Right: आम्रेण सह adds the mango to the four, as in verse 89.
The total is stated as five.
सह adds a new item to the group.
questions.explain: Verse 89 does the same: four salts + सामुद्रेण सह = five.
questions.rule: X-instrumental + सह + the group = the group plus X.
questions.teaches: सह with an instrumental adds a new item to a named group, and the stated total includes it.

questions.q: Verses 88-89 named the salts. What do you expect verse 90 to begin?
options: The names of five more salts
A list of the procedures in which the salts are used
optionExplain: Verse 89 already closed the set at five.
The urines are announced only at the end of verse 92.
Right: The verse says the salts are used for pastes and in several procedures.
The sages were listed in verses 8-13.
questions.explain: Verse 90 starts the uses of the salts, introduced by आलेपनार्थे … युज्यन्ते.
questions.rule: Verse 90 begins the uses of the salts.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words name four of the uses in the verse.
questions.rule: आलेपनार्थे = for pastes; स्नेहस्वेदविधौ = in oleation and sudation procedures; निरूहेषु = in decoction enemas; अनुवासने = in oil enema.

questions.q: The word meaning 'likewise' in the first line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: तथा links the oleation and sudation procedures to the pastes just named.
questions.teaches: तथा is an indeclinable meaning 'likewise, and so'; it adds one more item to the list of uses.
questions.rule: तथा = likewise.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निरूहेष्वनुवासने?
optionExplain: निरूहेष्व is not a word.
ष्वनुवासने is not a word.
वनुवासने is not a word; the व् comes from the join.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, so निरूहेषु + अनुवासने is written निरूहेष्वनुवासने.
questions.explain: निरूहेष्वनुवासने = निरूहेषु ('in decoction enemas') + अनुवासने ('in oil enema').
questions.rule: निरूहेष्वनुवासने = निरूहेषु + अनुवासने.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 90 as uses of the salts?
optionExplain: Right: the verse begins with आलेपनार्थे.
Right: अनुवासने closes the verse.
Right: निरूहेषु is in the second line.
Not in this verse; it is not named here.
Not in this verse; it is not named here.
questions.explain: Verse 90 names pastes, oleation and sudation, the two evacuations, decoction enemas and oil enema; surgery and collyrium are not in it.
questions.rule: Check each item against the words of the verse.

questions.q: Invented line: क्षारो दन्तधावनार्थे युज्यते (क्षार = ash; दन्तधावन = tooth-cleaning). What does it say?
options: The ash is used for the purpose of cleaning teeth
The ash is used after cleaning teeth
The teeth are cleaned to make ash
The ash is not to be used for cleaning teeth
optionExplain: Right: -अर्थे after a noun means 'for the purpose of', as in आलेपनार्थे; युज्यते is 'is used'.
-अर्थे gives the purpose, not a later time.
The ash is what is used; the cleaning is its purpose.
युज्यते says it is used; there is no negative.
questions.explain: X-अर्थे युज्यते = 'is used for the purpose of X', the pattern of verse 90.
questions.rule: X-अर्थे = for the purpose of X.
questions.teaches: A noun + -अर्थे names the purpose; you can read the purpose of any invented use from it.

questions.q: Verse 91 goes on listing uses of the salts. Which of these is named in it?
optionExplain: निरूह was named in verse 90, not here.
Right: शस्त्रकर्मणि is in the second line.
अनुवासन was named in verse 90, not here.
The urines are not a use of the salts; they come after verse 92.
questions.explain: Verse 91 adds surgery, among other uses; decoction and oil enemas were in verse 90.
questions.rule: Verse 91 adds new uses to the list begun in verse 90.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give four of the uses in the verse.
questions.rule: अभ्यञ्जने = in inunction; भोजनार्थे = for use in food; शस्त्रकर्मणि = in surgery; वर्त्यर्थम् = for suppositories.

questions.q: The word for 'of the head' in the first line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: शिरसः is the genitive of शिरस्, joined to च as शिरसश्च.
questions.teaches: -अः on शिरस् is the genitive singular: 'of the head'. Together with the evacuation word it gives 'evacuation of the head'.
questions.rule: शिरसः = of the head.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वर्त्यर्थम्?
optionExplain: वर्त्य is not the word; the wick is वर्ति.
यर्थम् is not a word; the य् comes from the join.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so वर्ति + अर्थम् is written वर्त्यर्थम्.
इ is not a word of its own here.
questions.explain: वर्त्यर्थम् = वर्ति ('suppository, wick') + अर्थम् ('for the purpose of').
questions.rule: वर्त्यर्थम् = वर्ति + अर्थम्.

questions.q: The printed text reads शिरसश्च चिरेचने, but चिरेचने is not a word. What does the sense require?
options: चिरेचने as printed, a correct word
optionExplain: The note marks चिरेचने as not a word.
Food was already named just before as भोजनार्थे.
Nothing in the verse or the note suggests it.
Right: The note reads विरेचने, and शिरसः 'of the head' fits it.
questions.explain: Printed चिरेचने is a slip for विरेचने; the line then reads 'and in evacuation of the head'.
questions.rule: Where a printed word is not a word, read the form the sense and the note require.

questions.q: Invented phrase: गुरुश्च शिष्यः. By the pattern of शिरसश्च, which gives गुरुश्च before sandhi?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as in शिरसः + च → शिरसश्च.
श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the join.
श् does not stand as a word-ending on its own here.
The second word is च, 'and'.
questions.explain: The same visarga + च → श्च rule gave भार्गवश्च्यवनः in verse 10.
questions.rule: Visarga + च → श्च.
questions.teaches: You can undo a श्च join: the first word ended in a visarga, the second is च.

questions.q: Verse 92 closes the talk on salts. What do you expect it to announce next?
optionExplain: The salts are said to have been described.
Right: The second line says 'learn from me the eight urines'.
These came earlier, not after the salts.
The sages were named at the start of the chapter.
questions.explain: मूत्राण्यष्टौ निबोध मे = 'learn from me the eight urines'.
questions.rule: After the salts come the eight urines.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words name conditions in which the salts are used.
questions.rule: अजीर्ण = indigestion; आनाह = distension; गुल्मे = in gulma; शूले = in colic.

questions.q: The verse says 'learn' with the word ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: निबोध is a command: 'learn, listen'.
questions.teaches: निबोध is the second person singular imperative of नि-√बुध्: the speaker tells the hearer to learn. The doer 'you' is not written.
questions.rule: निबोध = learn (a command to one hearer).

questions.q: Which is the right split of तथोदरे?
optionExplain: दरे is not a word here.
The word is तथा, with a long आ.
Right: आ + उ joins as ओ, so तथा + उदरे is written तथोदरे.
ओदरे is not a word; the ओ comes from the join.
questions.explain: तथोदरे = तथा ('and also') + उदरे ('in udara').
questions.rule: तथोदरे = तथा + उदरे.

questions.q: Which of these conditions are named in verse 92?
optionExplain: Right: गुल्मे is in the first line.
Right: शूले is in the first line.
Right: उदरे ends the first line.
Not in this verse; it is not named here.
Not in this verse; it is not named here.
questions.explain: The first line names indigestion, distension, Vāta disorders, gulma, colic and udara.
questions.rule: Check each condition against the first line.

questions.q: By the pattern of मूत्राणि + अष्टौ → मूत्राण्यष्टौ, how is अग्नि + अत्र joined?
optionExplain: That would drop the इ without a य्; the pattern keeps य्.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + अ.
Within a line the two words are joined, as in मूत्राण्यष्टौ.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so अग्नि + अत्र gives अग्न्यत्र.
questions.explain: The rule that turned भूतेषु + अनुक्रोशम् into भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम् works the same for इ: इ + vowel → य् + vowel.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.teaches: Once you know इ → य् before a vowel, you can join or split any such pair.

questions.q: Verse 93 begins naming the eight urines. Which animal's urine is named in it?
optionExplain: Right: अजामूत्रम् is in the second line.
The elephant comes in verse 94.
The camel comes in verse 94.
The donkey comes in verse 94.
questions.explain: Verse 93 names the sheep, goat, cow and buffalo; the camel, elephant, horse and donkey come after.
questions.rule: Verse 93 names four of the eight urines.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four animals of this verse.
questions.rule: अविमूत्रम् = sheep's urine; अजामूत्रम् = goat's urine; गोमूत्रम् = cow's urine; माहिषम् = of the buffalo.

questions.q: The word meaning 'principal' in the first line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: मुख्यानि is the first word of the verse.
questions.teaches: -आनि marks a neuter plural: मुख्यानि goes with the urines (neuter, plural), the things that are 'principal'.
questions.rule: मुख्यानि = principal (neuter plural).

questions.q: Which is the right split of सर्वाण्यात्रेयशासने?
optionExplain: सर्वाण्य is not a word.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so सर्वाणि + आत्रेयशासने is written सर्वाण्यात्रेयशासने.
यात्रेयशासने is not a word; the य् comes from the join.
The word is सर्वाणि, the neuter plural of 'all'.
questions.explain: सर्वाण्यात्रेयशासने = सर्वाणि ('all') + आत्रेयशासने ('in Ātreya's teaching').
questions.rule: सर्वाण्यात्रेयशासने = सर्वाणि + आत्रेयशासने.

questions.q: What does आत्रेयशासने tell you about where the list of principal urines comes from?
options: It is taught in Indra's teaching
It is a king's order to the physicians
It is the list taught in Ātreya's teaching
It is a list the speaker made up himself
optionExplain: Indra is not named in this verse.
Nothing in the verse speaks of a king.
Right: आत्रेय-शासने = 'in Ātreya's teaching'; the list rests on it.
The verse says they are taught in Ātreya's teaching.
questions.explain: आत्रेयशासने is a locative: 'in the teaching of Ātreya'.
questions.rule: आत्रेयशासने = in Ātreya's teaching.

questions.q: Invented: भरद्वाजशासने. By the pattern of आत्रेयशासने, what does it mean?
optionExplain: -ने (locative) says 'in', not 'from'.
The name is the teacher, not the one taught.
The two are joined as one compound, not listed as a pair.
Right: A name + शासने = 'in the teaching of' that person.
questions.explain: The compound name + शासने follows the same pattern.
questions.rule: X-शासने = in X's teaching.
questions.teaches: A teacher's name + शासने = 'in the teaching of that teacher'; the same pattern works with any name.

questions.q: Verse 93 named sheep, goat, cow and buffalo. Which animal's urine is named in verse 94?
optionExplain: Right: उष्ट्रस्य, 'of the camel', is in the first line.
The sheep was named in verse 93.
The goat was named in verse 93.
The buffalo was named in verse 93.
questions.explain: Verse 94 names the elephant, camel, horse and donkey.
questions.rule: Verse 94 names the other four of the eight urines.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four animals of this verse.
questions.rule: हस्ति = elephant; उष्ट्र = camel; हय = horse; खर = donkey.

questions.q: The word meaning 'pungent' in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: कटुकम् is one of the properties of the urines.
questions.teaches: The properties in line 2 end in -म्: neuter singular, agreeing with मूत्रम् understood. One word of the list, कटुकम्, is 'pungent'.
questions.rule: कटुकम् = pungent.

questions.q: Which gives the words of हस्तिमूत्रमथोष्ट्रस्य before sandhi?
optionExplain: मथो and ष्ट्रस्य are not words.
Right: म् joins the following अ, and अ + उ joins as ओ, so the three words give हस्तिमूत्रमथोष्ट्रस्य.
The second word is अथ; the ओ comes from the join with उ.
The camel is उष्ट्र, with a short उ, not औ.
questions.explain: हस्तिमूत्रमथोष्ट्रस्य = हस्तिमूत्रम् ('elephant's urine') + अथ ('and') + उष्ट्रस्य ('of the camel').
questions.rule: हस्तिमूत्रमथोष्ट्रस्य = हस्तिमूत्रम् + अथ + उष्ट्रस्य.

questions.q: Which of these properties does the second line state for the urines?
optionExplain: Right: उष्णम् opens the line.
Right: तीक्ष्णम् is in the line.
Right: कटुकम् is in the line.
Right: लवणान्वितम् ends the line.
Not in the line; it is the opposite of उष्ण.
questions.explain: The line gives hot, sharp, pungent and salty (and 'not dry' on the edition's reading).
questions.rule: Check each property against the second line.

questions.q: Invented: a teacher lists four oils, then adds उष्णं तीक्ष्णम्, neuter singular, with 'oil' understood. By the pattern of verse 94, what does he mean?
options: Only the last oil is hot and sharp
Only the first oil is hot and sharp
Every oil listed is hot and sharp
The properties belong to none of the oils
optionExplain: In verse 94 the properties are not limited to the last animal.
They are not limited to the first item either.
Right: In verse 94 the properties agree with an understood singular noun and apply to every urine listed.
Properties after a list describe the items listed.
questions.explain: In verse 94 the neuter singular properties agree with an understood noun and describe all items of the list.
questions.rule: Properties after a list, with the noun understood = shared by all.
questions.teaches: Properties agreeing with an understood noun, placed after a list, describe every item of the list.

questions.q: Which of these is named in verse 95 as a use of urine?
optionExplain: Surgery is not named in this verse.
Collyrium is not named in this verse.
Food is not named in this verse.
Right: आलेपनेषु is in the first line.
questions.explain: Verse 95 names unction, pastes, decoction enema and purgation.
questions.rule: Verse 95 lists the uses of urine.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words name the four uses of the verse.
questions.rule: उत्सादने = in unction; आलेपनेषु = in pastes; आस्थापने = in decoction enema; विरेचने = in purgation.

questions.q: The word meaning 'suitable' is repeated in the verse: ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: युक्तम् comes with each of the four uses.
questions.teaches: युक्तम् is a past participle of √युज्, neuter singular, agreeing with मूत्रम्: 'urine (is) suitable'.
questions.rule: युक्तम् = suitable.

questions.q: Which is the right split of युक्तमास्थापने?
optionExplain: Right: म् joins the following आ, so युक्तम् + आस्थापने is written युक्तमास्थापने.
मास्थापने is not a word.
स्थापने alone is not the word here.
The word is आस्थापने, with a long आ.
questions.explain: युक्तमास्थापने = युक्तम् ('suitable') + आस्थापने ('in decoction enema').
questions.rule: युक्तमास्थापने = युक्तम् + आस्थापने.

questions.q: In verse 95, which word names the thing that is 'suitable'?
optionExplain: It is a locative: the place of use, not the thing used.
Right: मूत्रम् is the subject; युक्तम् describes it.
It is a locative: the place of use, not the thing used.
It is a locative: the place of use, not the thing used.
questions.explain: मूत्रम् is the subject; the four locatives say where it is suitable.
questions.rule: Subject = मूत्रम्; locatives = uses.

questions.q: Invented line: घृतं पाने युक्तं युक्तं च सेचने (घृत = ghee; पान = drinking; सेचन = sprinkling). What does it say?
options: Drinking and sprinkling are suitable for making ghee
Ghee is suitable for drinking but not for sprinkling
Ghee is suitable for drinking and for sprinkling
Ghee is drunk and sprinkled by the same person
optionExplain: Ghee is the thing that is suitable.
च joins a second युक्तम्; nothing says 'not'.
Right: As in verse 95: the thing is named, then युक्तम् with each locative use.
The line speaks of suitability, not of a person.
questions.explain: The pattern of verse 95 carries to any thing and its uses.
questions.rule: Thing + युक्तम् + locative = suitable for that use.
questions.teaches: A repeated युक्तम् with locatives lists the uses of the one thing named.

questions.q: Which disease is named in verse 96?
optionExplain: Pāṇḍu comes in verse 98.
Fever is not named in this verse.
Prameha is not named in this verse.
Right: कुष्ठ is part of the last compound of the verse.
questions.explain: Verse 96 ends with the patients of gulma, kuṣṭha and kilāsa.
questions.rule: Verse 96 names kuṣṭha among its conditions.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words name four of the uses in the verse.
questions.rule: स्वेदेषु = in sudation; आनाहेषु = in distensions; अगदेषु = in antidotes; अर्शःसु = in piles.

questions.q: The word for 'it' (the urine) in the first line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: तद् joins युक्तम् as तद्युक्तम्.
questions.teaches: तद् / तत् is the neuter 'it', 'that'. Here it points back to the urine of the last verse; तत् + युक्तम् is written तद्युक्तम्.
questions.rule: तत् = it, that.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वेदेष्वपि?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, so स्वेदेषु + अपि is written स्वेदेष्वपि.
पि is not a word.
ष्वपि is not a word.
वपि is not a word; the व् comes from the join.
questions.explain: स्वेदेष्वपि = स्वेदेषु ('in sudation') + अपि ('also').
questions.rule: स्वेदेष्वपि = स्वेदेषु + अपि.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 96 as conditions or uses for the urine?
optionExplain: Right: आनाहेषु is in the first line.
Right: उदरेषु begins the second line.
Right: अर्शःसु is in the second line.
Not in this verse; it is not named here.
Not in this verse; it is not named here.
questions.explain: Verse 96 names sudation, distension, antidotes, abdominal diseases, piles, and gulma, kuṣṭha and kilāsa patients.
questions.rule: Check each item against the words of the verse.

questions.q: If कास means 'cough', what does कासिषु mean, by the pattern of गुल्मिकुष्ठिकिलासिषु?
options: Among those who suffer from cough
optionExplain: A disease alone would be कासेषु; -इ names the person.
Right: -इन् names the one who has the thing, and -षु gives 'among, in'.
-अर्थे would give the purpose; this ending does not.
'From' would need an ablative ending.
questions.explain: In गुल्मि- the person is meant ('one with gulma'); the same ending on कास gives 'one with cough'.
questions.rule: X-इन् = one who has X; plural locative = among such persons.
questions.teaches: An -इन् noun names the one who has the thing, so a locative plural reads 'among those who have it'.

questions.q: Which of these is said of the urine in verse 97?
optionExplain: The verse says the opposite.
Verse 94 called urines hot; nothing here changes that.
Right: क्रिमिघ्नम् means 'destroying worms'.
विषघ्नम् says it destroys poison.
questions.explain: Verse 97 declares the urine stimulating to digestion, poison-destroying and worm-destroying.
questions.rule: Verse 97 gives three properties: dīpanīya, viṣaghna, krimighna.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the last uses and two of the properties.
questions.rule: उपनाहेषु = in poultices; परिषेके = in affusion; विषघ्नम् = destroying poison; क्रिमिघ्नम् = destroying worms.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'is declared' in the verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: उपदिश्यते is the last word of the verse (with च before it).
questions.teaches: उपदिश्यते is a passive: 'is declared, is taught'. The doer is not named.
questions.rule: उपदिश्यते = is declared.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चोपदिश्यते?
optionExplain: पदिश्यते is not the verb here.
The verb begins with उ, not अ.
The first word is च, with a short अ.
Right: अ + उ joins as ओ, so च + उपदिश्यते is written चोपदिश्यते.
questions.explain: चोपदिश्यते = च ('and') + उपदिश्यते ('is declared').
questions.rule: चोपदिश्यते = च + उपदिश्यते.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 97?
optionExplain: Right: उपनाहेषु is in the first line.
Right: परिषेके is in the first line.
Right: दीपनीयम् opens the second line.
Not in this verse.
Not in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse names poultices, affusion and the three properties; surgery and oil enema are not in it.
questions.rule: Check each item against the words of the verse.

questions.q: Invented: शूलघ्नम्, with शूल = colic. By the pattern of विषघ्नम्, what does it mean?
