options: Outside the śāstra, not following its rules
optionExplain: बाह्य means 'outside', not 'inside'.
Right: X-बाह्य means 'outside X' or 'devoid of X'.
बाह्य gives no sense of teaching.
बाह्य does not name a person.
questions.explain: X-बाह्य = outside X, devoid of X.
questions.rule: X-बाह्य = devoid of X.
questions.teaches: बाह्य at the end of a compound means 'outside or without', as in युक्तिबाह्य; use it to read new words.

questions.q: In this verse, which is the worse for the patient?
options: Indra's thunderbolt falling on the head
A medicine prescribed by a physician who knows yukti
A medicine prescribed by an ignorant person
optionExplain: The verse says it might leave something remaining.
No such medicine is spoken of here.
Right: It is said not to leave the patient with anything remaining.
No chance poison is mentioned in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse says the thunderbolt might leave something, but an ignorant person's medicine would leave nothing.
questions.rule: अज्ञमतम् औषधम् is worse than वासवाशनिः.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words set the thunderbolt against the ignorant person's medicine.
questions.rule: वासवाशनिः = Indra's thunderbolt; मूर्ध्नि = on the head; आतुरम् = the patient; अज्ञमतम् = prescribed by an ignorant one.

questions.q: वासवाशनिः means the thunderbolt of वासव, that is, of ____ (type the god's name in Devanagari).
questions.explain: वासव is a name of Indra.
questions.teaches: वासव-अशनिः joins two words: 'of Vāsava' and 'thunderbolt'. Vāsava is Indra, the god Bharadvāja approached in verse 3.
questions.rule: वासव = Indra; वासवाशनिः = Indra's thunderbolt.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कुर्यान्नत्वज्ञमतमौषधम्?
optionExplain: That would lose the negative अ and make him 'knowing'.
न्नत्व is not a word.
त्वज्ञमतम् is not a word; तु and अज्ञ… are separate words.
Right: त् + न joins as न्न, and तु + अ gives त्व (तु + अज्ञ → त्वज्ञ).
questions.explain: कुर्यान्नत्वज्ञमतमौषधम् = कुर्यात् ('would make') + न ('not') + तु ('but') + अज्ञमतम् + औषधम्.
questions.rule: कुर्यान्नत्वज्ञमतमौषधम् = कुर्यात् + न + तु + अज्ञमतम् + औषधम्.

questions.q: Which statements agree with the verse?
options: A thunderbolt on the head might leave one with something remaining
A medicine prescribed by an ignorant person would leave the patient with nothing remaining
A thunderbolt on the head never leaves anything remaining
An ignorant person's medicine is milder than a thunderbolt
optionExplain: Right: सशेषं वासवाशनिः.
Right: सशेषमातुरं कुर्यान्न ….
The verse says it might.
The verse says the opposite.
questions.explain: The verse puts the thunderbolt, which might spare something, against the ignorant person's medicine, which would not.
questions.rule: वज्र: possibly सशेष; अज्ञ की औषध: not सशेष.

questions.q: By the pattern of सशेषम् (with a remainder), what does सफलः (as in सफलो वृक्षः) mean?
optionExplain: Right: स- at the start of such a word means 'with': स + फल = with fruit.
सशेषम् is 'with a remainder', not 'without'.
स- gives 'with', not 'only'.
The pattern gives 'having', not a profession.
questions.explain: स- + noun = 'having, with that noun'.
questions.rule: सX = with X.
questions.teaches: स- joined to a noun means 'with it'; you can read words like सफल the same way.

questions.q: Verse 129 describes a giver of medicine with 'यः'. How does the sentence end in this verse?
options: It ends by praising the giver
It does not end here; the main statement about him comes in the next verse
It ends by saying what the medicine cures
It ends by naming the patient
optionExplain: No praise appears; the sentence is unfinished.
Right: The यः clause waits for its तस्य in verse 130.
No cure is mentioned; the clause only describes the giver and the patient.
The patient is described, not named.
questions.explain: This is a relative clause (यः …) whose main statement is in verse 130.
questions.rule: यः … प्रयच्छति is completed in verse 130.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four describe the patient.
questions.rule: दुःखिताय = to the suffering; शयानाय = to the bedridden; श्रद्दधानाय = to the trusting; रोगिणे = to the sick person.

questions.q: The word meaning 'without knowing' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: अविज्ञाय means 'without knowing (having not known)'.
questions.teaches: It ends in -य, like वीक्ष्य in verse 123: the 'having done' ending after a prefix (वि). Here it is negated with अ-, an irregular but usual form in this text.
questions.rule: अविज्ञाय = without knowing.

questions.q: What does the compound प्राज्ञमानी mean?
optionExplain: -मानी means 'thinking himself', not 'being'.
The compound has no sense of being honoured.
Right: प्राज्ञ ('wise') + -मानी ('thinking himself') describes the giver.
The compound has no sense of teaching.
questions.explain: प्राज्ञमानी = प्राज्ञ + मानी: one who considers himself wise (and so need not be).
questions.rule: प्राज्ञमानी = thinking himself wise.

questions.q: Which describe the patient in this verse?
optionExplain: Right: दुःखिताय.
Right: शयानाय.
Right: श्रद्दधानाय.
Wealth is not mentioned.
This describes the giver, not the patient.
questions.explain: The patient is suffering, bedridden and trusting; 'thinking himself wise' describes the giver.
questions.rule: Patient: दुःखित, शयान, श्रद्दधान; giver: प्राज्ञमानी.

questions.q: A verse begins यो ऽविद्वान् चिकित्सति … and stops. Following verse 129, what should you expect?
options: A new topic unrelated to the clause
A following verse that finishes the sentence (for example with तस्य, 'of him')
optionExplain: A यः clause alone has no main statement.
The clause is completed, not dropped.
The clause shows only that the sentence goes on.
Right: A यः clause waits for its main statement, as in verses 129 and 130.
questions.explain: A relative clause (यः …) is finished by a main clause, which may come in the next verse.
questions.rule: यः … → तस्य … completes the sentence.
questions.teaches: When a verse has a यः clause with no main statement, look to the next verse for the answer (तस्य …).

questions.q: In verse 129, यः introduces the man who gives medicine without knowing it. Which word of verse 130 picks that 'he' up again?
optionExplain: Right: तस्य means 'of him' and refers back to the giver.
नरः is the man who talks with him, a different person.
स्यात् is a verb ('would be'), not a person.
अपि means 'even'; it names no one.
questions.explain: तस्य picks up यः: the whole of 129-130 is one sentence.
questions.rule: यः in 129 is answered by तस्य in 130.

questions.q: Match each description of the giver to its meaning.
questions.explain: All four describe the same person, the ignorant giver of medicine.
questions.rule: त्यक्तधर्म = abandoned dharma; पाप = sinful; मृत्युभूत = death itself; दुर्मति = evil-minded.

questions.q: संभाषणादपि = संभाषणात् + ____ (type the word meaning 'even' in Devanagari).
questions.explain: अपि means 'even': even from talking with him.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: संभाषणात् + अपि is written संभाषणादपि.
questions.rule: संभाषणादपि = संभाषणात् + अपि, 'even from conversing'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्यात्तस्य?
optionExplain: त्तस्य is not a word.
Right: The verb स्यात् ('would be') is followed by तस्य ('of him'); त् + त् simply stand together.
Neither piece is a word here.
That would be written स्यादस्य, with द्.
questions.explain: स्यात्तस्य = स्यात् + तस्य.
questions.rule: स्यात्तस्य = स्यात् + तस्य.

questions.q: Which of these describe the bad physician of verses 129-130?
optionExplain: Right: 'sinful' describes him.
This is the man who talks with him, not the physician.
Right: 'evil-minded' describes him.
This is the act of talking, not a description of him.
Right: 'who is death itself' describes him.
questions.explain: The words in the 'of him' form describe the giver; नरः and संभाषणात् belong to the man who talks.
questions.rule: The -स्य / -तेः words describe the giver.

questions.q: A new line reads क्रूरस्य लुब्धस्य तस्य सेवनादपि नरो दुःखी स्यात्. Whom do क्रूरस्य and लुब्धस्य describe?
optionExplain: नरः has a different ending; it is the man who suffers.
सेवनात् names an act, not a person.
Right: They end like तस्य ('of him') and describe the same person.
दुःखी is the result, said of the man.
questions.explain: Describing words stand in the same form as the person they describe: -स्य ... -स्य ... तस्य.
questions.rule: Words in the same ending as तस्य describe him.
questions.teaches: You can find whom a string of describing words refers to by matching its ending to the person-word (तस्य) that closes it.

questions.q: The verse opens with the word वरम्. What does it announce?
options: A question put to the sages
A comparison: the following things are called better
optionExplain: वरम् is not a verb of command.
Nothing here is a question.
The items named are harsh things, not medicines.
Right: वरम् means 'better': what follows is preferred to something.
questions.explain: वरम् sets up a comparison: A is better (than B).
questions.rule: वरम् = better; a comparison follows.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the harsh things named in the verse.
questions.rule: आशीविषविषम् = snake's venom; ताम्रम् = copper; अयोगुडाः = iron balls; क्वथितम् = boiled, molten.

questions.q: The word for 'drunk' that goes with the venom and the copper is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: पीतम् is 'drunk'.
questions.teaches: पीतम् is a past participle in the neuter singular, so it goes with the neuter singular nouns (the venom and the copper).
questions.rule: पीतम् = drunk; it agrees with the venom and the copper.

questions.q: भक्षिता वा in the second line has a long -आ ending, though the iron balls are plural. What explains it?
options: The visarga of -आः drops before the voiced sound भ् / व्
The word is a singular feminine noun
The poet left the ending out by mistake
optionExplain: Right: -आः + a voiced consonant gives -आ: सन्तप्ताः भक्षिताः → सन्तप्ता भक्षिता.
The data reads it as masculine plural, agreeing with अयोगुडाः.
The dual of such a word would end in -औ.
This is regular sandhi, not a mistake.
questions.explain: सन्तप्ताः and भक्षिताः lose their visarga before a voiced sound, leaving -आ.
questions.rule: -आः before a voiced consonant → -आ.

questions.q: Put the three things in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The venom comes first, the copper next, the iron balls last.
questions.rule: Venom, then copper, then iron balls.

questions.q: A speaker begins a new line with वरं मौनम् (invented) and then pauses. What do you expect next?
options: Something that silence is preferred to
optionExplain: Nothing in वरम् points to a prayer.
Right: वरम् starts a comparison, so the thing that is worse still has to be named.
वरम् starts a comparison, not a list of medicines.
वरम् opens a sentence, it does not close one.
questions.explain: As in 131 → 132, वरम् leaves the 'worse' side to be supplied.
questions.rule: वरम् A ... : the worse alternative follows.
questions.teaches: When a sentence opens with वरम्, look ahead for the alternative it is being preferred to.

questions.q: Verse 131 said what is better. The word न तु at the start of 132 does what?
options: It repeats that the venom is better
It starts a new, unrelated topic
It rules out the opposite: taking food, drink or money this way is not better
It asks the patient a question
optionExplain: न तु turns to something else.
The two verses form one sentence.
Right: न तु = 'but not': the second half of the comparison.
Nothing here is a question.
questions.explain: न तु completes the comparison: A is better, but not B.
questions.rule: वरम् ... न तु = better ..., but not ....

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The three things taken, and the one they are taken from.
questions.rule: अन्नम् = food; पानम् = drink; वित्तम् = money; रोगपीडितात् = from one afflicted by disease.

questions.q: नतु = न + ____ (type the second word, meaning 'but', in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The source writes नतु as one token; it is न + तु.
questions.teaches: नतु is न ('not') + तु ('but'), the pair that finishes the comparison begun by वरम्.
questions.rule: नतु = न + तु = 'but not'.

questions.q: Which word names the person who takes the food, drink or money?
optionExplain: This is the person it was taken from (the refugee).
This is also the patient it was taken from.
This means 'of the learned': the people whose garb is copied.
Right: It is the 'by' form; the wearer of the learned man's garb is the one who took.
questions.explain: बिभ्रता (by the wearer) is the taker; the two -आत् words are the patient.
questions.rule: बिभ्रता is a 'by' form of बिभ्रत्; the -आत् words are 'from' forms.

questions.q: Which three things does the verse say are taken from the patient?
optionExplain: Right: food.
Medicine is not among the things named in this verse.
Right: drink.
Right: money.
The garb is worn by the taker, not taken from the patient.
questions.explain: Food, drink and money are taken; the garb is worn.
questions.rule: अन्नम्, पानम्, वित्तम् are what is taken.

questions.q: In a new line धनुर्बिभ्रता वीरेण शत्रुर्जितः (invented), who carries the bow?
optionExplain: Right: बिभ्रता (carrying) and वीरेण (by the hero) are both 'by' forms, so बिभ्रता describes वीरेण, as it names the taker in 132.
The enemy was defeated; he is not the carrier.
The bow is what is carried.
वीरेण names him.
questions.explain: बिभ्रता agrees with the 'by' word: whoever it describes does the carrying.
questions.rule: बिभ्रता + 'by' person = the one who carries.
questions.teaches: A describing word in the 'by' case (here बिभ्रता) agrees with the 'by' person and names the doer, as in 132.

questions.q: According to verse 133, in what should an aspiring physician make the utmost effort?
optionExplain: Verse 132 condemned taking money from the pretender's patients; no such aim is given.
Right: स्वगुणसम्पदि = in the accomplishment of his own qualities.
Nothing in the verse speaks of rivals.
No patron or king is mentioned.
questions.explain: The effort is directed at his own qualities.
questions.rule: Effort goes into स्वगुणसम्पद्, one's own qualities.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words that carry the verse.
questions.rule: भिषक् = physician; बुभूषुः = wishing to be; मतिमान् = intelligent; प्राणदः = giver of life.

questions.q: The verse says he should make the utmost ____ (type the Devanagari word for 'effort', with or without the ending).
questions.explain: प्रयत्नम् means 'effort'.
questions.teaches: प्रयत्नम् is the object of आतिष्ठेत् ('should undertake'), qualified by परम् ('utmost').
questions.rule: परं प्रयत्नम् = utmost effort.

questions.q: Which word of the verse gives the purpose 'so that'?
optionExplain: अतः means 'therefore': it points back to the reason, not forward to the purpose.
परम् means 'utmost' and qualifies the effort.
Right: यथा with स्यात् ('may be') means 'so that he may be'.
सम्पदि means 'in the perfecting'; it names the field in which the effort is made.
questions.explain: अतः gives the reason from before; यथा gives the aim that follows.
questions.rule: अतः = therefore (reason); यथा = so that (purpose).

questions.q: A student who wishes to be a physician puts all his effort into earning, none into his own qualities. Which advice of 133 does he ignore?
options: Waiting until others approve of him
Making the utmost effort at the perfection of his own qualities
optionExplain: That is not what this verse says.
Nothing like this is said here.
No approval is mentioned in this verse.
Right: That is the effort the verse asks for.
questions.explain: He ignores the verse's main advice: effort at his own qualities.
questions.rule: The aim is one's own qualities, not income.

questions.q: A new word जिजीविषुः is built like बुभूषुः. What does it most likely mean?
options: One who is afraid of life
optionExplain: Right: The wish-form ending -षु (after a doubled syllable) means 'wishing to', so जिजीविषुः = wishing to live.
Past action would not use this wish-ending.
That is the sense of प्राणदः, a different word.
Nothing in the form suggests fear.
questions.explain: बुभूषुः = wishing to be; जिजीविषुः = wishing to live.
questions.rule: Doubled syllable + -षु = 'wishing to ...'.
questions.teaches: You can read a new wish-word by comparing it with बुभूषुः.

questions.q: According to verse 134, what makes a medicine proper (युक्त)?
options: That a famous physician gives it
optionExplain: Cost is never mentioned.
Right: यदारोग्याय कल्पते = which is capable of bringing about health.
Fame plays no part in the test.
The test is its effect on health, not its taste.
questions.explain: The test is whether it conduces to health.
questions.rule: Proper medicine = the one that conduces to health.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The words of the first line.
questions.rule: तत् = that; युक्तम् = proper; आरोग्याय = for health; कल्पते = conduces.

questions.q: सः भिषजां ____, meaning he is the best of physicians (type the Devanagari word for 'best', with or without the ending).
questions.explain: श्रेष्ठः means 'the best'.
questions.teaches: श्रेष्ठः is nominative singular, agreeing with सः; the visarga becomes ओ before the voiced र् of रोगेभ्यः (श्रेष्ठो रोगेभ्यः).
questions.rule: श्रेष्ठो = श्रेष्ठः (best).

questions.q: Verse 132 mentioned someone who wears the garb of the learned. By the test in 134, which marks the best physician?
options: Wearing the garb of the learned
Taking food, drink and money from patients
optionExplain: 134 never names the garb as a test.
132 rejects this.
Right: The test of 134 is the result for the patient.
The verse's test is freeing from disease.
questions.explain: The verse's test is freeing people from disease, not the garb.
questions.rule: Best physician = he who frees from disease (the garb is not the test).

questions.q: Which statements follow from verse 134?
options: A medicine that does not conduce to health is not 'proper' by this test
The best physician is the one who frees people from diseases
A medicine is proper if it is expensive
The verse says the physician frees people by diet alone
optionExplain: Right: only the one that conduces to health is called proper.
Right: this is the verse's own statement.
Cost is not a test in the verse.
The verse does not say how.
questions.explain: Both tests are about results: health for the medicine, freedom from disease for the physician.
questions.rule: Proper medicine → health; best physician → freedom from disease.

questions.q: A new line reads तदेव शस्त्रं यद्रणे जयाय कल्पते (invented). By the same rule, what makes a weapon proper?
options: That it is made of gold
That it is lighter than others
That it conduces to victory in battle
optionExplain: The rule is about serving the end, not material.
Ownership is not the test.
Weight is not mentioned.
Right: यत् … तत् with कल्पते + 'for ...' says: that which serves the end is the proper one.
questions.explain: 'तदेव X यत् Y-आय कल्पते' = that alone is the proper X which serves Y.
questions.rule: तदेव ... यत् ... कल्पते = that alone is proper which serves the end.
questions.teaches: The pattern तदेव X यत् ...-आय कल्पते lets you read any 'that alone is proper which serves such-and-such' line.

questions.q: In verse 135, what proclaims (आख्याति) the correct application of all procedures?
optionExplain: Right: सिद्धिः is the subject of आख्याति in both lines.
Trust appears in verse 129, not as the proclaimer here.
Wealth is not mentioned in 135.
Fame is not mentioned in 135.
questions.explain: सिद्धिः is the subject: success proclaims.
questions.rule: सिद्धिः आख्याति = success proclaims.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four key words.
questions.rule: सिद्धिः = success; आख्याति = proclaims; कर्मणाम् = of procedures; भिषक्तमम् = the best physician.

questions.q: भिषक्तमम् = भिषक् + ____: type the ending that means 'most' (it makes 'best') in Devanagari.
questions.explain: -तम is the ending of the superlative: भिषक् + तमम् = the best physician.
questions.teaches: -तम added to a word means 'the most ...': भिषक्तम = the most physician-like, the best physician.
questions.rule: भिषक् + तम = best physician.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सिद्धिराख्याति?
optionExplain: राख्याति is not a word.
Right: A visarga before a vowel becomes र्, so सिद्धिः + आख्याति is written सिद्धिराख्याति.
The verb is आख्याति, with आ.
That would give सिद्ध्याख्याति.
questions.explain: सिद्धिराख्याति = सिद्धिः + आख्याति.
questions.rule: सिद्धिः + आख्याति → सिद्धिराख्याति.

questions.q: A physician's procedures, done correctly, lead to success again and again. By verse 135, what does that success do?
options: It makes his procedures correct afterwards
It proves he took money from patients
It proclaims the correct application of his procedures
It shows that no medicine was needed
optionExplain: Success proclaims; it does not cause the correctness.
135 says nothing about money.
Right: सिद्धिः आख्याति सम्यक्प्रयोगम्.
Nothing like this is said.
questions.explain: Success shows that the application was correct.
questions.rule: सिद्धि shows सम्यक्प्रयोग.

questions.q: A new line reads समृद्धिर्गृहस्थस्य यत्नमाख्याति (invented). By the same sense of आख्याति, what does the prosperity do?
optionExplain: आख्याति means to proclaim, not to hide.
The effect proclaims the cause, not the reverse.
Nothing about ending is said.
Right: आख्याति = proclaims, shows: the result speaks for what lies behind it.
questions.explain: A result can 'proclaim' its cause, as success proclaims correct practice.
questions.rule: result + आख्याति + cause = the result shows the cause.
questions.teaches: You can read a result-word as a witness to its cause whenever आख्याति joins them.

questions.q: Verse 136 has no verb, only a string of nouns. What kind of passage is it?
options: A list of topics whose closing statement comes later
An order given to the student
optionExplain: Right: Nouns without a verb are items of a list; the closing statement is in verse 140.
No person or event is narrated.
There is no verb of command.
No god is addressed.
questions.explain: A run of nouns with no verb is a list; look ahead for what completes it.
questions.rule: A verbless run of nouns = list of topics.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the five topics.
questions.rule: आगमः = coming; प्रवर्तनम् = propagation; अभ्यनुज्ञानम् = approval; निर्णयः = definition.

questions.q: आयुर्वेदागमः = आयुर्वेद + ____ (type the second word, 'coming', in Devanagari).
questions.explain: आगमः is the second member.
questions.teaches: आयुर्वेद + आगमः: अ + आ → आ, giving आयुर्वेदागमः (and the visarga becomes ओ before the voiced ह of हेतुः).
questions.rule: आयुर्वेदागमः = आयुर्वेद + आगमः.

questions.q: आगमस्य can carry two senses. Which two?
optionExplain: Departure is not a sense of आगम.
Right: आगम means both: 'coming' and the teaching that came down.
आगम does not mean the student.
Those are हेतु and कार्य, different words.
questions.explain: आगम = what has come: both the arrival and the teaching received.
questions.rule: आगम = arrival / received teaching.

questions.q: Put the five topics in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Coming, cause, propagation, approval of composition, definition.
questions.rule: आगम → हेतु → प्रवर्तन → अभ्यनुज्ञान → निर्णय.

questions.q: A teacher announces: विषयाः शब्दः, अर्थः, प्रयोगः, निर्णयः (invented). What is this line?
options: A complete command to the class
A list of topics (nouns with no verb)
optionExplain: There is no verb, so there is no command.
The items are separate words.
Right: Nouns in a row without a verb are a list, as in 136.
Nothing here is a question.
questions.explain: As in 136 → 140, read a verbless row of nouns as a list and look for a summing-up line, if any.
questions.rule: Verbless nouns in a row = a list.
questions.teaches: When you meet a row of naming-form nouns with no verb, treat it as a list of topics and look ahead for a sentence that sums it up, if there is one.

questions.q: Which item of verse 137 names the purpose of Āyurveda?
optionExplain: दोषाः are the doṣas.
भेषजम् is medicine.
हेतवः are causes (of disease).
Right: प्रयोजनम् means 'purpose'; the compound is 'purpose of Āyurveda'.
questions.explain: आयुर्वेदप्रयोजनम् = the purpose of Āyurveda.
questions.rule: प्रयोजनम् = purpose.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the items of the list.
questions.rule: कारणम् = cause; कार्यम् = effect; दोषाः = doṣas; भेषजम् = medicine.

questions.q: In हेतवश्चैव the small emphatic word after च is ____ (type it in Devanagari; it means indeed, alone).
questions.explain: हेतवश्चैव = हेतवः + च + एव.
questions.teaches: च + एव joins into चैव (अ + ए → ऐ), and the visarga of हेतवः becomes श् before च.
questions.rule: हेतवश्चैव = हेतवः + च + एव.

questions.q: 136 had हेतुः and 137 has हेतवः. How do they differ?
options: हेतुः is singular 'the cause'; हेतवः is plural 'causes'
हेतुः is plural; हेतवः is singular
हेतुः is dual; हेतवः is singular
optionExplain: Right: Both are the naming form of the same noun; only the number differs.
It is the other way round.
Neither is dual.
They are one noun in two numbers.
questions.explain: हेतुः (136) is the one cause; हेतवः (137) are causes.
questions.rule: -उः singular / -अवः plural for words like हेतु.

questions.q: Which are named in the second line of verse 137?
optionExplain: Right: the causes.
रसाः belongs to the next verse.
Right: the doṣas.
कारणम् is in the first line.
Right: medicine.
questions.explain: Line 2: हेतवः, दोषाः, भेषजम् and then संग्रहेण (in brief).
questions.rule: Line 2 names causes, doṣas, medicine.

questions.q: A new line joins two words with च: पुत्रः + च. How is it written as one word?
optionExplain: The visarga does not simply vanish before च.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as in हेतवः + च → हेतवश्च.
ओ appears before voiced sounds, not before च.
स् appears before त्, not before च.
questions.explain: Visarga + च → श्च, the same rule as हेतवश्च and दोषाश्च.
questions.rule: visarga + च → श्च.
questions.teaches: You can join any word ending in a visarga with च by changing the visarga to श्.

questions.q: Which of these is named in verse 138?
optionExplain: क्षीराणि comes in the next verse.
मूत्रम् comes in the next verse.
Right: मूलिन्यः is in the second line.
That comes at the very end, in verse 140.
questions.explain: 138 names tastes, classes of substances, root-plants, fruit-plants, fats and salts.
questions.rule: 138 includes मूलिन्यः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the topics named.
questions.rule: रसाः = tastes; मूलिन्यः = root-plants; फलिन्यः = fruit-plants; स्नेहाः = fats.

questions.q: The verse speaks of a ____-fold classification of substances, त्रिविधः (type the number).
questions.explain: त्रि- means three.
questions.teaches: त्रिविधः = three kinds; the verse says the classification is threefold but does not list the three here.
questions.rule: त्रिविध = threefold.

questions.q: In सप्रत्ययद्रव्याः, what does the opening स- add?
options: 'Together with': the tastes with their underlying substances
optionExplain: स- does not mean 'without'.
The count 'six' would be षष्-.
'Not' would be अ-.
Right: स- here means 'with', giving 'with their underlying substances'.
questions.explain: सप्रत्ययद्रव्याः = tastes together with their underlying substances.
questions.rule: स- = with.

questions.q: Put the four plant and substance classes in the order of the second line.
questions.explain: Root-plants, fruit-plants, fats, salts.
questions.rule: मूलिनी → फलिनी → स्नेह → लवण.

questions.q: In a new line, सपत्रा लता (invented) is used of a creeper. How do you read सपत्रा?
options: With leaves, as in the form 'स- = with'
optionExplain: Right: सपत्रा = स + पत्रा, built like सप्रत्यय-: it means 'having leaves'.
That would need अ- or निः-.
स- is not the number six.
Nothing suggests salt.
questions.explain: स- + noun = 'having / together with' that noun.
questions.rule: स + X = together with X.
questions.teaches: The opening स- turns a noun into 'together with it', so you can read new words like सपत्र.

questions.q: By which useful parts does verse 139 describe the six trees?
optionExplain: Those belong to the plants of verse 138 (मूलिनी, फलिनी).
Right: क्षीरत्वगाश्रयाः = those whose seat of use is latex and bark.
Leaves and flowers are not mentioned.
Wood and seed are not mentioned.
questions.explain: The six trees are defined by latex and bark.
questions.rule: षड् वृक्षाः = क्षीर + त्वक् as आश्रय.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the topics of the verse.
questions.rule: मूत्रम् = urine; क्षीराणि = milks; वृक्षाः = trees; कर्माणि = actions.

questions.q: In क्षीरत्वगाश्रयाः the word for 'bark' is ____ (type its base form in Devanagari).
questions.explain: त्वक् / त्वच् means bark (skin).
questions.teaches: क्षीर-त्वक्-आश्रयाः: the क् becomes ग् before the vowel आ, giving त्वगाश्रयाः.
questions.rule: त्वक् = bark.

questions.q: In the pair योग / अयोग, what does अयोग stand for?
optionExplain: That is योग itself.
Neither word names a medicine.
Right: अ- reverses योग, 'proper application', giving 'improper application'.
सिद्धि is the word for success (verse 135).
questions.explain: योग = proper use; अयोग = improper use.
questions.rule: अयोग = the reverse of योग.

questions.q: Which are named in verse 139?
optionExplain: Salts are in verse 138.
Right: urine.
Fats are in verse 138.
Right: the milks.
Right: the six trees.
questions.explain: Urine, milks and the six trees are in 139; salts and fats are in 138.
questions.rule: 139: मूत्र, क्षीर, वृक्ष; 138: स्नेह, लवण.

questions.q: Following the pair गुण / अगुण, what does a new word अलवण most likely mean?
optionExplain: अ- does not mean 'full of'.
अ- turns the sense to its opposite.
Nothing in the word suggests fruit.
Right: अ- reverses or negates, so अलवण = without salt.
questions.explain: अ- + word = the opposite or lack of it.
questions.rule: अ + X = not X.
questions.teaches: The negative अ- before a consonant lets you read a new word like अलवण from the word it reverses.

questions.q: How does verse 140 end the list that began in verse 136?
options: It says that all this has been fully explained in the earlier ('first') chapter
It adds a new list of diseases
It asks the sages to explain more
It names the writer of the chapter
optionExplain: Right: सर्वमेतत् समाख्यातं पूर्वाध्याये = all this has been fully explained in the earlier ('first') chapter.
It closes the list; it adds none.
Nothing is asked.
The sage is called only महर्षिणा, 'by the great sage', not named.
questions.explain: The closing sentence sums the list up: सर्वमेतत् समाख्यातम्.
questions.rule: 140 closes the list with a summary sentence.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The key words of the closing verse.
questions.rule: वैद्यापवादः = censure of physicians; गुणाः = qualities; समाख्यातम् = fully explained; महर्षिणा = by the great sage.

questions.q: वैद्यापवादः = वैद्य + ____ (type the second word, meaning 'censure', in Devanagari).
questions.explain: अपवादः is 'censure'.
questions.teaches: वैद्य + अपवादः: अ + अ → आ, giving वैद्यापवादः; the visarga becomes ओ before the voiced य of यत्रस्थाः.
questions.rule: वैद्यापवादः = वैद्य + अपवादः.

questions.q: What does the verse itself say about the 'great sage'?
options: He is called only the great sage; no personal name is given here
optionExplain: Indra is not mentioned in 140.
Right: The verse says महर्षिणा and nothing more.
Bharadvāja is not mentioned in 140.
महर्षिणा is singular.
questions.explain: The sage is unnamed in this verse.
questions.rule: महर्षिणा = by the great sage (unnamed).

questions.q: समाख्यातम् is a past participle. What does it tell you about the topics of the list?
options: They are being asked about now
optionExplain: That would need a future form.
Nothing here is a question.
Right: A past participle states a finished action: 'has been explained'.
Nothing here forbids it.
questions.explain: समाख्यातम् = has been fully explained: the topics are already covered.
questions.rule: Past participle = a finished action.

questions.q: A new text lists topics and closes सर्वमेतद् उक्तं द्वितीयेऽध्याये (invented). What does the ending tell you?
options: They will be treated in a later chapter
The listed topics were treated in the second chapter
optionExplain: उक्तम् is a past participle: already said.
Nothing in the ending says so.
The list has just named them.
Right: As in 140, the closing line points back to where the listed topics were dealt with.
questions.explain: A closing 'all this has been said in chapter X' sends you back to that chapter.
questions.rule: सर्वमेतत् ... उक्तम्/समाख्यातम् + chapter = the summary points back.
questions.teaches: When a list ends with 'all this was said in chapter X', treat it as a table of contents pointing back.

questions.q: The sentence अथातो ऽपामार्गतण्डुलीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः opens Chapter 2. What does it announce?
options: A chapter called Apāmārgataṇḍulīya will now be expounded
A list of gruels and their cures
A story of sages meeting on a mountain
optionExplain: Right: अध्यायं and व्याख्यास्यामः show a chapter is named and promised.
No gruel or cure is named in this sentence.
No sages or mountain appear here; the sentence only introduces a chapter.
No god is addressed.
questions.explain: अध्यायम् (chapter) and व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall expound) show that a chapter is being introduced.
questions.rule: The opening sentence names the chapter and promises to explain it.

questions.q: Match each word of the opening sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole announcement.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; अध्यायम् = chapter; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall expound.

questions.q: The word for 'we shall expound' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The sentence ends with व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.teaches: व्याख्यास्यामः is first person plural, future: वि + आ + √ख्या with the ending -मः, 'we'.
questions.rule: -मः on a verb = 'we'; the future sense gives 'we shall'.

questions.q: The text prints अतो ऽपामार्ग…. What happens to अतः before the next word?
options: The visarga is dropped and the vowel stays अ
The visarga becomes ओ before a voiced sound; the following अ is shown by ऽ
The visarga becomes श् before the next word
Nothing changes; ओ and ऽ are misprints
optionExplain: The visarga does not drop after short अ; it turns into ओ here.
Right: अः + अ gives ओ, and the sign ऽ marks the अ that follows.
श् appears before च or छ, not before अ.
It is a regular sandhi change, not a misprint.
questions.explain: अतः + अपामार्ग… is printed अतो ऽपामार्ग…: the visarga turns to ओ, and ऽ marks the dropped-looking अ.
questions.rule: अः + voiced sound → ओ; ऽ marks the following अ.

questions.q: The title अपामार्गतण्डुलीय ends in -ईय. According to the card, what does this ending do?
options: It makes the verb first person plural
It makes an adjective, 'relating to' the two names before it
It turns the title into a god's name
optionExplain: That is the job of -मः in व्याख्यास्यामः.
The title is singular, matching अध्यायम्.
Right: The word breakdown reads it as: relating to अपामार्ग and तण्डुल (title).
Nothing in the data says that.
questions.explain: The title is a descriptive adjective: relating to अपामार्ग and तण्डुल; it agrees with अध्यायम्.
questions.rule: -ईय makes an adjective 'relating to'.

questions.q: A made-up chapter title is अभ्यङ्गीयम्. Which is the correct joined form of अतः before it?
optionExplain: अथ + अतः gives आ, but a visarga before अ does not give आ.
The visarga does not stay before a vowel here.
The result of अः + अ is ओ, not उ.
Right: अः + अ gives ओ with ऽ, as in अतो ऽपामार्गतण्डुलीयम्.
questions.explain: Same rule as in the opening sentence: अतः + अ… → अतो ऽ….
questions.rule: अतः + अ-initial title → अतो ऽ-….
questions.teaches: Any title beginning with अ after अतः is printed with ओ and ऽ.

questions.q: In इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः, who is named as the speaker?
options: The author of the chapter, speaking of himself
optionExplain: Right: भगवान् आत्रेयः is the subject of आह.
Bharadvāja is not named in this sentence.
No student is named.
The sentence names Ātreya, not a speaker in the first person.
questions.explain: आह (said) has भगवान् आत्रेयः as its subject.
questions.rule: The speaker is भगवान् आत्रेयः.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole sentence.
questions.rule: इति = thus; ह = indeed; आह = said; भगवान् = the venerable.

questions.q: The speaker's name in the sentence is ____ (type it in Devanagari, with ending as printed).
questions.explain: The last word is आत्रेयः, 'Ātreya'.
questions.teaches: आत्रेयः is nominative singular: the one who speaks. भगवान् 'the venerable' goes with it.
questions.rule: आत्रेयः = Ātreya, the speaker.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्माह?
optionExplain: स्मा is not a word; the particle is स्म.
Right: अ + आ gives आ, so स्म + आह is written स्माह.
The particle is स्म, not सम्.
स्मा is not a word; the particle is स्म.
questions.explain: स्म (a particle marking the past) + आह (said) → स्माह.
questions.rule: स्माह = स्म + आह.

questions.q: आह is a third person singular perfect of √अह्. What does that tell us?
options: One person spoke, in the past: 'he said'
optionExplain: A plural would need a plural ending; आह is singular.
That would be first person future, as in व्याख्यास्यामः.
Right: The singular third person names one speaker; the perfect is a past form.
आह is not a command form.
questions.explain: The data labels आह '3 sg. pf.': one speaker, past.
questions.rule: आह = he said (3rd singular, perfect).

questions.q: A made-up line needs अथ + आह joined. Which is the correct form?
optionExplain: The two vowels must be joined by sandhi.
अ + आ does not give ओ.
अ + आ does not give ए.
Right: अ + आ gives आ, as in स्म + आह → स्माह.
questions.explain: The rule that gave स्माह also gives अथाह.
questions.rule: अ/आ + आ → आ.
questions.teaches: Any word ending in अ followed by आह is joined with a long आ.

questions.q: Verse 3 names seeds, peppers, mustard and more. Which statement about it is true?
options: No verb: the verb दद्यात् comes in verse 5
The treatment these drugs are for
optionExplain: Right: Verses 3 to 5 are one sentence; verse 3 gives only the items.
दद्यात् is in verse 5, not here.
The treatment is named in verse 5.
No quantity is given anywhere in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse is a list of accusative-type items; the governing verb is in verse 5.
questions.rule: Verse 3 = list only; the verb comes later.

questions.q: Match each drug name in verse 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four names are glossed in the data.
questions.rule: पिप्पली = long pepper; मरिच = black pepper; सर्षप = mustard; शिग्रु = drumstick tree.

questions.q: पिप्पलीः + मरिचानि is printed पिप्पली____मरिचानि. Type the missing letter with its virāma, in Devanagari.
questions.explain: The printed word is पिप्पलीर्मरिचानि.
questions.teaches: After ई the visarga turns into र् before a voiced sound such as म.
questions.rule: Visarga after ई/उ + voiced sound → र्.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विडङ्गान्यथ?
optionExplain: The verse has विडङ्गानि (plural) before अथ; the split must end in the particle अथ.
Right: इ becomes य् before a vowel, so विडङ्गानि + अथ → विडङ्गान्यथ.
न्यथ is not a word.
थ alone is not a word; the particle is अथ.
questions.explain: विडङ्गानि (neuter plural) + अथ (and/now) → विडङ्गान्यथ.
questions.rule: Final इ + vowel → य् + vowel.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 3 name?
optionExplain: Right: मरिचानि.
Right: सर्षपान्.
Right: पिप्पलीः.
Cumin is named in verse 4.
Garlic is named in verse 5.
questions.explain: Verse 3 names seven items; cumin and garlic belong to the following verses.
questions.rule: Verse 3: अपामार्ग seeds, पिप्पली, मरिच, विडङ्ग, शिग्रु, सर्षप, तुम्बुरु.

questions.q: A made-up line has हरीतकीः + गृह्णीयात्. Which is the correct joined form?
optionExplain: The visarga drops after आ, not after ई.
A visarga cannot stay before a voiced ग in this join.
Right: After ई the visarga turns to र् before a voiced sound like ग.
श् appears before च or छ, not before ग.
questions.explain: Same rule as पिप्पलीः + मरिचानि → पिप्पलीर्मरिचानि.
questions.rule: Visarga after ई + voiced sound → र्.
questions.teaches: Any plural in -ईः followed by a voiced sound takes र् in place of the visarga.

questions.q: Verse 4 lists cumin, cardamom and other drugs. Which verse supplies its verb?
optionExplain: Verse 4 has only names, no verb.
Verse 3 is also a list without a verb.
Verse 6 gives conditions, after the verb has come.
Right: Verses 3 to 5 form one sentence; the verb comes at its end.
questions.explain: The sentence of verses 3 to 5 ends with दद्यात् in verse 5.
questions.rule: Verse 4 is part of the list; the verb is in verse 5.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 4 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are glossed in the data.
questions.rule: अजाजी = cumin; एला = cardamom; सुरसा = a basil; पीलूनि = pīlu fruits.

questions.q: चाजगन्धां splits into च + ____. Type the plant's name in Devanagari.
questions.explain: चाजगन्धां = च + अजगन्धां.
questions.teaches: अ + अ gives आ: the च joins the following अजगन्धां into one written word.
questions.rule: च + अजगन्धाम् → चाजगन्धाम्.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पीलून्येलां?
optionExplain: Right: इ becomes य् before the vowel, so पीलूनि + एलाम् → पीलून्येलाम्.
That would leave an extra य्; the plural form is पीलूनि.
There is no word इएलाम्.
लाम् is not a word here.
questions.explain: पीलूनि (neuter plural) + एलाम् (cardamom) → पीलून्येलाम्.
questions.rule: Final इ + vowel → य् + vowel.

questions.q: Which statements about verse 4 are right?
options: It names drugs but has no verb
The edition footnote gives another reading for अजगन्धां
कुठेरकफणिज्झकौ names a pair of plants
It says what the drugs are used for
optionExplain: Right: the verb comes in verse 5.
Right: अजमोदां.
Right: a dvandva in the dual.
No use is named until verse 5.
questions.explain: The verse is list and footnote only; the use comes in verse 5.
questions.rule: Verse 4 = more names, one variant, no verb, no use.

questions.q: A made-up phrase has च + अश्वगन्धाम्. Which is the correct joined form?
optionExplain: The two अ must be joined by sandhi.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, as in च + अजगन्धाम् → चाजगन्धाम्.
अ + अ does not give ओ.
अ + अ does not give ऐ.
questions.explain: The rule that gave चाजगन्धाम् gives चाश्वगन्धाम्.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: च before a word beginning with अ is joined into चा-.

questions.q: Verse 5 ends दद्याच्छीर्षविरेचने. For which treatment does it say to give these drugs?
optionExplain: Emesis is named in verse 8, for another list of drugs.
Purgation comes with the drugs of verses 9 and 10.
Right: शीर्षविरेचने is the locative: 'in head-purging'.
No bath is mentioned.
questions.explain: The verb दद्यात् with शीर्षविरेचने says: give these in head-purging.
questions.rule: Verses 3-5: drugs for head-purging.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 5 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are glossed in the data.
questions.rule: लशुन = garlic; नागर = dry ginger; हरिद्रे = the two haridrās; लवणद्वयम् = the pair of salts.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'one should give' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: दद्यात् is in the second line of verse 5.
questions.teaches: दद्यात् is third person singular optative of √दा: 'one should give'. It governs the lists of verses 3 to 5.
questions.rule: दद्यात् = one should give.

questions.q: Which is the right split of दद्याच्छीर्षविरेचने?
optionExplain: छीर्ष is not a word.
च्छीर्ष is not a word.
The word is शीर्ष, with श.
Right: त् + श becomes च्छ, so दद्यात् + शीर्ष… is printed दद्याच्छीर्ष….
questions.explain: दद्यात् + शीर्षविरेचने → दद्याच्छीर्षविरेचने.
questions.rule: त् + श → च्छ.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 5 itself name?
optionExplain: Right: लशुनम्.
Right: नागरम्.
Right: लवणद्वयम्.
Mustard is in verse 3.
Cumin is in verse 4.
questions.explain: The last list is in verse 5; mustard and cumin came earlier in the same sentence.
questions.rule: Verse 5: शिरीष seed, garlic, two haridrās, pair of salts, ज्योतिष्मती, dry ginger.

questions.q: A made-up line reads लशुनं सर्षपांश्च दद्याच्छीर्षविरेचने. What does it say?
options: Give garlic and mustard in head-purging
Garlic and mustard are given in emesis
Garlic and mustard were given yesterday
Garlic and mustard must never be given
optionExplain: Right: The list is the objects of दद्यात्; the locative names the treatment.
शीर्षविरेचने names head-purging, not emesis.
दद्यात् is 'should give', not a past tense.
Nothing forbids; दद्यात् advises giving.
questions.explain: The frame is: drugs + दद्यात् + the treatment in the locative.
questions.rule: Drug list + दद्यात् + treatment (locative) = 'give these in that treatment'.
questions.teaches: Read any such line by its frame: the list is what to give, the locative at the end is the treatment.

questions.q: Verse 6 is a list of conditions, nearly all in the 'in …' ending. What is it the list of?
options: More drugs to be added to the list
The conditions for the head-purging drugs of verse 5
The doses of the drugs of verse 5
optionExplain: These are disease names, not drugs.
Right: The data notes: it continues verse 5 and names the conditions for those drugs.
No quantity is given.
The verse names conditions, not conduct.
questions.explain: Locatives ('in …') list the conditions in which the drugs of verse 5 are used.
questions.rule: Verse 6 = conditions for the head-purging drugs of verse 5.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 6 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are glossed in the data.
questions.rule: शूले = in pain; अपस्मारे = in epilepsy; घ्राणनाशे = in loss of smell; क्रिमिव्याधौ = in worm disease.

questions.q: The word for 'in epilepsy' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The second line has क्रिमिव्याधावपस्मारे: worm disease and epilepsy run together.
questions.teaches: अपस्मारे is locative singular: 'in epilepsy'. The -ए ending is the locative of a word in -अ.
questions.rule: अपस्मारे = in epilepsy (locative).

questions.q: Which is the right split of क्रिमिव्याधावपस्मारे?
optionExplain: वपस्मारे is not a word.
क्रिमिव्याधाव is not a word.
Right: औ + vowel becomes आव् + vowel, so क्रिमिव्याधौ + अपस्मारे → क्रिमिव्याधावपस्मारे.
Before a vowel, -उ would give -व् (क्रिमिव्याध्वपस्मारे), not -आव्; the locative of क्रिमिव्याधि is -औ.
questions.explain: क्रिमिव्याधौ (in worm disease) + अपस्मारे (in epilepsy) → क्रिमिव्याधावपस्मारे.
questions.rule: औ + vowel → आव् + vowel.

questions.q: Which of these conditions does verse 6 name?
optionExplain: Right: घ्राणनाशे.
Right: अपस्मारे.
Right: अर्धावभेदके.
Fever is not named in the verse.
Hearing is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The verse names eight conditions; fever and loss of hearing are not among them.
questions.rule: Verse 6: heaviness, pain, पीनस, half-headache, worm disease, epilepsy, loss of smell, प्रमोहक.

questions.q: A made-up phrase needs व्याधौ + अस्मिन् joined. Which is the correct form?
optionExplain: The औ must change before the vowel.
औ + vowel gives आव्, not just आ.
औ + vowel does not give ए.
Right: औ + vowel becomes आव् + vowel, as in क्रिमिव्याधावपस्मारे.
questions.explain: The rule is the same as in क्रिमिव्याधावपस्मारे.
questions.rule: औ + vowel → आव् + vowel.
questions.teaches: A locative in -औ before a vowel is written -आव्; look for it when splitting.

questions.q: Verse 7 lists madana, neem, cardamom and more. Where does the sentence get its verb?
options: There is no verb in the whole sentence
optionExplain: Right: Verse 8 completes the sentence: one should administer.
Verse 7 only lists names.
That verb belongs to the earlier list for head-purging.
प्रयुञ्जीत in verse 8 is the verb.
questions.explain: The data notes: the sentence is completed in verse 8.
questions.rule: Verse 7 = list; verb in verse 8.

questions.q: Put these four names in the order they are printed in verse 7.
questions.explain: These are the first four names of the first line.
questions.rule: मदनं → मधुकं → निम्बं → जीमूतं.

questions.q: The word for 'neem' in verse 7 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: निम्बं is the third name of the verse.
questions.teaches: निम्बम् ends in -म्, an accusative singular, one item in the list.
questions.rule: निम्ब = neem.

questions.q: In पिप्पलीकुटजेक्ष्वाकूणि, which join gives the -जे- before क्ष्वा?
optionExplain: अ + इ does not give ई.
Right: अ + इ gives ए, so कुटज + इ… is written कुटजे….
ऐ comes from अ + ए or अ + ऐ.
ओ comes from अ + उ.
questions.explain: कुटज + इक्ष्वाकूणि → कुटजेक्ष्वाकूणि.
questions.rule: अ + इ → ए.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 7 name?
optionExplain: Right: निम्बम्.
Right: एलाम्.
Right: inside the compound पिप्पलीकुटजेक्ष्वाकूणि.
Garlic is in verse 5.
Trivṛt is in verse 9.
questions.explain: The verse names ten items; garlic and trivṛt belong to other verses.
questions.rule: Verse 7: मदन, मधुक, neem, जीमूत, कृतवेधन, पिप्पली, कुटज, इक्ष्वाकु, cardamom, धामार्गव.

questions.q: A made-up phrase needs नव + इदम् joined. Which is the correct form?
optionExplain: अ + इ does not give ई.
अ + इ does not give ऐ.
Right: अ + इ gives ए, as in कुटज + इ… → कुटजे….
The two vowels must join.
questions.explain: The rule that made कुटजेक्ष्वाकूणि also gives नवेदम्.
questions.rule: अ + इ → ए.
questions.teaches: A word ending in अ before इ-/ई- is joined with ए.

questions.q: Verse 8 says वमनार्थं प्रयुञ्जीत. For which treatment are the drugs of verse 7 used?
optionExplain: Head-purging is the treatment of verse 5.
Purgation is named later, with the drugs of verses 9 and 10.
No bath is mentioned.
Right: वमनार्थम् = for the purpose of emesis.
questions.explain: वमनार्थम् is a compound meaning 'for the purpose of emesis'.
questions.rule: Verses 7-8: these drugs are for emesis.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 8 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are glossed in the data.
questions.rule: उपस्थिते = present/aroused; व्याधौ = in disease; भिषक् = physician; देहम् = body.

questions.q: The verse says the disease has the ____ as its seat (type the Devanagari word for 'stomach').
questions.explain: आमाशयाश्रये = आमाशय + आश्रये: having the stomach as seat.
questions.teaches: आमाशय-आश्रय is a compound: the stomach is the seat (आश्रय) of the disease.
questions.rule: आमाशयाश्रये = having the stomach as seat.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भिषग्देहमदूषयन्?
optionExplain: Right: क् becomes ग् before the voiced द; म् joins the vowel अ unchanged.
ऊषयन् is not a word here.
The physician is भिषक्, with a क्.
मदूषयन् is not a word.
questions.explain: भिषक् (physician) + देहम् (body) + अदूषयन् (not harming) run together.
questions.rule: Final क् + voiced sound → ग्.

questions.q: A patient has Kapha and Pitta aroused and the disease seated in the stomach. What does verse 8 say?
options: Administer the drugs for emesis, without harming the body
Wait until the disease has moved elsewhere
optionExplain: The verse says वमनार्थम्, for emesis.
Right: That is the instruction of the verse.
The verse gives no instruction to wait.
The verse says emesis, not purgation.
questions.explain: उपस्थिते श्लेष्मपित्ते + आमाशयाश्रये व्याधौ → वमनार्थं प्रयुञ्जीत.
questions.rule: Kapha-Pitta aroused + disease in the stomach → administer for emesis.

questions.q: A made-up phrase needs भिषक् + जानाति joined. Which is the correct form?
optionExplain: The क् is voiceless and must turn voiced before ज.
ख् is not the voiced partner of क्.
Right: क् becomes ग् before a voiced sound like ज, as in भिषग्देहम्.
The stop must be written with its virāma, not as क.
questions.explain: The same rule gave भिषग्देहम्.
questions.rule: Final क् + voiced sound → ग्.
questions.teaches: A final voiceless stop becomes voiced before a voiced sound: क् → ग्.

questions.q: Verse 9 lists trivṛt, triphalā and more. In which verse is its sentence completed?
optionExplain: Verse 9 only names the drugs.
Verse 8 completes the earlier sentence about emesis.
Verse 5 completes the sentence for head-purging.
Right: The data notes: the sentence is completed in verse 10.
questions.explain: Verses 9 and 10 form one sentence; the verb comes in verse 10.
questions.rule: Verse 9 = list; verb in verse 10.

questions.q: Put these four names in the order they are printed in verse 9.
questions.explain: These are the first four names of the first line.
questions.rule: त्रिवृतां → त्रिफलां → दन्तीं → नीलिनीं.

questions.q: The plant named right after सप्तलां is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first line ends सप्तलां वचाम्.
questions.teaches: वचाम् is an accusative singular; the glosses call it sweet flag.
questions.rule: वचा follows सप्तला.

questions.q: Which is the right split of क्षीरिणीमुदकीर्यकाम्?
optionExplain: Right: म् joins the following vowel without change: two names.
मुदकीर्यकाम् is not a word.
दकीर्यकाम् is not a word.
इणीमुदकीर्यकाम् is not a word.
questions.explain: क्षीरिणीम् (kṣīriṇī) + उदकीर्यकाम् (udakīryakā) are two names run together.
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel: म् joins the vowel without change.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 9 name?
optionExplain: Right: त्रिवृताम्.
Right: वचाम्.
Right: कम्पिल्लकम्.
Āragvadha is in verse 10.
Dravantī is in verse 10.
questions.explain: Verse 9 names ten items; āragvadha and dravantī belong to verse 10.
questions.rule: Verse 9: त्रिवृत्, त्रिफला, दन्ती, नीलिनी, सप्तला, वचा, कम्पिल्लक, गवाक्षी, क्षीरिणी, उदकीर्यका.

questions.q: A made-up phrase needs वचाम् + उक्ताम् joined. Which is the correct form?
optionExplain: That would be वचा + उक्ताम्; here the म् stays.
Right: म् before a vowel joins it unchanged, as in क्षीरिणीमुदकीर्यकाम्.
No extra म् appears.
म् does not turn into न् before a vowel.
questions.explain: The rule that gave क्षीरिणीमुदकीर्यकाम् also gives वचामुक्ताम्.
questions.rule: म् + vowel: म् stays and joins the vowel.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel simply joins it in writing.

questions.q: Verse 10 names drugs to be administered for which treatment?
optionExplain: The verse does not use the word for emesis; it says विरेक.
Nothing in the verse mentions the head; the condition is the pakvāśaya, the lower gut.
Right: विरेकार्थम् means 'for the purpose of purgation'.
The oil enema (अनुवासन) is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: विरेकार्थं प्रयोजयेत् = one should administer for purgation.
questions.rule: Verse 10: these drugs are for purgation, when the doṣa is in the pakvāśaya.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 10 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words of the second line carry the condition and the instruction.
questions.rule: विरेकार्थम् = for purgation; पक्वाशयगते = gone to the lower gut; दोषे = when the doṣa; प्रयोजयेत् = one should administer.

questions.q: The word in verse 10 for 'purgation' is ____ (type the stem in Devanagari, without the ending -अर्थम्).
questions.explain: The compound is विरेकार्थम् = विरेक + अर्थम्.
questions.teaches: -अर्थम् at the end of a compound gives 'for the purpose of'; so विरेकार्थम् is 'for purgation'.
questions.rule: विरेक + अर्थम् → विरेकार्थम् (अ + अ → आ) = for the purpose of purgation.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पीलून्यारग्वधम्?
optionExplain: यारग्वधम् is not a word.
The second word is आरग्वधम् with long आ; with short अ it would be written पीलून्यरग्वधम्.
The plural of पीलु here is पीलूनि; पीलुनी is not the form in the verse.
Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्, and the vowel joins it: इ + आ gives या.
questions.explain: पीलून्यारग्वधम् = पीलूनि (pīlu fruits) + आरग्वधम् (āragvadha).
questions.rule: इ + असमान स्वर → य् + स्वर: पीलूनि + आरग्वधम् → पीलून्यारग्वधम्.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 10 say?
options: They are used when the doṣa has gone to the pakvāśaya
Grape (द्राक्षा) is one of the drugs named
They are given in a fixed dose
optionExplain: Right: विरेकार्थम्.
Right: पक्वाशयगते दोषे.
Right: द्राक्षां is in the first line.
Udāvarta is named in verse 13, for another list.
The verse gives no dose.
questions.explain: The first line names the drugs; the second line gives the condition and the purpose.
questions.rule: Verse 10: five drugs; condition = doṣa in the pakvāśaya; purpose = purgation.

questions.q: A made-up practice line reads पक्वाशयगते दोषे वमनार्थं प्रयोजयेत्, with वमन meaning emesis. What does it say?
options: Administer for emesis when the doṣa has gone to the pakvāśaya
Administer for purgation when the doṣa has gone to the pakvāśaya
Administer for emesis after the doṣa has left the pakvāśaya
Do not administer for emesis when the doṣa has gone to the pakvāśaya
optionExplain: Right: Same frame as verse 10: only the purpose word changes, विरेक → वमन.
That is verse 10; here the purpose word is वमन.
-गते means 'gone to', not 'left'.
प्रयोजयेत् says 'one should administer', not a prohibition.
questions.explain: The frame '… गते दोषे … अर्थं प्रयोजयेत्' reads 'when the doṣa has gone to …, administer for …'. This is a grammar drill, not a medical statement.
questions.rule: X-गते दोषे Y-अर्थं प्रयोजयेत् = administer for Y when the doṣa has gone to X.
questions.teaches: Once the frame is clear, you can read the condition and purpose of any similar line by the words before -गते and -अर्थम्.

questions.q: What does verse 11 mainly contain?
options: A list of drug names; the verb comes in verse 13
A list of the sages who taught
optionExplain: No disease is named in this verse.
Right: Every name in it is a drug, and the list is completed by युञ्ज्यात् in verse 13.
No quantity is named.
The names are all drugs, not teachers.
questions.explain: The verse is a list of accusative drug names whose verb comes later.
questions.rule: Verse 11: drug names only; the verb is in verse 13.

questions.q: Put these four drugs in the order of verse 11.
questions.explain: These four make up the first line, in this order.
questions.rule: पाटला → अग्निमन्थ → बिल्व → श्योनाक.

questions.q: The first drug of the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The second line opens with काश्मर्यं.
questions.teaches: In this verse each name is accusative singular (-म्/-ं masculine, -ाम्/-ीम् feminine): the drug is the object of the verb that comes later, in verse 13.
questions.rule: Here the accusative singular names are objects of the verb still to come.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चाग्निमन्थम्?
optionExplain: There is no word चा here.
The drug is अग्निमन्थ with short अ; the long आ comes from the join.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, so च + अग्निमन्थम् is written चाग्निमन्थम्.
निमन्थम् is not a word in this verse.
questions.explain: चाग्निमन्थम् = च (and) + अग्निमन्थम्.
questions.rule: च + अग्निमन्थम् → चाग्निमन्थम् (अ + अ → आ).

questions.q: Which of these statements about verse 11 are right?
options: Its list is governed by the verb युञ्ज्यात् of verse 13
It says which disease each drug is for
optionExplain: Right: बिल्वं is in the first line.
Right: both are in the second line.
Right: the sentence runs on to verse 13.
Barley is named in verse 12.
No disease is named here.
questions.explain: Verse 11 only names drugs; the use is given later in the same sentence.
questions.rule: Verse 11 = names; use = verse 13.

questions.q: A made-up verse reads only बलां च बिल्वं च, and the next verse ends with युञ्ज्यात्. Is the first verse a complete statement?
options: Yes; two drug names alone say how to use them
Yes; च च means 'one should use'
No; बलां and बिल्वं are verbs
No; its two names are objects of the verb in the next verse
optionExplain: A bare list says nothing about use.
च means 'and' and is not a verb.
Both are nouns.
Right: Like verse 11, it is a list waiting for its verb.
questions.explain: Verse 11 and this made-up verse are both lists; the verb arrives later, as युञ्ज्यात् does in verse 13.
questions.rule: A list of accusatives is completed by a verb in a later verse.
questions.teaches: When a verse is only a list of accusative names, look ahead for the verb that governs it.

questions.q: Which of these is named in verse 12?
optionExplain: Right: यवान् is in the second line.
Grape is named in verse 10, in the purgation list.
Bilva is named in verse 11.
Salts are named in verse 13.
questions.explain: Verse 12 names barley as यवान् in the second line.
questions.rule: Each verse of the list adds new names; barley is in verse 12.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 12 to its form.
questions.explain: All four are accusative; they differ in gender and number.
questions.rule: यवान् = m. acc. pl.; कोलानि = n. acc. pl.; बलाम् = f. acc. sg.; एरण्डम् = m. acc. sg.

questions.q: The word meaning 'together with punarnavā' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first line ends with सपुनर्नवम्.
questions.teaches: स- at the start of a compound means 'together with': सपुनर्नवम् describes the castor, 'with punarnavā'.
questions.rule: स- + noun = 'together with that noun' (a sahārtha bahuvrīhi).

questions.q: Which is the right split of बृहतीमेरण्डम्?
optionExplain: That would be written बृहत्येरण्डम्, because ई becomes य् before a different vowel.
Right: The final म् of बृहतीम् simply joins the vowel that follows.
रण्डम् is not a word; the castor is एरण्ड.
मेरण्डम् is not a word.
questions.explain: बृहतीमेरण्डम् = बृहतीम् (bṛhatī) + एरण्डम् (castor).
questions.rule: म् + स्वर: the म् is carried over onto the next vowel without any change.

questions.q: Which forms in verse 12 are neuter plural?
optionExplain: Right: n. acc. pl., ending -आनि.
Right: n. acc. pl., ending -आनि.
Masculine plural, ending -आन्.
Masculine plural, ending -आन्.
Singular, not plural.
questions.explain: Neuter plural accusative ends in -आनि; masculine plural accusative ends in -आन्.
questions.rule: -आनि = neuter plural; -आन् = masculine plural.

questions.q: In a made-up phrase वृक्षं सफलम्, what does सफलम् add about the tree?
options: A second thing, the fruit, besides the tree
Only the fruit, not the tree
optionExplain: Without would need a negating अ-, not स-.
सफलम् is one describing word agreeing with वृक्षम्, not a separate item.
Right: स- means 'together with', as in सपुनर्नवम्, and agrees with वृक्षम्.
वृक्षं is the main word; सफलम् describes it.
questions.explain: सफलम् = स + फलम्, an adjective of वृक्षम्: the same pattern as सपुनर्नवम् describing एरण्डम्.
questions.rule: स- + noun, agreeing with a noun = 'together with'.
questions.teaches: A स- + noun compound that agrees with a main noun (the sahārtha type of सपुनर्नवम्) tells you what the main noun comes with.

questions.q: In which conditions does verse 13 say to use the drugs?
options: When the doṣa has gone to the pakvāśaya, for purgation
In weak digestion and in pain
In udāvarta, in obstructions (vibandha) and in āsthāpana enemas
optionExplain: That is the condition of verse 10.
Those are the effects of the gruel of verse 18, not the conditions here.
The verse names only these conditions.
Right: उदावर्ते, विबन्धेषु and आस्थापनेषु name them.
questions.explain: The second line gives the conditions: उदावर्ते, विबन्धेषु, आस्थापनेषु.
questions.rule: Verse 13: use in udāvarta, in vibandha and in āsthāpana.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 13 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words of the second line carry the conditions and the instruction.
questions.rule: उदावर्ते = in udāvarta; विबन्धेषु = in obstructions; आस्थापनेषु = in āsthāpana; युञ्ज्यात् = one should use.

questions.q: The verb of the sentence in verses 11 to 13 is ____ (type the base form 'one should use' in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The second line has युञ्ज्यादास्थापनेषु = युञ्ज्यात् + आस्थापनेषु.
questions.teaches: युञ्ज्यात् is a third person singular optative: 'one should use'. Its final त् becomes द् before the vowel आ.
questions.rule: युञ्ज्यात् + आस्थापनेषु → युञ्ज्यादास्थापनेषु.

questions.q: स्नेहांश्च is स्नेहान् + च. What happens at the join?
options: न् becomes an anusvāra and श् is added before च
A visarga becomes श् before च
Nothing changes except that the space is closed
optionExplain: Right: न् + च gives ंश्च, as in स्नेहांश्च.
The change is to an anusvāra with श् added; there is no म् in स्नेहांश्च.
There is no visarga: स्नेहान् ends in न्.
The न् changes to ंश्.
questions.explain: स्नेहांश्च = स्नेहान् (oils/fats, acc. pl.) + च.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 13 as conditions or uses?
options: The doṣa gone to the pakvāśaya
optionExplain: Right: उदावर्ते.
Right: विबन्धेषु.
Right: आस्थापनेषु.
That is the condition of verse 10.
The oil enema is named in verse 14.
questions.explain: Verse 13 names three: udāvarta, vibandha and āsthāpana.
questions.rule: Verse 13 gives the verb युञ्ज्यात् and the three places of use.

questions.q: A made-up line ends विबन्धे शूले च प्रयोजयेत् (शूल = pain). By the pattern of verse 13, how do you read विबन्धे and शूले?
options: 'From obstruction and pain': they are the source
'In obstruction and in pain': the -ए ending shows the condition
'By obstruction and pain': they are the means
'Of obstruction and pain': they belong to something
optionExplain: Source would need the ablative, ending -आत्.
Right: Like उदावर्ते and विबन्धेषु, the locative gives the condition in which to use.
Means would be the instrumental, ending -एन.
That would be the genitive, ending -स्य.
questions.explain: -ए (singular) and -एषु (plural) of a masculine noun give 'in …', as in उदावर्ते and विबन्धेषु.
questions.rule: Locative -ए / -एषु = 'in …': the condition in which to use.
questions.teaches: Reading the ending of a word for a disorder tells you whether it is the condition, the means or the source.

questions.q: What does verse 14 say is to be prepared from the same group of drugs?
optionExplain: Gruels are announced in verse 17.
No emetic is mentioned in this verse.
Right: संकल्प्यमनुवासनम् = the anuvāsana is to be prepared.
Purgation was the purpose in verse 10, not here.
questions.explain: अत एव औषधगणात् संकल्प्यम् अनुवासनम्: from this very group, the oil enema is to be prepared.
questions.rule: Verse 14: the oil enema, anuvāsana, comes from the same drug group.

questions.q: Put these phrases in the order of verse 14.
questions.explain: The first line gives the source and the enema; the second line the quality and the closing words.
questions.rule: अत एवौषधगणात् → संकल्प्यमनुवासनम् → मारुतघ्नमिति → प्रोक्तः संग्रहः पाञ्चकर्मिकः.

questions.q: The oil enema is called ____ in the verse (type its name in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first line ends with संकल्प्यमनुवासनम्.
questions.teaches: अनुवासनम् ends in -म् as the subject (nominative) of 'is to be prepared': संकल्प्यम् अनुवासनम्.
questions.rule: अनुवासन = oil enema, here the thing to be prepared.

questions.q: Which is the right split of एवौषधगणात्?
optionExplain: The word is औषध, with औ, not उषध.
There is no word एवो.
वौषधगणात् is not a word.
Right: अ + औ gives औ, so एव + औषध… is written एवौषध….
questions.explain: एवौषधगणात् = एव + औषध-गणात्, 'from the very group of drugs'.
questions.rule: अ + औ → औ: एव + औषध → एवौषध.

questions.q: Which statements fit verse 14?
options: The oil enema is prepared from the same drug group
The oil enema is called wind-destroying
The compendium relating to the five procedures has been stated
The verse gives the dose of the oil
The verse says to use the drugs in udāvarta
optionExplain: Right: अत एव औषधगणात्.
Right: मारुतघ्नम्.
Right: प्रोक्तः संग्रहः पाञ्चकर्मिकः.
No dose is given.
Udāvarta is named in verse 13.
questions.explain: The first line gives the source and the enema; the second line the quality and the closing words.
questions.rule: Verse 14: anuvāsana from the same group; wind-destroying; compendium of the five procedures stated.

questions.q: A made-up line calls a drug ज्वरघ्नम् (ज्वर = fever). Following मारुतघ्नम्, what does it say?
optionExplain: Right: -घ्न at the end of a compound means 'destroying', as in मारुतघ्नम्.
-घ्न destroys; it does not cause.
There is no word for 'resembling' in the compound.
The first member names what is destroyed.
questions.explain: मारुत-घ्नम् = wind-destroying, so ज्वर-घ्नम् = fever-destroying.
questions.rule: X-घ्न = destroying X.
questions.teaches: The last part -घ्न tells what the thing does; the first part names what it acts on.

questions.q: Which two things does verse 15 tell the physician to consider?
optionExplain: Neither is named in the verse.
Right: मात्राकालौ विचारयन् = considering dose and time.
Neither is named in the verse.
Neither is named in the verse.
questions.explain: मात्राकालौ is the pair 'dose and time'; विचारयन् is 'considering'.
questions.rule: Verse 15: consider dose (मात्रा) and time (काल).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 15 to its meaning.
pairs: of those whose doṣas are aroused
questions.explain: Each word carries one part of the instruction.
questions.rule: उपस्थितदोषाणाम् = of those with aroused doṣas; स्नेहस्वेदोपपादनैः = by providing oleation and sudation; पञ्चकर्माणि = the five procedures; विचारयन् = considering.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'should perform' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The second line has पञ्चकर्माणि कुर्वीत.
questions.teaches: कुर्वीत is a third person singular optative (middle voice) of √कृ: 'one should do'.
questions.rule: कुर्वीत = one should perform.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तान्युपस्थितदोषाणाम्?
optionExplain: युपस्थित… is not a word.
The word is तानि, the neuter plural of 'that'.
Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्: इ + उ gives यु.
The word is उपस्थित, with its उ.
questions.explain: तानि (those) + उपस्थित-दोषाणाम् (of those with aroused doṣas).
questions.rule: इ + उ → यु: तानि + उपस्थित → तान्युपस्थित.

questions.q: Which statements fit verse 15?
options: The five procedures are to be performed
Dose and time are to be considered
The five procedures are named one by one
The dose is fixed at a quantity
optionExplain: Right: स्नेहस्वेदोपपादनैः.
Right: पञ्चकर्माणि कुर्वीत.
Right: मात्राकालौ विचारयन्.
They are not named in this verse.
No quantity is given.
questions.explain: The verse gives the preparation, the action and the care to be taken.
questions.rule: Verse 15: oleation and sudation; five procedures; consider dose and time.

questions.q: A made-up phrase reads बलकालौ विचारयन् (बल = strength). What does it say?
optionExplain: Two words are joined, and -औ marks two.
बल and काल are different words.
That would need a describing word, not a pair ending in -औ.
Right: The ending -औ of a pair joined by 'and' marks two things, as in मात्राकालौ.
questions.explain: बलकालौ = बल + काल, a pair 'strength and time', like मात्राकालौ 'dose and time'.
questions.rule: A pair joined into one word ending in -औ = 'X and Y' (two things).
questions.teaches: A compound of two nouns with the ending -औ names two things together.

questions.q: According to verse 16, what does yukti rest on?
optionExplain: Right: मात्राकालाश्रया युक्तिः = yukti has dose and time as its basis.
Knowledge of substances is what the lower group has, not the basis of yukti.
It is success (सिद्धि) that is established in yukti, not the reverse.
Nothing like this is named in the verse.
questions.explain: The first words say it: मात्रा and काल are the basis (आश्रय) of yukti.
questions.rule: Verse 16: yukti rests on dose and time.

questions.q: Put these in the order of the verse's chain, starting from the base.
questions.explain: Yukti rests on dose and time; success is established in yukti.
questions.rule: मात्रा-काल → युक्ति → सिद्धि.

questions.q: Success (सिद्धिः) is established in ____ (type the Devanagari word).
questions.explain: The verse says सिद्धिर्युक्तौ प्रतिष्ठिता.
questions.teaches: युक्तौ is the locative singular of युक्ति, 'in yukti'. Here -औ is not a dual ending.
questions.rule: -औ can be a locative singular ending of a feminine noun in -इ, not only a dual.

questions.q: सिद्धिर्युक्तौ comes from सिद्धिः + युक्तौ. Which change happened?
options: The visarga after इ became र् before the voiced sound य
optionExplain: ओ appears only when the visarga follows अ.
Right: After इ / उ, a visarga before a voiced sound becomes र्.
A visarga after इ does not drop before य; it becomes र्.
श् appears before च / छ, not before य.
questions.explain: सिद्धिः + युक्तौ → सिद्धिर्युक्तौ.
questions.rule: इः + घोष → इर् + घोष.

questions.q: Which statements fit verse 16?
options: Yukti rests on dose and time
The one who knows yukti stands above those with knowledge of substances
Yukti is the name of a drug
optionExplain: Right: मात्राकालाश्रया युक्तिः.
Right: सिद्धिर्युक्तौ प्रतिष्ठिता.
Right: तिष्ठत्युपरि युक्तिज्ञः ….
The verse only compares; it does not call it useless.
Yukti is rational planning, not a drug.
questions.explain: Each half-line of the verse gives one of the three right statements.
questions.rule: Verse 16: yukti on dose and time; success in yukti; yukti-knower above substance-knowers.

questions.q: Physician A knows many substances; physician B knows yukti, planning by dose and time. By this verse, who stands above?
options: Physician A, who knows many substances
Neither; the verse does not compare them
optionExplain: Those with knowledge of substances stand below the yukti-knower.
The verse puts the yukti-knower above.
Right: युक्तिज्ञः stands above those with knowledge of substances.
The verse does compare: तिष्ठत्युपरि युक्तिज्ञः.
questions.explain: The verse ranks the yukti-knower above those who have knowledge of substances.
questions.rule: युक्तिज्ञ stands above द्रव्यज्ञानवत्.
questions.teaches: Use the verse's comparison: the person who plans by dose and time ranks above one who only knows substances.

questions.q: What topic does verse 17 begin?
options: The dose and time of the five procedures
Gruels made with various drugs, for disorders curable by them
optionExplain: The enema lists ended in verse 14.
That is the topic of verses 15 and 16.
No sage is named in this verse.
Right: यवागूः विविधौषधाः … तत्साध्यानां निवृत्तये.
questions.explain: The speaker announces gruels with various drugs for the relief of the disorders they can cure.
questions.rule: Verse 17: announcement of the gruels.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 17 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole announcement.
questions.rule: ऊर्ध्वम् = after this; प्रवक्ष्यामि = I shall describe; यवागूः = gruels; निवृत्तये = for the cessation.

questions.q: The word for 'gruels' in the first line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first line has यवागूर्विविधौषधाः = यवागूः + विविधौषधाः.
questions.teaches: यवागू is a feminine noun; here the plural is meant, 'gruels'.
questions.rule: यवागूः = gruels (here accusative plural, the object of प्रवक्ष्यामि).

questions.q: अत ऊर्ध्वम् comes from अतः + ऊर्ध्वम्. What happened to the visarga?
options: It dropped, because it follows अ and a different vowel comes next
optionExplain: Right: अः before a vowel other than अ loses the visarga, leaving अत ऊ….
अः becomes ओ before a voiced consonant or a short अ; before ऊ the visarga simply drops.
र् appears after इ / उ, not after अ.
स् does not appear here.
questions.explain: अतः + ऊर्ध्वम् → अत ऊर्ध्वम्.
questions.rule: अः + भिन्न स्वर → अ + स्वर (विसर्ग लुप्त).

questions.q: Which statements fit verse 17?
options: The gruels are made with various drugs
The gruels are for disorders curable by them
The verse names the first gruel and its drugs
optionExplain: Right: विविधौषधाः.
Right: तत्साध्यानां विकाराणाम्.
Right: प्रवक्ष्यामि.
That comes in verse 18.
The verse says only those curable by them.
questions.explain: The verse announces a topic and sets its limit; it does not yet describe a gruel.
questions.rule: Verse 17: gruels with various drugs, for the disorders they can cure.

questions.q: A made-up line reads अत ऊर्ध्वं वक्ष्यन्ति. Following प्रवक्ष्यामि, who will speak?
optionExplain: 'I' would end in -आमि.
Right: -अन्ति marks 'they', as -आमि in प्रवक्ष्यामि marks 'I'.
'You' would end in -असि.
-स्य- marks the future and -अन्ति is plural.
questions.explain: प्रवक्ष्यामि = 'I shall describe' (first person, future); वक्ष्यन्ति = 'they will say'.
questions.rule: Future endings: -आमि = I, -अन्ति = they.
questions.teaches: The ending of a future verb shows who will do it: -आमि is 'I', -अन्ति is 'they'.

questions.q: Which two effects does verse 18 give for this gruel?
options: It kindles digestion and relieves pain
optionExplain: Neither purging nor vomiting is mentioned.
Neither fever nor cough is named.
Right: दीपनीया = kindling digestion; शूलघ्नी = pain-relieving.
Neither effect is named.
questions.explain: The second line gives the two effects: दीपनीया and शूलघ्नी.
questions.rule: Verse 18: the gruel is दीपनीया and शूलघ्नी.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 18 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words of the second line carry the subject and the effects.
questions.rule: यवागूः = gruel; दीपनीया = kindling digestion; शूलघ्नी = pain-relieving; उपसाधिता = prepared.

questions.q: The word meaning 'pain-relieving' is ____ (type it in Devanagari, without the preceding स्यात्).
questions.explain: The verse has स्याच्छूलघ्नी = स्यात् + शूलघ्नी.
questions.teaches: शूल-घ्नी = pain-destroying, feminine to agree with the feminine यवागूः; the same -घ्न as in मारुतघ्नम् of verse 14.
questions.rule: X-घ्न(ी) = destroying X; the ending agrees with the noun it describes.

questions.q: स्याच्छूलघ्नी is स्यात् + शूलघ्नी. Which change happened?
options: त् became द् and श् stayed
त् became च् and श् became छ्
optionExplain: द् appears before voiced sounds; श is not voiced.
त् + श is written च्छ, not त्श.
स् does not appear here.
Right: त् before श gives च्छ.
questions.explain: स्यात् + शूलघ्नी → स्याच्छूलघ्नी.
questions.rule: त् + श → च्छ.

questions.q: Which of these are named among the drugs of verse 18?
optionExplain: Right: पिप्पली.
Right: चव्य.
Right: नागर.
Bilva is named in verse 11.
Grape is named in verse 10.
questions.explain: The five drugs of the first line are the only drugs named here.
questions.rule: Verse 18: pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka, nāgara.

questions.q: A made-up line says बिल्वपिप्पलीनागरैर्यवागूः शूलघ्नी स्यात्. By the pattern of verse 18, what does it say?
options: A gruel prepared with bilva, pippalī and nāgara would relieve pain
Bilva, pippalī and nāgara are the ailments the gruel relieves
Three gruels, one for each drug
optionExplain: Right: -ऐः marks 'with / by' the drugs, as in verse 18; शूलघ्नी gives the effect.
-ऐः names the means (the drugs), not what is relieved.
शूलघ्नी means pain-relieving.
यवागूः is singular; the three drugs are for one gruel.
questions.explain: बिल्वपिप्पलीनागरैः = with bilva, pippalī and nāgara (instrumental plural), and the gruel is pain-relieving. This is a grammar drill, not a medical claim.
questions.rule: Drugs in -ऐः + यवागूः + effect = a gruel with these drugs has this effect.
questions.teaches: The frame 'drugs in -ऐः, यवागूः, effect' lets you read any gruel verse: the instrumental names the drugs it is prepared with.

questions.q: Gruel cooked with wood-apple, bilva, cāṅgerī, buttermilk and pomegranate is called what in verse 19?
optionExplain: This word is not in verse 19.
Right: These are the two words the verse gives for it.
This word is not in verse 19.
This word is not in verse 19.
questions.explain: पाचनी ग्राहिणी, पेया: the gruel is called digestive and binding.
questions.rule: The first gruel group of verse 19 is digestive and binding.

questions.q: Match each ingredient of the first line to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are four of the five things the gruel is cooked with.
