questions.rule: दधित्थ = wood-apple; बिल्व = bilva; तक्र = buttermilk; दाडिम = pomegranate.

questions.q: The word for 'thin gruel' in the verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse says पेया for the thin gruel.
questions.teaches: In verses 19-22 the gruel is called पेया (thin, to be drunk); verse 23 uses the word यवागू (thick gruel).
questions.rule: पेया = thin gruel.

questions.q: In सवाते, what does the beginning स- add to वाते (in Vāta)?
options: 'Without': the whole word means when Vāta is absent
'Against': the whole word means opposing Vāta
'With': the whole word means when Vāta is present
'From': the whole word means from Vāta
optionExplain: Absence would need a negative such as अ-, not स-.
स- does not mean 'against'.
Right: स- in this joined word means 'with, accompanied by', so सवाते is 'where Vāta is present'.
The ending -ए is 'in, when', not 'from'.
questions.explain: सवाते = स + वाते, a joined word in the locative: 'in the case accompanied by Vāta'.
questions.rule: स- at the start of a joined word = 'with'.

questions.q: Which of these is named in verse 19 itself?
optionExplain: Right: buttermilk is in the first line.
Right: pomegranate is in the first line.
Right: bilva is in the first line.
Honey appears in verse 24, not here.
Ghee appears in verse 26, not here.
questions.explain: The first line names wood-apple, bilva, cāṅgerī, buttermilk and pomegranate.
questions.rule: Verse 19 names buttermilk, pomegranate and bilva; honey and ghee come later.

questions.q: An invented line says बिल्वतक्रसाधिता पेया पाचनी. By the frame of verse 19, what does it say?
options: Gruel without bilva and buttermilk is digestive
Bilva and buttermilk are cooked in gruel to bind it
Digestive gruel is a name for buttermilk
Gruel cooked with bilva and buttermilk is digestive
optionExplain: साधिता says 'cooked with', not 'without'.
The word is पाचनी (digestive), not ग्राहिणी (binding).
The line describes a gruel; it does not rename buttermilk.
Right: 'Ingredients + साधिता' = cooked with them; पाचनी = digestive.
questions.explain: The sentence has the same frame as the first line of verse 19: ingredients + साधिता + पेया + effect.
questions.rule: Ingredients + साधिता + पेया + effect = 'gruel cooked with these has this effect'.
questions.teaches: साधिता agrees with the feminine पेया and the joined ingredient word before it means 'cooked with these'.

questions.q: Verse 20 calls the gruel cooked with śālaparṇī, balā, bilva and pṛśniparṇī beneficial for whom?
options: Those with diarrhoea due to Pitta and Kapha
optionExplain: Right: पित्तश्लेष्मातिसारिणाम् = of those with Pitta-and-Kapha diarrhoea.
Bloody diarrhoea (रक्तातिसार) is in the next verse, 21.
Painful urination (मूत्रकृच्छ्र) is in verse 22.
Worms (क्रिमि) are in verse 23.
questions.explain: The last word of the verse names the sufferers: those with diarrhoea from Pitta and Kapha.
questions.rule: Verse 20: the gruel is beneficial in Pitta-Kapha diarrhoea.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 20 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the sentence.
questions.rule: साधिता = cooked; हिता = beneficial; दाडिमाम्ला = soured with pomegranate; अतिसारिणाम् = of those with diarrhoea.

questions.q: The sour ingredient that gives the gruel its sourness is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: दाडिमाम्ला = दाडिम (pomegranate) + अम्ला (sour).
questions.teaches: A joined word ending in अम्ला names what makes something sour; here the gruel is soured with pomegranate.
questions.rule: दाडिमाम्ला = soured with pomegranate.

questions.q: विल्वैः and पृश्निपर्ण्या both mean 'with'. What does each ending show?
options: विल्वैः is instrumental plural; पृश्निपर्ण्या is instrumental singular
विल्वैः is singular; पृश्निपर्ण्या is plural
optionExplain: विल्वैः ends in -ऐः, which is plural.
Right: Both are instrumental, 'with'; -ऐः is plural and -ण्या singular.
The numbers are the other way round.
The genitive plural in this verse is अतिसारिणाम्.
questions.explain: The group शालपर्णी-बला-विल्वैः takes one plural ending at its end; पृश्निपर्ण्या stands alone with a singular ending.
questions.rule: -ऐः = instrumental plural; -या on a feminine word = instrumental singular.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 20 itself?
optionExplain: Right: first in the verse.
Right: second in the verse.
Right: named after bilva.
Buttermilk is in verse 19, not here.
Hrīvera is in verse 21, not here.
questions.explain: The verse names śālaparṇī, balā, bilva and pṛśniparṇī; buttermilk and hrīvera belong to other verses.
questions.rule: Verse 20 names śālaparṇī, balā, bilva, pṛśniparṇī and pomegranate.

questions.q: An invented line says बलाविल्वसाधिता पेया हिता वातातिसारिणाम्. By the frame of verse 20, what does it say?
options: Gruel cooked with balā and bilva is harmful for those with Vāta diarrhoea
Gruel is cooked by those with Vāta diarrhoea
Gruel cooked with balā and bilva is beneficial for those with Vāta diarrhoea
Vāta diarrhoea is cooked with balā and bilva
optionExplain: हिता means beneficial, not harmful.
वातातिसारिणाम् is genitive plural: 'of/for those with', not the cooks.
Right: '-साधिता' = cooked with; 'हिता' = beneficial; '-इणाम्' names the sufferers.
साधिता agrees with पेया (the gruel), not with the disease.
questions.explain: Same frame as verse 20: ingredients + साधिता + पेया + हिता + genitive plural of the sufferers.
questions.rule: Genitive plural in -इणाम् after हिता = 'beneficial for those with ...'.
questions.teaches: Joined word ending in -अतिसारिणाम् (genitive plural) names the people the remedy is for, after हिता.

questions.q: Verse 21 calls the gruel in goat's milk with half water 'रक्तातिसारघ्नी'. What does it destroy?
options: Diarrhoea due to Pitta and Kapha
optionExplain: That is verse 20, not this verse.
That is verse 22.
Thirst is in verse 24.
Right: रक्त + अतिसार + घ्नी = destroying diarrhoea with blood.
questions.explain: रक्तातिसारघ्नी ends in -घ्नी, 'destroying'; the thing destroyed is bloody diarrhoea.
questions.rule: Verse 21: goat's-milk gruel destroys diarrhoea with blood.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 21 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the sentence.
questions.rule: अर्धोदके = having half water; नागरैः = with dry ginger; साधिता = cooked; रक्तातिसारघ्नी = destroying bloody diarrhoea.

questions.q: The word for 'milk' in the first line is ____ (type it in Devanagari, as in 'पयस्यर्धोदके').
questions.explain: The milk word is पयः; in the verse it is पयसि, 'in milk'.
questions.teaches: पयः is the milk word; the locative पयसि 'in milk' joins to अर्धोदके by sandhi: इ becomes य् before a vowel.
questions.rule: पयः = milk; पयसि = in milk.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ह्रीवेरोत्पलनागरैः?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ joins to ओ, so ह्रीवेर + उत्पल is written ह्रीवेरोत्पल.
त्पल is not a word.
There is no word पल in the verse's list.
अः before a vowel other than अ drops the visarga and leaves a gap; it does not make ओ.
questions.explain: Three ingredients are joined: ह्रीवेर, उत्पल and नागरैः.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: ह्रीवेर + उत्पल = ह्रीवेरोत्पल.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 21 itself?
optionExplain: Right: first of the three joined ingredients.
Right: second of the three.
Right: dry ginger ends the group.

questions.explain: Verse 21 names hrīvera, utpala and dry ginger (and pṛśniparṇī in line 2).
questions.rule: Verse 21 names ह्रीवेर, उत्पल and नागर.

questions.q: An invented gruel is called ज्वरघ्नी. By the pattern of रक्तातिसारघ्नी, what does ज्वरघ्नी say? (ज्वर = fever)
optionExplain: -घ्नी means destroying, not causing.
Right: X + घ्नी = destroying X, so ज्वर + घ्नी = fever-destroying.
The pattern names what is destroyed, not an ingredient.
The pattern names what is destroyed, not a vessel or place.
questions.explain: In रक्तातिसारघ्नी the thing destroyed (bloody diarrhoea) comes before -घ्नी.
questions.rule: X + -घ्नी = destroying X.
questions.teaches: A feminine joined word ending in -घ्नी describes a gruel as 'destroying' whatever comes before it.

questions.q: Verse 22 gives gruel for two conditions. Which two?
options: The condition with āma, and painful urination
optionExplain: These are in verses 21 and 23.
These are in verse 24.
Right: सामे = when āma is present; मूत्रकृच्छ्रे = in painful urination.
These are in verse 27.
questions.explain: The two conditions are named by the two locative words सामे and मूत्रकृच्छ्रे.
questions.rule: Verse 22: āma and painful urination.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 22 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each word is one part of the instruction.
questions.rule: दद्यात् = one should give; सामे = when āma is present; मूत्रकृच्छ्रे = in painful urination; सफाणिताम् = with phāṇita.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'one should give' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: दद्यात् is the third person singular optative of √दा, 'one should give'.
questions.teaches: One optative verb serves both halves of the verse: दद्यात् governs the first gruel and, by understanding, the second.
questions.rule: दद्यात् = one should give; it serves both halves.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सामे?
optionExplain: Neither सा nor मे fits the sense 'when āma is present'.
A visarga there would give स आमे, not सामे.
सम् before आमे would be written समामे.
Right: अ + आ joins to आ, so स ('with') + आमे ('in āma') is written सामे.
questions.explain: सामे is a joined word: 'when āma is present'.
questions.rule: सामे = स + आमे.

questions.q: Which of these go into the gruel for painful urination in verse 22?
optionExplain: Right: the gruel is cooked with it.
Right: the gruel is cooked with it.
Right: the gruel is with phāṇita.
Ativiṣā belongs to the gruel for the āma condition.
Dry ginger belongs to the gruel for the āma condition.
questions.explain: The second line gives the painful-urination gruel; ativiṣā and dry ginger are in the first line.
questions.rule: Painful urination: श्वदंष्ट्रा, कण्टकारी, फाणित.

questions.q: An invented word सज्वरे follows the pattern of सामे. What does it mean? (ज्वर = fever)
optionExplain: Right: स + ज्वरे = in the case with fever, as सामे is 'with āma'.
स- means 'with', not 'without'.
The ending -ए is 'in, when', not 'from'.
-ए here is a locative, not a destroyer word like -घ्नी.
questions.explain: सामे and सवाते (verse 19) are built the same way: स- + noun in the locative.
questions.rule: स- + locative noun = 'when X is present'.
questions.teaches: A joined word स- + locative names the condition under which the remedy is given.

questions.q: What is the yavāgū of verse 23, cooked in buttermilk with viḍaṅga, pepper and others, called?
optionExplain: That belongs to verse 24.
Right: क्रिमिघ्नी = क्रिमि (worms) + घ्नी (destroying).
That belongs to verse 25.
That belongs to verse 26.
questions.explain: The last line gives the effect: क्रिमिघ्नी, worm-destroying.
questions.rule: Verse 23: the buttermilk-cooked yavāgū is worm-destroying.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 23 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the sentence.
questions.rule: तक्रसिद्धा = cooked in buttermilk; यवागूः = thick gruel; क्रिमिघ्नी = worm-destroying; मरिचेन = with pepper.

questions.q: The word for 'thick gruel' in this verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse says यवागूः.
questions.teaches: Verses 19-22 used पेया (thin gruel); this verse uses यवागू (thick gruel), the word the data glosses 'thick gruel'.
questions.rule: यवागू = thick gruel.

questions.q: Which is the right split of शिग्रुभिर्मरिचेन?
optionExplain: A visarga becomes ओ only after अ, not after इ.
रमरिचेन is not a word.
Right: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a voiced sound (म), so शिग्रुभिः + मरिचेन is written शिग्रुभिर्मरिचेन.
अरिचेन is not the word in the verse; the word is मरिचेन, 'with pepper'.
questions.explain: शिग्रुभिः is the instrumental plural 'with śigrus'; मरिचेन is 'with pepper'.
questions.rule: इः + voiced sound → इर्: शिग्रुभिः + मरिचेन = शिग्रुभिर्मरिचेन.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 23 itself?
optionExplain: Right: first in the verse.
Right: it is in the first line.
Right: pepper ends the first line.
Honey is in verse 24, not here.
Pomegranate is in verses 19-20, not here.
questions.explain: Verse 23 names viḍaṅga, śigru and pepper among its ingredients.
questions.rule: Verse 23 names विडङ्ग, शिग्रु and मरिच; honey and pomegranate belong elsewhere.

questions.q: An invented phrase is क्षीरसिद्धा यवागूः. By the pattern of तक्रसिद्धा, what does it describe? (क्षीर = milk)
options: A thin gruel for those who are cooked
A thick gruel cooked in milk
optionExplain: सिद्धा means 'cooked', not 'without'.
The gruel is what is cooked, in the milk.
यवागू is the gruel; there is no person in the phrase.
Right: X + सिद्धा = cooked in X, agreeing with the feminine यवागूः.
questions.explain: तक्रसिद्धा यवागूः and क्षीरसिद्धा यवागूः have the same build; only the liquid changes.
questions.rule: Liquid + सिद्धा + यवागूः = a thick gruel cooked in that liquid.
questions.teaches: Liquid + सिद्धा (feminine) names what the gruel is cooked in; the same build appears in मदिरासिद्धा (verse 27).

questions.q: Verse 24 names two effects of its two gruels. Which pair?
optionExplain: Right: पिपासाघ्नी and विषघ्नी, joined by च.
Worm-destroying is verse 23.
These are the two effects of verse 25.
These are the two effects of verse 26.
questions.explain: पिपासाघ्नी, विषघ्नी च: thirst-removing and poison-destroying.
questions.rule: Verse 24: one gruel removes thirst; the somarājī one destroys poison.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 24 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two effect words and two ingredients.
questions.rule: पिपासाघ्नी = thirst-removing; विषघ्नी = poison-destroying; मधु = honey; मृद्वीका = grapes.

questions.q: Inside पिपासाघ्नी, the word for 'thirst' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: पिपासा + घ्नी = thirst + destroying.
questions.teaches: The first part of a -घ्नी word names what is removed: पिपासा (thirst), as विष (poison) in विषघ्नी.
questions.rule: पिपासाघ्नी = पिपासा + घ्नी.

questions.q: Which ingredient does verse 24 tie to the poison-destroying gruel, not to the thirst-removing one?
optionExplain: Honey is in the thirst-removing group.
Right: सोमराजीविपाचिता: cooked with somarājī, and that gruel is विषघ्नी.
Dry ginger is in the thirst-removing group.
Grapes are in the thirst-removing group.
questions.explain: The first line lists the thirst-removing ingredients; the second line gives सोमराजी for the poison-destroying gruel.
questions.rule: सोमराजी → विषघ्नी; मृद्वीका ... नागर → पिपासाघ्नी.

questions.q: Which of these are named for the thirst-removing gruel in verse 24?
optionExplain: Right: first in the list.
Right: honey is in the list.
Right: dry ginger ends the list.
Somarājī belongs to the poison-destroying gruel.
Buttermilk is in verse 23, not here.
questions.explain: The first line lists the thirst-removing ingredients; somarājī is in the second line.
questions.rule: Thirst-removing: मृद्वीका, मधु, नागर and the others of the first line.

questions.q: An invented line says कासघ्नी च मरिचविपाचिता, like सोमराजीविपाचिता. What does it say? (मरिच = pepper, कास = cough)
options: And the one cooked with cough destroys pepper
And the one without pepper destroys cough
And the one cooked with pepper destroys cough
And pepper is cooked by cough
optionExplain: The roles are reversed: pepper is the ingredient, cough the thing destroyed.
विपाचिता says 'cooked with', not 'without'.
Right: X + विपाचिता = cooked with X, and च adds a second effect, as in verse 24.
मरिचविपाचिता describes the gruel, not pepper.
questions.explain: Verse 24 joins two gruels with च; each has an ingredient + विपाचिता and an effect ending in -घ्नी.
questions.rule: X + विपाचिता = cooked with X; च joins a second gruel and its effect.
questions.teaches: च joins a second gruel to the first; ingredient + विपाचिता names what it is cooked with, and -घ्नी names the effect.

questions.q: Which yavāgū does verse 25 call nourishing (बृंहणी)?
options: The one of roasted gavedhukā with honey
The one with ghee and sesame
The one cooked in boar broth
optionExplain: That one is reducing (कर्शनीया).
Buttermilk is in verse 23, not here.
That one is oleating and is in verse 26.
Right: सिद्धा वराहनिर्यूहे यवागूर्बृंहणी: cooked in boar broth, it is nourishing.
questions.explain: The first line gives the nourishing gruel: the boar-broth one.
questions.rule: Verse 25: boar-broth yavāgū = nourishing.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 25 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two effect words and two helpers.
questions.rule: बृंहणी = nourishing; कर्शनीया = reducing; समाक्षिका = with honey; निर्यूह = broth.

questions.q: The word for 'with honey' in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: स + माक्षिका: स- ('with') + माक्षिका (honey) gives समाक्षिका.
questions.teaches: A joined word with स- at the front and a feminine ending names a gruel 'with' that thing, as सवाते and सामे name conditions 'with' something.
questions.rule: समाक्षिका = with honey.

questions.q: Which is the right split of यवागूर्बृंहणी?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ऊ becomes र् before a voiced sound (ब), so यवागूः + बृंहणी is written यवागूर्बृंहणी.
र्बृंहणी is not a word.
That would be written यवागूरबृंहणी and would mean 'not nourishing'.
The word यवागू has a long ऊ, not a short उ.
questions.explain: यवागूः is the gruel; बृंहणी is its effect, 'nourishing'.
questions.rule: ऊः + voiced sound → ऊर्: यवागूः + बृंहणी = यवागूर्बृंहणी.

questions.q: Which yavāgū does verse 25 call reducing (कर्शनीया)?
options: The yavāgū cooked in boar broth
The yavāgū of roasted gavedhukā, with honey
Either one, since both are in the verse
optionExplain: That one is nourishing, not reducing.
Right: भृष्टानां गवेधुकानां कर्शनीया समाक्षिका: roasted gavedhukā, with honey, is reducing.
The two have opposite effects in the verse.
Buttermilk is not in verse 25.
questions.explain: The second line names the reducing gruel.
questions.rule: Reducing: roasted gavedhukā with honey.

questions.q: An invented line says सिद्धा मेषनिर्यूहे यवागूः. By the pattern of वराहनिर्यूहे, what does it say? (मेष = ram)
options: A yavāgū cooked without any ram broth
A ram cooked in a broth of yavāgū
A yavāgū cooked in a broth of ram
A yavāgū that makes the ram a broth
optionExplain: निर्यूहे names the broth the gruel is cooked in.
The gruel is what is cooked, in the broth.
Right: The ending -ए on the compound is 'in', and सिद्धा is 'cooked', agreeing with यवागूः.
No verb of making is in the line; सिद्धा means 'cooked'.
questions.explain: Verse 25 line 1: सिद्धा + (animal)निर्यूहे + यवागूः. Only the animal changes.
questions.rule: सिद्धा + X-निर्यूहे = cooked in a broth of X.
questions.teaches: Animal + निर्यूहे (locative) names the broth in which the gruel is cooked.

questions.q: Which yavāgū does verse 26 call oleating (स्नेहनी)?
options: The one of śyāmāka in kuśa-āmalaka decoction
The one cooked in boar broth
The one cooked in buttermilk with viḍaṅga
The one with ghee, much sesame and salt
optionExplain: That one is drying (विरुक्षणी).
That one is nourishing and belongs to verse 25.
That one is worm-destroying and belongs to verse 23.
Right: सर्पिष्मती बहुतिला स्नेहनी लवणान्विता: ghee, much sesame and salt make it oleating.
questions.explain: The first line gives the oleating gruel.
questions.rule: Verse 26: ghee + sesame + salt = oleating.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 26 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two effect words and two ingredient words.
questions.rule: स्नेहनी = oleating; विरुक्षणी = drying; सर्पिष्मती = with ghee; बहुतिला = with much sesame.

questions.q: The millet named in the drying gruel is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The second line says श्यामाकानां, 'of śyāmāka (millet)'.
questions.teaches: श्यामाकानां is the genitive plural of श्यामाक: 'of śyāmāka', the grain whose gruel is drying.
questions.rule: श्यामाक = millet; its gruel is drying here.

questions.q: Which is the right split of लवणान्विता?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ joins to आ, so लवण ('salt') + अन्विता ('accompanied') is written लवणान्विता.
A visarga after अ before अ would be written लवणोऽन्विता.
न्विता is not a word.
नन्विता is not a word.
questions.explain: लवणान्विता = 'accompanied by salt'.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: लवण + अन्विता = लवणान्विता.

questions.q: Which of these make the oleating gruel in verse 26?
optionExplain: Right: सर्पिष्मती, with ghee.
Right: बहुतिला, with much sesame.
Right: लवणान्विता, accompanied by salt.
Śyāmāka belongs to the drying gruel.
Āmalaka belongs to the drying gruel.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the oleating ingredients; line 2 gives the drying gruel.
questions.rule: Oleating: ghee, sesame, salt. Drying: śyāmāka in kuśa-āmalaka decoction.

questions.q: An invented word बहुघृता follows the pattern of बहुतिला. What does it describe? (घृत = ghee)
options: A gruel cooked in a decoction of ghee
optionExplain: बहु- means 'much', not 'none'.
Right: बहु- + noun in a joined word = 'having much X'.
That meaning would need a locative like -निर्यूहे.
Destroying would need -घ्नी.
questions.explain: बहुतिला = with much sesame; बहुघृता = with much ghee.
questions.rule: बहु- + noun (feminine) = 'with much X'.
questions.teaches: बहु- + noun in a feminine joined word describes a gruel 'with much' of that thing.

questions.q: What does the yavāgū cooked with madirā remove, in line 2 of verse 27?
optionExplain: Those belong to the ten-roots gruel in line 1.
Thirst is in verse 24.
Right: पक्वाशयरुजापहा: removing pain of the lower gut.
Worms are in verse 23.
questions.explain: The second line pairs madirā with pakvāśaya pain.
questions.rule: Verse 27 line 2: madirā-cooked gruel removes lower-gut pain.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 27 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three conditions of line 1 and one cooking substance of line 2.
questions.rule: कास = cough; हिक्का = hiccup; श्वास = breathlessness; मदिरा = spirituous drink.

questions.q: The part of the body whose pain the second gruel removes is the ____ (type the Devanagari word before रुजा).
questions.explain: पक्वाशयरुजापहा = पक्वाशय + रुजा + अपहा, 'removing pain of the pakvāśaya'.
questions.teaches: The data glosses पक्वाशय as the lower gut; रुजा is 'pain'.
questions.rule: पक्वाशय = lower gut.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कफापहा?
optionExplain: पहा is not a word.
A visarga after अ before अ would be written कफोऽपहा.
ए + अ is written कफेऽपहा; the word here is कफ.
Right: अ + अ joins to आ, so कफ + अपहा is written कफापहा ('removing Kapha').
questions.explain: कफ is the last item of the first compound; अपहा means 'removing'.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: कफ + अपहा = कफापहा.

questions.q: Which does the ten-roots yavāgū of verse 27 remove?
optionExplain: Right: cough.
Right: hiccup.
Right: breathlessness.
That belongs to the madirā gruel.
Thirst is in verse 24.
questions.explain: Line 1 names cough, hiccup, breathlessness and Kapha.
questions.rule: Ten roots: cough, hiccup, breathlessness, Kapha.

questions.q: An invented compound is ज्वरतृष्णापहा, like कासहिक्काश्वासकफापहा. What does it say? (ज्वर = fever, तृष्णा = thirst)
optionExplain: Right: A string of nouns + अपहा = removing all of them.
तृष्णा is also in the compound and is removed.
अपहा means 'removing'.
अपहा is 'removing', not 'bringing'.
questions.explain: In the verse four conditions come before अपहा and all are removed.
questions.rule: N1 + N2 + ... + अपहा = removing all of N1, N2 ...
questions.teaches: Nouns joined before अपहा are all removed; ā/a + a joins to ā (तृष्णा + अपहा = तृष्णापहा).

questions.q: In verse 28, line 1, a gruel is cooked with vegetables, meats, sesame and black gram. What does it do?
optionExplain: Binding is the effect of the second-line gruel, साङ्ग्राहिकी.
Right: The line ends वर्चो निरस्यति: it expels the stool.
Destroying hunger is said of the gruel in verse 33.
That is said of the gruel with the ten roots in verse 27.
questions.explain: वर्चः is the stool and निरस्यति means 'expels': the first gruel clears the stool out.
questions.rule: Vegetables, meats, sesame, black gram: stool expelled.

questions.q: Match each ingredient word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words are all instrumental plurals: the things the gruel is cooked with.
questions.rule: शाकैः = with vegetables; मांसैः = with meats; तिलैः = with sesame; माषैः = with black gram.

questions.q: The word for 'binding' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 calls the second gruel साङ्ग्राहिकी, binding.
questions.teaches: साङ्ग्राहिकी ends in -ई, feminine, agreeing with the understood word यवागू (feminine). It names the effect: the gruel holds the stool.
questions.rule: साङ्ग्राहिकी = binding.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वर्चो निरस्यति?
options: वर्चः + निरस्यति: the visarga after अ becomes ओ before the voiced न
optionExplain: There is no separate word ओ here.
The visarga becomes र् after other vowels; after short अ it becomes ओ.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant gives ओ, so वर्चः + निरस्यति is written वर्चो निरस्यति.
That would give वर्चोऽनिरस्यति, and अनिरस्यति is not the verb in the verse.
questions.explain: वर्चो निरस्यति is वर्चः (stool, object) + निरस्यति (expels).
questions.rule: अः + voiced consonant → ओ (after अ).

questions.q: A gruel is cooked with jambu, mango, wood-apple, a sour item and bilva (the line-2 group). What is it considered?
optionExplain: That is the gruel of line 1, with vegetables, meats, sesame and black gram.
Being vṛṣya is said of a gruel in verse 32.
Being good for the throat is said of a gruel in verse 31.
Right: Line 2 says this group makes the gruel साङ्ग्राहिकी मता, considered binding.
questions.explain: मता is 'is considered'; the line 2 gruel is considered binding.
questions.rule: Line 2 group → binding.

questions.q: An invented phrase says मुद्गैः सिद्धा (मुद्ग = green gram). By the pattern of शाकैः सिद्धा, what does मुद्गैः tell us?
options: The gruel is cooked with green grams
The gruel is cooked in the broth of green gram only
Green gram is the effect the gruel has
Green gram is the person who cooks it
optionExplain: Right: The ending -ऐः (instrumental plural) means 'with', as in शाकैः 'with vegetables'.
'Broth' would need a word like रसैः; मुद्गैः names the grains themselves.
Effects are named by words like निरस्यति or साङ्ग्राहिकी.
The cook is not named; -ऐः marks what it is cooked with.
questions.explain: A word in -ऐः beside सिद्धा names what the gruel is cooked with.
questions.rule: X-ऐः सिद्धा = cooked with X.
questions.teaches: A plural in -ऐः before सिद्धा lists the ingredients 'with' which the gruel is cooked.

questions.q: A gruel is cooked with alkali, citraka, asafoetida and amlavetasa. What does verse 29 call it?
options: A remover of the ill effects of ghee
optionExplain: Binding is the effect of the second gruel of verse 28.
Right: Line 1 ends भेदिनी मता: considered bhedinī.
That is said of the gruel cooked in buttermilk in verse 30.
That is said of a gruel in verse 32.
questions.explain: The first gruel of verse 29 is भेदिनी, considered to loosen and purge.
questions.rule: Alkali, citraka, asafoetida, amlavetasa: bhedinī.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 29 to its meaning.
pairs: moving Vāta in its proper course
questions.explain: Two of these are effects, two are drugs named in the verse.
questions.rule: भेदिनी = purgative; वातानुलोमनी = moving Vāta in its proper course; हिङ्गु = asafoetida; अभया = harītakī.

questions.q: Type the Devanagari word for dry ginger in the instrumental plural (meaning with dry ginger): ____.
questions.explain: Line 2 names dry ginger as विश्वैः, the last of its three drugs.
questions.teaches: विश्वैः ends in -ऐः, the instrumental plural: 'with'. It is the same ending as शाकैः and तिलैः in verse 28.
questions.rule: विश्वैः = with dry ginger.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वातानुलोमनी?
options: वात + अनुलोमनी: अ + अ gives आ
optionExplain: नुलोमनी is not a word.
आनुलोमनी is not the word; the word is अनुलोमनी.
Right: Two short अ-sounds join into long आ, so वात + अनुलोमनी is written वातानुलोमनी.
That would be written वातोऽनुलोमनी, with ओऽ.
questions.explain: वातानुलोमनी = वात (Vāta) + अनुलोमनी (moving it along its proper course).
questions.rule: वात + अनुलोमनी = वातानुलोमनी.

questions.q: Which of these drugs does verse 29 itself name?
optionExplain: Right: citraka is in line 1.
Right: asafoetida is in line 1.
Right: long-pepper root is in line 2.
Sesame is in verse 28, not here.
Black gram is in verse 28, not here.
questions.explain: Citraka, asafoetida and pippalī root are all in verse 29; sesame and black gram belong to verse 28.
questions.rule: Verse 29 names citraka, asafoetida, pippalī root; sesame and māṣa are verse 28.

questions.q: The understood subject यवागू is feminine. Which word fills the blank in an invented line ending ____ शृता, saying the gruel kindles appetite (दीपन)?
optionExplain: That is masculine and does not agree with यवागू.
That is neuter and does not agree with यवागू.
That is not a form agreeing with a feminine यवागू.
Right: A word describing a feminine यवागू ends in -ई or -आ; दीपनी fits, like भेदिनी in line 1.
questions.explain: The describing words agree with the unwritten feminine subject यवागू.
questions.rule: Feminine subject: describing word in -ई/-आ (भेदिनी, मता, दीपनी).
questions.teaches: Words like सिद्धा, मता, भेदिनी all end in feminine forms because the understood subject, यवागू, is feminine.

questions.q: A gruel is cooked in buttermilk alone. Which trouble does verse 30 say it would remove?
optionExplain: Right: Line 1: तक्रसिद्धा यवागूः … घृतव्यापत्तिनाशिनी.
Oil's ill effects need buttermilk and oil-cake together (line 2).
That is said of the broth gruel in verse 31.
That is said of the gruel in verse 33.
questions.explain: घृतव्यापत्ति-नाशिनी = remover of the ill effects of ghee.
questions.rule: Buttermilk-cooked gruel: ghee's ill effects.

questions.q: Match each phrase of verse 30 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four phrases carry the verse.
questions.rule: तक्रसिद्धा = cooked in buttermilk; नाशिनी = remover; शस्ता = recommended; तक्रपिण्याकसाधिता = cooked with buttermilk and oil-cake.

questions.q: The word for 'oil-cake' inside तक्रपिण्याकसाधिता is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The compound is तक्र + पिण्याक + साधिता: buttermilk and oil-cake, cooked.
questions.teaches: In the compound तक्रपिण्याकसाधिता the first two parts are a pair (buttermilk and oil-cake) and साधिता is 'cooked'. The stem is पिण्याक.
questions.rule: पिण्याक = oil-cake, the residue left after pressing oil.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्याद्घृतव्यापत्तिनाशिनी?
options: स्यात् + घृतव्यापत्तिनाशिनी: त् becomes द् before the voiced घ
optionExplain: द्घृत… is not a word.
Right: A final त् turns into द् before a voiced consonant, so स्यात् + घृत… is written स्याद्घृत….
The verb is स्यात्, 'would be', not स्यः.
आघृत… is not a word in the verse.
questions.explain: स्यात् (would be) + घृतव्यापत्तिनाशिनी (remover of ghee's ill effects).
questions.rule: त् → द् before a voiced consonant: स्यात् + घृत → स्याद्घृत.

questions.q: A gruel is cooked with buttermilk and oil-cake. For which trouble does the verse recommend it?
optionExplain: Ghee's ill effects go with the gruel cooked in buttermilk alone.
That is said of the madirā gruel in verse 27.
Right: Line 2: तैलव्यापदि शस्ता स्यात् तक्रपिण्याकसाधिता.
Destroying hunger is said of a gruel in verse 33.
questions.explain: तैलव्यापदि = in the ill effects of oil; शस्ता = recommended.
questions.rule: Buttermilk + oil-cake gruel: oil's ill effects.

questions.q: An invented line ends मधुव्यापदि शस्ता (मधु = honey), built like तैलव्यापदि शस्ता. What does it say?
options: (A gruel) is made from the ill effects of honey
(A gruel) is recommended in the ill effects of honey
optionExplain: That would need a word like नाशिनी; शस्ता is 'recommended'.
-इ marks 'in', not 'made from'.
Nothing here mentions buttermilk or cooking.
Right: The ending -इ on व्यापदि is 'in', and शस्ता is 'recommended'.
questions.explain: X-व्यापदि शस्ता = recommended in the ill effects of X.
questions.rule: व्यापदि = in the ill effects; शस्ता = recommended.
questions.teaches: A locative in -इ before शस्ता names the trouble 'in' which the gruel is recommended.

questions.q: A gruel is cooked with broths of cow's meat and a sour item. What does the verse say it destroys?
optionExplain: Right: Line 1: गव्यमांसरसैः साम्ला विषमज्वरनाशिनी.
That is said of the gruel with upodikā and curd in verse 33.
That is said of the cock-broth gruel in verse 32.
That is said of the buttermilk gruel in verse 30.
questions.explain: विषमज्वरनाशिनी = destroyer of irregular fever.
questions.rule: Cow's-meat broth plus a sour item: irregular fever destroyed.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 31 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four phrases carry the verse.
questions.rule: गव्यमांसरसैः = with broths of bovine meat; साम्ला = with a sour ingredient; कण्ठ्या = good for the throat; यवानाम् = of barley.

questions.q: The word for 'good for the throat' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 begins with कण्ठ्या.
questions.teaches: कण्ठ्या ends in feminine -आ, like सिद्धा and शृता, agreeing with the understood यवागू. It names the effect on the throat.
questions.rule: कण्ठ्या = good for the throat.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पिप्पल्यामलकैः?
options: पिप्पली + आमलकैः: ई + आ becomes या
optionExplain: यामलकैः is not a word.
Right: Final ई before a different vowel turns into य्, so ई + आ gives य् + आ: पिप्पल्यामलकैः.
That would give पिप्पलिरामलकैः.
That would be written पिप्पल्यमलकैः; the second word is आमलकैः.
questions.explain: पिप्पल्यामलकैः = पिप्पली (long pepper) + आमलकैः (with āmalaka).
questions.rule: ई + different vowel → य् + vowel.

questions.q: The barley gruel that the verse calls good for the throat is cooked with which two items?
optionExplain: Those belong to the stool-expelling gruel of verse 28.
Those belong to the purgative gruel of verse 29.
Right: Line 2: पिप्पल्यामलकैः शृता.
Those belong to the gruel of verse 32.
questions.explain: The two drugs of the throat gruel are long pepper (पिप्पली) and āmalaka.
questions.rule: Throat gruel: barley, long pepper, āmalaka.

questions.q: An invented phrase says सलवणा यवागूः, built like साम्ला. What does सलवणा say about the gruel?
options: It is made of salt only
optionExplain: 'Without' would need अ- or निर्; स- means 'with'.
Removing would need a word like नाशिनी.
स- does not mean 'only'; it means 'with'.
Right: The prefix स- here means 'with', as साम्ला means 'with a sour item'; लवण is salt.
questions.explain: स- before a noun gives 'with' (साम्ला = with a sour item).
questions.rule: सX-ā = with X.
questions.teaches: A word starting with स- (as साम्ला) describes the gruel as 'with' that item.

questions.q: A gruel is cooked in the broth of the cock (ताम्रचूड). What does verse 32 say it removes?
optionExplain: Right: Line 1: रेतोमार्गरुजापहा, remover of pain in the seminal passage.
That is said of the upodikā-and-curd gruel in verse 33.
That is said of the buttermilk-and-oil-cake gruel in verse 30.
That is said of the cow's-meat broth gruel in verse 31.
questions.explain: रेतोमार्ग-रुजा-अपहा = remover of the pain of the seminal passage.
questions.rule: Cock-broth gruel: pain of the seminal passage removed.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 32 to its meaning.
pairs: in the broth of the cock
questions.explain: These phrases carry the two halves of the verse.
questions.rule: ताम्रचूडरसे = in the cock's broth; वृष्या = aphrodisiac; समाषविदला = with split black gram; घृतक्षीर = ghee and milk.

questions.q: The word for 'aphrodisiac, promoting virility' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 says वृष्या for the gruel with split black gram.
questions.teaches: वृष्या ends in feminine -आ, agreeing with the understood यवागू. It names the effect: the gruel promotes virility.
questions.rule: वृष्या = aphrodisiac.

questions.q: Which is the right split of घृतक्षीरोपसाधिता?
options: घृतक्षीर + उपसाधिता: अ + उ becomes ओ
optionExplain: पसाधिता is not a word.
Right: Short अ and उ join into ओ, so क्षीर + उपसाधिता is written क्षीरोपसाधिता.
ओपसाधिता is not a word; ओ is made by the joining.
That would be written घृतक्षीर उपसाधिता, with no ओ.
questions.explain: घृत (ghee) + क्षीर (milk) + उपसाधिता (cooked with).
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 32 itself?
optionExplain: Right: the cock's broth opens the verse.
Right: split black gram is in line 2.
Right: ghee is in line 2.
Curd is in verse 33.
Apāmārga is in verse 33.
questions.explain: The cock's broth, split māṣa and ghee are all here; curd and apāmārga come in verse 33.
questions.rule: Verse 32: cock broth, split māṣa, ghee, milk. Curd and apāmārga are in verse 33.

questions.q: Joining क्षीर and उदक (milk and water, invented) into one word by the same rule as क्षीर + उपसाधिता gives what?
optionExplain: औ is made from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not from अ + उ.
ऊ would come from उ + उ.
Right: अ at the end of क्षीर and उ at the start of उदक join into ओ.
The joining always makes a new vowel; this leaves उ unchanged.
questions.explain: अ + उ → ओ, as in क्षीरोपसाधिता.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: When a word ends in अ and the next starts with उ, they join into ओ.

questions.q: A gruel is cooked with upodikā and curd. What does verse 33 say it destroys?
optionExplain: Hunger is destroyed by the apāmārga gruel of line 2.
That is said of the cow's-meat gruel in verse 31.
That is said of the ten-roots gruel in verse 27.
Right: Line 1: सिद्धा मदविनाशिनी, destroyer of intoxication.
questions.explain: मद-विनाशिनी = destroyer of intoxication.
questions.rule: Upodikā and curd gruel: intoxication destroyed.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 33 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the effects and one ingredient.
questions.rule: मदविनाशिनी = destroying intoxication; क्षुधम् = hunger; हन्यात् = would destroy; गोधा = monitor lizard.

questions.q: The word for 'hunger' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 begins क्षुधं हन्यात्, 'would destroy hunger'.
questions.teaches: क्षुधम् ends in -म्, the accusative: hunger is what is destroyed, the object of हन्यात्.
questions.rule: क्षुधम् = hunger (object of 'would destroy').

questions.q: Which is the right split of हन्यादपामार्ग…?
options: हन्यात् + अपामार्ग…: त् becomes द् before a vowel
optionExplain: Right: A final त् turns into द् before a vowel as well as before a voiced consonant, so हन्यात् + अपामार्ग is written हन्यादपामार्ग.
दपामार्ग… is not a word.
आपामार्ग is not the word; the word is अपामार्ग.
The verb is हन्यात्, not हन्यः.
questions.explain: हन्यात् (would destroy) + अपामार्ग… (the next word begins with अपामार्ग).
questions.rule: त् → द् before a vowel.

questions.q: Which of these are named in line 2 of verse 33?
optionExplain: Right: apāmārga opens the compound.
Right: the broth of the godhā is in the compound.
Right: milk is in the line-2 compound.
Curd is in line 1, with upodikā.
Upodikā is in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 2 names apāmārga, milk and godhā's broth; curd and upodikā belong to line 1.
questions.rule: Line 2: apāmārga, milk, godhā-rasa. Line 1: upodikā, curd.

questions.q: An invented line says तृषं हन्यात् (तृष् = thirst), built like क्षुधं हन्यात्. What does it say?
optionExplain: Thirst is in the object form, not the subject.
Right: तृषम् is the object (what is destroyed) and हन्यात् is 'would destroy', as in क्षुधं हन्यात्.
The word is तृषम्, thirst, not क्षुधम्.
Passive meaning would need a different verb form; हन्यात् is active.
questions.explain: Object in -म् + हन्यात् = 'would destroy that object'.
questions.rule: X-म् हन्यात् = would destroy X.
questions.teaches: An object in -म् before हन्यात् names what the gruel 'would destroy'.

questions.q: Verse 34 closes the gruel list. How many gruels does it say have been enumerated?
optionExplain: The verse says अष्टाविंशतिः, which is twenty-eight.
The verse says twenty-eight, not thirty-two.
Right: The verse says अष्टाविंशतिः (twenty-eight) यवाग्वः परिकीर्तिताः.
The verse says twenty-eight, not eighteen.
questions.explain: अष्टाविंशतिः means twenty-eight, and यवाग्वः is 'gruels'.
questions.rule: The verse sums up twenty-eight gruels.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 34 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words hold the content of the verse.
questions.rule: यवाग्वः = gruels; परिकीर्तिताः = enumerated; पञ्चकर्माणि = the five karmas; भैषज्यसंग्रहः = compendium of remedies.

questions.q: The word for 'the five karmas' (accusative plural) is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 begins with पञ्चकर्माणि, then cāśritya.
questions.teaches: पञ्चकर्माणि is पञ्च (five) + कर्म (action) joined as one word, neuter plural in -आणि: what the compendium relies on (आश्रित्य).
questions.rule: पञ्चकर्माणि = the five karmas.

questions.q: Why does आश्रित्य end in -य (written -त्य) and not in -त्वा?
options: Because the verse is in the past
Because it follows the word च
Because it has the prefix आ- before the root √श्रि
optionExplain: Absolutives do not change for number.
Tense does not choose -य or -त्वा; the prefix does.
च is a separate word and does not affect the ending.
Right: An absolutive from a root with a prefix ends in -य (after a short-vowel root, written -त्य); without a prefix it ends in -त्वा.
questions.explain: आश्रित्य = आ + श्रि + -य, 'having relied on' (the -य shows as -त्य after the short vowel); the prefix आ- brings -य.
questions.rule: Root with prefix: absolutive in -य; without: -त्वा.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 34 itself say?
options: The compendium of remedies was stated relying on the five karmas
The five karmas are named one by one here
Each gruel is given with its dose
The gruels are all for fever
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: line 2.
The verse says only 'the five karmas'; it lists none.
The verse gives no dose.
Verse 34 names no disease at all.
questions.explain: Verse 34 gives the count of gruels and says what the compendium rests on; it names no karma, dose or disease.
questions.rule: Verse 34: 28 gruels, and a compendium resting on the five karmas; nothing more.

questions.q: By the rule seen in आश्रित्य, which is the right absolutive (having come) of √गम् with the prefix आ-?
optionExplain: Right: With a prefix the absolutive takes -य (shown as -त्य here), as in आश्रित्य; आ + गम् gives आगत्य.
-त्वा goes with a root without a prefix.
That is a past participle, 'come', not 'having come'.
That is 'he comes', a present form.
questions.explain: Prefix + root → absolutive in -य.
questions.rule: आ + √गम् → आगत्य.
questions.teaches: Absolutives of prefixed roots take -य (shown as -त्य in आश्रित्य, आगत्य); without a prefix the ending is -त्वा.

questions.q: According to verse 35, for what purpose is the medicine told again?
options: For knowledge that rests on the five karmas
optionExplain: That was the purpose of the earlier statement.
Right: Line 2: पञ्चकर्माश्रयज्ञानहेतोः … कीर्तितं पुनः.
The verse does not mention gruels.
The verse does not mention doses.
questions.explain: The earlier telling was for roots and fruits; the repeat is for knowledge resting on the five karmas.
questions.rule: Told again for the five-karma knowledge.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 35 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the sense of the earlier and repeated telling.
questions.rule: पूर्वम् = earlier; पुनः = again; यत् = which; औषधम् = medicine.

questions.q: The word for 'again' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 ends with पुनः.
questions.teaches: पुनः is an indeclinable: it does not change. It marks that this medicine had been told before.
questions.rule: पुनः = again.

questions.q: Which is the right split of हेतोस्तत्?
options: हेतोः + तत्: the visarga before त becomes स्
optionExplain: स्तत् is not a word.
र् appears before voiced sounds or vowels, not before त.
Right: A visarga before a dental त turns into स्, so हेतोः + तत् is written हेतोस्तत्.
अतत् is not the word; the word is तत्, 'that'.
questions.explain: हेतोः (for the sake of) + तत् (that medicine).
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स् + त.

questions.q: Which statements does verse 35 support?
options: The medicine was stated earlier for knowing roots and fruits
It is told again for knowledge resting on the five karmas
The verse names the earlier chapter
The verse lists the five karmas
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: line 2.
No chapter is named.
The five karmas are not listed here.
questions.explain: The verse names two purposes, earlier and now; it names no chapter and lists no karma.
questions.rule: Earlier: roots and fruits. Now: knowledge based on the five karmas.

questions.q: An invented line says औषधज्ञानहेतोर्गुणाः कीर्तिताः. By the pattern of ज्ञानहेतोः, what does औषधज्ञानहेतोः mean?
options: For the sake of making medicines
For the sake of knowledge of medicines
optionExplain: The word names a purpose for knowledge, not a lack of it.
ज्ञान is knowledge, not making.
हेतोः gives a purpose, not a time after.
Right: X-हेतोः is 'for the sake of X'; here X is औषधज्ञान, medicine-knowledge.
questions.explain: X-हेतोः = for the sake of X.
questions.rule: हेतोः = for the sake of.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -हेतोः names the purpose: 'for the sake of' what comes before it.

questions.q: According to verse 36, which physician is fit to carry out treatment by combinations of medicines?
options: One who is mindful, self-controlled, knows cause and application, and is resourceful
One with the most famous teachers
optionExplain: Right: These are the four qualities named in line 1.
The verse names no wealth or store of drugs.
The verse names no family or rank.
The verse names no teacher.
questions.explain: The verse sets four personal qualities before the physician may treat.
questions.rule: Mindful, knowing cause and application, self-controlled, resourceful.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 36 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the verse.
questions.rule: स्मृतिमान् = mindful; जितात्मा = self-controlled; प्रतिपत्तिमान् = resourceful; भिषक् = physician.

questions.q: The word for 'self-controlled' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 1 has जितात्मा, from जित (conquered) + आत्मा (self).
questions.teaches: जितात्मा is जित-आत्मा, a compound meaning one by whom the self has been mastered. It is one of the four qualities.
questions.rule: जितात्मा = self-controlled.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भिषगौषधसंयोगैः?
options: भिषक् + औषधसंयोगैः: क् becomes ग् before a vowel
optionExplain: There is no word गौषध….
Right: A final क् turns into ग् before a vowel, so भिषक् + औषध… is written भिषगौषध….
भिषः + औषध… would give भिष औषध…, but the word ends in क्, not a visarga.
षधसंयोगैः is not a word.
questions.explain: भिषक् (physician) + औषधसंयोगैः (by combinations of medicines).
questions.rule: क् → ग् before a vowel.

questions.q: Which of these are qualities of the physician named in verse 36?
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: line 1.
Right: line 1.
Wealth is not named.
Being honoured by a king is not named.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives mindfulness, self-control and resourcefulness (and knowing cause and application); wealth and royal honour are not named.
questions.rule: Qualities in verse 36: mindful, self-controlled, resourceful, knows cause and application.

questions.q: By the pattern of स्मृतिमान् (having memory), what does an invented धृतिमान् mean (धृति = steadiness)?
options: One who is steady in memory only
optionExplain: 'Lacking' would use a negative prefix, not -मान्.
Destroying would need a word like नाशकः.
Right: The ending -मान् means 'having', so धृतिमान् is 'having steadiness'.
-मान् adds 'having'; it does not bring in memory.
questions.explain: -मान् after a noun = 'having that'.
questions.rule: X-मान् = having X.
questions.teaches: A noun plus -मान् (स्मृतिमान्, प्रतिपत्तिमान्) names someone who has that quality.

questions.q: The sentence अथात आरग्वधीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः opens a chapter. What does it announce?
options: A royal command to start a journey
A list of drugs and their doses
The chapter named Āragvadhīya will now be expounded
optionExplain: Nothing in the sentence concerns a king or a journey.
No drug and no dose is named in this sentence.
No god is addressed; the sentence introduces a chapter.
Right: आरग्वधीयम् names the chapter and व्याख्यास्यामः promises the exposition.
questions.explain: अध्यायम् (chapter) and व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall expound) show that a chapter is being introduced.
questions.rule: The opening sentence names the chapter and promises to explain it.

questions.q: Match each word of the opening sentence to its meaning.
pairs: the chapter's name, relating to āragvadha
questions.explain: These words carry the whole announcement.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; आरग्वधीयम् = the title; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall expound.

questions.q: The word for 'chapter' in the sentence is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The sentence says अध्यायम् for 'chapter'.
questions.teaches: अध्यायम् ends in -म् (accusative): the chapter is what is to be expounded, the object of the verb.
questions.rule: अध्यायम् = chapter, the thing expounded.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अथातः?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ gives आ, so अथ + अतः is written अथातः.
There is no word तः here.
आतः is not a word in this sentence.
थातः is not a word.
questions.explain: अथातः is अथ ('now') + अतः ('therefore') joined by sandhi.
questions.rule: अथातः = अथ + अतः (अ + अ → आ).

questions.q: Which of these statements about the opening sentence are right?
options: व्याख्यास्यामः is first person plural: 'we shall expound'
आरग्वधीयम् is the name of the chapter
The sentence says the speaker is Bhagavān Ātreya
The sentence names the first drug of the chapter
optionExplain: Right: -मः marks 'we', and the data labels it first person plural future.
Right: it stands before अध्यायम् and names the chapter.
Right: the data glosses अथ as 'now'.
The speaker is named in verse 2, not in this sentence.
The sentence names only the chapter; the drug is not stated here.
questions.explain: The first three statements are in the sentence; the last two are not.
questions.rule: Verse 1: the formula, the title आरग्वधीयम् and the promise to expound.

questions.q: A made-up chapter opens अथातो नवौषधीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः. Which word names that chapter?
optionExplain: That is the verb 'we shall expound'.
Right: The title stands before अध्यायम्, as आरग्वधीयम् does here.
That is the word for 'chapter', not its name.
That is the opening 'now, therefore'.
questions.explain: In this frame the title sits just before अध्यायम्; the rest of the sentence is the same formula.
questions.rule: The opening frame is shared; the chapter's name stands before अध्यायम्.
questions.teaches: Once you know the frame, you can find a chapter's title by looking at the word before अध्यायम्.

questions.q: In इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः, who is the speaker?
options: The physician who applies the pastes
optionExplain: No physician is mentioned in this verse.
No pupil or question appears here.
Right: भगवान् आत्रेयः is the subject of आह, 'said'.
The reader is not named; the speaker is Ātreya.
questions.explain: आह is the verb 'said' and भगवान् आत्रेयः is its subject.
questions.rule: Verse 2: the speaker is named as भगवान् आत्रेयः.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words give 'Thus indeed said the venerable Ātreya'.
questions.rule: इति = thus; ह = indeed; आह = said; भगवान् = the venerable.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'said' in verse 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari, without स्म).
questions.explain: The verb is आह, which joins the particle स्म to give स्माह.
questions.teaches: आह is third person singular perfect of √अह्; the speaker is in the nominative.
questions.rule: आह = he said; the subject stands in the nominative.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भगवानात्रेयः?
optionExplain: नात्रेयः is not a word.
The name is Ātreya with long आ, not Atreya.
भगवान् is the nominative singular; it has no visarga ending here.
Right: The final न् of भगवान् stands before the vowel आ and simply joins it.
questions.explain: भगवानात्रेयः is two words, भगवान् ('the venerable') and आत्रेयः.
questions.rule: भगवानात्रेयः = भगवान् + आत्रेयः.

questions.q: What does स्माह combine?
options: स्म + आह, with अ + आ → आ
optionExplain: Right: The particle स्म ends in -अ, and आह begins with आ; the two join as आ.
अह is not the form here; the verb is आह.
माह is not a word.
याह is not a word.
questions.explain: स्माह is the particle स्म joined to the verb आह.
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ: स्म + आह → स्माह.

questions.q: A made-up line reads इति ह स्माह वैद्यः. Which word is the speaker?
optionExplain: That is the verb 'said'.
Right: Like आत्रेयः here, it is the nominative subject of आह.
That means 'thus'.
That is the particle 'indeed'.
questions.explain: The frame इति ह स्माह is followed by the speaker in the nominative: here वैद्यः.
questions.rule: After इति ह स्माह the speaker's name follows in the nominative.
questions.teaches: You can find the speaker of any such report by looking for the nominative after आह.

questions.q: What does verse 3 mainly contain?
options: A list of drug names with no verb; the sentence is finished in verse 6
optionExplain: The verse gives no dose.
Diseases are named in verse 7, not here.
Right: Every item is a drug name or a drug part, and no verb appears.
Ātreya is named in verse 2; this verse is a list.
questions.explain: The verse runs from आरग्वधः to करवीरकत्वक् as a plain list.
questions.rule: Verse 3: a list of drug names, completed by verse 6.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four items are descriptive or grammatical, not just plant names.
questions.rule: हरिद्रे = the two haridrās; श्र्याह्वः = the one named Śrī; सुराह्वः = the one named Sura; करवीरकत्वक् = bark of karavīraka.

questions.q: The word in the last compound of verse 3 for 'bark' is ____ (type the final word of करवीरकत्वक् in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The compound is करवीरक + त्वक्, 'bark of karavīraka'.
questions.teaches: In करवीरकत्वक् the first part names the plant and the last part names the part used: 'bark of karavīraka'.
questions.rule: X-त्वक् = bark of X.

questions.q: Why is the printed form करञ्जो वासा and not करञ्जः वासा?
options: The visarga is dropped before any consonant
करञ्ज is a feminine word and takes ओ
अः before a voiced consonant (here व) becomes ओ
optionExplain: The visarga does not drop here; it turns into ओ.
Only the visarga changes, not the ज.
करञ्जः is nominative singular masculine; the ओ is sandhi, not a case ending.
Right: The visarga after अ turns into ओ before a voiced sound.
questions.explain: करञ्जः + वासा → करञ्जो वासा. The same rule gives खदिरो धवः and निम्बो विडङ्गम्.
questions.rule: अः + घोष (voiced sound) → ओ.

questions.q: Which of these statements are right for verse 3?
options: It names the disease each drug serves
It gives the dose of each drug
Each of its two printed lines is one drug group
optionExplain: Right: it only lists names.
Right: the data labels it feminine nominative dual.
Diseases are named in verse 7.
No dose appears in this verse.
Right: the data says each printed line is one group, six groups in all with verses 4 and 5.
questions.explain: Verse 3 is a bare list of two drug groups; the verbs and the uses come later.
questions.rule: Verse 3: two drug groups, no verb, no use, no dose.

questions.q: A made-up line lists लते शुष्के as subjects, nominative case (लता = creeper, feminine in -आ). By the pattern of हरिद्रे, how many creepers?
optionExplain: Right: -आ nouns form a feminine nominative dual in -ए, as हरिद्रा gives हरिद्रे.
The singular would be लता.
The plural would be लताः.
The word names creepers; it does not negate them.
questions.explain: The pair लते शुष्के has the dual ending -ए on both words: 'two dry creepers'.
questions.rule: Feminine -आ stem, nominative dual: -ए (हरिद्रा → हरिद्रे).
questions.teaches: You can spot a dual of a feminine -आ noun by the ending -ए.

questions.q: What does verse 4 mainly contain?
options: The diseases that the drugs remove
More drug names, continuing the list of verse 3, with no verb
How the drugs are soaked in cow's bile
optionExplain: Diseases come in verse 7.
Right: Verse 4 continues the list; the sentence is finished in verse 6.
That is verse 6, not verse 4.
The title was given in verse 1.
questions.explain: The verse runs on from ग्रन्थिः to सुमनःप्रवालाः as a plain list.
questions.rule: Verse 4: the drug list goes on; no verb, use or dose.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 4 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two of these are dual pairs; the others are a plural and a compound.
questions.rule: वत्सकसप्तपर्णौ and गुग्गुलुकृष्णगन्धे are dual pairs; पीलूनि is a neuter plural; सुमनःप्रवालाः = sumanas + shoots.

questions.q: In सुमनःप्रवालाः the word meaning 'shoots' is ____ (type the stem or the printed word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The compound is सुमनस् + प्रवालाः, 'sumanas shoots'.
questions.teaches: The last member प्रवालाः is plural; it names the part used, as त्वक् does in verse 3.
questions.rule: X-प्रवालाः = shoots of X.

questions.q: Why is the first word printed ग्रन्थिश्च?
options: ग्रन्थि + श्च: the word श्च means 'and'
ग्रन्थि + शच: शच is a drug
ग्रन्थिः + च: a visarga before च becomes श्
ग्रन्थिस् + च: the visarga turns to स्
optionExplain: The word for 'and' is च; श्च is not a word.
शच is not a word in this verse.
Right: The visarga of ग्रन्थिः turns to श् before च.
Before च the visarga becomes श्, not स्.
questions.explain: ग्रन्थिः + च → ग्रन्थिश्च; the same rule gives धवः + च → धवश्च in verse 3.
questions.rule: Visarga + च → श् + च.

questions.q: Which of these appear in verse 4 itself?
optionExplain: Right: it is in the second line.
Right: कुष्ठं is in the second line.
Right: लशुनः is in the first line.
Not in verse 4; it is the last item of verse 3 (also in verse 10).
Not in verse 4; it is in verse 5 (also in verse 10).
questions.explain: The first three are in verse 4; the last two belong to verses 3 and 5.
questions.rule: Know which list each name belongs to: verse 3, 4 or 5.

questions.q: A made-up compound पुत्रशिष्यौ joins पुत्र (son) and शिष्य (pupil). By the pattern of वत्सकसप्तपर्णौ, what does it name?
options: A single person who is both son and pupil
A son and a pupil, a pair
optionExplain: A dual pair names two members, not one person.
The plural would end in -आः.
-औ marks two, so a singular 'a son of a pupil' does not fit.
Right: The ending -औ marks two members, as in वत्सक and सप्तपर्ण.
questions.explain: In a pair of masculine -अ words, the dual ends in -औ: पुत्र + शिष्य → पुत्रशिष्यौ.
questions.rule: Dvandva of two masculine -अ stems, nominative dual: -औ.
questions.teaches: Reading -औ at the end of a joined pair as 'the two, A and B' gives the list sense.

questions.q: What does verse 5 contain?
options: The last drug names of the three-verse list; no verb
The diseases that the drugs remove
The soaking in cow's bile and the mustard oil
optionExplain: Right: Verse 5 only lists names; the verb comes in verse 6.
Diseases are named in verse 7.
That is verse 6.
Equal powders are in verse 8.
questions.explain: The verse runs from वचा to सर्जाः as a plain list.
questions.rule: Verse 5: the list of verses 3 to 5 ends; no verb.

questions.q: Put these words of the second line of verse 5 in verse order.
questions.explain: The second line begins with मनःशिलाले and ends with the long compound.
questions.rule: Second line: मनःशिलाले, गृहधूम, एला, then the final compound.

questions.q: In गृहधूम the part meaning 'house' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: गृहधूम = गृह (house) + धूम (smoke).
questions.teaches: गृहधूम is a compound whose first part is 'house' and last part is 'smoke'.
questions.rule: गृह + धूम = house-smoke.

questions.q: Which is the right split of हरेणुस्त्रिवृता?
optionExplain: स्त्रिवृता is not a word.
Right: A visarga before त is written as स्, so हरेणुः + त्रिवृता → हरेणुस्त्रिवृता.
रिवृता is not a word.
The second word is त्रिवृता; the स् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: हरेणुः + त्रिवृता → हरेणुस्त्रिवृता.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स् + त.

questions.q: Which of these names are in verse 5 itself?
optionExplain: Right: it opens the verse.
Right: it is in the first line.
Right: it is inside the final compound.
That is in verse 3.
That is in verse 4.
questions.explain: The first three are in verse 5; निम्बः and लशुनः belong to verses 3 and 4.
questions.rule: Know which list each name belongs to: verse 3, 4 or 5.

questions.q: A made-up compound is मूलफलपत्राणि (मूल root, फल fruit, पत्र leaf). Read like the final compound of verse 5, what is it?
options: The leaf of the fruit of the root
A list: root, fruit and leaf, in the neuter plural
A root that bears fruit and leaf
optionExplain: That would be a chain of 'of'-links, not a list.
The three parts are separate items, as in verse 5's compound.
Right: Only the last member carries the ending, as with सर्जाः.
The compound lists three parts; it does not describe a root.
questions.explain: In a long list compound, the parts are joined without endings and the last one takes the ending.
questions.rule: Dvandva: A + B + C, with the ending only on the last member.
questions.teaches: A long unbroken string of names with one ending at the end can be read as a list 'A, B and C'.

questions.q: In verse 6, what is said to be done to the six drug groups first?
options: They are given a fixed dose
They are soaked in cow's bile (गोपित्तपीताः)
