Nothing in the verse speaks of burning.
Buttermilk (तक्र) appears in verse 9, not here.
Right: गोपित्तपीताः comes first among the processes the verse names.
questions.explain: The verse lists the processes in this order: soaked in cow's bile, ground again, prepared, combined with mustard oil.
questions.rule: Verse 6: soaked in cow's bile → ground again → prepared → mustard oil.

questions.q: Match each word or phrase of verse 6 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four pieces carry the preparation and the one who applies.
questions.rule: गोपित्तपीताः = soaked in cow's bile; पिष्टाः = ground; सर्षपतैलयुक्ताः = combined with mustard oil; भिषजा = by the physician.

questions.q: The word for 'powder-pastes' in verse 6 is चूर्ण + ____ (type the second part in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The compound is चूर्णप्रदेहाः = चूर्ण (powder) + प्रदेह (paste).
questions.teaches: चूर्णप्रदेहाः are pastes (pradeha) made from powder (cūrṇa).
questions.rule: चूर्ण + प्रदेह = powder-paste.

questions.q: Which is the right split of इत्यर्धरूपैः?
optionExplain: Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्: इति + अर्ध… → इत्यर्ध….
र्धरूपैः is not a word.
र्धरूपैः is not a word.
यर्धरूपैः is not a word.
questions.explain: इत्यर्धरूपैः is इति ('thus') + अर्धरूपैः ('by half-verse forms').
questions.rule: इ + असमान स्वर → य् + स्वर: इति + अर्ध… → इत्यर्ध….

questions.q: Put these steps of verse 6 in the order the verse states them.
questions.explain: The verse names the processes in this order; the last is the physician's application.
questions.rule: गोपित्तपीताः → पुनरेव पिष्टाः → सिद्धाः → सर्षपतैलयुक्ताः → भिषजा प्रयोज्याः.

questions.q: A made-up line reads तिलतैलयुक्तानि चूर्णानि प्रयोज्यानि (तिल sesame, तैल oil). What does it say?
options: Powders free of sesame oil are to be applied
Powders combined with sesame oil are to be applied
Sesame oil is to be ground from powders
Powders must not be applied with sesame oil
optionExplain: -युक्ताः means 'combined with', not 'free of'.
Right: -युक्ताः means 'combined with' and प्रयोज्याः 'to be applied', as in verse 6.
The line combines powders with oil; it does not make oil from powders.
प्रयोज्याः is a gerundive 'to be applied', not a prohibition.
questions.explain: The frame is X-तैलयुक्तानि चूर्णानि प्रयोज्यानि: 'powders combined with X-oil are to be applied'. This is a grammar drill, not a medical statement.
questions.rule: X-तैलयुक्तानि + प्रयोज्यानि = combined with X-oil, to be applied.
questions.teaches: Once the frame is clear, you can read 'combined with … oil, to be applied' in any similar line.

questions.q: What does verse 7 say the applied pastes would do?
options: Give no result for a long time
Quickly destroy the named troubles in people
Give the dose for each trouble
optionExplain: The verse says अचिरात्, 'quickly'.
The verb is हन्युः, 'would destroy'.
Right: हन्युः means 'they would destroy' and अचिरात् 'quickly'.
No dose is given in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse names the troubles as objects of हन्युः and says अचिरात् for the speed.
questions.rule: Verse 7: applied, they would quickly destroy the named troubles.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 7 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the force of the verse.
questions.rule: कृच्छ्राणि = difficult; अचिरात् = quickly; हन्युः = they would destroy; सपामाम् = together with pāmā.

questions.q: The word in verse 7 for 'quickly' is ____ (type the form with त् or the printed form in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The word is अचिरात्; in the printed text it appears as अचिरान् before नराणाम्.
questions.teaches: अचिरात् is an ablative used as an adverb: 'quickly'. Before the न of नराणाम् its त् becomes न्.
questions.rule: अचिरात् + नराणाम् → अचिरान्नराणाम्.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अचिरान्नराणाम्?
optionExplain: अन्नराणाम् is not a word.
That would leave a single न; the printed form has न्न.
राणाम् is not a word.
Right: त् + न → न्न, so अचिरात् + नराणाम् is written अचिरान्नराणाम्.
questions.explain: अचिरात् ('quickly') + नराणाम् ('of men') → अचिरान्नराणाम्.
questions.rule: त् before न becomes न्: अचिरात् + न… → अचिरान्न….

questions.q: Which of these are said by verse 7?
options: The pastes would quickly destroy the troubles in people
Kuṣṭhas are listed, and they are called difficult
Kiṭibha is listed together with dadru
The pastes are soaked in cow's bile
The pastes are fixed at one dose
optionExplain: Right: हन्युः … अचिरात् … नराणाम्.
Right: कुष्ठानि कृच्छ्राणि.
Right: किटिभं सदद्रु.
That is verse 6.
No dose appears in the verse.
questions.explain: The first three follow from verse 7; the soaking is in verse 6 and no dose is given anywhere here.
questions.rule: Verse 7: the troubles and the speed; the preparation is in verse 6.

questions.q: A made-up line reads सकण्डूं पिडकां हन्युः (कण्डू itching, पिडका boil). By the pattern of सपामाम्, what would they destroy?
options: A boil in place of itching
A boil that comes after itching
optionExplain: Right: सकण्डूम् means 'together with itching', as सपामाम् means 'together with pāmā'.
स- means 'together with', not 'in place of'.
The line destroys the boil; the itching is joined to it.
The prefix स- gives 'together with', not an order in time.
questions.explain: स- before a noun gives 'together with'. This is a grammar drill, not a medical statement.
questions.rule: स-X = together with X (सदद्रु, सपामाम्).
questions.teaches: The prefix स- turns a name into 'together with that name' in lists of troubles.

questions.q: What does verse 8 tell one to do with the drugs it lists?
options: Make equal powders of them (चूर्णानि समानि कुर्यात्)
optionExplain: Nothing in the verse speaks of burning.
Right: The verb कुर्यात् means 'one should make' and समानि 'equal'.
The soaking is in verse 6, a different formulation.
The verse names no boiling and no oil.
questions.explain: The last words of the second line state the instruction: equal powders are to be made.
questions.rule: Verse 8: make equal powders of the listed drugs.

questions.q: Match each form in verse 8 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two of these are dual pairs; the other two are the neuter plurals of the instruction.
questions.rule: हरिद्रे and निम्बाश्वगन्धे are dual; चूर्णानि = powders; समानि = equal.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'one should make' in verse 8 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verb is कुर्यात्, third person singular optative of √कृ.
questions.teaches: कुर्यात् is an optative: 'one should make'. It is the verb that governs चूर्णानि समानि.
questions.rule: कुर्यात् = one should make.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निम्बाश्वगन्धे?
optionExplain: श्वगन्धे is not a word.
निम्बः + अश्वगन्धे would give निम्बोऽश्वगन्धे, not निम्बाश्वगन्धे.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, so निम्ब + अश्वगन्धे is written निम्बाश्वगन्धे.
The second word is अश्वगन्धे with short अ.
questions.explain: निम्बाश्वगन्धे is a joined pair, निम्ब and अश्वगन्धे.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: निम्ब + अश्वगन्धे → निम्बाश्वगन्धे.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 8 say?
options: The powders are to be made equal
The instruction is in the optative: 'one should make'
Mustard is named together with the other drugs
The weight of each drug is given
The powders are ground with buttermilk
optionExplain: Right: चूर्णानि समानि.
Right: कुर्यात्.
Right: ससर्षपम् means 'together with mustard'.
The verse says only 'equal', with no weight.
Buttermilk is in verse 9.
questions.explain: The first three are in verse 8; the weight is nowhere given, and the buttermilk comes next.
questions.rule: Verse 8: equal powders; no weight; the buttermilk is in verse 9.

questions.q: A made-up line reads चूर्णानि सूक्ष्माणि कुर्यात् (सूक्ष्म = fine). What does it say?
options: One should not make the powders fine
One should make fine ones out of the powders
The powders have made it fine
One should make the powders fine
optionExplain: कुर्यात् says 'one should make', not a prohibition.
सूक्ष्माणि describes the powders; it is not a new product.
कुर्यात् is the optative 'one should make', not a statement of a past result.
Right: सूक्ष्माणि agrees with चूर्णानि like समानि, and कुर्यात् is 'one should make'.
questions.explain: The frame is चूर्णानि X कुर्यात्: the adjective X agrees with चूर्णानि and the verb says 'one should make'. This is a grammar drill, not a medical statement.
questions.rule: चूर्णानि + adjective + कुर्यात् = one should make the powders X.
questions.teaches: An adjective that agrees with चूर्णानि (neuter plural) says what the powders should be like.

questions.q: In verse 9, what is the body like before the rubbing, and with what are the powders ground?
options: Smeared with oil; the powders are ground with buttermilk
Dry and bare; the powders are ground with cow's bile
Smeared with oil; the powders are ground with mustard
Washed with water; the powders are ground with milk
optionExplain: Right: तैलाक्तम् is 'smeared with oil' and तक्रपिष्टैः 'ground with buttermilk'.
Cow's bile belongs to verse 6, and the body is oil-smeared here.
The grinding is with buttermilk (तक्र).
Neither washing nor milk appears in the verse.
questions.explain: तैलाक्तं शरीरम् is the oil-smeared body, and तक्रपिष्टैः says the powders are ground with buttermilk.
questions.rule: Verse 9: oil-smeared body; powders ground with buttermilk.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 9 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the method and the result.
questions.rule: तक्रपिष्टैः = ground with buttermilk; तैलाक्तम् = smeared with oil; उद्वर्तयितुम् = to rub; शमम् = calm.

questions.q: In तक्रपिष्टैः the part meaning 'buttermilk' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: तक्रपिष्टैः = तक्र (buttermilk) + पिष्टैः (ground).
questions.teaches: The compound तक्रपिष्टैः says what the powders are ground with: buttermilk.
questions.rule: तक्र + पिष्टैः = ground with buttermilk.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तैस्तक्रपिष्टैः?
optionExplain: स्तक्रपिष्टैः is not a word.
Right: A visarga before त is written as स्, so तैः + तक्र… → तैस्तक्र….
स्तक्रपिष्टैः is not a word.
तैस is not a word; the pronoun is तैः.
questions.explain: तैः is 'by those' (instrumental plural), joined to तक्रपिष्टैः.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स् + त.

questions.q: Which of these are said to subside (शमं व्रजन्ति) in verse 9?
optionExplain: Right: कण्डूः.
Right: शोफाः.
Right: कुष्ठानि.
Bhagandara is in verse 7, not in this verse.
Apacī is in verse 7, not in this verse.
questions.explain: Verse 9 names the itching, boils with koṭha, kuṣṭhas and swellings.
questions.rule: Know which list each trouble belongs to: verse 7 or verse 9.

questions.q: A made-up phrase is घृताक्तं पात्रम् (घृत ghee, पात्र vessel). By the pattern of तैलाक्तम्, what is it?
optionExplain: अक्त means smeared, not filled.
अक्त does not mean 'free of'.
Right: -अक्त means 'smeared with', as तैलाक्तम् (तैल + अक्तम्) is 'smeared with oil'.
The phrase describes the vessel, not what the ghee is for.
questions.explain: X + अक्तम् reads 'smeared with X'. This is a grammar drill, not a medical statement.
questions.rule: घृत + अक्तम् → घृताक्तम्; X-अक्त = smeared with X (अ + अ → आ).
questions.teaches: Once -अक्त is clear, you can read any 'smeared with X' phrase like तैलाक्तम्.

questions.q: What does verse 10 mainly contain?
options: A rule for making powders equal
A list of drug names, with no verb
optionExplain: That is verse 8.
Troubles are named in verses 7 and 9.
The speaker is named in verse 2.
Right: The verse is a long compound of names plus five more items.
questions.explain: The verse runs from कुष्ठ… to करवीरकत्वक् as a plain list.
questions.rule: Verse 10: a list of drug names; no verb, use or dose.

questions.q: Match each item of verse 10 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two items are 'X-of' compounds, one is a pair, one is a name kept as it is.
questions.rule: सर्जरसः = sap of sarja; करवीरकत्वक् = bark of karavīraka; मनःशिलाले = manaḥśilā and āla; सौगन्धिकम् = saugandhika.

questions.q: In सर्जरसः the second part, meaning resin or sap, is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: सर्जरसः = सर्ज + रसः, 'the resin or sap of sarja'.
questions.teaches: सर्जरसः names a part of the sarja plant; the second member रस is the sap or resin.
questions.rule: सर्ज + रस = sap of sarja.

questions.q: Why is the printed form सर्जरसो विडङ्गम् and not सर्जरसः विडङ्गम्?
options: अः before a voiced consonant (here व) becomes ओ
The visarga drops before any consonant
सर्जरस is a feminine word and takes ओ
optionExplain: Right: The visarga after अ turns into ओ before a voiced sound.
It does not drop here; it turns into ओ.
Only the visarga changes, not the स.
सर्जरसः is nominative singular masculine; the ओ is sandhi.
questions.explain: सर्जरसः + विडङ्गम् → सर्जरसो विडङ्गम्; the same rule gives करञ्जो वासा in verse 3.
questions.rule: अः + घोष (voiced sound) → ओ.

questions.q: Which of these items appear in verse 10 itself?
optionExplain: Right: it is in the second line.
Right: it ends the verse.
Right: it is inside the opening compound.
Buttermilk is in verse 9.
Mustard oil is in verse 6.
questions.explain: The first three are in verse 10; buttermilk and mustard oil are in other verses.
questions.rule: Know which verse each name belongs to.

questions.q: A made-up phrase is इक्षुरसः (इक्षु sugarcane). By the pattern of सर्जरसः, what is it?
optionExplain: The phrase names the juice of the cane, not a cane made of juice.
Right: X-रसः reads 'sap or juice of X', as सर्जरसः is the sap of sarja.
Bark is त्वक्, as in करवीरकत्वक्; this phrase ends in रसः.
रसः is not negated here.
questions.explain: The compound pairs a plant with its sap: X-रसः. This is a grammar drill, not a medical statement.
questions.rule: X-रसः = sap or juice of X; X-त्वक् = bark of X.
questions.teaches: Plant-part compounds like सर्जरसः and करवीरकत्वक् read 'the part of the plant'.

questions.q: On what kind of body does verse 11 say the powders are to be applied?
options: One whose body has been bathed in cold water
One whose body is covered with ash
One whose body is smeared with oil
One who has been given an emetic
optionExplain: No water or bath is mentioned; the word is तैल, oil.
Ash is not mentioned in this verse.
Right: तैलाक्तगात्रस्य = of one whose body (गात्र) is smeared (आक्त) with oil (तैल).
No emetic or other treatment is named in this verse.
questions.explain: The first word, तैलाक्तगात्रस्य, gives the condition of the body: smeared with oil.
questions.rule: Verse 11: powders for dusting, on an oil-smeared body.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 11 to its meaning.
pairs: of one whose body is smeared with oil
questions.explain: These four words carry the application and the result.
questions.rule: तैलाक्तगात्रस्य = of the oil-smeared body; चूर्णानि = powders; अवचूर्णनार्थम् = for dusting; शान्तिम् = calm.

questions.q: The last disease named in the verse, next to चैव, is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 ends the list with पामा विचर्चिका चैव.
questions.teaches: The disease names दद्रूः, पामा, विचर्चिका are nominative singular; किटिभानि is neuter plural. They are the subjects that come to rest.
questions.rule: The things that come to rest (शान्तिम् एति) are in the nominative.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चूर्णान्येतानि?
optionExplain: येतानि is not a word.
The second word is एतानि, 'these', not अतानि.
अन्येतानि is not a word.
Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्, and the vowel joins it: इ + ए gives ये.
questions.explain: चूर्णान्येतानि = चूर्णानि ('powders') + एतानि ('these').
questions.rule: इ + असमान स्वर → य् + स्वर: चूर्णानि + एतानि → चूर्णान्येतानि.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 11 say?
options: The body is smeared with oil first
Dadru with itching is among those that come to rest
The ingredients of each powder are listed
The powders are ground with buttermilk
optionExplain: Right: दद्यादवचूर्णनार्थम्.
Right: तैलाक्तगात्रस्य.
Right: दद्रूः सकण्डूः ... शान्तिम्.
The verse lists no ingredients; it points to powders given earlier.
Buttermilk is not mentioned in verse 11.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the way of use and the condition of the body; line 2 gives the diseases that come to rest.
questions.rule: Verse 11: oil-smeared body, dusting, four diseases come to rest.

questions.q: A made-up phrase reads घृताक्तगात्रस्य नरस्य. Following तैलाक्तगात्रस्य, what does it mean?
options: Of a man whose body is smeared with ghee
Of a man who eats ghee
Of ghee smeared on the body of a man's friend
Of a man whose body is smeared with oil
optionExplain: Right: Same compound as तैलाक्तगात्र, with घृत (ghee) in place of तैल (oil).
आक्त means smeared, and गात्र means body; eating is not in the compound.
The compound describes the man himself: his body is smeared.
That is the verse's compound; here the first part is घृत, ghee.
questions.explain: The compound is X-आक्त-गात्र: 'one whose body is smeared with X'. Only X changes, and the genitive -स्य is kept.
questions.rule: X-आक्तगात्रस्य = of one whose body is smeared with X.
questions.teaches: Once you know this compound, any 'X-आक्तगात्र' reads as 'body smeared with X'.

questions.q: What does line 1 of verse 12 call the preparation of manaḥśilā, āla, peppers, oil and arka milk?
options: An enema for the lower gut
optionExplain: No gruel is mentioned; the word is प्रदेहः.
Right: कुष्ठहरः प्रदेहः = a pradeha (paste) removing kuṣṭha.
No enema is named here.
Nothing in the verse speaks of vomiting.
questions.explain: The first line closes with कुष्ठहरः प्रदेहः.
questions.rule: Verse 12, line 1: these ingredients make a kuṣṭha-removing pradeha.

questions.q: Put these four items in the order they stand in line 1 of verse 12.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins मनःशिलाले मरिचानि तैलमार्कं पयः.
questions.rule: मनःशिलाले → मरिचानि → तैलमार्कं → पयः.

questions.q: The word in line 2 meaning 'likewise' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 reads ... लोध्रं च तद्वत् समनःशिलं स्यात्.
questions.teaches: तद्वत् is an indeclinable: 'in that way, likewise'. It links the second list to the first pradeha.
questions.rule: तद्वत् = likewise; the second list is made on the pattern of the first.

questions.q: Which is the right split of समनःशिलम्?
optionExplain: नःशिलम् is not a word.
There is no long सा here; the prefix is short स.
Right: स- as the first part means with: 'with manaḥśilā'.
समन is not a word, and शिल alone is not the drug named here.
questions.explain: समनःशिलम् = स ('with') + मनःशिलम् ('manaḥśilā'): the second list is to be taken with manaḥśilā.
questions.rule: स- + noun = 'with that noun'.

questions.q: Which of these stand in line 2 of verse 12?
optionExplain: Right: तुत्थं opens line 2.
Right: लोध्रं च is in line 2.
Right: मरिचानि is named in both lines.
Oil (तैलम्) is in line 1, not line 2.
Arka milk (आर्कं पयः) is in line 1, not line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 names tuttha, viḍaṅga, peppers, kuṣṭha and lodhra, then tells us to take them with manaḥśilā.
questions.rule: Line 2: तुत्थ, विडङ्ग, मरिच, कुष्ठ, लोध्र.

questions.q: A made-up phrase reads तुत्थं सलोध्रं स्यात्. Following समनःशिलं स्यात्, what does it say?
options: Tuttha should be taken without lodhra
Tuttha should be taken in place of lodhra
Tuttha should be taken with lodhra
optionExplain: स- means with, not without.
सलोध्रम् means with lodhra, not instead of it.
The phrase joins two drugs; it does not say they are the same.
Right: सलोध्रम् = स ('with') + लोध्रम्, just as समनःशिलम् is 'with manaḥśilā'.
questions.explain: स + लोध्रम् gives सलोध्रम् (अ-ending stem, no sandhi change): 'with lodhra'.
questions.rule: सX = with X, so 'A सX स्यात्' = 'A should be with X'.
questions.teaches: The स- rule lets you read any 'सX' in a drug list as 'together with X'.

questions.q: In what liquid is the second preparation of verse 13 ground?
optionExplain: Right: गोमूत्रपिष्टम् = ground (पिष्ट) in cow's urine (गोमूत्र).
Kapittha juice is used for the first preparation, in line 1.
Buttermilk is not mentioned in this verse.
Arka milk is not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 says गोमूत्रपिष्टं च परः प्रदेहः: ground in cow's urine, another pradeha.
questions.rule: Verse 13: first preparation with kapittha juice; second ground in cow's urine.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 13 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words give the liquids and the way each paste is made.
questions.rule: रसेन = with the juice; लेपः = paste; सकुष्ठम् = with kuṣṭha; गोमूत्रपिष्टम् = ground in cow's urine.

questions.q: Rasāñjana is mixed with the juice of ____ (type the fruit's name in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 1 says युक्तं कपित्थस्य रसेन: mixed with the juice (रस) of kapittha.
questions.teaches: कपित्थस्य is genitive singular ('of kapittha'); रसेन is instrumental ('with the juice').
questions.rule: 'X-स्य रसेन' = 'with the juice of X': genitive for the source, instrumental for the means.

questions.q: Which is the right split of करञ्जबीजैडगजम्?
optionExplain: डगजम् is not a word.
Right: अ + ए gives ऐ: करञ्जबीज + एडगजम् is written करञ्जबीजैडगजम्.
ऐडगजम् is not a word; the drug is एडगज.
With a visarga the two words would stay apart: करञ्जबीज एडगजम्.
questions.explain: करञ्जबीजैडगजम् = करञ्जबीज ('karañja seeds') + एडगजम् ('eḍagaja').
questions.rule: अ + ए → ऐ: करञ्जबीज + एडगजम् → करञ्जबीजैडगजम्.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 13 say?
options: Rasāñjana is taken with prapunāḍa seeds
The first preparation is mixed with kapittha juice and is called a lepa
The second preparation contains karañja seeds, eḍagaja and kuṣṭha
The verse names the disease these are for
Mustard oil is added to the second preparation
optionExplain: Right: सप्रपुनाडबीजम्.
Right: युक्तं कपित्थस्य रसेन लेपः.
Right: करञ्जबीजैडगजं सकुष्ठम्.
No disease is named in verse 13.
Mustard oil is not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the first preparation and its liquid; line 2 gives the second and its liquid.
questions.rule: Verse 13: two preparations, kapittha juice and cow's urine; no disease.

questions.q: A made-up phrase reads लोध्रं तक्रपिष्टं च लेपः (तक्र = buttermilk). Following गोमूत्रपिष्टम्, what does it say about the lodhra?
options: It is mixed with buttermilk after cooking
It is the buttermilk that has been ground
It is ground in cow's urine
optionExplain: पिष्ट means ground, not cooked.
In X-पिष्टम्, the thing ground is the noun described (lodhra), and X is the liquid.
Right: तक्रपिष्टम् = ground (पिष्ट) in buttermilk (तक्र), like गोमूत्रपिष्टम् with cow's urine.
That is the verse's phrase; the made-up one has तक्र, buttermilk.
questions.explain: X-पिष्ट is a compound 'ground in X'. Here X is तक्र, buttermilk, so lodhra is ground in buttermilk. This is a grammar drill.
questions.rule: X-पिष्टम् = ground in X.
questions.teaches: Any 'liquid + पिष्ट' compound in these verses reads as 'ground in that liquid'.

questions.q: What does verse 14 tell the reader to do with the listed items?
options: Burn them to ash and drink the ash
Prepare a lepa of them, mixed with tila-kṣāra
optionExplain: No gruel is mentioned; the object is लेपम्, a paste.
No enema is mentioned in this verse.
Nothing is said about burning or drinking.
Right: लेपं तिलक्षारयुतं विदध्यात् = one should prepare a lepa mixed with sesame alkali.
questions.explain: The accusative items are the ingredients; the verb विदध्यात् and its object लेपम् give the instruction.
questions.rule: Verse 14: prepare a lepa of these, with tila-kṣāra.

questions.q: Match each phrase of verse 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each phrase names one ingredient or the thing it is mixed with.
questions.rule: उभे हरिद्रे = both haridrās; कुटजस्य बीजम् = kuṭaja seed; सुमनःप्रवालान् = sumanas shoots; तिलक्षारयुतम् = mixed with tila-kṣāra.

questions.q: The verb of verse 14, meaning 'one should prepare', is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The last word of the verse is विदध्यात्.
questions.teaches: विदध्यात् is the third person singular optative of वि-√धा: 'one should prepare'. It governs the object लेपम्.
questions.rule: The optative -यात् gives 'one should'; the accusatives are what is prepared or used.

questions.q: In उभे हरिद्रे, what does the ending -ए of हरिद्रे show?
optionExplain: Right: उभे means 'both' (two); हरिद्रे is accusative dual.
उभे 'both' needs two things.
उभे means both of two, not many.
The genitive in this verse is कुटजस्य; हरिद्रे is the object, accusative.
questions.explain: उभे हरिद्रे = the two haridrās (accusative dual feminine).
questions.rule: Feminine -आ stems: dual -ए (nominative/accusative).

questions.q: Which of these does verse 14 say?
options: Karañja seed is one of the items
The bark of hayamāraka is one of the items
The lepa is mixed with tila-kṣāra
The verse says which plant hayamāraka is
The verse gives the quantity of each item
optionExplain: Right: करञ्जबीजम्.
Right: त्वचं हयमारकस्य.
Right: तिलक्षारयुतम्.
The identity of hayamāraka is not given.
No quantity is named.
questions.explain: Line 1 and the start of line 2 list the ingredients; the end of line 2 gives the mixing and the verb.
questions.rule: Verse 14: ingredients, tila-kṣāra, verb विदध्यात्; no identity and no quantity.

questions.q: A made-up phrase reads उभे बले दद्यात्. Following उभे हरिद्रे, what does it say?
options: One should give of the balā
optionExplain: उभे 'both' shows two.
Right: उभे बले is like उभे हरिद्रे: feminine -आ stem in the dual, accusative.
उभे does not mean many.
बले is not a genitive; दद्यात् takes an object, here in the dual.
questions.explain: बला (feminine, -आ) has dual -ए, as हरिद्रा has हरिद्रे. उभे also marks two. This is a grammar drill.
questions.rule: Feminine -आ stems: dual in -ए; उभे = both.
questions.teaches: You can now spot a pair of feminine drugs by -ए plus उभे or द्वे.

questions.q: With what liquid are the powders of verse 15 to be prepared?
optionExplain: Cow's urine is in verse 13, not in this verse.
Buttermilk is not named in this verse.
Right: तुषोदकेन = with husk-water (तुष + उदक).
Mustard oil is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The last word, तुषोदकेन, is the instrumental of the liquid.
questions.rule: Verse 15: powders prepared with tuṣodaka.

questions.q: Put these four items in the order they stand in verse 15.
questions.explain: सलोमशः stands in line 1 (after सकुष्ठात्); line 2 then runs ग्रन्थिश्च, भौर्जः, करवीरमूलं.
questions.rule: सलोमशः → ग्रन्थिश्च → भौर्जः → करवीरमूलं.

questions.q: The word in line 2 meaning 'to be prepared' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: It stands in line 2, second word from the end.
questions.teaches: साध्यानि is a gerundive, neuter plural, agreeing with चूर्णानि: 'to be prepared'.
questions.rule: साध्यानि = to be prepared (gerundive of √साध्).

questions.q: Which is the right split of तुषोदकेन?
optionExplain: दकेन is not a word.
केन is a word ('by what'), but तुषोद is not a word here.
ओदकेन is not a word.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, so तुष + उदकेन is written तुषोदकेन.
questions.explain: तुषोदकेन = तुष ('husk') + उदकेन ('with water').
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 15 say?
options: The root of karavīra is among the items
The powders are to be prepared with tuṣodaka
The verse names the disease they are for
The powders are to be ground with buttermilk
optionExplain: Right: मनःशिला opens the verse.
Right: करवीरमूलम्.
Right: चूर्णानि साध्यानि तुषोदकेन.
No disease is named in verse 15.
Buttermilk is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse lists the items, then says the powders are to be prepared with husk-water.
questions.rule: Verse 15: items, powders, husk-water; no disease.

questions.q: A made-up compound तिल + उदकेन (sesame-water, with). Using the rule of तुष + उदकेन, how is it written joined?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in तुषोदकेन: तिल + उदकेन → तिलोदकेन.
अ + औ gives औ, not अ + उ.
ऊ would come from उ + उ, not अ + उ.
The two vowels do merge; they are not left side by side.
questions.explain: तिल ends in short अ; उदकेन starts with उ. अ + उ → ओ. This is a grammar drill with an invented word.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: The same अ + उ → ओ rule joins any -अ stem to a following उ-word.

questions.q: What name does verse 16 give to this application?
optionExplain: Tuṣodaka is the husk-water of verse 15, not the name of this application.
Right: दर्वीप्रलेपं प्रवदन्ति: they call it the darvī-pralepa.
Āḍhaka is a measure named in the verse, not the name of the lepa.
Karṣa is a measure (a weight) named in the verse, not the name of the lepa.
questions.explain: The second line says: they call this lepa the darvī-pralepa.
questions.rule: Verse 16: the lepa is named darvī-pralepa.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 16 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the naming and the praise.
questions.rule: प्रवदन्ति = they call; परम् = supreme; कुष्ठनिसूदनाय = for destroying kuṣṭha; दर्वीप्रलेपम् = the darvī-pralepa.

questions.q: The last word of verse 16, meaning 'for destroying kuṣṭha', is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse ends परं कुष्ठनिसूदनाय.
questions.teaches: -आय is the dative: 'for'. So कुष्ठनिसूदनाय is 'for the destroying of kuṣṭha'. Some texts may spell it with ष (निषूदन).
questions.rule: Dative -आय = for (the purpose of).

questions.q: Which is the right split of कर्षोद्धृतानि?
optionExplain: द्धृतानि is not a word.
ओद्धृतानि is not a word.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, so कर्ष + उद्धृतानि is written कर्षोद्धृतानि.
A visarga would keep the words apart, not join them as ओ.
questions.explain: कर्षोद्धृतानि = कर्ष ('karṣa') + उद्धृतानि ('taken out').
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: कर्ष + उद्धृतानि → कर्षोद्धृतानि.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 16 say or imply?
options: कर्षोद्धृतानि points back to the powders of verse 15
It is called supreme for destroying kuṣṭha
The verse says how many karṣas to take
The powders are ground in cow's urine
optionExplain: Right: it is neuter plural with no noun here, and agrees with चूर्णानि of verse 15.
Right: दर्वीप्रलेपं प्रवदन्ति.
Right: परं कुष्ठनिसूदनाय.
Karṣa and āḍhaka are named as measures; no number is given.
Cow's urine is in verse 13, not here.
questions.explain: Verse 16 uses the powders of 15, names the lepa, and states its purpose.
questions.rule: Verse 16: powders of 15, darvī-pralepa, supreme against kuṣṭha.

questions.q: A made-up phrase reads व्रणनिसूदनाय लेपः (व्रण = wound). Following कुष्ठनिसूदनाय, what is the lepa for?
optionExplain: In the compound, the destroying is aimed at व्रण; व्रण is not the destroyer.
The ending -आय gives purpose, 'for', not cause.
That is the verse's phrase; the made-up one names व्रण.
Right: Same dative: व्रण + निसूदनाय = for the destroying of wounds.
questions.explain: X-निसूदनाय is 'for the destroying of X'. Here X is व्रण (wound). This is a grammar drill, not a medical claim.
questions.rule: X-निसूदनाय = for destroying X.
questions.teaches: The dative of -निसूदन names the thing to be destroyed in the first member.

questions.q: What is the main action ordered by उद्वर्तयेत् in verse 17?
options: To rub down the kuṣṭhas of an oil-anointed man
To burn the leaves to ash
optionExplain: Right: कुष्ठान्युद्वर्तयेत् with तैलाक्तगात्रस्य नरस्य: rub the kuṣṭhas of a man whose body is oil-anointed.
Buttermilk is what the leaves are ground with, not something to drink.
Nothing is said about burning.
No enema is named in this verse.
questions.explain: The main verb is उद्वर्तयेत्; the earlier verb पिष्ट्वा is only the preparation.
questions.rule: Verse 17: grind the leaves, then rub down the kuṣṭhas.

questions.q: Put these four items in the order they stand in verse 17.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives caturaṅgula, then buttermilk, then kākamācī; line 2 ends with the aśvahana leaves.
questions.rule: चतुरङ्गुलस्य → तक्रेण → काकमाच्याः → अश्वहनच्छदैः.

questions.q: The word meaning 'with buttermilk' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 1 reads पर्णानि पिष्ट्वा चतुरङ्गुलस्य तक्रेण.
questions.teaches: तक्रेण is the instrumental singular: 'with, by means of buttermilk'.
questions.rule: Instrumental -एन/-एण = with, by means of.

questions.q: पिष्ट्वा ends in -त्वा. What does the form show?
options: Having ground, an action done before the main verb
optionExplain: A command would be an optative like उद्वर्तयेत्; पिष्ट्वा is a different form.
Right: √पिष् has no prefix here, so the absolutive is -त्वा: 'having ground'.
A noun would not end in -त्वा.
-त्वा does not make a passive.
questions.explain: पिष्ट्वा is the absolutive of √पिष् (abs. in the data): 'having ground'. The main verb comes later.
questions.rule: -त्वा on a prefix-less root = 'having done'; the main verb follows.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 17 say?
options: The leaves of caturaṅgula are ground with buttermilk
The leaves of kākamācī come next (अथ)
The man's body is anointed with oil
The verse says what plant caturaṅgula is
It is stated how the aśvahana leaves are used
optionExplain: Right: पर्णानि पिष्ट्वा चतुरङ्गुलस्य तक्रेण.
Right: पर्णान्यथ काकमाच्याः.
Right: तैलाक्तगात्रस्य नरस्य.
None of the three names is identified in the verse.
Only 'also with aśvahana leaves' is said; no method.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the grinding; line 2 gives the condition of the body, the rubbing and the extra leaves.
questions.rule: Verse 17: grind with buttermilk, rub down; no identification, no method for aśvahana.

questions.q: A made-up compound लोध्र + छदैः (lodhra leaves, with). Using the rule of अश्वहन + छदैः, how is it written joined?
optionExplain: After a short vowel the छ is not left single; च् is added.
No श् comes between a short vowel and छ; the added letter is च्.
Right: A short vowel before छ takes च्: as in अश्वहनच्छदैः.
The added letter is च्, not त्.
questions.explain: अश्वहन ends in a short अ; before छदैः, a च् is added: अश्वहन + छदैः → अश्वहनच्छदैः. So लोध्र + छदैः → लोध्रच्छदैः. This is a grammar drill.
questions.rule: Short vowel + छ → च्छ.
questions.teaches: You can now see why leaf-names like -च्छद appear with a doubled sound after a short vowel.

questions.q: For whom does verse 18 say this pradeha is meant?
options: Those who have taken an emetic
Those with a skin disease only
optionExplain: Headache is not named in this verse.
Nothing about an emetic is said here.
The verse names vāta, not a skin disease; कुष्ठम् is a drug in the list.
Right: वातामयिनाम् = of those afflicted (आमयिन्) with vāta.
questions.explain: The condition is in the second line: वातामयिनां प्रदेहः.
questions.rule: Verse 18: warm ingredients, a pradeha for vāta sufferers.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 18 to its meaning.
pairs: of those afflicted with vāta disorders
questions.explain: These four words give the condition and the state of the ingredients.
questions.rule: वातामयिनाम् = of those with vāta disorders; उष्णानि = warm; यवचूर्णम् = barley flour; अम्लम् = a sour substance.

questions.q: The word in line 2 meaning 'warm' (neuter plural) is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 reads यवचूर्णमम्लमुष्णानि वातामयिनां प्रदेहः.
questions.teaches: उष्णानि is neuter plural and agrees with the whole list of ingredients: all of them are to be warm.
questions.rule: A neuter plural adjective can stand for a whole list.

questions.q: In verse 18, कुष्ठम् stands inside a list of ingredients. What is it there?
options: A drug, one of the ingredients
The disease the pradeha is meant for
A method of preparing the paste
optionExplain: Right: The condition is named separately as वातामयिनाम्; so कुष्ठम् is a listed drug.
The disease is vāta (वातामयिनाम्), not kuṣṭha.
Measures in this chapter are named differently (e.g. कर्ष, आढक in verse 16).
No method word stands here; कुष्ठम् is a name in the list.
questions.explain: कुष्ठम् is nominative singular neuter, in the same list as वचा, शताह्वा, यवचूर्णम्. The data glosses it as the drug.
questions.rule: Same word, two roles: a drug in verse 18, the disease in verse 16.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 18 say?
options: The pradeha is for those afflicted with vāta disorders
The ingredients are to be warm
Barley flour is among the ingredients
The verse gives the dose of each item
optionExplain: Right: वातामयिनां प्रदेहः.
Right: उष्णानि.
Right: यवचूर्णम्.
Headache is not named in verse 18.
No quantity is named.
questions.explain: The first line and the start of the second give the items; the end of the second line gives the warmth and the purpose.
questions.rule: Verse 18: a list of ingredients, warm, for vāta sufferers; no dose.

questions.q: A made-up phrase reads कुष्ठामयिनां प्रदेहः. Following वातामयिनाम्, for whom is it?
optionExplain: That is the verse's phrase; here the first part is कुष्ठ.
Right: Same compound X-आमयिन्, genitive plural: कुष्ठ + आमयिनाम्.
आमयिन् means afflicted, not maker.
The genitive plural names people, those afflicted, not the drug.
questions.explain: X-आमयिनाम् = of those afflicted with X; अ + आ → आ makes कुष्ठामयिनाम्. This is a grammar drill.
questions.rule: X-आमयिनाम् = of those afflicted with X.
questions.teaches: Once you know X-आमयिन्, any 'illness-name + आमयिनाम्' reads as 'for those with that illness'.

questions.q: With what is the first-line pradeha of verse 19 made?
options: Warm vesavāras of the flesh of marsh animals and fish
optionExplain: Those are in verse 20, not here.
Husk-water is in verse 15, not here.
Right: आनूपमत्स्यामिषवेसवारैः उष्णैः: with warm vesavāras of marsh-animal and fish flesh.
Not named in this verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the first preparation and says it removes Vāta (पवनापहः).
questions.rule: Verse 19, line 1: warm vesavāras; pradeha removing Vāta.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 19 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words in the plural instrumental describe what the pradehas are made with.
questions.rule: उष्णैः = with warm; चतुर्भिः = with four; दशमूलमिश्रैः = mixed with daśamūla; गन्धौषधैः = with fragrant drugs.

questions.q: The word before प्रदेहः in line 2, meaning destroying Vāta, is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 ends ... गन्धौषधैश्चानिलहः प्रदेहः.
questions.teaches: अनिल means wind (here Vāta) and -हः means destroying; the whole describes the pradeha.
questions.rule: X-हः = that which destroys X.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वेसवारैरुष्णैः?
optionExplain: The word ends in a visarga (-ः); the र् comes from it, not from a separate word.
रुष्णैः is not a word.
ऐरुष्णैः is not a word.
Right: The visarga after ऐ becomes र् before a vowel: वेसवारैः + उष्णैः → वेसवारैरुष्णैः.
questions.explain: वेसवारैरुष्णैः = वेसवारैः ('with vesavāras') + उष्णैः ('with warm').
questions.rule: ऐः + स्वर → ऐर् + स्वर: वेसवारैः + उष्णैः → वेसवारैरुष्णैः.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 19 say?
options: A pradeha with warm vesavāras removes Vāta
A second pradeha is mixed with daśamūla
The four fats are named in this verse
The ten roots of daśamūla are listed
optionExplain: Right: उष्णैः प्रदेहः पवनापहः.
Right: दशमूलमिश्रैः.
Right: पवनापहः and अनिलहः.
Only चतुर्भिः (four) is said; the fats are not named.
Daśamūla is named as a group; its ten roots are not listed.
questions.explain: Each line names a preparation that removes Vāta; line 2 does not name the four fats or the ten roots.
questions.rule: Verse 19: two Vāta-removing pradehas; the four fats and ten roots are not named.

questions.q: A made-up pair of words: उष्णैः + अम्लैः. Following वेसवारैः + उष्णैः, how are they joined?
optionExplain: Right: ऐः before a vowel becomes ऐर्: उष्णैः + अम्लैः → उष्णैरम्लैः.
A visarga before a vowel (after ऐ) changes to र्; it is not left.
श् appears before च/छ, not before a vowel.
स् appears before त/थ, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: After ऐ, a visarga before a vowel becomes र् and moves to the vowel: उष्णैरम्लैः. This is a grammar drill with invented words.
questions.rule: ऐः + स्वर → ऐर् + स्वर.
questions.teaches: Plural instrumental words in -ऐः join with a following vowel as -ऐर्.

questions.q: According to the first half of verse 20, what does warm barley flour with buttermilk and alkali destroy?
optionExplain: Flank pain is in verse 25, not here.
Right: सक्षारमर्तिं जठरे निहन्यात्: it would destroy pain in the abdomen.
Headache is not named in this verse.
Itching is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 ends अर्तिं जठरे निहन्यात्: pain (अर्ति) in the abdomen (जठर).
questions.rule: Verse 20, line 1: barley flour with buttermilk and alkali, warm, for abdominal pain.

questions.q: Put these four words in the order they stand in line 1 of verse 20.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins तक्रेण युक्तं यवचूर्णमुष्णं सक्षारमर्तिं ...
questions.rule: तक्रेण → यवचूर्णम् → उष्णम् → सक्षारम्.

questions.q: The word meaning 'in the abdomen' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 1 ends अर्तिं जठरे निहन्यात्.
questions.teaches: जठरे is the locative singular: 'in the abdomen'. The locative gives the place where the pain is.
questions.rule: Locative -ए (singular) = in, at.

questions.q: In line 2, वाते is built like जठरे. What does the ending -ए show?
optionExplain: A dual would need a pair; nothing here points to two.
A plural subject would not end in -ए here; and no verb agrees with it.
Right: वाते = 'in Vāta (disorder)', locative singular.
The instrumental sense is with -एन; वाते is a place or condition.
questions.explain: In the data, वाते is locative singular, like जठरे: 'in Vāta'.
questions.rule: -ए can be a locative singular (in) or a dual (two); the sense decides.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 20 say?
options: Barley flour for pain in the abdomen is joined with buttermilk
It is warm and joined with alkali
In Vāta, kuṣṭha and śatāhvā with vacā are prescribed
The second half calls the preparation a pradeha
optionExplain: Right: तक्रेण युक्तं ... जठरे.
Right: उष्णम् and सक्षारम्.
Right: कुष्ठं शताह्वां सवचाम् ... वाते.
The word प्रदेह does not appear in the second half.
Headache is not named in verse 20.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives barley flour for abdominal pain; line 2 gives the list for Vāta, without the word pradeha.
questions.rule: Verse 20: two statements; the second does not say pradeha.

questions.q: A made-up line reads अर्तिं पार्श्वे निहन्यात् (पार्श्व = flank). Following जठरे, what does it say?
options: It would destroy pain of two flanks
It would destroy pain caused by the flank
It would destroy pain in the flank
optionExplain: The ending -ए here is a locative singular, not a dual; the line does not say two.
-ए gives a place, not a cause.
अर्तिम् (pain) is the object, not the flank.
Right: पार्श्वे is a locative singular like जठरे: 'in the flank'.
questions.explain: Same frame as अर्तिं जठरे निहन्यात्: अर्तिम् is destroyed, and the locative gives the place. This is a grammar drill, not a medical claim.
questions.rule: अर्तिं X-ए निहन्यात् = it would destroy pain in X.
questions.teaches: The frame 'अर्तिं + locative + निहन्यात्' tells you where the pain is.

questions.q: Verse 21 ends कुर्यात् प्रदेहं पवने सरक्ते. For which condition is the pradeha made?
optionExplain: Right: पवने सरक्ते = in Vāta accompanied by blood (rakta).
Head pain (शिरोरुजा) is the subject of verses 23 and 24.
Poison is the subject of verse 28.
Body smell is the subject of verse 29.
questions.explain: The pradeha is made in Vāta accompanied by blood.
questions.rule: कुर्यात् प्रदेहं + locative = make a pradeha in that condition.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 21 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the action, what is made, and where.
questions.rule: कुर्यात् = one should make; प्रदेहम् = pradeha; पवने = in Vāta; सितोपलाम् = rock sugar.

questions.q: The word for 'ghee' in the first word of line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 opens with घृतं, the ghee.
questions.teaches: घृतम् is neuter accusative singular, one of the things the pradeha is made with.
questions.rule: घृतम् = ghee, one of the listed items.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सितोपलां?
options: सित + उपलां: अ + उ joins as ओ
optionExplain: पलां is not a word in this verse.
Right: The first word सित means white; अ + उ gives ओ, so सित + उपलां is written सितोपलां.
That loses the उ of उपलां.
ए + उ would not give सितोपलां.
questions.explain: सितोपलां = सित (white) + उपलां (crystal, lump): rock sugar.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: सित + उपला → सितोपला.

questions.q: उभे शताह्वे: the ending -ए and the word उभे show what about the śatāhvās?
options: Many kinds of śatāhvā are meant
Two kinds of śatāhvā are meant
The two kinds are named in the verse
optionExplain: A singular would not be joined by उभे, 'both'.
The plural of such a word ends in -आः, not -ए.
Right: On a word like शताह्वा, the dual ending is -ए, and उभे means 'both'.
The verse names neither of the two; it only says 'both'.
questions.explain: Dual -ए with उभे = the two śatāhvās, which the verse leaves unnamed.
questions.rule: Feminine word in -आ: dual ending -ए = two.

questions.q: An invented line reads कुर्यात् प्रदेहं ज्वरे (ज्वर = fever). By the pattern of verse 21, what does it say?
options: One should make fever with a pradeha
A pradeha is made of fever
One should make a pradeha in fever
optionExplain: The doer of 'make' is not ज्वरे; its ending -ए marks a place or condition.
प्रदेहं (-म्) is what is made, not ज्वरे.
The locative -ए says 'in', not 'of'.
Right: A locative like पवने or ज्वरे names the condition in which it is made.
questions.explain: The pattern is: कुर्यात् + प्रदेहं (what is made) + locative (the condition).
questions.rule: Locative -ए = the condition in which the pradeha is made.
questions.teaches: After कुर्यात् प्रदेहं, a locative word names the condition, as पवने does in verse 21.

questions.q: Verse 22 ends रक्तानिलार्तिं प्रणुदेत् प्रदेहः. What pain would this pradeha drive out?
optionExplain: Right: रक्त = blood and अनिल = wind, Vāta; आर्ति = pain.
Head pain is in verses 23 and 24.
Flank pain is in verse 25.
Poison is in verse 28.
questions.explain: रक्तानिलार्तिं = the pain (आर्ति) of blood (रक्त) and Vāta (अनिल).
questions.rule: रक्त-अनिल-आर्ति = pain of blood and Vāta.

questions.q: Put the first four items of verse 22 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse opens with these four items.
questions.rule: रास्ना → गुडूची → मधुकं → बले द्वे.

questions.q: The word meaning 'cooked, prepared' that describes the ghee is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 2 reads घृतं च सिद्धं: the ghee that has been cooked.
questions.teaches: सिद्धम् is a 'having been done' word (past participle of √सिध्) in the neuter singular, agreeing with घृतम्.
questions.rule: सिद्धम् = cooked, prepared; it describes the ghee.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पयश्च?
options: पयः + च: a visarga before च becomes श्
optionExplain: श्च is not a word.
Right: पयः is 'milk'; ः + च is written श्च.
पयश् is not a word; the word is पयः.
The word is पयः, not पया.
questions.explain: पयश्च = पयः (milk) + च (and).
questions.rule: Visarga + च → श्च.

questions.q: सजीवकं सर्षभकं: the prefix स- is 'with'. What does this say about jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka?
options: They are left out of the pradeha
They go with the listed drugs
optionExplain: 'With' adds them; it does not remove them.
The milk is named separately with पयश्च.
Right: सजीवकम् = with jīvaka; सर्षभकम् = with ṛṣabhaka: they are joined to the list.
The diseases are in रक्तानिलार्तिम्.
questions.explain: A स- word in this list adds an item together with the others.
questions.rule: स- + name = together with that item.

questions.q: An invented line has सदुग्धं चूर्णम् (दुग्ध = milk, चूर्ण = powder). By the pattern of सजीवकम्, what does it mean?
optionExplain: 'Without' would be a different prefix; स- means 'with'.
सदुग्धम् describes the powder, saying it comes with milk.
Nothing in the word names a person.
Right: स- means 'with', so सदुग्धम् is 'with milk'.
questions.explain: The स- prefix works with any name: स + name = with that thing.
questions.rule: स- = with, in verse 22 and in new examples.
questions.teaches: स- before a name makes an adjective 'together with that': सजीवकम् 'with jīvaka', सदुग्धम् 'with milk'.

questions.q: Verse 23 gives pradehas for two conditions. Which pair is it?
options: Vāta with blood, and head pain
optionExplain: Right: वाते सरक्ते in the first half and शिरोरुजायाम् in the second.
Flank pain is verse 25 and poison is verse 28.
Body smell is in verse 29, not here.
Poison is in verse 28, not here.
questions.explain: The first half is for Vāta with blood; the second is for head pain.
questions.rule: वाते सरक्ते + शिरोरुजायाम् = the two conditions of verse 23.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Match each word of verse 23 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words give the conditions, two give the base materials of the first half.
questions.rule: वाते सरक्ते = in Vāta with blood; शिरोरुजायाम् = in head pain; गोधूमचूर्णम् = wheat flour; छगलीपयः = goat's milk.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: The word for 'with ghee' in the verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: सघृतम् occurs in both halves.
questions.teaches: सघृतम् = स + घृतम्: the prefix स- means 'with', so it is 'together with ghee'.
questions.rule: सघृतम् = with ghee.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Which is the right split of नतोत्पलं?
options: नत + उत्पलं: अ + उ joins as ओ
optionExplain: त्पलं is not a word.
Right: नत and उत्पल are the two names; अ + उ is written ओ.
The second name is उत्पल, not ओत्पल.
That would not give नतोत्पलं.
questions.explain: नतोत्पलं = नत + उत्पलं, read as two drugs.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: नत + उत्पल → नतोत्पल.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Which items does the second half name for the head-pain pradeha?
optionExplain: Right: the card reads it as the pair nata and utpala.
Right: it is joined with candana.
Right: it is joined with kuṣṭha.
Wheat flour belongs to the first half.
Goat's milk belongs to the first half.
questions.explain: The second half names nata, utpala, candana and kuṣṭha (with ghee). Wheat flour and goat's milk are in the first half.
questions.rule: First half: Vāta with blood; second half: head pain with nata, utpala, candana, kuṣṭha.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: An invented half-line: ज्वरे सघृतं प्रदेहो यवचूर्णम् (ज्वर = fever, यव = barley). By the pattern of verse 23, what does it say?
options: In barley flour, a pradeha for fever
Fever is made from barley flour
In fever, a pradeha of barley flour with ghee
A pradeha of ghee without barley flour
optionExplain: ज्वरे is the condition; यवचूर्णम् is the material.
The locative -ए says 'in', so it names the condition.
Right: Locative = condition; सघृतम् = with ghee; चूर्णम् = the flour.
सघृतम् is 'with ghee', and the flour is named.
questions.explain: As in the first half of verse 23: condition (locative) + सघृतं प्रदेहः + the flour.
questions.rule: Condition in locative + सघृतं प्रदेहः + material.
questions.teaches: A half-line of this verse has the shape: condition (locative), pradeha 'with ghee', and the material in the nominative.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Verse 24 has शिरोरुजायां सघृतः प्रदेहः. What is its pradeha for?
optionExplain: Flank pain is in verse 25.
That is in verses 21 to 23.
That is in verse 29.
Right: शिरोरुजायाम् = in head pain (शिरः = head, रुजा = pain).
questions.explain: The pradeha of verse 24 is made for head pain.
questions.rule: शिरोरुजायाम् = in head pain.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Match each word of verse 24 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the condition, the ghee, a pair of drugs and the preparation.
questions.rule: शिरोरुजायाम् = in head pain; सघृतः = with ghee; कमलोत्पले = kamala and utpala; प्रदेहः = pradeha.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: कमलोत्पले ends in -ए. This ending shows the ____ number (singular, dual or plural).
questions.explain: The dual ending -ए on a neuter word means two.
questions.teaches: On neuter words in -अ, the dual nominative ends in -ए. कमलोत्पले joins two names, कमल and उत्पल.
questions.rule: Neuter -अ word + dual -ए = two items.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Which is the right split of यष्ट्याह्वमेला?
options: यष्टि + आह्वम् + एला: इ + आ becomes या
optionExplain: Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so यष्टि + आह्वम् is written यष्ट्याह्वम्.
ह्वम् is not a word.
The middle word is आह्वम्, 'named'.
ला is not a word here.
questions.explain: यष्ट्याह्वमेला = यष्टि + आह्वम् + एला: 'the one named yaṣṭi' and elā.
questions.rule: इ + आ → या: यष्टि + आह्वम् → यष्ट्याह्वम्.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: The last pāda ends -कैश्च, an instrumental plural. On this card's reading, how does it relate to the list?
options: It adds further ingredients: 'and with these'
It names the place of application
optionExplain: No disease is named in that pāda.
Right: The instrumental 'with' adds loha, erakā, padmaka and coraka to the list.
It is a list of names in the instrumental, not a verb.
No part of the body is named there.
questions.explain: The instrumental -ऐः / -कैः means 'with'; the pāda gives more ingredients.
questions.rule: Instrumental plural = 'with these'.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: In verse 24, प्रदेहः is printed प्रदेहो before a voiced letter. By the same sandhi, how is प्रदेहः + मृदुः (मृदु = soft) written?
optionExplain: र् replaces a visarga after इ or उ, not after अ.
The visarga after अ does not become आ.
Right: After अ, a visarga before a voiced consonant becomes ओ.
Before a voiced consonant the visarga after अ is changed to ओ.
questions.explain: The same rule gives प्रदेहो in verse 24 and प्रदेहो मृदुः here.
questions.rule: अः + voiced consonant → ओ (after अ).
questions.teaches: A word ending in -अः followed by a voiced consonant turns into -ओ, as in प्रदेहो in verse 24.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Verse 25 ends पार्श्वरुजासु. Pains of which part of the body is the application for?
optionExplain: Head pain is in verses 23 and 24.
Skin is not named in verse 25.
The throat is not named in verse 25.
Right: पार्श्व = flank or side; रुजा = pain.
questions.explain: पार्श्वरुजासु = in pains of the flank.
questions.rule: पार्श्व-रुजा = flank pain.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Match each word of verse 25 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give two of the ingredients, the oil, and the condition.
questions.rule: हरिद्रे = the two haridrās; पार्श्वरुजासु = in pains of the flank; जीवन्तिमूलम् = root of jīvantī; सतैलम् = with oil.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: The word meaning 'application, anointing' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The line reads सतैलमालेपनं, which is सतैलम् + आलेपनम्.
questions.teaches: आलेपनम् names the preparation. Here it takes the place of the word प्रदेह used in the other verses.
questions.rule: आलेपनम् = application, anointing.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Which is the right split of कोष्णम्?
options: क + उष्णम्: अ + उ joins as ओ
optionExplain: Right: क is a prefix meaning 'a little' and उष्ण is 'warm'; अ + उ is written ओ.
ष्णम् is not a word.
उ + उ would give कूष्णम्.
The second word is उष्ण, not ओष्ण.
questions.explain: कोष्णम् = क (slightly) + उष्णम् (warm): lukewarm.
questions.rule: क + उष्ण → कोष्ण = slightly warm.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Which two fats does verse 25 name for the application?
optionExplain: सतैलम् adds oil to the ghee.
Right: सघृतं सतैलम् = with ghee, with oil.
Milk is not named in verse 25 and ghee is.
Neither is named in verse 25.
questions.explain: सघृतं सतैलम् = with ghee and with oil.
questions.rule: सघृतम् + सतैलम् = ghee and oil.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: An invented phrase: जानुरुजासु (जानु = knee). Compared with शिरोरुजायाम्, what does the ending -सु show?
options: A single pain: 'in one knee pain'
The thing made, not a condition
optionExplain: The single form would end like शिरोरुजायाम्.
A doer would be in the nominative, not -सु.
Right: -सु is the locative plural, as in पार्श्वरुजासु 'in pains of the flank'.
-सु is a locative, which gives the condition.
questions.explain: -आयाम् is the singular locative, -आसु the plural: शिरोरुजायाम् 'in head pain' against पार्श्वरुजासु 'in pains of the flank'.
questions.rule: Locative singular -आयाम्; locative plural -आसु.
questions.teaches: Feminine words in -आ end the locative in -आयाम् (one) and -आसु (several): 'in a pain' against 'in pains'.
questions.section: वातरक्त, सिरदर्द और पार्श्व-शूल के प्रदेह

questions.q: Verse 26 ends निर्वापणः स्यात् सघृतः प्रदेहः. What kind of pradeha is it said to be?
options: Lukewarm, like the application in verse 25
A remover of body smell, like verse 29
optionExplain: कोष्ण, 'lukewarm', is the word in verse 25.
Poison is the subject of verse 28.
Body smell is the subject of verse 29.
Right: निर्वापण = cooling, quenching, as the data glosses it.
questions.explain: The verse calls this ghee pradeha निर्वापण: cooling.
questions.rule: निर्वापणः = cooling, quenching.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Match each word of verse 26 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make up the closing clause of the verse.
questions.rule: निर्वापणः = cooling; सघृतः = with ghee; स्यात् = it would be; प्रदेहः = pradeha.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: The word meaning 'it would be' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The clause is निर्वापणः स्यात् सघृतः प्रदेहः.
questions.teaches: स्यात् is the third person singular optative of √अस्: 'it would be, it may be'. The verse says what the pradeha would be.
questions.rule: स्यात् = it would be (optative of √अस्).
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: सघृतः is masculine, nominative singular. Which word in verse 26 does it describe?
optionExplain: Right: Both are masculine nominative singular: the pradeha comes with ghee.
चन्दनानि is neuter plural, so it does not match.
This compound is neuter plural, so it does not match.
स्यात् is a verb, not a describing word.
questions.explain: A describing word copies the gender, number and case of its noun: सघृतः goes with प्रदेहः.
questions.rule: Describing word and noun agree in gender, number and case.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Verses 24 and 26 both name prapauṇḍarīka and utpala. What does each verse give for its own pradeha?
optionExplain: The two are the wrong way round.
Right: 24 ends शिरोरुजायाम्; 26 ends निर्वापणः स्यात्.
Verse 26 names no condition, only निर्वापण.
Verse 24 names head pain.
questions.explain: The shared names do not make the two pradehas the same: each verse states its own purpose.
questions.rule: Same drug names, different stated purpose: read the verse's own ending.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: An invented line: लेपो मृदुः स्यात् (लेप = paste, मृदु = soft). By the pattern of निर्वापणः स्यात्, what does it say?
optionExplain: स्यात् is optative, not a past form.
An order would use another verb form.
Right: स्यात् = it would be, as in निर्वापणः स्यात्.
Nothing in the line negates it.
questions.explain: स्यात् states what something would be: निर्वापणः स्यात् 'would be cooling', लेपो मृदुः स्यात् 'the paste would be soft'.
questions.rule: X स्यात् = X would be.
questions.teaches: स्यात् with a describing word says what the thing would be; the word before it names the quality.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Verse 27 contains निर्वापणः, the word also found in verse 26. Which effect does it name?
optionExplain: Warming is the opposite of निर्वापण.
Poison is the subject of verse 28.
That is verse 25.
Right: निर्वापण = cooling, quenching.
questions.explain: The list closes with निर्वापणः स्यात्: it would be cooling.
questions.rule: निर्वापणः = cooling.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Match each word of verse 27 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the closing statement and the roots.
questions.rule: निर्वापणः = cooling; मूलम् = root; कुशकाशयोः = of kuśa and of kāśa; स्यात् = it would be.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: कुशकाशयोः names kuśa and kāśa; its ending -ओः marks the ____ number (singular, dual or plural).
questions.explain: -ओः on a name in -अ is the genitive dual: 'of the two'.
questions.teaches: -ओः is the genitive (and locative) dual ending of words in -अ. कुशकाशयोः means 'of kuśa and of kāśa'.
questions.rule: -ओः on a word in -अ = dual: of two.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्याज्जलमेरका?
options: स्यात् + जलम् + एरका: त् before ज becomes ज्
optionExplain: Right: त् + ज is written ज्ज; म् + ए is written मे.
ज्जलमेरका is not a word.
The last name is एरका.
स्याज् is not a word.
questions.explain: स्याज्जलमेरका = स्यात् ('would be') + जलम् ('water') + एरका.
questions.rule: Final त् + ज → ज्ज.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: निर्वापणः is masculine singular, and the verse has no noun for it. Which word is understood?
optionExplain: जलम् is neuter, so it could not take the masculine निर्वापणः.
Right: प्रदेहः is masculine singular, like निर्वापणः, and the neighbouring verses use it.
एरका is feminine, so it does not match.
दूर्वा is feminine, so it does not match.
questions.explain: A describing word needs a noun of the same gender and number: the understood noun is प्रदेहः.
questions.rule: निर्वापणः (masculine) agrees with an understood प्रदेहः.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: An invented phrase: यवगोधूमयोश्चूर्णम् (यव = barley, गोधूम = wheat). By the pattern of कुशकाशयोश्च, what does it mean?
options: Flour for the barley and wheat eaters
Barley and wheat made of flour
Flour of barley and of wheat
optionExplain: No eaters are named; -योः is 'of the two things'.
चूर्णम् is the flour; barley and wheat are in the genitive.
Right: -योः is 'of the two': the flour belongs to both barley and wheat.
-योः names two things, so wheat is included.
questions.explain: Genitive dual + a noun = 'of the two': यवगोधूमयोः + चूर्णम्, joined by visarga + च → श्च.
questions.rule: Name + name in -योः = of the two.
questions.teaches: A genitive dual in -योः joins two names: 'of kuśa and of kāśa', 'of barley and of wheat'.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Verse 28 says the pradeha would quickly destroy something (निहन्यात्). What is it?
optionExplain: Body smell is in verse 29.
Head pain is in verses 23 and 24.
Flank pain is in verse 25.
Right: विषं निहन्यात् = it would destroy poison.
questions.explain: The object of निहन्यात् is विषम्, poison.
questions.rule: विषं निहन्यात् = would destroy poison.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Match each word of verse 28 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the main statement.
questions.rule: विषम् = poison; अचिरात् = quickly; निहन्यात् = it would destroy; सकुष्ठे = with kuṣṭha.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Without sandhi, निहन्यादचिरात् is निहन्यात् + ____ (type the second word in Devanagari).
questions.explain: निहन्यादचिरात् = निहन्यात् + अचिरात्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्: निहन्यात् + अचिरात् is written निहन्यादचिरात्.
questions.rule: Final त् + vowel → द् + vowel.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Which is the right split of शिरीषस्तु?
options: शिरीषः + तु: a visarga before त becomes स्
optionExplain: Right: ः + त is written स्त.
स्तु is not a word.
ओ appears before a voiced consonant, and त is not voiced.
र् replaces a visarga after इ or उ, not after अ.
questions.explain: शिरीषस्तु = शिरीषः + तु: 'but, and' joined to śirīṣa.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स्त.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: ससिन्धुवारः has the prefix स-. What does it say about śirīṣa?
options: It is the opposite of sindhuvāra
It is a disease named sindhuvāra
optionExplain: 'With' joins; it does not replace.
Right: स- means 'with': śirīṣa with sindhuvāra.
Nothing in the word says opposite.
सिन्धुवार is listed beside śirīṣa as a drug name.
questions.explain: ससिन्धुवारः = स + सिन्धुवारः: with sindhuvāra.
questions.rule: स- + name = together with that thing.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: An invented line: ज्वरं निहन्यादयं लेपः (ज्वर = fever, अयम् = this). By the pattern of विषं निहन्यात् प्रदेहः, what is destroyed?
options: Nothing, since this is a question
optionExplain: लेपः ends in -ः, the doer.
The line is a statement.
Right: ज्वरं ends in -म्, the thing acted on, like विषम्; लेपः is the doer.
No physician is named.
questions.explain: Masculine nominative -ः names the doer (प्रदेहः, लेपः); neuter accusative -म् names the thing acted on (विषम्, ज्वरम्).
questions.rule: Accusative names what is destroyed; nominative names what destroys.
questions.teaches: With निहन्यात्, the accusative (-म् on neuter -अ nouns, as विषम्) names what is destroyed; the nominative (-ः on masculine -अ nouns, as प्रदेहः, लेपः) names what destroys.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: In verse 29, the pradeha of patra, ambu, lodhra, abhaya and candana removes what?
optionExplain: Poison is in verse 28.
Head pain is in verses 23 and 24.
Flank pain is in verse 25.
Right: The second half ends शरीरदौर्गन्ध्यहरः प्रदेहः: remover of body smell.
questions.explain: The second half is for body smell.
questions.rule: शरीरदौर्गन्ध्यहरः = remover of body smell.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Put the four items of the first half in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The first half lists these four, ending with lodhra in the instrumental.
questions.rule: शिरीष → लामज्जक → हेम → लोध्र.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: The first half names its means with a word meaning 'rubbing': ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The first half ends प्रघर्षः, the second half प्रदेहः.
questions.teaches: प्रघर्षः (rubbing) is the means of the first half; the second half uses प्रदेहः. The verse uses two different words for the two applications.
questions.rule: प्रघर्षः = rubbing (first half); प्रदेहः = pradeha (second half).
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Which is the right split of त्वग्दोष?
options: त्वक् + दोष: क् before the voiced द becomes ग्
optionExplain: Right: त्वक् is 'skin'; क् + द is written ग्द.
The first word is त्वक्, ending in a consonant.
The second word is दोष.
ग्दोष is not a word.
questions.explain: त्वग्दोष = त्वक् (skin) + दोष (disorder).
questions.rule: Final क् + voiced consonant → ग्.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Which pairing matches the two halves of verse 29?
options: Rubbing: body smell. Pradeha: skin disorders and sweating
Rubbing: skin disorders and sweating. Pradeha: body smell
optionExplain: That swaps the two halves.
Right: The first half ends प्रघर्षः, the second ends प्रदेहः.
Poison is in verse 28.
The first half names skin disorders and sweating.
questions.explain: Each half has its own means and its own effect.
questions.rule: First half: प्रघर्ष → skin and sweat; second: प्रदेह → body smell.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: An invented phrase: दाहहरः प्रदेहः (दाह = burning). By the pattern of शरीरदौर्गन्ध्यहरः, what is it?
options: A burning that removes the pradeha
optionExplain: -हरः means removing, not causing.
The pradeha is the subject, and burning is what is removed.
Right: A compound ending in -हरः means 'remover of the first part'.
-हरः is the last part of the compound, not a person addressed.
questions.explain: X-हरः = remover of X: शरीरदौर्गन्ध्यहरः 'remover of body smell', दाहहरः 'remover of burning'.
questions.rule: X-हरः = removing X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -हरः names what is removed in its first part.
questions.section: शीतल प्रदेह, विष, त्वचा और दुर्गन्ध

questions.q: Verse 30 sums up the chapter. Who is said to have declared the pradehas?
options: A physician of a later age, not named in the verse
The pupil who asks the questions
optionExplain: The verse names the speaker: आत्रिजः.
No pupil is named in this verse.
जगतः is the world, for whose benefit they are declared, not the speaker.
Right: इहात्रिजः = इह + आत्रिजः; आत्रिजः is the son of Atri, Ātreya, who said (उवाच) them.
questions.explain: आत्रिजः is the subject of उवाच: Ātreya declared the pradehas.
questions.rule: आत्रिजः (nominative) + उवाच = Ātreya said.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 30 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say where, who did what, and why.
questions.rule: इह = here; उवाच = said, declared; जगतः = of the world; हितार्थम् = for the benefit.

questions.q: The word meaning 'thirty-two' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: Line 1 has द्वात्रिंशतं.
questions.teaches: द्वात्रिंशतम् is a number word in the accusative singular, standing beside the plural चूर्णप्रदेहान्: 'the thirty-two (pradehas)'.
questions.rule: द्वात्रिंशतम् = thirty-two.

questions.q: सिद्धतमान् ends in -आन्, an accusative plural. Which word of the verse does it describe?
optionExplain: Right: Both are accusative plural masculine: 'the most effective powder pradehas'.
द्वात्रिंशतम् is singular, so it does not match.
जगतः is a genitive singular, so it does not match.
आत्रिजः is a nominative singular, so it does not match.
questions.explain: A describing word copies the case and number of its noun: सिद्धतमान् goes with चूर्णप्रदेहान्.
questions.rule: सिद्धतमान् + चूर्णप्रदेहान् = the most effective powder pradehas.

questions.q: Which statements does verse 30 itself make about the pradehas?
options: They are declared for the benefit of the world
Each one cures exactly one named disease
They were first taught by Indra
optionExplain: Right: द्वात्रिंशतम्.
Right: चूर्ण-प्रदेहान्.
Right: विविधामयघ्नान्.
Right: जगतो हितार्थम्.
The verse says 'various diseases' and names none.
Indra is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives the number, the powder form, the effect on various diseases, and the purpose.
questions.rule: Verse 30: 32 powder pradehas, destroying various diseases, for the world's benefit.

questions.q: An invented phrase: जनानां सुखार्थम् (जन = people, सुख = happiness). By the pattern of जगतो हितार्थम्, what does it mean?
options: From the happiness of the people
For the happiness of the people
The happiness of people has no purpose
optionExplain: 'From' would need a different ending.
Right: -अर्थम् means 'for the sake of'; the genitive names whose benefit it is.
-अर्थम् does not name a doer.
-अर्थम् states a purpose, not its absence.
questions.explain: Genitive + X-अर्थम् = for the sake of X, for those people: जगतः + हितार्थम्, जनानाम् + सुखार्थम्.
questions.rule: Genitive + X-अर्थम् = for X of those.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -अर्थम् states a purpose: 'for the sake of' what comes before it.
